src: For every pair of odors, the distance between the two odors' KC responses is one minus the cosine similarity of the two population response vectors (one entry per KC, trial-averaged), computed per recording and averaged over recordings; the 120 pair distances of a genotype form its 16 × 16 matrix. For the ORNs every comparison over the 16 odors uses one minus the Pearson correlation across the 36 glomeruli imaged in both ORN panels (the glomeruli of the model's ORN input), between the two odors' fly-mean responses: each glomerulus's response averaged over a fly's trials and then over the flies of the odor's panel (the megamat panel for 12 of the odors, the validation2 panel for paa, -aPine, euc and B-myr; the two were imaged in different flies). src: - **Noise floor and the distance without the trial noise:** two noisy response vectors are never parallel, so noise inflates every cosine distance toward 1. From the three trials of each odor, the distance between two independent trial means of the same odor is the noise floor ({{data:ctrl_trial_mean_floor ~ .2f}} in control flies, {{data:tnt_trial_mean_floor ~ .2f}} with APL output blocked (TNT); between single trials {{data:ctrl_single_trial_floor ~ .2f}} and {{data:tnt_single_trial_floor ~ .2f}}). The distance that a recording without the noise would show is estimated across repeats: one minus the cosine between single trials of the two odors from different repeats, divided by the geometric mean of the two odors' cosines between their own trials across the same repeats, which assumes only that the noise of different repeats is independent. Without the noise the relation between the two matrices is nearly what it is as measured (ρ={{data:noise_free_rho_ctrl_tnt ~ .2f}} on odor-odor distances between the two KC matrices, isotonic R² {{data:noise_free_iso_r2 ~ .2f}}) and the block is somewhat larger; mostly the level moves, and a deterministic model is compared with that level. Until the recordings' repeats were examined, this page used a correction that divided each pair's cosine by the odors' signal norms (the trial mean's squared norm minus its noise share). It takes the noise of two odors to be independent, which the repeats contradict, and it put the distances too low ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)); where a result was made with it, the text says so.
out: - **Noise ceiling and the correlation without the trial noise:** two noisy response vectors are never parallel, so noise pulls every correlation toward 0. src: - **The amplitude part and the shape part of the pattern part:** the pattern part splits once more, again exactly and with nothing fitted ([how, and what each part can say](#fn-pattern-split)). The spread of an effect is its standard deviation across the 120 pairs, which says how unevenly APL moves the pairs apart. The amplitude part is the difference between the model's spread and the flies': the cost of moving the pairs apart too unevenly, or too evenly, whatever the pattern. The shape part is the rest, the cost of moving the wrong pairs most: it is zero for a model whose effect is the flies' stretched or squeezed about its mean. The squared pattern part is the squared amplitude part plus the squared shape part. Both are given with the model's spread as a multiple of the flies', because a model that spreads its effect widely has a larger shape part for the same pattern.

src: **How well the mean is known.** The data's mean effect carries two uncertainties of about the same size. One is the sample of flies: the 90 % interval in the table. The other is how the distances are computed: from the mean distances with sub-threshold responses set to 0, the convention closest to a model's spike counts, the mean effect is smaller, and without the trial noise it is hardly above the measured one (both in the table; the noise correction used before, which put it higher, was biased: [the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). The loss uses the matrices as measured, so a mean part smaller than these differences is within what the data leave open. A third choice is on the model's side: whether its spike counts are compared raw, as here, or compressed as the calcium indicator compresses them, which for the best models moves the mean effect by more than either ([the main target under a compressive readout](#readout)), unless the model's KCs are given a ceiling on their firing, with which the two come to nearly the same number ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). A fourth is the length of the model's odor pulse, 0.5 s where the flies' was 2 s: at the flies' pulse the mean effect of the breadth-2 APL-effect fit halves on raw counts and hardly moves under the readout ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)); with a firing ceiling whose adaptation outlasts the odor, raw counts read as the flies were recorded keep the mean effect of the 0.5 s pulse ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)). src: **Realism is a constraint, not a target.** The mean part of the loss can be lowered without APL doing anything right pair by pair: if more KCs respond with APL off, the APL-off distances fall and the effect grows. src: **What the data's trial-to-trial noise means for these targets.** Every model on this page is one deterministic run, while the KC matrices are means of three noisy trials. Putting [trial-to-trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) into the reference model at the level that reproduces the data's single-trial and three-trial floors, and passing ten pseudo-recordings through the data's own pipeline, shows three things. Fast noise on the PN rates cannot reach the data's floors at all (it averages out over the response window), while per-trial jitter of each KC's excitability or of each glomerulus's input gain can, at an unchanged response rate. Measured that way, the model's block shrinks by about a third, so a deterministic block equal to the measured one understates the data's block without the noise ({{data:noise_free_block ~ +.3f}} by the estimate across repeats, 90 % interval {{data:noise_free_block.lo ~ +.3f}} to {{data:noise_free_block.hi ~ +.3f}}; the correction in use when these runs were made gave {{E43/onoff_noise.csv:model=data;matrix=corrected;transform=graded:block ~ +.3f}}). And this noise lowers the model's mean distances, where the flies' noise raises theirs. The reason was found later in the recordings' repeats: the jitter is one draw per KC and trial, so the odors of a trial share all of it, while in the flies only part of the trial-to-trial variability is shared between the odors of a repeat. With the noise re-specified to the flies' shares the reference model's three-trial means lie above its distances without noise, as the flies' do (mean distance with APL on {{E81/mix_scores.csv:name=E44-thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:mean_on ~ .2f}} against {{E81/mix_scores.csv:name=E44-thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=det:mean_on ~ .2f}}), and the scores of the populations of wirings read through the noise hardly move ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). The odor-odor order (ρ on odor-odor distances, isotonic R², response rate ρ) is unchanged by the noise.

src: **Fitting the block through the noise does not find a noise-robust one.** Where the fitted block lives: the KCs that separate a fruity × small-ester pair with APL on are ordinary responders (the same threshold margins and spike counts as every other APL-on response), and the APL-on response as a whole sits at threshold (about half of all responses within one jitter σ, against a third with APL off), so the block's fragility is the APL-on response's, not a special population's; the block-specific weak point is the KCs that APL turns into separators, whose suppressed odor sits just below threshold and comes back on one trial in seven. Joint fits whose block term was computed on nine jittered runs (three pseudo-recordings of three trials, fixed draws) found no noise-robust block in any of the three bases: the fit of the eight at 1.25 stayed at its seed, the fit of the reference model at 40 Hz tuned its own draws' block onto the target by lowering the deterministic block while the block through independent noise followed the deterministic one, and the fit of the reference model at 70 Hz, whose seed's own-draw block already sat on the target, did not move at all. With nine draws the fitted statistic carries a sampling error as large as the effect, so the fits fit the draw. One direction did appear: two simplex vertices one step from the eight at 1.25, with KC–KC inhibition at 27–33 instead of 12 and a lower somatic threshold, keep three times the optimum's block through independent noise (half the data's), paid with the APL-off response rate; whether that survives once a fit recovers the APL-off statistics is the next experiment.

src: **The margins alone do not predict the block through the noise where it matters.** Each KC × odor entry's [threshold margin](#fn-margin), read off the deterministic run, gives the probability that the entry changes on a jittered trial. [Replaying every KC at the pipeline's own jittered thresholds](#fn-replay) with the rest of the network held at the deterministic run reproduces the pipeline exactly for the bouton base without KC–KC inhibition (block {{E55/per_model.csv:model=base70:obs_block_raw ~ +.3f}} in both), ranks the {{E55/agreement.csv:key=block_raw:n ~ .0f}} models' block through the noise (ρ {{E55/agreement.csv:key=block_raw:spearman ~ .2f}}, mean absolute error {{E55/agreement.csv:key=block_raw:mae ~ .3f}}) and matches their response rates and mean distances, but it misses what the KC–KC inhibition does with the jitter, in proportion to the inhibition's weight relative to the somatic threshold (the network's share of the single-trial floor against KC–KC / somatic threshold: ρ {{E55/agreement.csv:key=net_floor_vs_kckc:spearman ~ .2f}}). In the gain-1.5 family, where the fitted KC–KC is weak, the margins give the pipeline's block within its own sampling error; for the eight at 1.25 they promise too much; and in the strong-KC–KC models that carry a block through the noise they are off in either direction (KC–KC held at 30: {{E55/per_model.csv:model=E53-thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc30_k2_cap3:pred_block_raw ~ +.3f}} promised against {{E55/per_model.csv:model=E53-thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc30_k2_cap3:obs_block_raw ~ +.3f}} delivered). A margin term in the loss would therefore reward the KC–KC direction for block the network does not deliver: noise-robustness in that direction has to be simulated, or the proxy has to include the network's first response. A single margin statistic, the fraction of APL-on responses within one σ of threshold, is unrelated to the block a model loses through the noise (ρ {{E55/agreement.csv:key=within_sigma_vs_lost:spearman ~ .2f}}).

src: **[Iterating the KC–KC loop over the replayed trials](#fn-network-proxy) recovers the pipeline, at a cost that scales like a simulation.** Feeding each KC the inhibition from the other KCs' replayed spikes of the same trial, and repeating, closes the margin proxy's gap: after five passes the block through the noise of {{E56/agreement_pass.csv:key=block_raw;pass=5:n ~ .0f}} models agrees with the pipeline to a mean absolute error of {{E56/agreement_pass.csv:key=block_raw;pass=5:mae ~ .3f}} (ρ {{E56/agreement_pass.csv:key=block_raw;pass=5:spearman ~ .2f}}; the margins alone {{E56/agreement_pass.csv:key=block_raw;pass=1:mae ~ .3f}}), the APL-on single-trial floor to {{E56/agreement_pass.csv:key=floor_on;pass=5:mae ~ .3f}}, the response rates and mean distances having matched from the first pass. The iteration is a damped oscillation that has converged by the fifth pass for KC–KC up to about 33 over somatic thresholds near 60 (KC–KC held at 30: {{E56/per_model_pass.csv:model=E53-thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc30_k2_cap3;pass=5:pred_block_raw ~ +.3f}} against the pipeline's {{E56/per_model_pass.csv:model=E53-thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc30_k2_cap3;pass=5:obs_block_raw ~ +.3f}}) and still oscillates at the strongest inhibition tested (KC–KC held at 45: {{E56/per_model_pass.csv:model=E53-thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc45_k2_cap3;pass=5:pred_block_raw ~ +.3f}} against {{E56/per_model_pass.csv:model=E53-thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc45_k2_cap3;pass=5:obs_block_raw ~ +.3f}}). Each pass is a network computation over every trial, so five passes cost about a sixth of the pipeline's thirty simulated trials and twenty-five times a deterministic evaluation: enough to score candidates and to stand in for the pipeline as the validation of a KC–KC-carried block, not yet cheap enough to sit inside a fit.

src: **The glomerulus gain above 1.5 makes a smaller block more robust and lowers the agreement with both KC matrices.** The other candidate carrier of a noise-robust block, a drive large enough that the block's carriers sit well above threshold, was tested along the gain axis: the eight-glomerulus gain at 1.75 and 2, fitted from the gain-1.5 optima at both per-claw thresholds and scored through the trial-noise pipeline, with the no-gain and gain-1.25 fits run through the same pipeline as the lower anchors. On the reference base (40 Hz) the block through the noise falls above 1.5 ({{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.5:block_raw ~ +.3f}} at 1.5, {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.75:block_raw ~ +.3f}} at 1.75, {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain2:block_raw ~ +.3f}} at 2; the data {{data:block ~ +.3f}}) with the deterministic block ({{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.5:block_det ~ +.3f}} to {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain2:block_det ~ +.3f}}), the APL-off response rate overshoots ({{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.75:rate_trial_off ~ .3f}} and {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain2:rate_trial_off ~ .3f}} against the data's {{data:tnt_frac ~ .3f}}) and the loss rises from {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.5:loss_recorded ~ .2f}} to {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain2:loss_recorded ~ .2f}}. At 70 Hz the share of the deterministic block that survives the noise rises with the gain (three-trial means {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain1.25:block_raw ~ +.3f}}, {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain1.5:block_raw ~ +.3f}}, {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain1.75:block_raw ~ +.3f}}, {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain2:block_raw ~ +.3f}} at gain 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2) while the deterministic block falls ({{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain1.25:block_det ~ +.3f}} to {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain2:block_det ~ +.3f}}) and the loss rises from {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain1.5:loss_recorded ~ .2f}} to {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain2:loss_recorded ~ .2f}}. At both thresholds ρ on odor-odor distances with the two KC matrices falls along the axis (40 Hz: {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.5:rho_raw_on ~ .2f}} / {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.5:rho_raw_off ~ .2f}} at 1.5 to {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain2:rho_raw_on ~ .2f}} / {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain2:rho_raw_off ~ .2f}} at 2; 70 Hz: {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain1.5:rho_raw_on ~ .2f}} / {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain1.5:rho_raw_off ~ .2f}} to {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain2:rho_raw_on ~ .2f}} / {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain2:rho_raw_off ~ .2f}}), as do the natural-source alignment and the structure beyond the ORN input: the gain's contribution to noise-robustness is spent by 1.5, and above it the gain is closed for the agreement with the two KC matrices as KC–KC inhibition is bounded by the APL-off per-odor spread. The lower anchors reverse the picture for the block: the two no-gain fits, which the loss ranks worst, carry the most block through the noise of any fitted model ({{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1:block_raw ~ +.3f}} three-trial means / {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1:block_grand ~ +.3f}} grand mean at 40 Hz with KC–KC {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1:kc_kc_inh ~ .0f}}, the data's measured {{data:block ~ +.3f}}; {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain1:block_raw ~ +.3f}} / {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain1:block_grand ~ +.3f}} at 70 Hz with KC–KC {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain1:kc_kc_inh ~ .0f}}), reach the data's APL-on single-trial floor and, at 40 Hz, the best APL-off agreement with the KC matrix in the noise tables ({{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1:rho_raw_off ~ .2f}}), at the cost of the APL-off response rate ({{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1:rate_trial_off ~ .3f}} and {{E58/comparison.csv:key=thr70_gain1:rate_trial_off ~ .3f}} against {{data:tnt_frac ~ .3f}}) and its per-odor pattern: across the table the block through the noise follows the fitted KC–KC scale, not the gain, so the gain and KC–KC inhibition are the two ways the fits make the deterministic block and only the KC–KC way survives the noise, which the deterministic loss cannot see. The two-ρ fit ([below](#gap-pairs)) later separated the two for the no-gain base: re-fitted out of the strong-KC–KC regime, it keeps {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_nogain_rho:block_raw ~ +.3f}} through the noise (three-trial means) with KC–KC at {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_nogain_rho:kc_kc_inh ~ .0f}}, so across the gain the block through the noise goes with the absence of the gain rather than with the KC–KC scale.

src: **Fitting the block through the noise does not find a noise-robust one.** Where the fitted block lives: the KCs that separate a fruity × small-ester pair with APL on are ordinary responders (the same threshold margins and spike counts as every other APL-on response), and the APL-on response as a whole sits at threshold (about half of all responses within one jitter σ, against a third with APL off), so the block's fragility is the APL-on response's, not a special population's; the block-specific weak point is the KCs that APL turns into separators, whose suppressed odor sits just below threshold and comes back on one trial in seven.

src: On the main target the fit moved the wrong way, to where the held fits already were. Its [APL-effect loss](#apl-effect) is {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E60_proxy_fit;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_proxyP3r_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} against the seed's {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E45_gain_at_ctrl_frac;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} (the fits held at 20 and 30: {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E53_kckc_held_block;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc20_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} and {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E53_kckc_held_block;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc30_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}; the data's floor {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}}), its mean APL effect {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E60_proxy_fit;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_proxyP3r_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} against {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E45_gain_at_ctrl_frac;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} (the data {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}) and its ρ on the per-pair APL effect {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E60_proxy_fit;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_proxyP3r_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_spearman ~ .2f}} against {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E45_gain_at_ctrl_frac;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_spearman ~ .2f}} (ceiling {{data:apl_effect_rho_ceiling ~ .2f}}); under the calibrated readout of the spike counts ([below](#readout)) the loss rises as well, from {{E65/by_variant_readout.csv:folder=E45_gain_at_ctrl_frac;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=saturating_cal_pr:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} to {{lit:0.107 # the saturating readout calibrated on the APL-on participation ratio (E65_spike_count_readout.score_readout) applied to data/model_outputs/E60_proxy_fit/thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_proxyP3r_k2_cap3 spike counts; E60_proxy_fit.md, part B table}}. Three models in this regime, one found by the optimizer and two imposed, sit at the same place on the main target, so the cost belongs to the regime: in it more of the inhibition is carried by the KC–KC connections, which remain when APL is blocked, the somatic threshold is lower and the KCs that respond fire harder, and blocking APL changes the distances less. On this base the block that survives the noise and the main target therefore pull against each other, and a model that is to have both needs a carrier of the block other than the strength of KC–KC inhibition; the candidates are the mechanisms that act on which KCs respond, whose block survives the compressive readout ([below](#readout)). src: **Does weak claw input have to count for nothing?** Letting a claw's input below the threshold count with a reduced slope, a quarter or a half, instead of nothing removes most of what the threshold does: the structure beyond the ORN input and the natural-source alignment fall steadily toward the model without a dead zone, the decorrelation level drops, and the weak odors are not recruited, since their PNs sit too far below the knee for a reduced slope to matter. What the slope buys is agreement with the APL output blocked (TNT) matrix, at the cost of more over-sharing among the esters with APL on, and at the fitted combined models it raises the extended loss ({{E41/stats_variants.csv:B_thr40_g0:xl_loss ~ .2f}} to {{E41/stats_variants.csv:B_thr40_g0.25:xl_loss ~ .2f}} with a quarter slope at 40 Hz). The per-claw threshold therefore works as a hard rectifier, which predicts that PN input below about 50 Hz contributes little to a claw's drive onto the soma, against the graded claw calcium reported in imaging. In the best models the question was asked again on the main target, with the knee near the largest PN rate, and it has the same answer from the other side: what such a knee does for the pairs of odors it was tried for, it does only with nothing passed below it ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)).

src: Three models in this regime, one found by the optimizer and two imposed, sit at the same place on the main target, so the cost belongs to the regime: in it more of the inhibition is carried by the KC–KC connections, which remain when APL is blocked, the somatic threshold is lower and the KCs that respond fire harder, and blocking APL changes the distances less. On this base the block that survives the noise and the main target therefore pull against each other, and a model that is to have both needs a carrier of the block other than the strength of KC–KC inhibition; the candidates are the mechanisms that act on which KCs respond, whose block survives the compressive readout ([below](#readout)).

src: **Why it works.** With the threshold re-tuned, the term reassigns responses: the oracle's co-responder set supplies 55–67 % of the fruity / small-ester responses lost but gets only 25–42 % of those gained, so shared responders fall for the block pairs while other pairs keep theirs. A KC's lateral inhibition grows with how many of its connectome neighbours are co-active, which is largest in the dense, overlapping ester populations: the oracle's suppression without the oracle. The weight structure is part of it: with KC identities shuffled or uniform all-to-all weights, the generic effects (decorrelation, excess sharing, the APL-off matrix) are unchanged but the block falls to the noise floor, so the hemibrain's claw-to-claw contacts, which pair KCs sharing calyx neighbourhoods, are what make the term find the ester co-responders.

src: **What the gain's response-rate cost is.** Comparing the per-odor response fractions of the fits with and without the gain against the KC data (figure below), the cost is confined to the APL-on condition: against the APL output blocked (TNT) data the gain costs nothing at 70 Hz and helps at 40 Hz. With APL on, three esters and three weak odors carry the loss. 2-but and 2h, the two odors the control flies respond to most, and IaA fall to ranks 10 to 14 of 16, because the gain fit's stronger APL removes 3.1 to 3.6 times as many responders as it leaves (the data: 1.8 to 2.4 times). ms, paa and B-myr, the odors the gain was meant to recruit, remain the three sparsest with APL on: the fit still removes 69 to 84 % of their APL-off responders (the data remove 52 to 59 %), although with APL off the gain brings them close to the data. And 1-8ol and euc, which the data do not place among the sparse odors, are over-recruited.

src: **What this leaves.** The per-claw-transfer family is closed: a cap, a soft knee, a convex power and the hard knee itself all leave the weak odors unrecruited, and scaling their input recruits them without the fly's fruity-ester overlap. (That closed it for recruiting the weak odors; on the main target the family was taken up once more in the best models, with a knee near the largest PN rate, and is closed there as well: [the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee).) The reason is at the PN level (table below): the ORN-to-PN transform compresses rates so that no odor has an unusually strong PN; the weak odors drive two or three PNs above the knee where the esters drive five to seven, and any rule applied alike to every claw rewards breadth. What would recruit them is glomerulus-specific: claws from their glomeruli counting for more, which the oracle gain confirmed (above), while the hemibrain's per-claw synapse counts do not supply that gain and the centrifugal pathway does not either. The input side itself remains uncertain for the five odors (concentration, glomerular profile); the next subsection tests it with the one alternative dataset.

Spearman's ρ is one minus a constant times the sum over pairs of the squared rank residual (a pair's rank among the 120 distances in the model minus its rank in the KC data), so the gap, one minus ρ, splits exactly into a share per pair and per odor. The per-pair decomposition of the gap did this for the reference model, the first joint fit (the best APL-on ρ of any model), the best APL-off fit (the structure-loss fit on a re-drawn wiring), the bouton baseline, the centrifugal input and the ORN input itself, against the control flies with APL on and against APL output blocked (TNT) with APL off.

src: The misses have two signs. paa, B-myr and 2-but are far too close to each other in the model: the three recruit nearly the same KCs, so the model puts paa / B-myr at a cosine distance of {{E61/worst_pairs.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on;pair=paa / B-myr:model_distance ~ .2f}} where the control flies have {{E61/worst_pairs.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on;pair=paa / B-myr:data_distance ~ .2f}} (nearly orthogonal), and 2-but / paa and 2-but / B-myr likewise; paa / euc and paa / -aPine are too close as well. Every model does this, with or without the glomerulus gain and the per-claw threshold, and the ORN input has the same pairs too close at about half the rank residual, so the input carries the seed of it and the KC stage amplifies it: the three odors' modelled input drives two or three glomeruli strongly, with DM1 the strongest PN of both paa and B-myr (the PN table above), so they recruit the KCs that carry those glomeruli and few others. 1-8ol and ms have the opposite sign, too far from everything, in both conditions and in the input itself (their pairs with 1-6ol are missed by the input by as much), which is the APL-blocked sharing deficit above seen from the other side. With APL off, paa adds a third miss: in flies with APL output blocked paa comes close to the aldehydes t2h and 6al and the model keeps them apart. The models with the eight-glomerulus gain miss pairs of their own more than the models without it: the reference model's residuals follow the ORN input's at ρ {{E61/residual_correlations.csv:condition=on;model_a=reference 40 Hz;model_b=ORN input:spearman ~ .2f}} with APL on and {{E61/residual_correlations.csv:condition=off;model_a=reference 40 Hz;model_b=ORN input:spearman ~ .2f}} with APL off, the first joint fit's at {{E61/residual_correlations.csv:condition=on;model_a=first joint fit;model_b=ORN input:spearman ~ .2f}} and {{E61/residual_correlations.csv:condition=off;model_a=first joint fit;model_b=ORN input:spearman ~ .2f}} and the best APL-off fit's at {{E61/residual_correlations.csv:condition=on;model_a=best APL-off fit (re-drawn wiring);model_b=ORN input:spearman ~ .2f}} and {{E61/residual_correlations.csv:condition=off;model_a=best APL-off fit (re-drawn wiring);model_b=ORN input:spearman ~ .2f}}; the gain, which bought the block and the natural-source alignment, moved the disagreement with the KC matrices off the input's own misses and onto the model, consistent with the two ρ's falling along the gain axis (the gain as the carrier of a noise-robust block, above). The centrifugal input is the one model unlike the rest (its residuals agree with the reference model's at {{E61/residual_correlations.csv:condition=on;model_a=reference 40 Hz;model_b=centrifugal input:spearman ~ .2f}} / {{E61/residual_correlations.csv:condition=off;model_a=reference 40 Hz;model_b=centrifugal input:spearman ~ .2f}}) and the only one with paa / B-myr near the data, because it adds structure at the KCs that does not come from the ORN input; that is how it reaches the best APL-off ρ while losing the per-odor pattern and the block.

src: **The KCs behind the collapse.** In the reference model {{E61/shared_kcs/triple.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on:all_three}} KCs respond to all three of paa, B-myr and 2-but with APL on ({{E61/shared_kcs/triple.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on:expected_all_three ~ .1f}} expected if the three responder sets were independent) and {{E61/shared_kcs/triple.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=off:all_three}} with APL off ({{E61/shared_kcs/triple.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=off:expected_all_three ~ .1f}} expected); paa's and B-myr's responders overlap at {{E61/shared_kcs/overlap.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on;pair=paa / B-myr:ratio ~ .1f}} times the independent expectation against {{E61/shared_kcs/overlap.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on;pair=paa / B-myr:data_ratio ~ .1f}} in the control flies, whereas the terpenes' overlaps (B-myr with euc and -aPine, euc with -aPine) are as large in the flies as in the model. The shared KCs carry claws from DM1 ({{E61/shared_kcs/glomerulus_enrichment.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on;set=paa & B-myr & 2-but;glomerulus=DM1:frac_set ~ .0%}} of them against {{E61/shared_kcs/glomerulus_enrichment.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on;set=paa & B-myr & 2-but;glomerulus=DM1:frac_all ~ .0%}} of all KCs) and DP1m ({{E61/shared_kcs/glomerulus_enrichment.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on;set=paa & B-myr & 2-but;glomerulus=DP1m:frac_set ~ .0%}} against {{E61/shared_kcs/glomerulus_enrichment.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on;set=paa & B-myr & 2-but;glomerulus=DP1m:frac_all ~ .0%}}), the two gained glomeruli that all three odors drive above the per-claw knee, and for every shared KC one glomerulus drives it for both odors. Neither the gain nor the input's size makes the collapse: with DM1's gain removed paa / B-myr sits at a cosine distance of {{E39/model_pair_distances_long.csv:tag=thr40__loo_DM1;condition=on;odor_a=paa;odor_b=B-myr:distance ~ .2f}} with APL on and with no gain at {{E39/model_pair_distances_long.csv:tag=thr40__none;condition=on;odor_a=paa;odor_b=B-myr:distance ~ .2f}}, against {{E39/model_pair_distances_long.csv:tag=thr40__full;condition=on;odor_a=paa;odor_b=B-myr:distance ~ .2f}} with the full gain and {{E61/worst_pairs.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on;pair=paa / B-myr:data_distance ~ .2f}} in the control flies, and the rate oracle's scales leave it where it is. DM1 is the strongest ORN glomerulus of paa and of B-myr and the third of 2-but; the per-claw threshold reduces each odor to its strongest glomeruli, and the three meet there. The flies do something else with paa: its responders overlap with the aldehydes' (6al, t2h), and paa's second glomerulus in the ORN input, VL2a, responds to nothing else in the panel but the aldehydes, so the fly's paa channel looks like VL2a's where the model's is DM1's, which the bounded-input oracle (below) can test (DM1 down and VL2a up for paa) and an ORN measurement at Yang's concentrations can settle.

src: The recruitment level was then removed as a cause (the per-odor rate oracle). Each odor's ORN input was scaled so that the reference models' per-odor response fractions equal the KC data's, once with APL on against the control flies and once with APL off against APL output blocked (TNT), at the fitted scales and thresholds, with the agreement of the odor-odor distances as the free readout. It does not move: with the recruitment pattern exactly right with APL on (response rate ρ {{E62/stats_variants.csv:tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_on:spearman_rate_on_vs_data ~ .2f}} against {{E62/stats_variants.csv:tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_untuned:spearman_rate_on_vs_data ~ .2f}} as fitted) the reference model's agreement with the control flies' matrix goes from {{E62/stats_variants.csv:tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_untuned:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman ~ .2f}} to {{E62/stats_variants.csv:tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_on:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman ~ .2f}} and with the APL-output-blocked matrix from {{E62/stats_variants.csv:tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_untuned:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman ~ .2f}} to {{E62/stats_variants.csv:tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_on:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman ~ .2f}}; the scales set on the APL-off fractions give {{E62/stats_variants.csv:tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_off:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman ~ .2f}} and {{E62/stats_variants.csv:tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_off:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman ~ .2f}}; the other two models move by the same few hundredths. The scales needed are modest (2h up by {{E62/scales.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;arm=on;odor=2h:scale ~ .2f}}, B-myr by {{E62/scales.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;arm=on;odor=B-myr:scale ~ .2f}}, ms by {{E62/scales.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;arm=on;odor=ms:scale ~ .2f}}, -aPine down to {{E62/scales.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;arm=on;odor=-aPine:scale ~ .2f}}), and the pairs that carry the gap do not open: paa / B-myr sits at cosine distance {{E62/model_pair_distances_long.csv:tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_untuned;condition=on;odor_a=paa;odor_b=B-myr:distance ~ .2f}} as fitted and {{E62/model_pair_distances_long.csv:tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_on;condition=on;odor_a=paa;odor_b=B-myr:distance ~ .2f}} with the scales, against {{E61/worst_pairs.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on;pair=paa / B-myr:data_distance ~ .2f}} in the control flies. What the oracle does expose is the per-odor APL effect: B-myr's response fraction is {{E62/scales.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;arm=untuned;odor=B-myr:fraction_on ~ .3f}} with APL on against {{E62/scales.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;arm=untuned;odor=B-myr:data_on ~ .3f}} in the control flies, and {{E62/scales.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;arm=untuned;odor=B-myr:fraction_off ~ .3f}} with APL off against {{E62/scales.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;arm=untuned;odor=B-myr:data_off ~ .3f}} with APL output blocked, so the model's APL suppresses it two to three times too strongly (paa likewise), while it suppresses the broad esters eb, ep and 1-6ol too weakly; the breadth-weighted APL takes the few broad, gained KCs that carry the weak odors. So the gap in the agreement is which KCs an odor recruits, not how many: the glomerular pattern of the weak odors' input, and the APL's per-odor action, are what remain. The APL's per-odor action has since been set by an oracle as well (each odor's input scaled to the flies' response fraction with APL off, then its APL strength to the flies' with APL on): the two ρ's on odor-odor distances move by a few hundredths in opposite directions and [the main target stays where it was](#apl-effect-parts).

src: The target for each column is the same alignment computed from Yang's KC data: the KC distances averaged over recordings for the {{data:n_ref_pairs ~ .0f}} pairs of the 12 odors the APL16 panel shares with the megamat panel, their residual around the linear ORN prediction, and its ρ with the natural-source (VCF embedding) distances. That gives {{data:ctrl_vcf ~ .2f}} for control flies, the APL-on target (90 % interval over recordings {{data:ctrl_vcf.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:ctrl_vcf.hi ~ .2f}}); {{data:tnt_vcf ~ .2f}} for APL output blocked (TNT), the APL-off target ({{data:tnt_vcf.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:tnt_vcf.hi ~ .2f}}); and {{data:vcf_apl_effect ~ +.2f}} for their difference ({{data:vcf_apl_effect.lo ~ +.2f}} to {{data:vcf_apl_effect.hi ~ +.2f}}). src: **Putting the two ρ's on odor-odor distances first in the loss does not raise them.** The two-ρ fit asked how far the present mechanisms reach when the agreement with the two KC matrices is the objective (its terms at four times their usual weight, the response-rate terms kept as constraints, the block and structure terms unweighted), starting from the structure-loss optimum of each base in the table. Little moved, and no fit raised both ρ's: the reference model went from {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.5_seed:fit_on_spearman ~ .3f}} / {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.5_seed:fit_off_spearman ~ .3f}} (APL on / off, deterministic) to {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.5_rho:fit_on_spearman ~ .3f}} / {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.5_rho:fit_off_spearman ~ .3f}}, the 70 Hz and gain-1.25 fits about as little, the freed weight going to the response rates at the deterministic block's cost. The no-gain base moved furthest, out of its strong-KC–KC regime, and traded one ρ for the other ({{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_nogain_seed:fit_on_spearman ~ .3f}} / {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_nogain_seed:fit_off_spearman ~ .3f}} to {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_nogain_rho:fit_on_spearman ~ .3f}} / {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_nogain_rho:fit_off_spearman ~ .3f}}). All four end near the ORN input's own agreement with APL on ({{data:rho_ctrl_orn ~ .2f}}), below it with APL off ({{data:rho_tnt_orn ~ .2f}}) and far from the ceilings ({{data:ctrl_ceiling ~ .2f}} / {{data:tnt_ceiling ~ .2f}}): the weighting was not the limit (one start per base), and the gap is in the input or in a mechanism not in hand. The no-gain fit recovers the APL-off response rate and keeps its block through the noise ({{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_nogain_rho:block_raw ~ +.3f}} in three-trial means; the data {{data:block ~ +.3f}}) with KC–KC at {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_nogain_rho:kc_kc_inh ~ .0f}}, where the gain-1.25 fit at {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.25_rho:kc_kc_inh ~ .0f}} keeps {{E63/comparison.csv:key=thr40_gain1.25_rho:block_raw ~ +.3f}}: the fragile block goes with the gain, not with a weak KC–KC scale (one fit, one noise seed). None of these fits moves the APL-effect loss (the root mean squared difference between the model's and the KC data's per-pair APL effect, each pair's APL-on minus APL-off distance): the mean APL effect stays at half the data's or less and ρ on the per-pair APL effect far below its ceiling.

src: **Searching the weak odors' input within a factor of two opens the collapsed pairs and raises both ρ's on odor-odor distances; it changes which pairs APL moves, not how far.** The weak-input odors' input as a bounded oracle tested what was left on the input side, each weak odor's pattern across glomeruli: on the reference model at its fitted scales and threshold, the ORN response of paa, B-myr, 2-but, euc, -aPine, ms and 1-8ol, one odor after the other, was multiplied in every glomerulus by a factor between one half and two, searched for the highest sum of the two ρ's on odor-odor distances with a penalty once the odor's response fraction left ±15 % of the KC data's; 2h and 6al, two strongly driven odors whose pairs the model already orders well, were searched the same way as the control. It is an [oracle](#fn-oracle), and an in-sample one, searched against the same two KC matrices it is scored on with nothing held out and no scale re-fitted: what a corrected input could at most buy, not a measurement. Both agreements rise, with APL on from {{E64/stats_variants.csv:tag=I_untuned:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman ~ .2f}} to {{E64/stats_variants.csv:tag=I_searched_pass1:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman ~ .2f}} (the best earlier model, the first joint fit, has {{E61/rhos.csv:short=first joint fit:rho_on ~ .2f}}) and with APL off from {{E64/stats_variants.csv:tag=I_untuned:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman ~ .2f}} to {{E64/stats_variants.csv:tag=I_searched_pass1:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman ~ .2f}} (the best earlier model, the structure-loss fit on a re-drawn wiring, has {{E61/rhos.csv:short=best APL-off fit (re-drawn wiring):rho_off ~ .2f}}): both in one model, above the ORN input's own agreement in both conditions, and still far from the ceilings (table). The collapsed pairs open, paa / B-myr from a cosine distance of {{E64/model_pair_distances_long.csv:tag=I_untuned;condition=on;odor_a=paa;odor_b=B-myr:distance ~ .2f}} to {{E64/model_pair_distances_long.csv:tag=I_searched_pass1;condition=on;odor_a=paa;odor_b=B-myr:distance ~ .2f}} with APL on ({{E61/worst_pairs.csv:short=reference 40 Hz;condition=on;pair=paa / B-myr:data_distance ~ .2f}} in the control flies) and 2-but's pairs with the two likewise, though paa still does not come close to the aldehydes with APL off. The natural-source alignment with APL on, its APL-on minus APL-off difference and the structure against the wild-type somata, none of them scored by the search, move toward the data at a small cost in the block, while response rate ρ is raised by the penalty itself; the control search raises neither agreement, so a free input within the same bounds is not what buys the gain. B-myr's search is worth the most ({{diff:E64/per_odor_gains.csv:label=weak;pass_no=1;odor=B-myr:rho_on_after -- E64/per_odor_gains.csv:label=weak;pass_no=1;odor=B-myr:rho_on_before ~ +.3f}} with APL on, {{diff:E64/per_odor_gains.csv:label=weak;pass_no=1;odor=B-myr:rho_off_after -- E64/per_odor_gains.csv:label=weak;pass_no=1;odor=B-myr:rho_off_before ~ +.3f}} with APL off), then paa's and 2-but's, the three odors the decomposition named; the other four add a hundredth or less. {{lit:99 of the 252 # counted in results/E64_input_oracle/factors_weak_pass1.csv (factors at 0.5 or at 2); the note of the experiment gives the share, 39 %}} factors end at a bound, so the factor of two binds. For paa the search doubles VL2a (as the shared-KC analysis above expected), halves DP1m, DM4, DL2v and VM7d, lowers DM6 by nearly as much (Hallem's receptor data put it above the lab's value) and leaves DM1 where it was (factor {{E64/factors_weak_pass1.csv:odor=paa;glomerulus=DM1:factor ~ .2f}}; expected down); for B-myr it halves DM1 and doubles DC1 and D. The search thus names paa's VL2a, DP1m, DM6 and DM4 for measurement at 10^-3, the KC data's concentration ([the lab's recording is at 10^-4](#fn-concentrations)); B-myr's recording is already at that concentration, so its searched input is either within the spread of the ORN recordings or a statement about how the model weighs DM1, DC1 and D. On [the main target](#apl-effect) the searched input improves the pattern and not the size: ρ on the per-pair APL effect rises from {{E64/apl_effect.csv:tag=I_untuned:rho ~ .2f}} to {{E64/apl_effect.csv:tag=I_searched_pass1:rho ~ .2f}} (ceiling {{data:apl_effect_rho_ceiling ~ .2f}}; {{E64/apl_effect.csv:tag=I_controls:rho ~ .2f}} after the control search) and the pattern part of the APL-effect loss falls from {{E64/apl_effect.csv:tag=I_untuned:pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E64/apl_effect.csv:tag=I_searched_pass1:pattern ~ .3f}}, still above the {{data:apl_effect_sd ~ .3f}} that an effect with no pattern at all would score, while the mean APL effect stays at half the data's ({{E64/apl_effect.csv:tag=I_searched_pass1:mean ~ +.3f}} against {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}), so the loss goes only from {{E64/apl_effect.csv:tag=I_untuned:loss ~ .3f}} to {{E64/apl_effect.csv:tag=I_searched_pass1:loss ~ .3f}} (floor {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}}), inside all four realism bands in every column. On the fourth band, the number of odors each KC responds to, the searched input brings the model a little closer to the flies with APL off (from {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E64_input_oracle;tag=I_untuned:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E64_input_oracle;tag=I_searched_pass1:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution, against a band of {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}), about twice the move the control search makes ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E64_input_oracle;tag=I_controls:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}}). The weak odors' input bears on which pairs APL moves apart, and through them on both matrices; how far APL moves odors apart is not on the input side.

src: Every model on this page is tuned or fitted so that 5 % of KCs respond with APL on, a convention from the lab's earlier modelling, while {{data:ctrl_frac ~ .1%}} of the control flies' KCs respond (and {{data:tnt_frac ~ .1%}} with APL output blocked). Re-fitted with the response-rate target at the control flies' fraction instead, the reference model keeps everything the fit measures: the block, ρ on odor-odor distances with both KC matrices and the structure vs wild-type somata stay where they were at 5 %, response rate ρ with APL on rises slightly, and the loss without its response-rate term is no worse (the fit does it with a stronger APL↔KC loop and a weaker APL→bouton scale). Moving only the somatic threshold to the new operating point, with every other fitted scale held, costs the 40 Hz model almost half of its block, so a threshold-only change of operating point is not neutral. What the operating point does change is the response fractions: at 6.8 % the weak-input odors respond more, and the reference model, whose gain was fitted at 5 %, now over-recruits them with APL off. Its weak odors were already too strong relative to the mean at 5 % (the absolute match there came from an overall APL-off response rate below the data's), so the gain of 1.5 on eight glomeruli is more than the data's operating point needs. In the bouton bases tuned from 3.4 % to 10 %, ρ on odor-odor distances barely moves and the block stays at zero; the weak odors' share of the mean APL-off response rate rises from {{E44/comparison.csv:A_thr70_t0.050:weak_share_off ~ .2f}} at 5 % to {{E44/comparison.csv:A_thr70_t0.068:weak_share_off ~ .2f}} at 6.8 % in the 70 Hz base (data {{data:tnt_weak_share ~ .2f}}), a fifth to a quarter of the way, and the APL-off mean pair distance falls toward the data's as more KCs respond ({{E44/comparison.csv:A_thr70_t0.050:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}} to {{E44/comparison.csv:A_thr70_t0.068:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}}; data {{data:tnt_mean_dist ~ .2f}}). Fitting at the data's fraction costs nothing and compares response fractions with the data at the same mean; the gain is the parameter to re-fit there.

src: At the fitted scales every kind of shuffle loses part of the block, and the draw-to-draw spread is as large as the differences between kinds, so no kind separates from the others: the within-type Curveball keeps the most for the eight at 1.5 and the claw permutations the least at 40 Hz, but the eight at 1.25 reverse that order. Agreement with the two KC matrices does not move; what the shuffles cost besides the block is the APL-on response-rate pattern and the natural-source alignment. Re-fitted, the block comes back, but by an amount set by the draw and not by the kind of shuffle. On the first draw the two shuffles that ignore KC type made the data's block in full, on a wiring whose every claw was re-assigned at random across all KCs, and the two within-type shuffles kept the least; the follow-up on four draws each of the plain claw permutation and the within-type Curveball (the fitted block on more shuffle draws) found the two kinds indistinguishable, their means in the opposite order and both between half and three quarters of the data's block, with single draws recovering anything from none of it to all of it, none above the real wiring's value, and the four draws with the lowest loss carrying the four largest blocks. So the fitted block does not need the hemibrain's pairing of glomeruli on KCs: a re-fit recovers it on a random wiring with these claw counts to a degree that varies from draw to draw, and the re-draws' loss of it above was the typical draw's loss (their within-type claw-permutation draws recovered what a typical draw of either kind recovers), not a sign that the block rides on the real wiring. What every shuffle loses, re-fitted or not, is the natural-source alignment with APL off, which on the real wiring sits at the data's value and on no shuffled wiring the model was re-fitted on comes close to it; APL's effect on it (on minus off) is at or below zero on the real wiring and on the within-type shuffles, where the data's is positive, and positive only on the plain claw permutation, the one statistic that told the two kinds apart. The structure against wild-type somata is kept by every shuffle for the eight at 1.5 and lost only for the eight at 1.25. The real wiring's own contribution to the fitted models is therefore the natural-source alignment, not the block; a block difference between two wirings means something only once several draws of each have been re-fitted.

src: Which part of the wiring carries the natural-source alignment was then asked directly (the glomerulus pairs behind the natural-source alignment). Counting, for each pair of the 54 glomeruli of the claw wiring, the KCs with claws from both glomeruli against 200 draws of each kind of shuffle finds two layers of structure beyond the margins. Fifty-five of the 1431 pairs are over-shared against every kind, and they are the food glomeruli converging on common KCs (DM1 with DM4, DM2, DM5 and DP1m, DM2 with DM4 and DM5, VM5d with VM5v and VA3; DM1 / DM4 on 92 KCs where the margins predict 50), the convergence the connectome literature reports. And 76 of the 162 glomerulus x KC-type counts are far from what a type-ignoring shuffle predicts: the food glomeruli are concentrated on the α/β KCs and depleted on the γ KCs (DM2 reaches 22 % of the α/β KCs and 8 % of the γ KCs where a type-ignoring shuffle gives 14 % of each), and a second set (DC3, VA5, VA6, VL2a, DA2, D, DL1) the other way round; this is the layer the within-type shuffles keep and the type-ignoring ones destroy. Turned into a score per odor pair (the shared-KC counts summed over glomerulus pairs, weighted by the two odors' ORN input), the type layer predicts which odor pairs the fitted real-wiring model brings closer than its shuffles do (ρ {{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=typestruct;null_class=claw_permutation;target=model_contrib_off_thr40_gain1.5:rho ~ +.2f}} with the reference model's APL-off residual minus the shuffle mean), which pairs the control flies bring closer than the ORN input predicts ({{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=typestruct;null_class=claw_permutation;target=resid_ctrl:rho ~ +.2f}}) and, less strongly, the natural-source-close pairs ({{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=typestruct;null_class=claw_permutation;target=vcf_hyp:rho ~ +.2f}}); the over-shared pairs' excess beyond type predicts chemical distance instead ({{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=curveball_within_type;target=chem:rho ~ +.2f}}) and none of those ({{E52/score_correlations.csv:weighting=norm;kind=excess;null_class=curveball_within_type;target=vcf_hyp:rho ~ +.2f}} with the natural-source distance). Lesioning only the 55 pairs' excess, by claw swaps that keep every KC's and every bouton's claw count (a tenth of the claws moved), takes the reference model's alignment with APL off at its fitted scales from {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}} to {{E52/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_targeted:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}, where the within-type shuffles sit, while a control lesion of the same size on count-matched pairs leaves it at {{E52/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_control:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}; the block does not move. So the alignment the models owe to the real wiring has two carriers: the KC-type organization of the glomerular input, the larger and the one organized along the natural-source axis, and the within-type convergence of the food glomeruli, the smaller and organized by chemistry. A within-type shuffle is the right null for the first and the targeted lesion for the second; the type-ignoring shuffles lose both, which is why a model re-fitted on one loses more of the alignment than any pairwise feature accounts for.

src: Whether the two carriers are sufficient was then asked by putting the convergence back (building the natural-source alignment back). On within-type Curveball draws (the type structure kept, the convergence destroyed) and on plain Curveball draws (both destroyed), the 32 over-shared pairs with ORN data were raised to the real wiring's shared-KC counts by claw swaps that keep every KC's and every bouton's claw count (10 to 12 % of the claws moved), with the same raises on count-matched control pairs as the control, and the reference models were run at their fitted scales with the threshold re-tuned. The answer splits by APL state. With APL on the convergence brings the alignment back: on the within-type draws the reference model goes from {{E47/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} untreated to {{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} (the real wiring {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}}; the control raises {{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_control:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}), a rise of {{E57/paired_differences.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type;kind=transplant;stat=spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp:mean_diff ~ +.2f}} per draw that is positive on every draw and for all three models, to within a few hundredths of the real wiring; on the plain draws it gets about halfway ({{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_transplant:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} from {{E47/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}}). With APL off it does not move: {{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} after the transplant against {{E47/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} untreated and the real wiring's {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp ~ .2f}}, on either class of draw, although the lesion of exactly these counts on the real wiring had cost it ({{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=lesion_orn_all:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} against {{E54/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=control_orn_all:spike_counts_cosine__off_spearman_resid_vs_vcf_hyp__mean ~ .2f}} for the control lesions). So APL on minus off, which the KC data have at {{data:vcf_apl_effect ~ +.2f}} and the real-wiring models about level, moves on the within-type draws from {{E47/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type:vcf_on_minus_off__mean ~ +.2f}} to {{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:vcf_on_minus_off__mean ~ +.2f}}. The convergence as a pairwise count is what carries the APL-on side of the alignment, and with the type structure under it it is close to sufficient for that side; the APL-off side that the lesions lose is the convergence in its real-wiring arrangement, which KCs hold the pairs and what else those KCs sample, which no pairwise transplant restores. The structure against the wild-type somata rises with the transplant above the real wiring's value ({{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_remap_wt__mean ~ .2f}} against {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__on_spearman_resid_vs_remap_wt ~ .2f}}), the block is not restored ({{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:spike_counts_cosine__block_fruity_small_iso__mean ~ +.3f}} against {{E47/comparison.csv:A_thr40_gain1.5_real_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__block_fruity_small_iso ~ +.3f}}), and the response rate ρ with APL on rises under the control raises ({{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_control:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}}) nearly as much as under the transplant ({{E57/per_class.csv:model=thr40_gain1.5;shuffle=curveball_within_type_transplant:spearman_rate_on_vs_data__mean ~ .2f}}), so that statistic answers to the swaps rather than to the pairs.

src: On the main target no model reaches the data, and only the fit with a firing ceiling comes near it, at about one and a half times the floor. That number is of the model's 0.5 s odor pulse. Read as the flies were recorded, at their 2 s pulse and through their response window with the indicator's kinetics as measured in the recordings, the same fit stands at {{E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=B1_fit1;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss ~ .3f}} with the adaptation it was fitted with and at {{E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=B6_fit1_tau3;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss ~ .3f}} with an adaptation that outlasts the odor ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol) and [the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course), at the end of this section). Without a ceiling the lowest APL-effect loss in the table is more than twice the floor, and most columns sit at the bouton baseline's level: the per-claw threshold, the oracle gain, the structure targets, the interpretable bounds and KC-spike-driven APL were built for other statistics and left this one where it was, the reference model included (what its larger mean effect gains over the bouton baseline, its pattern loses). Only the first joint fit, the two APL-effect fits and the last column do clearly better inside the realism bands, all four of them (next paragraph); the 70 Hz joint fit with the structure targets does worst. In every column APL moves the pairs apart less than it does in the flies: outside the last two columns the mean effect is below the lower end of the data's 90 % interval ({{data:apl_effect_mean.lo ~ +.3f}}), two thirds of the data's in the APL-effect fit without a firing ceiling and at most a little over half in the others. In all but four columns (the current reference model, the two APL-effect fits and the last) this shortfall, not the pattern, is the larger part of the loss. For the first joint fit, the APL-effect fit of its family and the 40 Hz fits with the oracle gain, most of it belongs to the comparison of raw spike counts with a calcium signal and not to the models: compressed as the indicator compresses them, their counts give a mean effect inside the flies' interval, while the others, the last two columns apart, stay below it ([the main target under a compressive readout](#readout), at the end of this section); with the firing ceiling the raw counts themselves give it ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). That agreement is with the recordings as measured, and the models reach it with their responders alone, where a third of the flies' mean effect comes from products with values below the response criterion (same subsection). They also reach it with more broadly responding KCs with APL off than the flies have (the row on KCs responding to eight or more odors), and in the three columns checked, the current reference model, the APL-effect fit and its re-fit with the firing ceiling, these are the many-claw KCs: about a third of the responses that removing APL adds go to the {{E72/release.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:frac_kcs_9+ ~ .0%}} of KCs with nine or more claws. A threshold scaled to each KC's input moves the release off those cells at a cost on the main target, and a fit then makes as many broad responders from other cells ([the input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold), at the end of this section). The flies' own effect rests on broadly responding KCs too: split by the number of odors each KC responds to, most of it sits in the KCs that respond to eight or more odors when APL output is blocked, and the part below the response criterion is for the most part the weaker responses of broadly responding KCs to their other odors ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class), at the end of this section). Counted by the recordings' own criterion, in their z-scored units, most of the rest sits in a second kind of KC, those that respond to four to seven odors, which the models lack. With each KC's responses in baseline-noise units, the unit of the realism bands, there is no second kind: the KCs at eight or more odors carry the flies' effect alone, as they do in the models ([the data side of the main target](#data-side), further down in this section). The columns with the larger mean effects all carry breadth-weighted APL (in the breadth-weighted APL experiment the mean effect grew with the breadth exponent at unchanged response rates), though not every column that carries it has one. The pattern is no closer. ρ on the per-pair APL effect stays well under its ceiling in every column; the per-claw threshold and breadth-weighted APL each lift it from the bouton baseline's, and the two 40 Hz fits with the gain on all eight glomeruli, the reference model among them, have the lowest values. Nor has a positive ρ lowered any loss yet: with the means removed, no column's pattern part is clearly below the data's own standard deviation across pairs ({{data:apl_effect_sd ~ .3f}}), which is what a model with the same effect on every pair would score, and in the columns with breadth-weighted APL and no firing ceiling it is well above it ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E34_gain_bounded;tag=thr40_gain1.5_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} for the reference model; {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} with the ceiling). There the effect is spread over the pairs more unevenly than in the flies ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E34_gain_bounded;tag=thr40_gain1.5_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_sd_ratio ~ .1f}} times the flies' spread for the reference model, {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_sd_ratio ~ .1f}} times with the ceiling; the row on the spread), and that is why a positive ρ has not lowered the pattern part: a model's pattern part falls below the score of an effect with no pattern only when its spread, as a multiple of the flies', is less than twice its Pearson r, which at the spreads of these columns would take a correlation near the ceiling ([how the pattern part is split](#fn-pattern-split)). In every column without the ceiling some pairs move closer with APL on, which no pair does in the flies; which pairs, through which KCs, and what the breadth weighting has to do with it is taken up [at the end of this section](#apl-effect-parts). Two columns are outside the band on the response-rate ratio, both with KC–KC inhibition at 100: the inhibition that remains without APL keeps the response rate from doubling when APL is removed, as it does in the flies (the row of response-rate ratios further down), so the low loss of the breadth 3 column does not count.

src: The fourth band, on the number of odors each KC responds to, puts three of the fourteen model columns outside: the bouton baseline, with APL on and with APL off, and the two columns with KC–KC inhibition at 100, with APL off, which are outside the band on the ratio as well (the realism row; the three rows under it give every column's distance from the flies' distribution and the two ends of that distribution). One column is at its limit with APL on, the per-claw threshold at 70 Hz with the oracle gain ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E27_glomerulus_gain;tag=oracle_g1.5:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} against {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}), and of the columns inside it the first joint fit is the nearest to the limit with APL off ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} against {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}). Inside the band or outside it, the models' responses with APL off sit in fewer KCs than the flies': in every column close to half of the KCs or more respond to none of the 16 odors, against {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_0 ~ .0%}} in the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), and the KCs that respond to between one and seven odors are too few to match; in the current reference model and in the two APL-effect fits more KCs than in the flies respond to eight or more. Part of this is the operating point. Eleven columns are tuned to 5 % of KCs responding with APL on, which leaves fewer responses to spread than the flies have and more silent KCs in both conditions, and this band, unlike the band on the ratio, is on the distribution itself and makes no allowance for it. The two reference-model columns are the same fit at the two operating points: the re-fit at the flies' response rate takes the distance from the flies' distribution from {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E34_gain_bounded;tag=thr40_gain1.5_k2_cap3:opk_on_tv ~ .2f}} to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:opk_on_tv ~ .2f}} with APL on and from {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E34_gain_bounded;tag=thr40_gain1.5_k2_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .2f}} to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .2f}} with APL off, inside the band at both operating points. The rest is the model. At the flies' overall response rates the current reference model still leaves about half of its KCs silent with APL off and has a larger share responding to eight or more odors than the flies have: removing APL brings in about half as many new KCs as it does in the flies and makes more of the responding ones broad; the band, set by the most atypical recording, allows that much. Eleven columns are inside all four bands, every fitted model of the table among them, so the bands do not separate the columns that are ahead on the main target from the others: the first joint fit, the last column and the two APL-effect fits are all inside. Without a firing ceiling the APL-effect fit has the lowest loss in the table but the last column's and that of its own re-fit with the ceiling, and the lowest of the columns without a ceiling once the two highest-firing KCs are left out (the row under the loss, which was not computed for the column with the ceiling) ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)). With the ceiling it has the lowest loss in the table, on raw spike counts nearly what it has under the calibrated readout, with less than half the block of the fit without it and no change in which KCs respond with APL off ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). Read as the recordings themselves were made, each KC's signal in units of its own standard deviation over the session, the saved models keep nearly the order that the calibrated readout gives them, and fitted under that reading the fit without a ceiling and the fit with one end level, at the loss that the first has under the readout ([the per-KC normalization of the recordings](#per-kc-normalization), at the end of this section). Of the saved models, {{lit:423 of the 918 # counted in results/apl_effect/by_variant.csv as written 2026-11-10 18:27: rows with a non-empty realism_flag, of all rows}} scored are outside at least one band, {{lit:197 # counted in results/apl_effect/by_variant.csv as written 2026-11-10 18:27: rows whose realism_flag names only odors per KC}} of them on this band alone.

src: The bands also do not see where APL acts. In the breadth-2 family of the APL-effect fits, to which the third column from the end belongs, most of what APL does to the KCs' input is done at the PN boutons. On the eight wirings on which the family has been fitted ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P2:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:bouton_share ~ .2f}} of the drive that APL removes from the claws is removed at the boutons, as a subtraction that is nearly the same for every odor, where the connectome puts a fraction of {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, all:share_pn ~ .3f}} to {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, assigned, KCs with a type:share_pn ~ .3f}} of APL's calyx synapses on PN boutons. The family's match needs that path at about its fitted strength. Through the calibrated readout the pattern part of the mean over four wirings is {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} as fitted. It is {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher with the path at a tenth of its fitted strength, the setting nearest the connectome's share, and {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} higher when the family is fitted again with the path held there, while half the fitted strength is inside the margin of an equal and a strength above the bound reads worse ([the PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition](#bouton-share), at the end of this section). Most of the refit's cost belongs to how the family's APL weights the KCs and not to the site: with a part of the APL→KC weights that is the same on every claw, which the connectome's own weights are not, the family fitted again with the path held there is {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} higher than as fitted, just outside the margin of an equal ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold), at the end of this section). With weights that the connectome has in that part's place, the synapses that APL makes on the KCs outside their claws, which the model's weights leave out, the refit is {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} higher than as fitted, and its mean APL effect is {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} where the family as fitted has {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} ([APL's synapses on the KCs outside the claws](#offclaw-synapses), at the end of this section). At fixed scales, what loses the mean with counted weights is that KCs with the same number of claws get unequal amounts, which do not follow what the bouton path takes from each KC either; that a KC's amount grows with its number of claws less than in proportion loses none of it, and for the weights on the claws how the synapses lie over a KC's claws loses little of it through the calibrated readout, so that no part made of each KC's counted synapses holds the mean ([the evenness of APL's weights among KCs and over a KC's claws](#weight-evenness), at the end of this section). A share of synapses is not a share of inhibition, so that this is a note on the family's realism beside the bands and not a band, and whether a limit on the bouton share replaces the bound on the APL→bouton scale is a choice still to be made. The share has been measured for this family only, and not for the other columns of the table. Nor do the bands see what kind of inhibition the family's APL is. What it takes from a KC's drive is nearly the same for every odor, and with the whole APL replaced by a fixed inhibition of each KC that is present only with APL on, the mean over four wirings reads {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} to {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C1_bck:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher in the pattern part through the calibrated readout and, with one amount per KC, no higher on raw counts. For the main target the family's APL is thus close to a threshold difference per KC between the two conditions, where in the flies' own responses the inhibition grows with an odor's response over all KCs ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)). This too is a description of this family alone, beside the bands and not one of them ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)). A third description comes from APL's own activity, imaged in the flies together with the KCs' dendrites in the calyx. There the flies' APL responds {{lit:3.69 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r1, quantity=APL; column readings, the point estimate at pa @ -3.806, as printed there ~ .2f}} to {{lit:5.28 # results/E101_apl_vs_kc_claws/c_x2_flies.csv (the table opens with a caveat line, which the filler does not read, so the value is entered by hand): row flies=L, reading=carrying, b_mult=0, ratio_id=r1, quantity=APL; column readings, the point estimate at pa @ -2, as printed there ~ .2f}} times as strongly to pa as to ms, where the family's APL, read in proportion, responds {{E101/a3_x2_summary.csv:wiring=M2;ratio_id=r1;estimate=ms;baseline=blank:apl_linear ~ .2f}} to {{E101/a3_x2_summary.csv:wiring=real;ratio_id=r1;estimate=ms;baseline=blank:apl_linear ~ .2f}} times as strongly. The family's flatness is set before its APL, which follows the summed input to the claws: with Hallem's receptor data as the input the same fits give {{E101/c4_hallem_ratios.csv:wiring=M1;series=pa over ms;log10_conc=-4.0;cond=on;quantity=APL:linear ~ .2f}} to {{E101/c4_hallem_ratios.csv:wiring=real;series=pa over ms;log10_conc=-2.0;cond=on;quantity=APL:linear ~ .2f}}. By the rule fixed beforehand the family is inside the flies' interval, which is wide, through the steepest readings of the indicator, and the quality of those recordings has not yet been checked by the experimenter who made them, so that this too stands beside the bands and is not one of them ([the flies' APL against their KC claws in the dual-colour recordings](#apl-vs-claws), at the end of this section). A fourth is a verdict fixed beforehand, on recordings of APL alone. From paa at 10^-4 to paa at 10^-5 the flies' APL falls to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}} of its response (the interval over resampled flies), and the family's, read in proportion, to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:model_linear_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:model_linear_max ~ .2f}}: flatter than the flies on all eight wirings, under every reading that the measurement leaves open, and against recordings with the concentrations in shuffled order as well. Across odors near the panel's concentration the same recordings decide less, since the class of paa against ms turns on which estimate of ms's ORN input the model is given. A further series of the same genotype, held out from every rule and read since, does not settle it from the flies' side: the family is inside those flies' interval under every estimate, the series of recordings disagree about how strongly APL responds to ms, and a ratio between two odors read from one pair of vials is known to no better than a factor of about one and a half, so that across odors the flies' APL does not at present say whether the family's is too even or too uneven ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out), at the end of this section). A weaker normalization in the model's antennal lobe is the one change read so far that moves the fall towards the flies', and what it costs on the main target is being measured (with the pending work at the end of the page). This too is a note on the family's realism beside the bands and not a band ([the strength of APL's response in the flies against the model's APL](#apl-strength), at the end of this section).

A further series of the same genotype, held out from every rule and read since, does not settle it from the flies' side: the family is inside those flies' interval under every estimate, the series of recordings disagree about how strongly APL responds to ms, and a ratio between two odors read from one pair of vials is known to no better than a factor of about one and a half, so that across odors the flies' APL does not at present say whether the family's is too even or too uneven ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out), at the end of this section). A weaker normalization in the model's antennal lobe is the one change read so far that moves the fall towards the flies', and what it costs on the main target is being measured (with the pending work at the end of the page). This too is a note on the family's realism beside the bands and not a band ([the strength of APL's response in the flies against the model's APL](#apl-strength), at the end of this section).
