src: The last column holds the lowest APL-effect loss in the table among the models saved before the main target was fitted directly, and held the lowest of any model on the real wiring until then ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)). It was chosen as the lowest inside the three bands on the response rates, and it is inside the fourth, on the number of odors each KC responds to, as well. It is the 70 Hz fit of the reference model's family with the oracle gain kept on DM1 alone, every fitted scale held and the somatic threshold re-tuned to the fit's response rate, one of the variants of [the oracle gain decomposed by glomerulus](#gain-decomposition). Among the columns without a firing ceiling its mean effect is the only one inside the data's 90 % interval, at the reference model's response rates, so the larger effect is not bought with the overall response rates, and its ρ on the per-pair APL effect is the highest. Its loss is then almost all pattern (a pattern part of {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} in a loss of {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}), and that part is within the range of the other columns with breadth-weighted APL, not below it. What the larger effect does come with is a response with APL off that sits in fewer KCs. The same fit with the gain removed everywhere is {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__none:opk_off_tv ~ .2f}} from the flies' distribution of odors per KC with APL off (the band is {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .2f}}), at a loss of {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__none:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}; the gain on DM1 lowers the loss and takes the distance to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:opk_off_tv ~ .2f}}, with more KCs silent and more responding to eight or more odors. In the 70 Hz family and in the 40 Hz family alike, the variant with the gain on DM1 alone has both the lowest loss of the decomposition and the largest distance from the flies' distribution with APL off. The distance stays inside the band, so the loss counts. The rows further down the column show what it gives up: the lowest ρ on odor-odor distances of any column, with APL on and with APL off, a block under half the data's and a negative natural-source alignment with APL off. Its matrices (the button in the bottom row opens each column's APL-on and APL-off matrices and their difference, under the KC data's) show how a low loss and poor matrices go together: 2-but, paa and B-myr nearly coincide in both conditions, as [in the reference model](#gap-pairs), and a pair that is equally wrong with APL on and with APL off costs this loss nothing. The column is also a selection after the fact, the best of the decomposition's variants on this statistic, with a gain set by hand. The same variant of the 40 Hz fit is the lowest of its family too ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__only_DM1:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} against the reference model's {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E34_gain_bounded;tag=thr40_gain1.5_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}), so DM1's part is not an accident of the selection, but the column is a lead for a fit, not a result: a lead on raw spike counts only (under [the compressive readout](#readout) it is the one column whose loss rises). It also rests on two of the model's {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:n_kcs ~ .0f}} KCs: with the two that fire most with APL on left out of both conditions after the fact, nothing simulated again, its loss is {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr70__only_DM1:raw__top2__rmse ~ .3f}} (the row under the loss), above the first joint fit's, which the same leave-out leaves at {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2:raw__top2__rmse ~ .3f}}. In every other column the loss stays where it was or falls with the two KCs left out, most in the three 40 Hz fits with the oracle gain, whose mean effect a few such KCs hold down ([the high-firing KCs that survive APL](#high-firing-kcs), at the end of this section). The fit that the column was a lead for has since been run, among [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits): with the same per-claw threshold and the gain on DM1 alone, fitted on raw counts at the flies' response rate, the model reaches {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3_DM1:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} inside all four bands, the lowest loss on raw counts of those fits, by giving up the block; it rests on a few KCs as the column does, and it loses that lead once the flies' trial-to-trial noise is put into the model. Among the models on the real wiring saved before those fits that are scored on all four bands and inside them, the column's loss is the lowest; without any glomerulus gain the lowest is {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, that of the first joint fit's family at breadth exponent 3, which is at the limit of the fourth band with APL off ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution, the band's own value to three decimals; the first joint fit itself, at {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, is inside it); the APL-effect fit of the third column from the end is a little below that, well inside all four bands and without a gain ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}). Breadth-weighted APL alone on the bouton baseline has about the same loss ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E12_breadth_apl;tag=spikes_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}) and is outside the band with APL off, as the bouton baseline is: the weighting leaves the model with APL off as it was. A few single draws of shuffled wirings have losses inside all four bands as low as the lowest of the APL-effect fits (the lowest {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E47_wiring_features;tag=A_thr40_gain1.5_claw_permutation-seed5_retuned:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}), below the last column's, with a larger mean effect than the real wiring gives at the same parameters ([about half of that difference is a few high-firing KCs of the real wiring](#high-firing-kcs)); they are controls, not candidate models.

src: **One gap, in the distances that the two conditions share.** A matrix with APL on is the matrix with APL off plus the per-pair APL effect, so each ρ can be computed again with one of the two taken from the flies. src: **Below the response criterion the recordings are not empty, and what is there is mostly signal.** In the recordings a KC counts as responding to an odor when its mean over the three trials is above 1 in the recordings' z-scored units (1 z); everything at or below that is sub-threshold. A model KC without a spike reads exactly 0, on raw counts and through the readout alike, while in the control flies {{E65/data_amplitude_summary.csv:genotype=TNT3c:share_subthreshold ~ .0%}} of an odor's squared response vector lies in sub-threshold trial means, {{E65/data_amplitude_summary.csv:genotype=TNT3c:share_negative ~ .0%}} in negative ones. The low end of the readout asked what those values are, whether a model's scores change when its readout is given the same low end, and whether the model holds such values under its spike threshold ([how each step was done](#fn-readout-low-end)). They are mostly signal, not measurement noise. Entries picked by their mean over two trials come back on the third: the weakly positive ones (0.3 to 1 z) at {{E68/data_cv_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT3c;band=(0.3, 1]:reproducible_share ~ .0%}} of that mean in the control flies and {{E68/data_cv_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT;band=(0.3, 1]:reproducible_share ~ .0%}} with APL output blocked (TNT), the negative ones (at or below −0.3 z) at {{E68/data_cv_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT3c;band=(-inf, -0.3]:reproducible_share ~ .0%}} and {{E68/data_cv_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT;band=(-inf, -0.3]:reproducible_share ~ .0%}}. Blocking APL output nearly doubles the share of weak values, while the share of strong ones barely rises and the responders' mean amplitude does not change (the KC data column of the table of amplitudes further down). The negative values are more frequent for the odors with more responders, in the control flies and with APL output blocked (TNT) alike (a Spearman correlation across odors of {{E68/data_neg_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT3c:rho_within_recording_mean ~ .2f}} and {{E68/data_neg_by_genotype.csv:genotype=TNT:rho_within_recording_mean ~ .2f}} within a recording), so they are not a mark of APL's output. A pair's cosine similarity is a sum over KCs, and each KC's part belongs to one of three terms: both of its entries responders, one a responder and the other sub-threshold, or both sub-threshold. Of the flies' mean APL effect of {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:both__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} is in the first term, {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} in the second (90 % interval {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one__effect_mean:lo ~ +.3f}} to {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one__effect_mean:hi ~ +.3f}}) and {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:neither__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} in the third; of the effect's pattern across the 120 pairs, {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:both__pattern_share:observed ~ .0%}} is in the first. The sub-threshold values thus carry about a third of how far APL moves odors apart in the flies, and a tenth of which pairs it moves most.

src: With APL on, the reference model read through the noise is close to the flies' amplitudes above 0.5 z (figure below). With APL off it is not. What blocking APL output adds in the flies is weak: the share between 0.5 and 1.5 z nearly doubles, and the share above 4 z and the responders' mean amplitude hardly move. What removing APL adds in the model is strong: about five times the flies' share above 4 z, and a mean amplitude more than a third higher than with APL on. The potential terms do not supply the weak values. The depolarization term calibrates to almost nothing in four of the six models, the reference model among them: the measurement noise alone already puts more of the model's APL-on entries between 0.25 and 1 z ({{E68/partB_amplitude.csv:model=ref40;config=floor_noise:share_025_1_on ~ .1%}}) than the control flies have ({{data:ctrl_share_z_025_1 ~ .1%}}), which leaves the term nothing to supply. The hyperpolarization term gives the model the flies' negative values with APL on and, with APL off, more of them where the flies have fewer: in five of the six models removing APL makes more KCs fire, and their KC–KC inhibition hyperpolarizes the rest. The cosine term that grows in the flies turns negative (last row), and the terms add strongly negative values that the flies do not have. Where a loss falls with the potential terms it falls with the mean effect, and in every model the same terms do as well or better with the potential shuffled across the non-spiking KCs or with the APL-on potential used for both conditions, so nothing in the potential's own pattern helps. The missing low end is therefore not hidden under the model's spike threshold. It is missing from what the model recruits when APL is removed, in all six models: strong responses where the flies have weak ones. What the weak values carry of the flies' APL effect sits for the most part in broadly responding KCs, as their weaker responses to their other odors, not in cells that respond weakly throughout ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class), at the end of this section). The realism bands hold a model to which KCs respond, not to how strongly, and do not see this; it is taken up with the pending work at the end of the page.

src: **The first is excluded, the second has no support, and the result points at the input.** Wild-type flies shown paa at the concentration of its ORN input hold paa and B-myr apart, so that paa's concentration is not the reason. src: **The pattern part is a per-odor error and a pair-specific error, and the models are at about twice the data's floor, or more, on each.** Once the readout has supplied the mean, what is left of the best models' loss is its pattern part, and the per-odor profile of the APL effect took that part apart. Part of a per-pair effect is the sum of two per-odor terms, one for each odor of the pair (an odor's share of the effect in every pair it is in); the rest belongs to the pair alone. In the flies the per-odor terms hold {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=measured_additive_r2:mean ~ .0%}} of the effect's variance across the 120 pairs, and an odor's share follows how much its response fraction rises when APL output is blocked (Pearson r {{E66/data_share_correlates.csv:data=graded;correlate=gain:pearson ~ .2f}} across the 16 odors). A model's pattern error [is split the same way](#fn-apl-effect-parts): the per-odor part is the error that 16 per-odor terms account for, the pair-specific part is the rest, and their squares add up to the squared pattern part. Each has a floor of its own, from recordings drawn again with replacement, as the loss has. The two parts are not measured equally firmly. Scored against two random halves of the recordings, on raw spike counts, the saved models keep their order on the pair-specific part (an agreement of {{apl_effect_metrics/split_half_reliability.csv:pair_specific_part:split_half_rho ~ .2f}}, where one is the same order against both halves) far better than on the per-odor part ({{apl_effect_metrics/split_half_reliability.csv:per_odor_part:split_half_rho ~ .2f}}; [the statistics compared](#fn-pattern-split)). What is said below about single odors' shares of an error is therefore a lead to be tested, not a result.

src: **The pair-specific part comes with breadth-weighted APL.** On raw spike counts it is about twice the bouton baseline's in the first joint fit and in the reference model (first table), and in the breadth-weighted APL experiment it rose with the exponent of the spike-total breadth at unchanged response rates (from {{E66/by_variant_parts.csv:folder=E12_breadth_apl;tag=k0;readout=raw:apl_effect_pair_specific ~ .3f}} without the weighting to {{E66/by_variant_parts.csv:folder=E12_breadth_apl;tag=spikes_k3;readout=raw:apl_effect_pair_specific ~ .3f}} at exponent 3). DM5, DM1 and DP1m carry the oracle gain, but the first kind of error leads in the first joint fit as well, which has no gain (a pair-specific error of {{E66/worst_pairs.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2;readout=raw;odor_a=eb;odor_b=1-8ol:pair_specific ~ +.2f}} for eb / 1-8ol against the reference model's {{E66/worst_pairs.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=raw;odor_a=eb;odor_b=1-8ol:pair_specific ~ +.2f}}): it comes with the breadth weighting, and the gain on DM5 enlarges it (among the variants of [the oracle gain decomposed by glomerulus](#gain-decomposition) for the 40 Hz fit, the pair-specific part on raw counts is {{E66/by_variant_parts.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__full;readout=raw:apl_effect_pair_specific ~ .3f}} with the gain on all eight glomeruli, {{E66/by_variant_parts.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__loo_DM5;readout=raw:apl_effect_pair_specific ~ .3f}} with DM5's removed and {{E66/by_variant_parts.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__none;readout=raw:apl_effect_pair_specific ~ .3f}} with none).

src: **Lowering the breadth exponent trades the pair-specific part against the mean effect and the block.** The breadth exponent is the power of a KC's breadth (its spike total over the 16 odors with APL off) by which breadth-weighted APL scales that KC's APL→KC weight; the reference model was fitted with 2. It was changed in the reference model at otherwise fitted parameters, the APL→KC scale re-tuned to the fitted response rate with APL on, so that the model with APL off is the same in every column (last three columns of the table). Without the weighting the pair-specific part falls to near the bouton baseline's level, by half on raw spike counts, and on raw counts the mean APL effect and the block all but disappear with it: keeping APL off the high-firing KCs is what moves odors apart overall and makes the block, and where two odors share such KCs it is also the pair-specific error. On raw counts the trade has no good point. Under the calibrated readout, which supplies the mean by itself, exponent 1 gives the reference model a lower loss than the fitted exponent 2, the lowest of the series, with most of the block on raw counts and the response rates unchanged; it is a one-parameter change of the fitted model and not a fit, and the two 70 Hz fits of the family gain nothing from it (figure). Taking a KC's breadth as the number of odors it responds to, instead of its spike total, raises the pair-specific part less for the same mean effect and gives the lowest loss of the series on raw counts, with a smaller block. Removing the weighting, or weighting by the number of odors, also concentrates the response with APL on in fewer KCs, which the bands on the response rates do not see; the band on odors per KC counts responders and not their amplitudes, and with APL on every column passes it, the one without the weighting nearest its limit ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E66_per_odor_apl_profile;tag=C_thr40_gain1.5_spikes_k0:opk_on_tv ~ .2f}} from the control flies' distribution, against {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E66_per_odor_apl_profile;tag=C_thr40_gain1.5_spikes_k2:opk_on_tv ~ .2f}} as fitted and a band of {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .2f}}; a participation ratio among responders of {{E66/parts_bc_table.csv:C_thr40_gain1.5_spikes_k0:participation_ratio_resp_on ~ .1%}} without the weighting, against {{E66/parts_bc_table.csv:O_thr40_gain1.5_untuned:participation_ratio_resp_on ~ .1%}} as fitted and at exponent 1, and {{data:ctrl_participation_ratio_resp ~ .1%}} in the control flies), and that ratio is what the readout is calibrated on.

src: In the breadth-2 family the definition changes the number, not the model: fitted on raw counts, the same start ends at nearly the same parameters and scores (first two columns). The other bases come apart: fitted on raw counts they give up most or all of their KC–KC inhibition and the block for a larger mean effect, and two then go below the breadth-2 fit on raw counts, the breadth-3 family and the 70 Hz base with the gain on DM1 alone (fourth and last columns). Through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) the order changes. The 70 Hz base's loss rises, and it rests on a few of its KCs ([the next subsection](#high-firing-kcs)). The breadth-3 fit holds, with part of a block coming back, and the breadth-2 fit's loss falls with its block kept, so that it is the lowest of the three, but narrowly: its margin over the breadth-3 fit is about the difference between the two noise levels, on one seed of the noise.

src: **On raw spike counts about twenty KCs of the real wiring hold the reference model's mean APL effect down.** The shortfall of the mean APL effect is the larger part of most losses in the best-models table, and at the same fitted scales the reference model's mean effect is larger on shuffled wirings than on the real one. The pairwise co-input examined in [the wiring experiments](#wiring-feature) is not the reason: with the excess of the over-shared glomerulus pairs removed from the real wiring the mean effect stays at {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E52_glomerulus_pairs;tag=C_thr40_gain1.5_lesion_targeted-seed1_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E52_glomerulus_pairs;tag=C_thr40_gain1.5_lesion_targeted-seed2_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} over three draws, against {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} untouched, and on the six shuffled draws matched to the real wiring on every glomerulus pair's count of shared KCs it is {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E59_coinput_shuffle;tag=M_thr40_gain1.5_curveball_within_type_matched-seed3_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E59_coinput_shuffle;tag=M_thr40_gain1.5_curveball_within_type_matched-seed2_retuned:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} (the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}). The experiment on the high-firing KCs that survive APL looked for the reason in single cells. Two sets were fixed before any simulation: a model's high-firing set, its KCs with twenty or more spikes to some odor with APL off, and its survivors, those of them that also reach twenty spikes to some odor with APL on. src: **The gain is all in the mean part, and the block goes with the cells.** The loss barely moves: what the mean part gains, the pattern part loses (second and third rows of the table above), and under the calibrated readout, where the real wiring's mean effect is already above the flies', the loss rises in every draw. The fruity × small-ester block, which the reference model has at the data's size on the real wiring, falls to half or less with the survivors re-drawn and keeps most of its size in all but one draw of the controls ({{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_ctl_outside-seed1_retuned:raw__block ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_ctl_outside-seed2_retuned:raw__block ~ +.3f}} / {{E70/partB_scores.csv:tag=B_thr40_gain1.5_ctl_outside-seed3_retuned:raw__block ~ +.3f}} with the matched KCs from outside the high-firing set re-drawn); put back into the claw permutations, the survivors' claws bring part of it back in two of the three. APL's effect on the natural-source alignment (APL on minus APL off), of the wrong sign on the real wiring, moves further from the flies' when the survivors are re-drawn and toward it when their claws are put back. The cells that hold the mean effect down on raw counts are therefore the ones that carry the reference model's block, and on raw counts the two statistics pull against each other through the same twenty KCs. None of this costs a realism band: the re-drawn models stay at the flies' response rates, and the distance of the odors-per-KC distribution from the flies' with APL off, inside its band on the real wiring, shrinks.

src: Every model on this page is tuned or fitted so that 5 % of KCs respond with APL on, a convention from the lab's earlier modelling, while {{data:ctrl_frac ~ .1%}} of the control flies' KCs respond (and {{data:tnt_frac ~ .1%}} with APL output blocked). Re-fitted with the response-rate target at the control flies' fraction instead, the reference model keeps everything the fit measures: the block, ρ on odor-odor distances with both KC matrices and the structure vs wild-type somata stay where they were at 5 %, response rate ρ with APL on rises slightly, and the loss without its response-rate term is no worse (the fit does it with a stronger APL↔KC loop and a weaker APL→bouton scale).

src: **Most of the reference model's survivors are the cells through which the oracle gain lifts euc and -aPine, and they are not realistic KCs.** On the real wiring the survivors' claws are concentrated on fewer glomeruli than those of the rest of the high-firing set ({{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=survivor:max_claws_one_glomerulus ~ .2f}} claws from their most-sampled glomerulus against {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=high_firing_other:max_claws_one_glomerulus ~ .2f}}, {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=survivor:n_glomeruli ~ .1f}} distinct glomeruli against {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=high_firing_other:n_glomeruli ~ .1f}}); The cells themselves are far from recorded KCs: with APL on the reference model's survivors fire up to {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes to one odor, and with APL off {{E70/wiring_by_class.csv:key=ref40;kc_class=survivor:max_count_off ~ .0f}} on average and up to {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:max_count_off ~ .0f}}, against a bound of about {{lit:14 # the bound the firing ceiling for the KCs (E69) takes for a KC's response with APL on: the mean plus three standard deviations of the 4.9 ± 3.0 spikes per 0.5 s response of α′/β′ KCs in Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent (2008), as quoted in E70_high_firing_kcs.md, Realism; not re-derived for this page}} spikes that [the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling) takes from recordings of KCs (the mean plus three standard deviations of the counts in Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent, 2008). src: **One fly is about as far from the other flies as the best models are from the data.** Scored as a model is, one control recording paired with one recording with APL output blocked (TNT), against the mean of the remaining recordings, has an APL-effect loss of {{lit:0.111 # median of column rmse over the 88 pairs of one control recording and one recording with APL output blocked (TNT) in results/E70_high_firing_kcs/yardstick.csv}} (the median over the pairs; {{lit:0.074 # minimum of column rmse in results/E70_high_firing_kcs/yardstick.csv}} to {{lit:0.263 # maximum of column rmse in results/E70_high_firing_kcs/yardstick.csv}}) and a pattern part of {{lit:0.092 # median of column rmse_centered in results/E70_high_firing_kcs/yardstick.csv}}, measurement noise included; the floor of {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} is that of the mean over all recordings. src: **What follows for the definition of the target, the block and the realism of the models.** On raw spike counts the shortfall of the mean effect in the models with the oracle gain is in good part the amplitude of about one in a hundred of their KCs, the least realistic cells they have. The calibrated readout takes that amplitude away without choosing cells, which is how it supplied these models' mean effect ([above](#readout)), and a firing ceiling in the model takes it away at the source ([the next subsection](#firing-ceiling)); under the readout the same cells support the mean effect, so in a model without a ceiling whether they count against it depends on the definition that is still open. Three things do not depend on it. The order of the best models on raw counts turns on two to six cells of one wiring, and the order under the calibrated readout does not, which favours the first joint fit's family over the fits with the gain on DM1 alone under either definition. The reference model's block is carried by its survivors, so whatever removes them, re-wiring here and the readout's compression before, removes the block with them; a model that is to have the block together with the flies' mean effect needs a carrier of the block that is not a few over-driven cells, which is what the mechanisms acting on the set of responding KCs are. And the weak-input odors have to reach their response rates through many moderately driven KCs: the ORN input of euc, -aPine and paa scaled toward the recordings' concentrations, or a gain kept off the glomeruli that give the survivors most of their claws, is the place to start.

src: **With a ceiling on how many spikes a KC fires to an odor, the model's raw spike counts score on the main target as the calibrated readout does, inside the realism bands; the block is lost as it is under the readout, and which KCs respond with APL off does not change.** Until this experiment the model's KCs had neither a refractory period nor adaptation: after a spike the potential was reset and integration went on at once. The hardest-driven KC of the current reference model fires {{E69/stats_variants.csv:ref40_base:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes to one 0.5 s odor with APL on and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:ref40_base:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with APL off, where a reading of whole-cell recordings of KCs puts the bound at about {{lit:14 # the bound on a KC's spike count to one odor with APL on that the firing ceiling for the KCs takes from whole-cell recordings: the mean plus three standard deviations (4.9 + 3 x 3.0 = 13.9) of the spikes per response of α′/β′ KCs to a 500 ms odor in Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent (2008); E69_kc_firing_ceiling.md, Design (part B) and Caveats}} spikes (the mean plus three standard deviations of the counts of the α′/β′ KCs in Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent, 2008). The firing ceiling for the KCs adds both to the model ([how it works and how its settings were chosen](#fn-firing-ceiling)): a refractory period of 3 ms, and an adaptation that raises a KC's threshold by a fixed fraction of itself at every spike and decays over 1 s, longer than the odor, so that within one odor it acts as a budget of spikes. It was applied first at fixed scales, to the current reference model and to the best APL-effect fit under each definition of the model's side ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)), with both response rates held at each model's own by re-tuning the somatic threshold and the APL scales, so that nothing is bought with the response rates. The breadth-2 fit was then fitted again under the APL-effect loss, with the ceiling fixed and both definitions in the loss, at two strengths of the adaptation: the literature setting ({{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:kc_adapt_inc ~ .0%}} of the threshold per spike), at which its largest count with APL on is nearest the recordings' bound, and a stronger setting ({{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:kc_adapt_inc ~ .0%}}), the weakest at which the calibrated readout has nothing left to compress. The reference model was fitted again at the stronger setting, where its own largest count with APL on is at the recordings' bound.

src: **The raw counts now give what the readout gave.** On raw counts the loss of the breadth-2 family falls by a third at the literature setting and by nearly half at the stronger one, and the reference model's halves (first row). The mean APL effect, below the flies' 90 % interval on raw counts without a ceiling, is inside it in every fit with one, and the two definitions come together: at the stronger setting they give one number, and at the literature setting they are about a tenth as far apart as without a ceiling. The calibrated readout was standing in for firing that the model did not bound, and with a ceiling of this kind the choice between raw counts and the readout matters little. Most of this is there before any fitting: at fixed scales, with both response rates held, the breadth-2 fit goes from {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67cal_base:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} on raw counts to {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67cal_r3_a1_t1000:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} at the literature setting and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67cal_r3_a2_t1000:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} at the stronger one. The best fit on raw counts without a ceiling, the 70 Hz base with the gain on DM1 alone, gets worse with one ({{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67raw_base:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67raw_r3_a1_t1000:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67raw_r3_a2_t1000:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} at the two settings) and was not fitted again; its lead rested on a few high-firing KCs ([above](#high-firing-kcs)). The data are not reached. The fit at the stronger setting has the lowest loss of any model on the real wiring inside all four realism bands, under either definition, and is still a third above the floor, nearly all of it pattern: ρ on the per-pair APL effect stays well under its ceiling, and the per-odor and the pair-specific part of the loss are {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:apl_raw_per_odor ~ .3f}} and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:apl_raw_pair_specific ~ .3f}}, against floors of {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_per_odor:mean ~ .3f}} and {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_pair_specific:mean ~ .3f}}. Through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) both fits with the ceiling stay below every APL-effect fit without one on raw counts (the fourth row here and the same row of the table of [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)), and the stronger setting's lead over the literature setting is gone, so the setting that agrees with the recordings loses nothing. All of these are numbers of the model's 0.5 s odor pulse. At the flies' 2 s pulse, with parameters fitted at 0.5 s, the loss on raw counts rises in both families, by a fifth with the ceiling at its stronger setting and by more than half without a ceiling, so the ceiling's gain on raw counts stays and its level does not ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates), at the end of this section). The level comes back with an adaptation that outlasts the odor: with it decaying over 3 s in place of 1 s, the fit at the stronger setting, the literature setting as a mean over four wirings and a fit made at the flies' pulse all read through the flies' response window what they read at 0.5 s ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol), at the end of this section).

src: **The ceiling costs what the readout costs, and it does not change which KCs respond.** In the breadth-2 family the block falls to about two thirds of the flies' at the literature setting and a third at the stronger one, and the reference model's is all but gone; the natural-source alignment with APL on falls at the stronger setting, and the mean distances fall below the flies' in both conditions. src: **Other wirings, and a strength that is a reading.** Under the readout, one draw of the wiring moves this family's loss by more than the fits with a ceiling differ from the fit without one. The same family fitted without a ceiling on seven re-drawn wirings (four within-type claw permutations and three shuffles matched to the real wiring on every glomerulus pair's count of shared KCs; [the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population), at the end of this section) ends between {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} under the readout, the real wiring's {{E72/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} among them, and between {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:raw_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E72/stats_variants.csv:wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:raw_loss ~ .3f}} on raw counts. Under the readout the fits with a ceiling are therefore as good as the fit without one, not better; on raw counts they are below the fit of every one of those wirings, and the gain holds through the trial noise. The ceiling at the literature setting has since been fitted on three of those wirings as well, each beside the fit without a ceiling on the same wiring: on raw counts the loss changes by between {{E72/partG_paired.csv:wiring=P2:raw_loss_diff ~ +.3f}} and {{E72/partG_paired.csv:wiring=P1:raw_loss_diff ~ +.3f}} on the three, as by {{E72/partG_paired.csv:wiring=real:raw_loss_diff ~ +.3f}} on the real wiring, and under the readout by no more than {{E72/partG_paired.csv:wiring=P2:cal_loss_diff ~ .3f}} on any of the four, so the gain on raw counts is the family's and not the hemibrain wiring's. The stronger setting has been fitted on the real wiring only. Its strength is a reading of the recordings, not a measurement: they give the mean and the standard deviation of the spike counts per response ({{lit:4.9 ± 3.0 # spikes per response of α′/β′ KCs to a 500 ms odor (mean ± standard deviation, whole-cell recordings, APL intact), Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent (2008), as quoted in E69_kc_firing_ceiling.md, Design (part B), Realism and Caveats}} for α′/β′ KCs and {{lit:2.2 ± 1.2 # spikes per response of α/β KCs to a 500 ms odor (mean ± standard deviation, whole-cell recordings, APL intact), Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent (2008), as quoted in E69_kc_firing_ceiling.md, Realism and Caveats}} for α/β KCs, to other odors and concentrations than the KC data's) and no largest count, and the stronger setting, at which no KC of the breadth-2 fit fires more than {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes with APL on, allows the α′/β′ KCs less than they show. Both fits of the breadth-2 family also ended with more KCs responding with APL off than they started with (a response rate {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}} and {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}} times that with APL on, from {{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67cal_base:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}}; the flies' {{data:rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}, 90 % interval {{data:rate_ratio_fraction.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:rate_ratio_fraction.hi ~ .2f}}), which by itself raises the mean effect, so part of what the fits add to the runs at fixed scales may be bought that way; the ratio was not held in the fits. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

src: **A somatic threshold that scales with each KC's input moves the release of KCs, when APL is removed, off the many-claw cells, as the flies' numbers of odors per KC ask, and in every family the main target pays for it; fitted again, each family gets the mean effect back with as many broadly responding KCs as before, drawn from other cells, and loses on the pattern.** In the model every KC has the same somatic threshold, apart from a term proportional to its spontaneous input, so a KC with many claws crosses it for more odors than a KC with few. Breadth-weighted APL inhibits the broadly responding KCs most, so when APL is removed they are the ones released. In the breadth-2 APL-effect fit ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)) the KCs that respond to eight or more odors with APL off have {{E70/opk_features.csv:key=e67__rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;feature=n_claws:mean_8plus_off ~ .1f}} claws on average and the silent ones {{E70/opk_features.csv:key=e67__rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;feature=n_claws:mean_silent_off ~ .1f}}, and the {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:rel_g9plus_n_kcs ~ .0f}} KCs with nine or more claws, of {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:n_kcs_on ~ .0f}}, take a third of the responses that removing APL adds. More of its KCs stay silent than in the flies, more respond to eight or more odors, and the number of odors per KC is spread more widely than in any recording. With every KC × odor entry counted only as a response or none (binarized: two or more spikes in the model, a trial mean above 1 in the recordings), removing APL then adds more overlap between odors than it does in the flies, although under the calibrated readout the fit's mean APL effect is the flies' (first model column of the table below). The low end of the readout found the same from the amplitudes ([above](#readout)): with APL off the models add strong responses where the flies add weak ones, and what the weak ones carry of the flies' APL effect is for the most part the weaker responses of their broadly responding KCs to their other odors ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class), further down in this section). [The firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling) changes how much the released KCs fire and not which KCs they are, and KC–KC inhibition strong enough to spread the release brings the silent share below the flies' ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E53_kckc_held_block;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc45_k2_cap3:opk_off_0 ~ .0%}} in the 70 Hz model with the gain at 1.25 and KC–KC held at 45, against {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_0 ~ .0%}}) at a mean APL effect of {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E53_kckc_held_block;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc45_k2_cap3:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} on raw counts and {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E53_kckc_held_block;tag=thr70_gain1.25_rate0.068_kckc45_k2_cap3:cal__mean ~ +.3f}} under the readout. The one earlier test of thresholds by claw count, in the KC heterogeneity experiment, had not applied them.

src: The input-scaled KC threshold multiplies each KC's threshold by a power of the KC's summed claw weight relative to the mean over KCs, the same with APL on and with APL off, so that it is a property of the cell and not of APL; with the power at zero it is the model as it was. Through the spontaneous-input term the threshold of the breadth-2 fit already grows with a KC's summed claw weight, with a log-log slope of {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:thr_loglog_slope_W ~ .2f}}; a power of 0.5 brings the slope to {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a0.5:thr_loglog_slope_W ~ .2f}}, a threshold about proportional to the input. The power was swept at fixed scales, from 0.25 to 1 and at −0.5 as a control of the sign, on three models: the breadth-2 fit, the same fit with the firing ceiling at its literature setting, and the current reference model. At every setting both response rates were held at the model's own by re-tuning the somatic threshold on the APL-off response rate and then the APL→KC and APL→bouton scales together on the APL-on one, so that no change is bought with the response rates, and the per-KC breadth behind the APL→KC weights was computed again with the scaled thresholds, the weights forming on the cells as they then are. For each model the power kept is the one that brings the number of odors per KC with APL off closest to the flies' among the settings that stay inside the bands on odors per KC and on the response rate ρ with APL on, a choice that involves no distance between odors. Each of the three was then fitted again under the APL-effect loss with that power fixed, both definitions in the loss and the usual four parameters free.

src: **At fixed scales the release moves the way the flies' numbers ask.** With the power at 0.5 the few-claw KCs of the breadth-2 fit take over the responses that removing APL adds (first row), and with APL off a KC with nine or more claws then responds to fewer odors than a KC with one to four ({{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a0.5:rel_g9plus_opk_off ~ .1f}} against {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a0.5:rel_g1_4_opk_off ~ .1f}} on average, from {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:rel_g9plus_opk_off ~ .1f}} against {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:rel_g1_4_opk_off ~ .1f}}). The distance of the odors-per-KC distribution from the flies' with APL off falls by more than a quarter, and the binarized mean APL effect and its loss come down toward the data's. The other two models move the same way, and the reference model, inside the band on odors per KC with APL off as it stands, comes to a third of its distance from the flies' distribution with the scaling. The flies' distribution is not reached: about four KCs in ten still respond to none of the odors with APL off, a little more than the flies' {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_0 ~ .0%}}, and in the breadth-2 fit, with or without the ceiling, the spread of the number of odors per KC stays above every recording's (the reference model's comes inside their range). The control of the sign moves the release the other way: at a power of −0.5 the KCs with nine or more claws take {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a-0.5:rel_g9plus_share_added ~ .0%}} of the added responses, the distance with APL off rises to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E71_input_scaled_threshold;tag=c2_a-0.5:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}}, more than twice the unscaled fit's and near the band's limit of {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}, and the binarized mean APL effect rises to {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a-0.5:apl_bin_mean ~ +.3f}}. Beyond the power kept the few-claw KCs become the over-driven ones: at a power of 1 the largest spike count of the breadth-2 fit with APL on is {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} and the distance with APL off is above the unscaled fit's again ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E71_input_scaled_threshold;tag=c2_a1:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}}).

src: **The release stays off the many-claw KCs, and the broad responders come back from other cells.** In all three fits the KCs with nine or more claws take a fifth or less of the responses that removing APL adds, where they took a third (the row on who is released), and the spread of the number of odors per KC with APL off comes inside the recordings' range (the row under it). But between {{E71/fits.csv:thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.75_k2:fit_opk_off_8plus ~ .0%}} and {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:fit_opk_off_8plus ~ .0%}} of the KCs again respond to eight or more odors with APL off, about as many as without the scaling and against the flies' {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_8plus ~ .0%}}, and with the power at 0.5 or 0.75 they are now KCs with few claws: the KCs of the breadth-2 family that respond to eight or more odors with APL off average {{lit:5.0 # computed from the archived response matrices of this fit (data/model_outputs/E71_input_scaled_threshold/, tag rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.5_k2) and the claw counts of data/model_outputs/inputs/wPNKC_bouton_base.parquet, as release_stats in E71_input_scaled_threshold.py does for part A (the same computation reproduces part A's cells of input_readouts.csv); unrounded 4.96; not in a results table}} claws, from {{E70/opk_features.csv:key=e67__rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;feature=n_claws:mean_8plus_off ~ .1f}} without the scaling, and those of the reference model's set {{lit:5.1 # computed from the archived response matrices of this fit (data/model_outputs/E71_input_scaled_threshold/, tag thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.75_k2) and the claw counts of data/model_outputs/inputs/wPNKC_bouton_base.parquet, as release_stats in E71_input_scaled_threshold.py does for part A (the same computation reproduces part A's cells of input_readouts.csv); unrounded 5.09; not in a results table}}, from {{E70/opk_features.csv:key=ref40;feature=n_claws:mean_8plus_off ~ .1f}}. The binarized mean APL effect returns with them, to between {{E71/fits.csv:thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.75_k2:responses_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} and {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:responses_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} against the flies' {{data:apl_effect_binary_mean ~ +.3f}}, where the settings at fixed scales had brought it to between {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_a0.5:apl_bin_mean ~ +.3f}} and {{E71/input_readouts.csv:ref40_a0.75:apl_bin_mean ~ +.3f}}. The breadth-2 family's distance from the flies' distribution of odors per KC with APL off is therefore back where it was (sixth row), with other cells as the broad responders. The other two families also leave fewer KCs silent and come closer to the flies' distribution, the reference model's set to about half the distance of its earlier fits, which were inside the band as well: its fits under the APL-effect loss were {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplraw_k2_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} and {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution, and its fits with a firing ceiling {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} and {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplbothopk_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}}. In this family the flies' graded mean effect is reached through a response-set term that overshoots, carried by KCs that turn into broad responders when APL is removed; the scaling changes which cells those are, and a fit of the main target makes them again. The flies' own effect is not of another kind. Split by the number of odors each KC responds to ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class), further down in this section), it also rests on KCs that respond broadly when APL output is blocked, and the third of the mean effect that comes from products with values below the response criterion ([above](#readout)) is those KCs' weaker responses to their other odors. Counted by the recordings' own criterion, in their z-scored units, the flies have two kinds of such KCs, a few that respond to eight or more odors and many that respond to four to seven, where the models have the first kind alone. That difference belongs to the unit: with each KC's responses in baseline-noise units the KCs at eight or more odors carry the flies' effect alone, as in the models ([the data side of the main target](#data-side), further down in this section). In either unit the flies have no route through amplitudes in place of broad responders.

src: **Read as the recordings are, the scaling is nearly free in the family with the firing ceiling.** The per-KC normalization of the recordings ([further down in this section](#per-kc-normalization)) reads every saved model as the KC data are produced: each KC's signal is put in units of its own standard deviation over the whole recording, and an odor's response is taken relative to the frames before it, so that a KC that responds to many odors has every one of its responses scaled down. Read that way (the two rows of the second table that carry this reading) the breadth-2 family and the reference model's set lose as much with the scaling as under the calibrated readout, or more; under the recordings' own response criterion the reference model is itself inside the band on odors per KC with APL off, and its set with the scaling is further inside. The family with the firing ceiling loses {{diff:E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E71_input_scaled_threshold;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse -- E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}, a small part of what the loss varies by over wirings under the same reading ({{E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E73/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} over the seven re-drawn wirings of the breadth-2 family, fitted without a ceiling), and its distance from the flies' distribution of odors per KC with APL off is the smallest in the table. If that reading becomes the definition of the model's side of the target, the firing ceiling together with the input-scaled threshold at a small power is the combination to fit under it. That fit has been made ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class)): under the reading it ends level with the fit without the scaling, but it gets there by weakening APL and KC–KC inhibition until its response rate at two or more spikes with APL on is {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:rate_on ~ .3f}}, twice the flies' response rate and outside the band, so it is a measurement and not a candidate base; the question is open again with the fits' operating point held on two spikes.

src: **A single pseudo-recording of the breadth-2 fit is closer to the data's mean than a single pair of recordings is.** The comparison that [the high-firing KCs that survive APL](#high-firing-kcs) left open was made here, the trial-noise pipeline now saving every pseudo-recording. One pseudo-recording with APL on paired with one with APL off (three trials each through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise), {{E71/partC_summary.csv:reading=matched_each:n ~ .0f}} pairs), scored against the KC data's mean per-pair effect as a model is, has a median APL-effect loss of {{E71/partC_summary.csv:reading=matched_each:rmse_median ~ .3f}} ({{E71/partC_summary.csv:reading=matched_each:rmse_min ~ .3f}} to {{E71/partC_summary.csv:reading=matched_each:rmse_max ~ .3f}}) and a median mean effect of {{E71/partC_summary.csv:reading=matched_each:mean_median ~ +.3f}}. One control recording paired with one recording with APL output blocked (TNT), scored against the mean of the remaining recordings, has {{E71/partC_summary.csv:model=KC data (E70 yardstick):rmse_median ~ .3f}} ({{E71/partC_summary.csv:model=KC data (E70 yardstick):rmse_min ~ .3f}} to {{E71/partC_summary.csv:model=KC data (E70 yardstick):rmse_max ~ .3f}}) and {{E71/partC_summary.csv:model=KC data (E70 yardstick):mean_median ~ +.3f}}. The model's pairs vary far less than the flies': they have the trial noise, but one wiring and no differences between flies. The best fit on one wiring is therefore already as close to the data's mean as a single pair of recordings is, and what separates it from the floor is no more than single recordings show. Averaged over four wirings and read through the same noise, as the data's mean is an average over flies and trials, the breadth-2 family has a loss on raw counts of {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} with the noise matched to the control flies and {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=population;level=match_off;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} with the noise matched to APL output blocked (TNT), against {{E71/input_readouts.csv:c2_base:apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} for the one wiring without noise ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population), the next subsection). src: **What the scaling gains is realism, and what it costs is the main target.** Every setting kept and every fit with the scaling is inside all four realism bands, the reference model's set comes to half its distance from the flies' distribution of odors per KC with APL off, and the spread of the number of odors per KC with APL off is inside the recordings' range in all three fits, which none of the three families is without the scaling. The fit of the reference model's set has a common somatic threshold and APL scales within about a fifth of the baseline's and KC–KC inhibition all but off (last row of the second table). The fit with the firing ceiling keeps a common somatic threshold under half the baseline's, as the breadth-2 fit has, which is hard to defend, and at a power of 0.5 the scaling itself asks for thresholds from {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.5_k2:kc_thr_input_factor_min ~ .2f}} to {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_thrin0.5_k2:kc_thr_input_factor_max ~ .2f}} times the common value; whether the thresholds of KCs vary that much with their claw input is a question for the physiology. Without a firing ceiling the scaling at fixed scales makes few-claw KCs the highest-firing cells of the breadth-2 fit (the row of largest spike counts in the first table), which the fits undo (the same row of the second). Each fit is a local search from one start on the real wiring, the scaling has one functional form, a power of the summed claw weight, and as everywhere the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

src: **The breadth-2 APL-effect fit owes its standing to its family and not to the hemibrain wiring: fitted again on seven re-drawn wirings it ends around the same loss. One wiring's loss carries a draw term as large as the margins between recent fits, and the mean over wirings, the counterpart of data that are a mean over flies, has a lower loss, the whole gain in the pattern part. What is left is the same on every wiring: too little APL effect among the esters, where the flies have the block.** Every loss by which the models above are ranked is one wiring's. A model has the hemibrain wiring with APL on and with APL off, while the data's per-pair APL effect is the mean over {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} control recordings minus the mean over {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), from different flies, so that what is particular to one fly's wiring is averaged out of the data and kept whole in the model. The APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings fitted the best family of [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits) (breadth exponent 2, no per-claw threshold, no glomerulus gain; both definitions of the model's side in the loss, which on the real wiring scores as the fit under the readout does) again on seven re-drawn wirings, each from the real wiring's fitted parameters: four within-type claw permutations, and three shuffles matched to the real wiring on every glomerulus pair's count of shared KCs ([the wiring experiments](#wiring-feature)). The model's counterpart of the data's mean over flies is a mean over wirings: the pair distances are averaged over the wirings in each condition, and the APL effect and its loss are taken from the averages.

The hemibrain's exact wiring holds no special share of the match, so the family is the model to build on. src: **What remains is common to the wirings, and it sits where the block is.** The pattern error of the mean over the eight wirings is what every wiring shares, and each wiring adds a smaller remainder of its own. Under the readout the per-pair errors of any two wirings correlate between {{E72/error_corr_cal.csv:P1:P3 ~ .2f}} and {{E72/error_corr_cal.csv:M2:M3 ~ .2f}} over the 120 pairs (on raw counts between {{E72/error_corr_raw.csv:P3:P4 ~ .2f}} and {{E72/error_corr_raw.csv:real:M1 ~ .2f}}). In the common error the model's APL effect is too small on every pair among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms (the largest, 2h with IaA, by {{E72/common_error_pairs.csv:odor_a=2h;odor_b=IaA:abs_common ~ .3f}} once the means are removed) and on eb with 1-8ol and 1-6ol, and too large on every pair among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al. These are the pairs of the block and around it: under the readout the flies' APL separates these esters from one another more than the model's does on every one of the eight wirings. The block itself is smaller in the mean over wirings than on the real wiring (sixth row of the first table), whose block is the second largest of the eight; six of the seven re-drawn wirings have less, as shuffled wirings had in [the wiring experiments](#wiring-feature). No draw of the wiring removes this error, and averaging over wirings cannot: it is what a further mechanism has to supply. The one rule about which KCs APL acts on that is the same on every wiring, a profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli, has since been tried and does not supply it ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile), at the end of this section), and neither does a fixed change of what reaches the KCs ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)). Searched on several wirings at once, neither kind of change passes its test on wirings and recordings it was not fitted to, and what holds there is a small part of the error ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)).

src: **Nothing here is bought with realism, and what the bands do not see is the same on every wiring.** Every fit of the experiment, on every wiring, and every mean over wirings is inside all four realism bands (the lower rows of the first table give the odors-per-KC distances by the recordings' own criterion, the bands' until 2026-11-10; by the present one every fit is inside as well): averaging over wirings changes the comparison and not the model, and the shared parameter set is as realistic as the per-wiring fits. Beyond the bands the wirings agree with the real one. On each of the eight the KCs with nine or more claws take between a quarter and a third of the responses that removing APL adds, the number of odors per KC with APL off is spread more widely than in any recording ([the input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold)), and more KCs stay silent and more respond to eight or more odors than in the flies (last row of the first table). The somatic threshold is under half the baseline's on every wiring and the APL→bouton scale near its bound, which are hard to defend (what that scale does in these fits, and what a smaller one costs, has been measured since: [the PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition](#bouton-share)), and as everywhere the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations). The release through the many-claw KCs is thus the family's and survives every draw, and a stricter reading of realism, one that also held the spread of the number of odors per KC to the recordings' range, would put every one of the eight wirings outside. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

src: **Read the same way, the models are ordered as under the calibrated readout.** To read a model as the recordings were made, each model KC's spike counts are passed through a saturating map and placed in a simulated recording of the same 51 presentations, each response confined to its window, with frame noise and a slow drift (the drift set from the flies' KCs that respond to no odor). The trace is divided by its standard deviation over the session, a response is taken against the frames before it, and it counts as a response when its three-trial mean is above 1 z, as in the recordings; this is the per-KC reading. Three numbers are set for each model on its counts with APL on and kept for APL off, so that the APL effect stays a prediction: the frame noise, so that the response rate is the control flies'; the map's half-saturation, so that the responders' mean amplitude is the control flies' {{data:ctrl_resp_amp_mean_z ~ .1f}} z; and the measurement noise of a response, so that a non-responding entry varies from trial to trial as in the control flies. Every saved model with both conditions ({{E73/order.csv:reading=graded;present=present_cal:n_variants ~ .0f}} variants) was read this way and scored against the KC data as measured. Across them the APL-effect loss under the reading follows the loss under [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), with a Spearman correlation of {{E73/order.csv:reading=graded;present=present_cal:rho_all ~ .2f}} between the two and a median change of the loss of {{E73/order.csv:reading=graded;present=present_cal:median_change_loss ~ +.3f}}, and not the loss on raw counts ({{E73/order.csv:reading=graded;present=present_raw:rho_all ~ .2f}}). The readout was a fair stand-in for the recordings' normalization; raw counts were not. The lowest loss under the reading of any fit saved until then is that of [the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling) at its stronger setting ({{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}, with the flies' mean effect, {{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:mean ~ +.3f}}). The breadth-2 APL-effect fit, the best fit under the readout without a ceiling, has a higher loss under the reading than under the readout because its mean effect is smaller there (first, third and sixth rows of the table below; its mean effect under the readout is {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_mean ~ +.3f}}): part of the mean effect that the readout gave it came from the readout's compression of its strongest responders, which the per-KC normalization does not repeat.

src: **What the normalization had hidden.** In the flies a KC's unit grows with the number of odors the KC responds to ([the footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units) has the ratios), so that the responders' mean amplitude, about {{data:ctrl_resp_amp_mean_z ~ .0f}} z whatever the KC's breadth, is in baseline-noise units nearly twice as large in the control flies' KCs that respond to eight odors as in those that respond to one (the last row but one of the table; few KCs respond to exactly eight odors with APL on, in the flies and in the models, so the values at eight are rough). The flat amplitude in z is strongly growing responses compressed by the normalization. The models' responses grow much less: read the same way, their responders' amplitudes in baseline-noise units start lower and rise by a half to two thirds, their units hardly grow (the row above it), and with the firing ceiling both are lower still. The models' responses fill their sessions much less than the flies' do, so in the amplitudes the models are further from the flies than the comparison in z had said ([the low end of the readout](#readout) made it in z). The realism bands hold a model to which KCs respond, not to how strongly, and do not see this.

src: **Split by how many of the 16 odors a KC responds to, with a response counted as the recordings count it, above 1 z, the flies' APL effect rests on broadly responding KCs of two kinds, the few that respond to eight or more odors when APL output is blocked and the many that respond to four to seven. The models make theirs with the first kind alone, in every best fit and on every wiring. The difference belongs to that unit: with each KC's responses in baseline-noise units the flies' effect, too, sits in the KCs at eight or more odors alone (the data side of the main target, at the end of this section). In the z-scored units it is real, and it is not where the pattern error is: across the saved models a split closer to the flies' does not go with a lower pattern part, and a fit that is asked for the flies' split pays for it on the total.** [The input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold) left open which KCs carry the effect, in the flies and in the models. A pair's cosine similarity is a sum over KCs (the sum that [the low end of the readout](#readout) divided by whether its two entries are responses), so the per-pair APL effect can be divided among groups of KCs. The APL effect split by odors per KC put every KC, in each condition, in one of the five groups of the realism band on odors per KC, by the number of the 16 odors it responds to in that condition (none, one, two or three, four to seven, eight or more; one to three are shown together below), and took each group's part of every pair's similarity. A class's APL effect is its part of the similarity with APL off minus its part with APL on, and the classes' effects add up to the pair's APL effect. A KC can change class between the conditions, so the split says how much of each condition's similarity sits in KCs of a given tuning width; it needs no pairing of cells between the conditions, which the recordings cannot give, the control flies and the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) being different animals. In the recordings a response is a trial mean above 1 z, each genotype's class parts are averaged over its recordings, and the 90 % intervals are over recordings drawn again with replacement. Every archived model with both conditions saved ({{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=zcell;subset=all variants:n ~ .0f}} variants) was read in two ways: through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) with a response at two or more spikes, and as the recordings are produced, each KC in units of its own standard deviation over the session (the per-KC reading of [the subsection before this one](#per-kc-normalization)), with the recordings' criterion and through that reading's measurement noise, as ten pseudo-recordings of three trials, so that a model KC enters a class as a recorded KC does.

src: **The common error is in almost every saved model.** For each of the {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_n_variants:value ~ .0f}} saved variants with both conditions, the part of its own pattern error that lies along the common error was measured as a projection: 1 if the variant has as much of the common error as the mean over the eight wirings has, 0 if it has none. Under the readout the median is {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_median_cal_proj_common:value ~ .2f}} (on raw counts {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_median_raw_proj_common:value ~ .2f}}): the error is older than the best family and belongs to nothing particular to it. src: **Simulated, the cell profile helps the real wiring and not a left-out odor.** By the plan a failed test closed the experiment. Because the failed part had read the recordings, and both parts rested on single changes that do not add up, the cell profile was simulated all the same, as a diagnostic in stages that kept the test's thresholds. Of the strengths tried, half its scores (every factor at its square root) is the one at which its change takes away the largest share of the common error: were the change it makes on the real wiring the same on every wiring, {{E75/report_scalars.csv:d2_stage1_transfer_x0.5:value ~ .0%}} of it (15 % was asked), where the same scores permuted across the glomeruli would add to the error (two draws). The next stage failed. The sixteen profiles each fitted without one odor, simulated at the same strength and scored on that odor's pairs, remove {{E75/report_scalars.csv:d2_stage2_pooled_heldout:value ~ .1%}} of the common error there, pooled, against the 15 % asked and the {{E75/profile_cv.csv:profile=cell;variant=ridge:loo_odor_reduction ~ .1%}} that the added-up changes had predicted. They help most for B-myr, IaA, pa and paa ({{E75/report_scalars.csv:d2_stage2_fold_B-myr:value ~ .0%}} of the common error on B-myr's pairs) and add to the error for 6al, t2h, 2-but and -aPine. The splits of the recordings with the two recordings kept apart did not run, and neither did the fits with a profile on several wirings, for which the test was the gate. A fixed profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli, found by adding up single-glomerulus changes, therefore does not carry the common error. The result goes no further than that: scores fitted directly in simulation, on several wirings at once, were not tried here (they have been since, and carry a small part of the common error to wirings and recordings they were not fitted to, short of the test set for them: [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)), nor was APL inhibition that depends on the odor at the scale of a bouton (one form of it, inhibition that grows with a bouton's or a claw's own input, has since been emulated and does not lower the pattern part: [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side); another, inhibition that follows the calyx space that glomeruli share, has since been tested as a proxy on the input, from connectome tables whose use is on hold, and its reading is withheld: [the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)).

src: Without noise the mean over the four wirings with the ceiling is far below the mean without it; through the noise the two are level, apart by well under what one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}). The noise raises the mean APL effect of the family without the ceiling and lowers that of the family with it, to nearly the same value, short of the flies' (third and fourth rows), and the pattern parts are the same (last row). On each of the four wirings singly the fit with the ceiling is still the lower one through the noise (between {{E75/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} and {{E75/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} at the noise matched to the control flies, against {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} without it, the last column of the second table [above](#wiring-population)): averaging over wirings helps the family without the ceiling more. Read as the data are made, a mean over flies and over trials, the ceiling thus gives no clear gain on raw counts, as it gave none under the per-KC reading ([above](#per-kc-normalization)); its lead there belongs to the model without noise and to single wirings, and what it adds beyond that is realism, bounded spike counts and the spread of an odor's response over its KCs. The trial noise of this reading is all shared between the odors of a trial, where only part of the flies' is. Re-specified to the flies' shares it gives {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} without the ceiling and {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} with it, apart by less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss, so the reading holds ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)).

src: **The unit in which each KC's responses are taken moves the mean of the flies' APL effect and not its pattern. In baseline-noise units, the unit of the realism bands, the mean effect is about a third larger than in the recordings' z-scored units, the pattern across pairs is the same within its floor, and the saved models keep their order on raw counts. In those units the KCs that respond to eight or more odors carry the flies' effect alone. The two recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) that stand apart from the other six are stronger and not different, so the mean over all eight stands as the target, and neither a weaker APL nor a shifted somatic threshold makes their state in the model. Fitted to the effect in baseline-noise units, the family with the firing ceiling raises its mean effect by more than half of what was missing, at a cost on the pattern and with more broad responders, and read through the trial noise it keeps little of the gain.** Every loss elsewhere on this page is against the flies' per-pair APL effect computed from the recordings as they were made, each KC's trace z-scored over its whole recording. That unit grows with how much a KC responds, which is why the realism bands now count the flies' responses in baseline-noise units ([footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units)); the target itself stayed on the z-scored values, and what the choice of unit does to it was not known. Nor was it known what the target owes to two of the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), whose distances are much lower than those of the other six and through which a test on split halves of the recordings had failed ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile)). The data side of the main target measured both from the recordings and the saved models: the effect in every unit the recordings allow, every saved model scored against it, and the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) taken one by one. It then moved the model along its own two axes, the strength of APL's output and the somatic threshold, to see whether either makes what sets the two recordings apart, and fitted the best family to the effect in baseline-noise units.

src: A pair's cosine similarity is a sum over KCs, and each KC's part belongs to one of three terms: both of its entries responders, one a responder and the other sub-threshold, or both sub-threshold. Of the flies' mean APL effect of {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:both__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} is in the first term, {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} in the second (90 % interval {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one__effect_mean:lo ~ +.3f}} to {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one__effect_mean:hi ~ +.3f}}) and {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:neither__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} in the third; of the effect's pattern across the 120 pairs, {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:both__pattern_share:observed ~ .0%}} is in the first. The sub-threshold values thus carry about a third of how far APL moves odors apart in the flies, and a tenth of which pairs it moves most.
