src: **In their distances the two strongest recordings are stronger, not different.** The recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) differ among themselves in level far more than the control flies' do. In the z-scored units, as in the rest of this paragraph unless the other unit is named, two of them have mean distances of {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT two:mean_dist_z_min ~ .2f}} and {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT two:mean_dist_z_max ~ .2f}}, where the other six have {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT six:mean_dist_z_min ~ .2f}} to {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT six:mean_dist_z_max ~ .2f}} and the control recordings {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT3c:mean_dist_z_min ~ .2f}} to {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT3c:mean_dist_z_max ~ .2f}}, and the effect computed against the two alone is more than twice the effect against the six (tenth row). A first look had found that the step from the six to the two has another pattern across pairs than the step from the control flies to the six, the ρ between the two steps being near zero. Set against the other ways of splitting the recordings, that is not a difference. Any split of the eight into six and two pulls this ρ negative, because the six's mean enters the two steps with opposite signs; the actual split ranks {{E76/axis_tests.csv:reading=z;genotype=TNT:rank_rho_steps ~ .0f}} of the {{E76/axis_tests.csv:reading=z;genotype=TNT:n_splits ~ .0f}} splits, counted from the lowest, and the two recordings' own steps from the six agree with each other more than two recordings do in most splits (eleventh and twelfth rows; figure below). The same holds in baseline-noise units and with each recording's cosine corrected for trial-to-trial noise (by the correction then in use, which is too low in the level of the distances: [the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). The two are unusual in their level alone, and what makes them strong is the pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms, which blocking APL output brings far closer in them: the effect over those 15 pairs is {{E76/subset_floors.csv:unit=z;subset=two:ester ~ +.3f}} against the two and {{E76/subset_floors.csv:unit=z;subset=six:ester ~ +.3f}} against the six. Of what was looked at then, nothing recorded with the flies sets the two apart beforehand, neither the time since the toxin was induced nor the number of KCs. Within the session one thing does: the response rates of the other six run down over the three repeats and those of the two do not ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). The frame-by-frame traces have since added two things: the responses of the two decay about three times faster than those of every other recording, and the stimulus record of one of them says that APL was not labelled, so that whether the two were measured like the others is a question for the experimenter ([the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)). Until it is answered the mean over all eight stands as the target, with the six given beside it, and the failed test on split halves is as it was read, a half with both of the two recordings and a half with neither being different in level. The common error is not made by the two either: against the six alone it has the root mean square it has against all eight ({{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=six_z:rms ~ .3f}} and {{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=eight_z:rms ~ .3f}}) and the same sign in both groups of pairs, with about half of its part among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al gone ({{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=six_z:err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} against {{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=eight_z:err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}), and against the effect in baseline-noise units it is as large ({{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=eight_noise:rms ~ .3f}}).

src: **Realism.** The three fits are inside all four realism bands, as the two they start from are (last row). The fits to the effect in baseline-noise units paid for the larger mean in breadth with APL off. At an unchanged response rate with APL on, the family has more responses with APL off, so that the ratio of the two rates moves from near the flies' toward the upper end of the flies' interval and of the band (ninth row), and more of its KCs respond to eight or more odors with APL off, where it already had more than the flies (tenth row); the reference model's set does the same. In the family the distance of the odors-per-KC distribution from the flies' with APL off grows, and in both it stays well inside its band (eleventh row). KC–KC inhibition, which no band measures, falls to less than half in both. A fit held at the flies' ratio of response rates would likely end further from the flies' mean, so the shortfall given above is the least this family leaves open. The parts on the recordings change no model, and as everywhere the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

src: **What follows.** Which unit the flies' side of the main target is held to is a choice about its mean part, like the choice of the model's readout, and it is not yet made; the mean over all eight recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) stands in either unit. The pattern part and the order of the models on raw counts do not depend on the choice, so until it is made the families are ranked on the pattern part, and the mean part is given against both effects. If the target moves to baseline-noise units, the mean part is open again for every model, and more responses with APL off is a route that the fit has already taken, at a cost; what the flies have there and the models lack is responses that grow with a KC's breadth ([the per-KC normalization of the recordings](#per-kc-normalization)). Two later readings qualify this: weighting a fit's spike counts by the KC's breadth moves its mean effect by {{diff:E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p_is_flies=True;target=noise:mean -- E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p=0.0;target=noise:mean ~ +.3f}} at most, and the comparison of raw counts with the effect in baseline-noise units is one at the model's 0.5 s odor pulse, the same fit's mean effect on raw counts being {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} at the flies' 2 s pulse against {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)), and {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3;kernel=counts:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} there once the ceiling's adaptation outlasts the odor ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)). src: **About two fifths of the common error is within the reach of a change of the input.** A change of the input acts with APL on and with APL off alike: it moves a pair's distance in both conditions. If a model's distances with APL on follow from its distances with APL off by a relation of its own, such a change moves a pair along that relation, and the part of the error that it reaches in this way is the part that comes from where the model's distances with APL off differ from the flies'. The pattern error was therefore [split into three terms that add up to it](#fn-inherited-split): the inherited part, the error a model would have if it followed the flies' relation between the two conditions exactly, starting from its own distances with APL off; the difference between the model's relation and the flies'; and the two sides' pair-by-pair departures from their own relations, the block among them. For the mean over the eight wirings the inherited part is {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:share_inherited ~ .0%}} of the common error's squared sum, and {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z6;data_curve_fit=insample:share_inherited ~ .0%}} against the six recordings that are alike; with the flies' relation fitted on halves of the recordings it lies between {{E77/report_scalars.csv:inherited_halves_cal_q05:value ~ .0%}} and {{E77/report_scalars.csv:inherited_halves_cal_q95:value ~ .0%}}. The departures hold {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:share_pair_specific ~ .0%}}, and the difference between the two relations offsets a little ({{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:share_curve ~ +.2f}} as a share; the three add to one). Without its inherited part the pattern part of the mean over the eight wirings would be {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:pattern_rms_without_inherited ~ .3f}} in place of {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:pattern_rms ~ .3f}}. Most of the common error is thus in what APL does to particular pairs, which a change shared by the two conditions does not reach in this way. Read since from the flies' own responses, on the spike counts of the fits, this part is not in the form of APL's inhibition either: an inhibition that grows with an odor's response over all the KCs nearly gives the flies' effect when it is applied to the flies' responses without APL, and applied to the model's responses with APL off it gives no more than the model's own APL does. What the split assigns to particular pairs then lies, by that reading, in which KCs respond without APL and how strongly, which the distances with APL off do not show. It does not lie in how many KCs each odor recruits there alone: with that set to the flies' on four wirings the pattern part does not fall, and the same reading then puts a part of what is left on the side of the model's APL ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)). The split is not a bound on what a search can do on one wiring, as the last part of this subsection shows.

src: **Two descriptions of the common error came with the split.** Taken apart by odor ([above](#apl-effect-parts)), an odor's term in the common error, its share of the error on every pair it is in, follows how much more its response fraction grows in the model than in the flies when APL is removed: where the model gains more responses than the flies, its APL effect on the odor's pairs is too large. Across the 16 odors the two correlate at Pearson r {{E77/report_scalars.csv:per_odor_share_gain_corr_cal_z8:value ~ .2f}} against all eight recordings and {{E77/report_scalars.csv:per_odor_share_gain_corr_cal_z6:value ~ .2f}} against the six that are alike (the flies' responses counted by the recordings' own criterion), so this is a lead and not a result, and one that leans on the two strongest recordings; the per-odor part of an error is, besides, the part that the recordings pin down less firmly ([above](#apl-effect-parts)). And the model's antennal lobe evens out the odors' total drive: summed over the glomeruli, the model's PN rates lie between {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=B-myr:pn_sum ~ .0f}} and {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=2h:pn_sum ~ .0f}} Hz for the 16 odors, where the summed ORN responses run from {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=B-myr:orn_sum_pos ~ .0f}} Hz for B-myr to {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=1-6ol:orn_sum_pos ~ .0f}} Hz for 1-6ol.

src: **No handle on the input lowers the pattern part, and each would add to the common error.** Six handles that the model has on its input were screened on the fit at fixed settings: a weaker antennal-lobe normalization; other input for the weak odors with nothing fitted again; each odor's input compressed or expanded across glomeruli at an unchanged sum; a cap on each claw's input; a more equal weight for the glomeruli, by per-glomerulus drive normalization or by each glomerulus's number of claws; and bouton vesicle depletion. At every setting the somatic threshold and the APL scale were set again until the numbers of responses with APL off and with APL on were the fit's, with the breadth weights computed again for the changed input. Beside them ran two [oracle](#fn-oracle) emulations that act with APL on only, the run with APL off being the fit's own: APL's weight on each bouton, or on each claw, multiplied by a power of that bouton's or claw's own input to the odor. For each setting, the change it makes to the per-pair APL effect on the real wiring was also set against the common error: the transfer is the share of the common error's squared sum that the change would remove if it were the same on every wiring.

src: **Realism.** Every model of this subsection has the control flies' response rate with APL on, fitted or held, and the four columns of the first table are inside all four realism bands, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the bands count now, and by the recordings' own criterion, as they did until 2026-11-10 (lower rows). So are both searched inputs on each of the four wirings. Every setting of the screen is inside the four bands as they count now; counted by the recordings' own criterion, the two compressive exponents on the input, the lowest cap, the stronger of the two bouton emulations and the stronger depletion leave a band on the number of odors per KC, and no reading above rests on them. The searched inputs are oracle inputs, each glomerulus's response between half and twice the recorded one and many of them at those bounds, which no measurement supports and on which the two halves of the recordings do not agree. What the bands do not see is the fit's own and unchanged: the release through the many-claw KCs when APL is removed, a somatic threshold under half the baseline's and an APL→bouton scale near its bound ([above](#wiring-population)). Nothing here was bought with realism: at the size searched nothing was gained beyond one wiring, and the reduced inputs, read since on all eight wirings, are inside the four bands as well ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)). As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations), and Hallem's values are at ten times the concentration of the KC recordings for ms, paa and 1-8ol.

src: **What follows.** No draw of the wiring carries the common error, no amount of inhibition per odor ([above](#apl-effect-parts)), no fixed profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli of the kind tried ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), and now no handle on the input and no APL inhibition that grows with a bouton's or a claw's own input. In this family the common error as a whole is therefore not on the input side, as far as these handles and a search within a factor of two go, and it stays unexplained by the mechanisms the family has; the searched input, reduced, has since been found to remove a small part of it on wirings and recordings that it had not seen ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)), a part that its controls confirm and that a second split of the flies does not repeat ([the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input)). Most of it lies in the two sides' pair-by-pair departures from their own relations between the conditions, which a change acting through the distances that the conditions share does not reach. Of the changes to what reaches the KCs, one was not among the handles, a per-claw knee near the largest PN rate; it has been run since and does not carry the common error either ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)). What else is left lies outside what was screened: how APL's inhibition unfolds in time, differences between types of KCs, and inhibition that depends on the odor in another form (one such form, inhibition that follows the calyx space that glomeruli share, has since been tested as a proxy on the input, from connectome tables whose use is on hold, and its reading is withheld: [the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps), the next subsection; the length of the odor pulse, the types of KCs and changes that a long block could have left in the KCs have been run as well, and none of these carries the common error: [the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)). The two descriptions above go with them as leads, each odor's growth in responses when APL is removed and the evening-out of the odors' total drive in the model's antennal lobe, with the caution that weakening that normalization alone cost the pattern part. The evening-out has since been set against recordings of the PN dendrites, which do not show it, while the model's distances between odors at that stage are within 0.05 of the dendrites' once the noise between flies is removed ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)). The input has since been taken up again in that form, as a change fitted on several wirings at once and tested by whether two halves of the recordings give the same factors: they do not, and the fitted input does not hold on the half that it did not see (the same subsection). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

src: **APL's activity in the calyx, imaged for three odors, is reliable and for the most part one pattern that all odors share. The part that is an odor's own is smaller, repeats between presentations and varies over several micrometres, and pa's response lies lower in the image than ms's at equal strength. The maps of the model with local APL units are flatter and less alike between odors than the flies' at every coupling. Two further readings, of maps predicted from where the PN boutons lie in seven connectome calyces against the measured differences between odors, and of inhibition that follows each glomerulus's neighbourhood in the calyx against the common error, rest on connectome tables whose use is on hold, and are withheld until those tables are cleared or the readings are made again from other connectome outputs. A spatially local APL at the boutons has not been fitted.** [The input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side) left the common error unexplained by the mechanisms that the best family has, and all of them treat APL as one cell that inhibits the whole calyx alike. An APL that acts locally would be a mechanism of another kind: glomeruli whose PN boutons lie in the same part of the calyx would be inhibited together, and of the six odors among which the model's APL effect is too small, the five esters (2h, IaA, pa, eb and ep) have strongly driven glomeruli in common. Local APL units had been tried early, on a model without the later mechanisms, and had left the KCs' odor-odor distances where a single APL puts them (among what did not matter, further up), with nothing measured to say how local APL is. The APL calyx maps against the connectome took that measurement from Yang's calcium imaging of APL itself and asked two things of it without fitting a model, both fixed beforehand: whether maps of APL's activity predicted from the wiring match the measured ones, and whether the nearness of glomeruli in the calyx predicts the common error on odors it was not fitted to, by removing 15 % or more of its squared sum and more than permuted glomerulus labels remove. Only with both was a spatially local APL to be fitted in the best family.

src: **One pattern shared by all odors, and a smaller part that is each odor's own.** The maps are reliable: the two presentations of a stimulus correlate, pixel by pixel inside the outline, at Pearson r {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:repeat_r_top_median ~ .2f}} (the median over recordings at each odor's highest concentration; {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=all_pfo:repeat_r_top_median ~ .2f}} and {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=first_in_block:repeat_r_top_median ~ .2f}} with two other ways of taking the baseline from the solvent presentations). Maps of different odors are almost as alike, at {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:different_odor_r_top_median ~ .2f}}, though not in every fly: in {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:n_recordings_ms_vs_pa_top_below_0p8 ~ .0f}} of the {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:n_recordings ~ .0f}} recordings the maps of ms and pa correlate below 0.8. Most of a recording is one spatial pattern common to all its stimuli. The first singular vector of its matrix of stimuli by pixels holds {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means kept;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} of the summed squares at the finest smoothing (2 pixels) and {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=20.0;mode=means kept;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} at the coarsest (20 pixels), and {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means removed;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} and {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=20.0;mode=means removed;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} when each map's mean is removed first, so that shapes alone are compared (medians over recordings; left column of the figure). What is left of a map without that pattern, the remainder (the residual of the figure), is what is specific to a stimulus, and it is not noise. It repeats between the two presentations at every smoothing (second column), and the remainders of the two presentations stay correlated over {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means kept;column=resid_crossrep_len:measured_all_median_px ~ .0f}} pixels, {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means kept;column=resid_crossrep_len:measured_all_median ~ .1f}} µm at the assumed pixel size (right column): an odor's own part of APL's activity varies over several micrometres, a small fraction of the calyx. The two presentations of a stimulus lay in one block, so that these maps could not say whether that part belongs to the odor or to the block. A later series with three vials of one odor in separate blocks says that it is the odor's: what repeats within a block returns with another vial of the same odor and not with another odor ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out)).

src: At every coupling the model's maps are less alike between odors than the flies' and far more even over the calyx (first and third rows): in the flies the odors share most of a map that varies strongly from place to place, and in the model each odor has a weak pattern of its own on a nearly even ground. Coupling the units evens the maps out further without making them more alike, and only the distance over which an odor's own part varies is near the measured one. Part of the flies' shared pattern may be anatomy, the density of APL's neurites in the imaged plane, which unit potentials do not have, and pa was imaged more than one log unit below the model's pa. If local units are taken up again, how uneven a map is and how alike two odors' maps are is what their coupling would be set by.

src: What was asked stands, and is described here as the plan of the two readings ([how the maps were predicted and both tests scored](#fn-calyx-maps)). For the first question, a map of APL's activity is predicted for an odor from every PN bouton of a calyx at its position, weighted by its number of release sites and by the PN rate of its glomerulus in the breadth-2 APL-effect fit, and the predicted differences between odors, pa minus ms and paa minus ms at matched strength, are set against the measured ones. The null is the same procedure with the glomerulus labels of the PN rates permuted, and because the orientation and the depth of the images were not known when the test was made, every orientation and depth is scored, for the prediction and for the permutations alike. Any reading of this question carries two limits of the input: every pa map was imaged more than one log unit below the pa of the model's input (10^-4.4 and lower against 10^-3), outside the one log unit within which data at another concentration stand in on this page ([footnote](#fn-concentrations)), and paa's PN rates come from ORN data at 10^-4, the substitute used throughout. For the second question, which does not need the maps, a proxy on the model's PN rates, without simulation, inhibits each glomerulus in proportion to the activity near its own boutons, the rates of all glomeruli weighted by their co-localization with it, instead of in proportion to the odor's mean rate, as an APL that acts on the whole calyx would inhibit it. The change that this makes in the 120 pairs' input distances is scaled to the common error on the pairs of 15 odors and scored on the 15 pairs of the odor left out, against the same with the glomeruli permuted.

src: **Under the readout the pulse does not matter; on raw counts it does.** Through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) the breadth-2 fit's loss at the flies' pulse is within {{diff:E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held:cal_loss -- E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse0.5_fixed:cal_loss ~ .3f}} of its loss at 0.5 s, less than one draw of the wiring moves it ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}), with the mean effect still near the flies' and the pattern part where it was (first three rows, second values). On raw counts the mean effect falls with each lengthening of the pulse, to half at 2 s, and the loss rises by more than half (first values). A longer pulse had been expected to raise the mean effect on raw counts; it lowers it because of when the model's KCs fire. With APL on nearly all spikes of the 2 s pulse fall in its first 0.5 s, and with APL off a third come later (sixth row): the model's APL all but silences the response that outlasts the onset. The late spikes with APL off come from few KCs, with patterns further apart between odors than the onset's (a mean distance of {{E80/pulse_windows.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;window=0.5-1:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}} in the second half second against {{E80/pulse_windows.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;window=0-0.5:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}} in the first). They raise the distances with APL off toward those with APL on, which hardly move (fifth row), so the effect shrinks; the readout's saturation removes most of what the late spikes add to a KC's count, which is why its numbers hold. In the family with the firing ceiling the adaptation cuts the late spikes with APL off as well, and the mean effect falls less; but there the readout has nothing left to compress, so the one number that both definitions give rises with the pulse, to about the breadth-2 fit's loss under the readout (last two columns). All of this is at parameters fitted with the 0.5 s pulse: what shapes a sustained response in the model (the adaptation of the PNs, KC–KC inhibition, APL) had not been fitted at 2 s (both families have been since: [the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)), and with APL on the response after the first half second is too sparse for a per-pair APL effect of its own ({{E80/pulse_windows.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;window=0.5-1:n_pairs_defined ~ .0f}} of the 120 pairs are defined in the second half second).

src: **A per-claw knee near the largest PN rate holds the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input apart, as the flies' KCs do, only when a claw passes nothing below it. That hard knee leaves ms and B-myr without responses and about doubles the pattern part of the APL-effect loss. As soon as a claw passes a tenth of its input below the knee, the gain on those pairs is gone, and a knee set relative to each odor's strongest input does not reach them either. The per-claw transfer is therefore closed for the best family on the main target. What the hard knee does bring toward the flies is which KCs are released when APL is removed.** Six of the 120 odor pairs have nearly the same ORN input, a distance between the two odors' ORN responses below 0.25: eb with ep, 6al with t2h, IaA with pa, 2h with pa, 1-5ol with 1-6ol and 2h with IaA, none of them with an odor at a substituted ORN concentration. The flies' KCs hold these pairs apart, and more so with APL than without. The breadth-2 APL-effect fit separates them less in both conditions and has about half the flies' APL effect on them, the mean of the per-pair APL effect over the six (the KC data and the first model column of the table below). Four of the six are among the esters, where the common error has the model's APL effect too small. On the bouton model without the later mechanisms, what holds these pairs apart is a per-claw knee near the top of the PN rates, which in the model reach {{E78/partA_scored.csv:thr130_rate0.068_aplboth_k2:top_pn_rate ~ .0f}} Hz: a knee at 130 Hz with nothing passed below it takes the six pairs' APL effect on raw counts from {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr130:base_raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr130:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}}, where knees at 40 to 100 Hz leave it between {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr100:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} and {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr70:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}}, and it leaves 1-8ol, ms and B-myr without a responding KC. With such a knee the somatic threshold falls and a KC responds through the one or two claws that sit on an odor's strongest boutons: the responders are selected at the claw and no longer at the soma. The high per-claw knee without a dead zone asked whether that selection holds the six pairs apart in the best family without silencing the weak odors, once the knee has no dead zone, the range of input below it that counts for nothing: a claw then passes a fraction of its input below the knee (the reduced slope that had been tried below the 70 Hz threshold of the early models, further up). The other form tried is a knee set relative to each odor's strongest input.

src: **With any input passed below the knee the gain on the six pairs is gone.** With a tenth of a claw's input passed below the knee, the six pairs' APL effect is below the fit's at every knee ({{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee100_g0.1:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}}, {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee115_g0.1:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} and {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.1:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} at 100, 115 and 130 Hz), and it stays below it with a quarter and with half. The ester group's error is still more than halved with a tenth passed, at losses of {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.1:cal_loss ~ .3f}} to {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee100_g0.1:cal_loss ~ .3f}}, and returns to the fit's as the fraction grows. What comes back with the fraction passed is the fit itself. With half passed below 130 Hz, the setting with the lowest loss, the ester group's error and the weak odors' response fractions are nearly the fit's and the loss is {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.5:cal_loss ~ .3f}} against the fit's {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:cal_loss ~ .3f}}, still above the {{E78/gate.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.5:loss_limit ~ .3f}} that had been set (second model column). Softening the knee changes little. The five settings nearest the fit were repeated on the same family with the firing ceiling at its literature setting and on a re-drawn wiring (claw permutation P1), each at its own fit. With the ceiling the six pairs' effect moves by {{E78/gate.csv:fit1_pp_knee100_g0.5:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}} to {{E78/gate.csv:fit1_pp_knee115_g0.5_w15:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}}; on the re-drawn wiring it moves by {{E78/gate.csv:P1_pp_knee100_g0.5:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}} to {{E78/gate.csv:P1_pp_knee115_g0.5_w15:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}}, and the ester group's error is further from zero at each of the five. A knee at half of each odor's largest bouton rate keeps the mean APL effect and has the highest response rate ρ of all the settings, but it leaves the six pairs' effect where the fit has it, doubles the alcohol group's error and raises the pattern part by half (fourth model column). Set higher it cannot hold the response rates: at 0.7 of the largest bouton rate the response rate with APL off stops at {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_rel0.7:ratio ~ .2f}} times that with APL on, outside the band on the ratio, and at 0.85 no somatic threshold gives the fit's responses. No setting did what had been set beforehand, on any of the three fits, so no fit of a knee without a dead zone followed.

src: **Without the trial noise the six pairs are short by as much.** The table sets a model without noise against recordings that have it. With [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) put into the fit (the noise matched to the control flies), the distances of both sides can be estimated without their noise from single trials: one minus the cosine between trials of the two odors from different repeats, divided by the cosine between trials of one odor across the same repeats, which assumes only that the noise of different repeats is independent. By that estimate the fit has the six pairs at {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_noise_free_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_noise_free_off ~ .3f}} with APL off, an APL effect of {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_effect_noise_free ~ +.3f}}, and the flies at {{data:noise_free_six_ctrl ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_free_six_tnt ~ .3f}}, an effect of {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six ~ +.3f}} (90 % interval {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.lo ~ +.3f}} to {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.hi ~ +.3f}}). The fit thus has about half the flies' APL effect on these pairs with or without the noise, and the larger shortfall is in their distance with APL on. The correction for trial-to-trial noise that this page used until then is not the one to read the model's six pairs by, nor the flies' ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). It assumes that the noise of two odors is independent, and in the recordings and in the model's trial noise alike two odors of one repeat are more alike than across repeats; applied to the fit's trials it puts the six pairs at {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_corrected_on ~ .3f}} and {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_corrected_off ~ .3f}}, as if they were one odor, which is not what the model does.

src: **What follows.** The per-claw transfer is closed for this family on the main target. It had been closed for recruiting the weak odors (the section on the weak-input odors, further up), and a knee near the top of the PN rates does not lower the APL-effect loss in any form: as a hard knee it trades the ester group's error for the alcohol group's and for silent odors, and with input passed below it, or set relative to the odor, it does nothing for the six pairs. Those pairs stay a target of their own, at about half the flies' APL effect and short mostly with APL on. What holds them apart in the flies is then not a transfer of this kind at the claw, nor a fixed change of the input ([above](#input-side)), nor the differences between flies in what reaches the KCs, which move these pairs apart with APL on and with APL off alike ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)); for inhibition that follows the calyx space that glomeruli share, the reading made with a static proxy is withheld with the connectome tables that it rests on ([above](#apl-calyx-maps)). Read since against recordings of the stages before the somata, these pairs are the one case in which the model's step from claws to somata with APL on is too small in every reading, which keeps their shortfall where it had been placed ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)). What the hard knee did for the release with APL off is kept as a lead: whether responders can be selected at the claw without a dead zone that silences the weak odors is open. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

src: **In the recordings, two different odors presented in the same repeat of the panel are more alike than the same two odors in different repeats: part of the flies' trial-to-trial variability is shared by the odors of a repeat, and that part is nearly three times larger with APL output blocked (TNT) than in control flies. About three quarters of it follows the time between the two presentations, mostly a slow drift over the session, and the rest is tied to the repeat itself; neither the per-pair APL effect nor the error common to all wirings follows the order in which the odors were presented. Responses also run down over the session, faster in control flies, so that the ratio of the two response rates rises from the first repeat to the third. The correction for trial-to-trial noise that this page had used takes the noise of two odors to be independent, and it put the distances without noise too low; an estimate that needs only independence between repeats replaces it. The main target, the effect as measured, is not touched: the saved models keep their order against the effect without the noise, and the error common to all wirings is there from the first repeat. The model's trial noise has the wrong make-up, all of it shared between the odors of a trial, but set to the flies' shares it leaves the populations of wirings where they stood, and the firing ceiling's standing with them. What the model does not make is the asymmetry: its odors of one trial are hardly more alike with APL off than with APL on.** Every comparison of a model with the KC data as the data are made passes the model through [trial-to-trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) calibrated on one number, how far apart two presentations of one odor are, and every level quoted without the trial noise came from a correction that takes the noise of different odors to be independent. Each recording holds three repeats of the panel, so both can be checked against the flies. The flies' variability across the three repeats did that from the per-trial responses of the {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} control recordings and the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} with APL output blocked (TNT), with 90 % intervals from resampling the recordings. It then scored the saved models against the effect without the noise and read the best families again through a noise with the flies' make-up. No model was fitted.

src: **The odors of one repeat share part of their variability, and more of it with APL output blocked.** The same-repeat gap is the distance between two different odors presented in different repeats minus the distance between the same two odors presented in the same repeat, both between single trials. If the variability of two odors' responses were independent it would be zero. It is positive in every recording, {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl ~ .1f}} times larger with APL output blocked (TNT) than in control flies (90 % interval {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl.lo ~ .1f}} to {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl.hi ~ .1f}}), and largest over the six pairs with near-identical ORN input (table below). The size of the responses does not make it: with every entry reduced to responding or not, the gap is about the same. Of the trial-to-trial variance of a responding KC's response, the part common to that KC's odors within a repeat is {{E81/variance_parts.csv:units=z;genotype=TNT3c;level=genotype;cls=responders;statistic=share_shared:value ~ .0%}} in control flies and {{E81/variance_parts.csv:units=z;genotype=TNT;level=genotype;cls=responders;statistic=share_shared:value ~ .0%}} with APL output blocked (TNT). The variability also has a slow part: two presentations of one odor are further apart between the first and the third repeat than between adjacent repeats.

src: **Most of what the odors of a repeat share follows the time between presentations, and the order of the odors does not make the target.** A repeat is one block of the session in which every odor is presented once, so two odors of one repeat are also closer in time than two odors of different repeats, and the order of the presentations tells the two apart: {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=TNT3c;statistic=separation_share:value ~ .0%}} of the same-repeat gap in control flies and {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=TNT;statistic=separation_share:value ~ .0%}} with APL output blocked (TNT) follows how many presentations apart the two were, and the rest is a step for the same repeat at equal separation (the two rows under the gap in the table above). Most of the first part is a slow drift over the session, two presentations growing less alike with the time between them up to the first repeat against the third (figure below), and both parts are larger with APL output blocked (TNT), by {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=ratio;statistic=separation_part:value ~ .1f}} and {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=ratio;statistic=block_part:value ~ .1f}} times. Across the 120 pairs neither the per-pair APL effect nor the error common to all wirings (under the calibrated readout) follows how far apart the two odors of a pair were presented: their Spearman correlations with the pair's mean separation within a repeat, control flies minus APL output blocked (TNT), are {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_effect_sep_diff:value ~ .2f}} and {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal_sep_diff:value ~ .2f}}, where 90 % of orders drawn at random with the same reuse of orders give {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_effect_sep_diff:null_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_effect_sep_diff:null_hi ~ .2f}} and {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal_sep_diff:null_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal_sep_diff:null_hi ~ .2f}} (the strongest of the twelve such correlations, with the error also on raw counts and the separation also in each genotype alone and in all recordings, is {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_raw_sep_tnt:value ~ .2f}}, at p = {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_raw_sep_tnt:p_null ~ .2f}}, which the strongest of twelve often reaches by chance). The shift of the per-pair effect that the separations predict has a root mean square of {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=confound_rms:value ~ .3f}}, against {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} for the floor of the loss. The re-specified noise of the models (below) was matched to the gap as a whole, a jitter per repeat standing in for the drift, so what is concluded below about the models' noise stands.

src: **The ceiling costs what the readout costs, and it does not change which KCs respond.** In the breadth-2 family the block falls to about two thirds of the flies' at the literature setting and a third at the stronger one, and the reference model's is all but gone; the natural-source alignment with APL on falls at the stronger setting, and the mean distances fall below the flies' in both conditions. The APL-effect loss scores none of these, and the calibrated readout costs the same, as expected if the two do the same job: on raw counts the block and the alignment were carried by the strong responders ([the high-firing KCs that survive APL](#high-firing-kcs)).

src: **With the flies' shares in the model's noise, the populations of wirings stay where they stood.** The trial noise put into the models is one draw per KC and trial, applied to the KC's threshold for all odors of the trial, so all of it is of the shared kind. At the level that matches the flies' distance between two presentations of one odor, the breadth-2 APL-effect fit has a same-repeat gap of {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;condition=both:gap_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;condition=both:gap_off ~ .3f}} with APL off, where the flies have {{data:repeat_gap_ctrl ~ .3f}} and {{data:repeat_gap_tnt ~ .3f}}. The noise was therefore re-specified with the flies' two shares. The shared jitter was lowered to the level at which the model's same-repeat gap is the flies' (for that fit a standard deviation of {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=on:sigma ~ .3f}} of the threshold with APL on and {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:sigma ~ .3f}} with APL off, against {{E81/jitter_at_flies_gap.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:sigma_matched_on ~ .3f}} in the pipeline), by interpolation between saved runs of the pipeline without noise, at half its matched jitter and at the matched level, and a factor drawn independently for every KC, odor and trial was added until the distance between two presentations of one odor was the flies' as well. The two populations of four wirings that had been read through the pipeline, the breadth-2 family without and with the firing ceiling at its literature setting ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), were scored again through this noise.

src: **What the model does not make.** Two features of the flies' variability are in the model under no noise that was tried. The first is the asymmetry between the conditions. In the flies the same-repeat gap is {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl ~ .1f}} times larger with APL output blocked (TNT). In the model, a jitter per KC gives a gap with APL off that is {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;condition=both:gap_ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} times the gap with APL on for the breadth-2 fit and {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=F1;condition=both:gap_ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} times for the fit with the ceiling, and the re-specified noise reaches the flies' two gaps only by taking a larger jitter with APL off than with APL on. A slow change of the whole population does not make the asymmetry either. A factor on every KC's threshold of 0.8, 1 and 1.2 in three successive trials, a wider swing than the flies' run-down amounts to (for the fit with the ceiling the control flies' run-down corresponds to a threshold that rises by a factor of {{E81/rundown_axes.csv:unit=z;experiment=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;repeat=0:thr_change_first_to_last ~ .2f}} from the first repeat to the third), leaves a same-repeat gap of {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;triplet=0.8/1/1.2;readout=raw;condition=on:gap ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;triplet=0.8/1/1.2;readout=raw;condition=acute_off:gap ~ .3f}} with APL off in the breadth-2 fit. The second is how alike the responders of one repeat are with APL off. With every entry reduced to responding or not, the same-repeat gap with APL off is {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit and {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=F1;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} for the fit with the ceiling through the re-specified noise, against the flies' {{data:repeat_gap_binary_tnt ~ .3f}}, and the same with the jitter per presentation ({{E81/per_presentation_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} and {{E81/per_presentation_checks.csv:model=F1;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}}); with APL on it is close to the flies' ({{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=on:bin_gap ~ .3f}} against {{data:repeat_gap_binary_ctrl ~ .3f}}). The shortfall is thus a property of which KCs the model has responding with APL off and not of how the noise is drawn: the flies' larger shared variability with APL output blocked (TNT) has no counterpart in the model.

A factor on every KC's threshold of 0.8, 1 and 1.2 in three successive trials, a wider swing than the flies' run-down amounts to (for the fit with the ceiling the control flies' run-down corresponds to a threshold that rises by a factor of {{E81/rundown_axes.csv:unit=z;experiment=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;repeat=0:thr_change_first_to_last ~ .2f}} from the first repeat to the third), leaves a same-repeat gap of {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;triplet=0.8/1/1.2;readout=raw;condition=on:gap ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;triplet=0.8/1/1.2;readout=raw;condition=acute_off:gap ~ .3f}} with APL off in the breadth-2 fit. The second is how alike the responders of one repeat are with APL off. With every entry reduced to responding or not, the same-repeat gap with APL off is {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit and {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=F1;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} for the fit with the ceiling through the re-specified noise, against the flies' {{data:repeat_gap_binary_tnt ~ .3f}}, and the same with the jitter per presentation ({{E81/per_presentation_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} and {{E81/per_presentation_checks.csv:model=F1;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}}); with APL on it is close to the flies' ({{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=on:bin_gap ~ .3f}} against {{data:repeat_gap_binary_ctrl ~ .3f}}). The shortfall is thus a property of which KCs the model has responding with APL off and not of how the noise is drawn: the flies' larger shared variability with APL output blocked (TNT) has no counterpart in the model.

src: **The effect is there from the first second, and it falls through the response.** Without the trial noise the mean APL effect over the 120 pairs is {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} over the 2 s pulse, {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=target;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} in the target's window and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=4-8.1;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} in the second part of that window, from 4 s on (third row of the table for the windows one by one). The pulse exceeds the second part of the window by {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:value ~ +.3f}} ({{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:lo_rec ~ +.3f}} to {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:hi_rec ~ +.3f}}; {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:lo_fly ~ +.3f}} to {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:hi_fly ~ +.3f}} when flies are resampled in place of recordings), and past the window the effect goes on falling. What changes is the distances with APL output blocked: there the odors start more alike than they end, their mean distance rising through the window and past it, while the control flies' rises little after the third second (first row). The effect is thus not something that a slow signal gathers; it is in the first frames of the response. Its pattern across the pairs is the target's from the second second on and least so in the first (sixth row). In baseline-noise units the fall from the pulse to the second part of the window is smaller ({{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=noise;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:value ~ +.3f}}, {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=noise;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:lo_rec ~ +.3f}} to {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=noise;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean_minus_late:hi_rec ~ +.3f}}). It is there in the six recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) that are alike and in the two strongest, each set against the control flies: {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=six_typical;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}}, {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=six_typical;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=2-4;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=six_typical;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=4-8.1;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} over the pulse, from 2 to 4 s and from 4 to 8 s with the six, and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=two_strongest;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}}, {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=two_strongest;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=2-4;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=two_strongest;units=z;estimator=noise_free;window=4-8.1;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} with the two, so that no window makes the two like the six. For the main target the window is therefore a choice on the data's side that moves the mean part and not the pattern. As measured, the mean effect is {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=measured;window=pulse;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} over the pulse, {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} in the target's window and {{E84/effect_by_window.csv:subset=all;units=z;estimator=measured;window=4-8.1;statistic=effect_mean:value ~ +.3f}} in its second part, so a model scored against the pulse would be asked for a larger mean effect still. The saved models keep their order: scored against the effect of the pulse and against that of the second part of the window, the losses of the {{E84/variants_by_window_summary.csv:estimator=measured;window=pulse:n_variants ~ .0f}} saved models have Spearman correlations of {{E84/variants_by_window_summary.csv:estimator=measured;window=pulse:rho_with_present ~ .3f}} and {{E84/variants_by_window_summary.csv:estimator=measured;window=4-8.1:rho_with_present ~ .3f}} with their losses against the target.

src: **The indicator is slow.** The mean trace of the responding KC × odor entries, chosen on two repeats and averaged on the third, peaks {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=peak_t:others_min ~ .1f}} to {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=peak_t:others_max ~ .1f}} s after the odor's onset in every recording but the two taken up below, more than a second after the pulse has ended, and when the target's window ends it is still at {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=v8.1_over_peak:others_min ~ .2f}} to {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=v8.1_over_peak:others_max ~ .2f}} of its peak (figure, left; table below). A kernel for the indicator's response to a single spike, a rise with one time constant times a decay with another, was fitted to the control flies' trace under two limits of the firing, between which the KCs' firing lies. If the KCs fire in a burst at the odor's onset, the rise is {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=onset:rise ~ .2f}} s and the decay {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=onset:decay ~ .1f}} s (the onset-burst kernel). If they fire evenly through the pulse, the decay is {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=steady:decay ~ .1f}} s and the rise goes to the lower bound of the fit, the pulse making the rise of the trace (the steady-drive kernel). The first fits better, with a root mean square misfit of {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=onset:rms ~ .3f}} against {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=steady:rms ~ .3f}} of a KC's baseline noise, and on synthetic traces with the recordings' volume rate and noise the fit tells firing that lasts 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 s apart in every draw. But the fitted rise shortens as the firing is taken to last longer, so that what the traces leave open is the form of the kernel between the two limits, and both are carried below. Either way the decay is several times the 3 s that the reading of the models as the flies were recorded had assumed, and four times the slowest that it read beside it. The control flies' responses also shorten as they run down over the session ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)): from the first repeat to the third the peak of their responders' trace falls from {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=by_repeat;genotype=TNT3c;repeat=1.0:peak_mean ~ .2f}} to {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=by_repeat;genotype=TNT3c;repeat=3.0:peak_mean ~ .2f}} times the baseline noise, and its mean signal from 4 to 8 s over its mean signal during the pulse from {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=by_repeat;genotype=TNT3c;repeat=1.0:late_over_early_mean ~ .2f}} to {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=by_repeat;genotype=TNT3c;repeat=3.0:late_over_early_mean ~ .2f}}.

src: **The two strongest recordings were not measured like the others.** The two recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) whose distances stand apart from the other six ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)), those of 2024-07-17 (fly 3) and of 2024-07-25 (fly 1), also stand apart in time. Their responders' traces peak about a second earlier and decay about three times faster than those of every other recording, with time constants of {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=decay_tau_from_8.1:strong_2024-07-17_fly_3_L ~ .1f}} and {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=decay_tau_from_8.1:strong_2024-07-25_fly_1_L ~ .1f}} s after the window where the others have {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=decay_tau_from_8.1:others_min ~ .1f}} to {{E84/kinetics_relations.csv:selection=resp;measure=decay_tau_from_8.1:others_max ~ .1f}} s (table of the traces' shape above; figure, left). On seven of the eight measures of the trace's shape both lie outside the range of all the other recordings, the control flies' included, and on the eighth, the time to half the peak, one of them does. They stay outside when the responses compared are matched in amplitude, and no measure follows how bright a recording is or how noisy its baseline. In the pattern of their distances the two had been found stronger and not different; in the time course of their responses they are different, in a way that the size of a response does not explain. Something in how these two were prepared or imaged differs from the rest, and the recordings' own records name one thing, for one of them: the stimulus record of the recording of 2024-07-17 says that APL was not labelled, which no other recording of the dataset with APL output blocked (TNT) says. src: **Searched on four wirings and one half of the recordings at once, neither a profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli nor an input changed glomerulus by glomerulus for each odor passes the test set for it on four other wirings and the other half of the recordings. The profile carries a small part of its gain there, with a higher loss on raw counts and a smaller mean effect. The input search fits the half of the recordings it was run against, on wirings it never saw as well, and gains nothing against the other half. One change does hold on both, by a little more than the test asks: the input that had been searched on the real wiring alone, reduced to 0.6 of its size. It was read here without its control. The control and a replication of its search have been run since: the controls hold, and the input carries a part of the common error that is smaller than the test asks ([the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input), the next subsection).** [The glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile) and [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side) had each found, on the real wiring, a change that lowers the pattern part of the APL-effect loss there, and neither change had been shown to hold beyond that wiring. Both kinds were therefore searched in simulation on four wirings at once (the real one, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle), for the lowest pattern part of the mean over the four against one half of the recordings, once against each half: the 36 scores of a glomerulus profile at the cell site (a KC's APL weight multiplied once for each claw it has from a glomerulus), and, one odor after the other for the ten odors of the earlier search, a factor between one half and two on each glomerulus's ORN response. Every wiring is at its own breadth-2 APL-effect fit ([above](#wiring-population)), the halves are those of the earlier search, split by fly with the two strongest recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) apart, and at every reading both response rates were set again. The test was fixed before any run. It is read on the mean over the four other wirings (two claw permutations and two matched shuffles), with each change at 0.6 of its size (its scores, or the logarithms of its factors, multiplied by 0.6), the share of one half's pattern that the other half reproduces. Through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), the pattern part against the half that a search had not seen had to fall by 0.003 or more for both halves' changes, and on six or more of the eight single wirings and halves; the loss on raw counts could rise by no more than 0.005, with the mean effect within 0.01 of the flies' and every point inside the realism bands; and the squared pattern error against all recordings had to fall by 15 % in the mean of the two halves' changes, and by half that against the six recordings that are alike. A change that got that far was to be set against the same scores or factors permuted across the glomeruli. Before the searches, the changes that existed were read where they had never been run: the profiles of the earlier experiment on the seven re-drawn wirings, and the two inputs searched on the real wiring on the four held-out wirings, whole and at 0.6 of their size.

src: **The input searched on the real wiring alone holds on both once it is reduced.** Whole, the two inputs of the earlier search gain {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=A;size=1.0;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=B;size=1.0;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} on the held-out wirings' pattern part against the half they did not see (the unchanged fits minus the change): nothing, as that experiment had found on the re-drawn wirings it read ([above](#input-side)). At 0.6 of their size they lower it by {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=A;size=0.6;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=B;size=0.6;unit=T;against=unseen:gain ~ .4f}} (last column), on as many of the single wirings and halves as the test asks, with a loss on raw counts below the unchanged fits', the flies' mean effect, and more of the squared pattern error removed than the test asks, against all recordings and against the six that are alike. The search had overshot: its input points the way that wirings and recordings it never saw ask, and goes too far. Read with the test's thresholds, the reduced input meets every part that was read. It was not one of the two changes that the test was set for, so the control with its factors permuted was not run on it here, and with two inputs chance was not excluded. Both have been taken up since: the controls hold, a second draw of the search carries as much, and a search on a second split of the flies does not ([the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input), the next subsection). Nor is it understood why a search on one wiring gives an input that holds when reduced and the same search on four wirings does not, the two having taken the half they were run against about equally far; only 0.6 and the whole were read, and 0.6, fixed beforehand, may be too large for the inputs searched on four wirings. What the reduced input removes is small beside what is left: against all recordings, one half of which each input has seen, the held-out wirings' pattern part falls from {{E83/readings.csv:change=none;unit=T;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=A;size=0.6;unit=T;against=all:changed ~ .3f}} and {{E83/two_by_two_A2.csv:searched_on=B;size=0.6;unit=T;against=all:changed ~ .3f}}, where the floor is {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}.

src: **The reduced searched input carries a small part of the error common to all wirings, about half of what the test set for it asks, and at no cost elsewhere. Its controls hold: on four wirings and the half of the recordings that its search never saw, the same factors permuted across each odor's glomeruli gain nothing on average and the factors inverted lose, so the gain depends on which glomerulus is given which factor. A second draw of the search against the same halves of the recordings carries as much as the first, so the input was not the lucky draw of a short search. A search on a second split of the flies does not: one of its two inputs gains and the other loses. What a fitted input can be shown to carry thus depends on how the recordings are split, and it is the recordings, not the wirings or the search, that set the limit. What the input is has been read from the six inputs that the search has now given. They move the same odor pairs, the way the recordings ask, and hardly agree on the glomeruli. A few changes of a single glomerulus's response do recur in all six, more of them than chance gives, and are named as a list that a measurement could test, VM7d's response to eb, DM5's to 1-8ol and DM4's to ep lowered, DM1's to IaA raised and DP1m's lowered for ms, 6al and 2h first among them. Each is about as large as the difference between two ORN flies, and no data on hand show it to be what reaches the KCs of the recorded flies.** [The input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit) left one change that held where it had not been fitted: the input searched on the real wiring alone ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)), at 0.6 of its size. It had been read without the control that the test keeps for a change that gets that far, and it was the better pair of four fitted inputs. Everything here is read as there: the mean over the four held-out wirings, each at its own breadth-2 APL-effect fit, every input at 0.6 of its size with both response rates set again, through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout). An input's gain is the pattern part of the APL-effect loss of the unchanged fits minus that with the input, against the half of the recordings that its search did not see. The input has two controls: each odor's factors permuted across its 36 glomeruli (four permutations of each half's input), and the factors inverted, each glomerulus's response divided where the search had multiplied it. And the search was run again on the real wiring: a second draw of its random steps against the same two halves, and once against each half of a second split of the flies, which keeps the two strongest recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) apart as the first does and has {{lit:four # recording_halves(0) against recording_halves(1) in experiments/E77_input_side_common_error.py: the second split's first half holds 8 of the 11 recordings of the first split's second half and 1 of the 8 of its first half, and its second half 7 of those 8 and 3 of the 11, so 4 of the 19 recordings (2 of control flies, 2 with APL output blocked) are on the other side}} of the recordings on the other side. What would count was fixed before any run. The controls hold if no permuted input gains as much as the input, the first two of the four less than half of it and the four less than a quarter of it on average, and if the inverted input gains nothing. The input passes if, in addition, the earlier test holds on the mean over the two splits (a gain of 0.003, 12 of the 16 single wirings and halves lower, and its limits on the loss on raw counts, the mean effect, the realism bands and the squared pattern error) and the four new inputs gain 0.002 on average with at least three gaining. It carries a part, short of a pass, if they gain 0.001 on average with at least three gaining, and it falls otherwise. If the input passed or carried a part, what it is was to be read from the six inputs that the search had then given on the real wiring, two draws against each half of the first split and one against each half of the second: each on the seven re-drawn wirings, on none of which a search was run; their agreement with one another, in the pairs they move and in their factors; where the new ones lie in the spread between the ORN flies and against Hallem's receptor data, as the earlier ones had been set ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)); and the entries that recur. An entry is one glomerulus's response to one odor, 360 of them for the ten odors searched. Those that at least five of the six inputs change in the same direction, and in the mean of the six by more than half of what the search allows on a log scale, were to be named as a list that a measurement could test if there were ten or more of them; with fewer, the input was to stay described by the pairs it moves.

src: **The input averaged over the ORN flies is a fair stand-in, on the main target, for the inputs of the flies behind the KC data. With each of nine ORN flies' own input on each of the eight wirings, the mean over the 72 model flies has the pattern part of the APL-effect loss that the eight wirings have at the averaged input, and the flies' mean effect as before. Neither bound on how much of the spread between the ORN recordings is the flies' own changes this, nor does a control with each fly's deviations shuffled, nor letting the response rates differ between model flies. Both distance matrices move a little toward the flies', and the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input move apart with APL on and with APL off alike, so that their APL effect stays at half the flies'. What the input flies add is spread: single model flies then differ from one another about as much as single recordings do.** Every model above takes as its input the average over the ORN flies of each glomerulus's response to each odor, the lab's input of the earlier subsections, while the KC data are averages over recordings of distances computed within a fly, and each of those flies had its own input. [The APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population) made the wiring a population of flies and left the input one averaged fly. The ORN input as a population of flies gave the input its flies as well. Its main reading fits nothing to the KC data, so what limited [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit), that a fitted change is confirmed only in small part by recordings it has not seen, does not limit this reading.

src: The flies are those of the megamat ORN recordings: nine flies, three trials per odor, the 12 odors of that panel, and {{E85/flies.csv:fly=f1:n_gloms ~ .0f}} to {{E85/flies.csv:fly=f0:n_gloms ~ .0f}} of the model's 36 glomeruli in each fly. No fly has the averaged input: across the flies a response differs from the average by a factor of one and a half to nearly two (a standard deviation of {{lit:0.56 # results/E85_orn_fly_population/part_a.json, spread.median_sd_log2_above30: the median, over the glomerulus-by-odor entries whose mean response is above 30 % of the largest, of the SD across the nine flies of log2(fly / mean)}} for the strong responses and of {{lit:0.89 # results/E85_orn_fly_population/part_a.json, spread.median_sd_log2_all: the median over all glomerulus-by-odor entries of the SD across the nine flies of log2(fly / mean)}} over all, on a scale of logarithms to base 2), and per glomerulus a median of {{lit:0.91 # results/E85_orn_fly_population/part_a.json, reliability.r_g_median: the median over glomeruli of the share of the fly-to-fly variance that repeats across trials}} of that variance repeats across a fly's trials. A model fly is one wiring with one ORN fly's input: the averaged input plus the fly's deviation from the average over the nine flies, for the 12 odors and the glomeruli measured in that fly, so that the average over the nine inputs is the averaged input exactly. In the main reading each deviation is multiplied by the share of its glomerulus's variance between flies that repeats across trials (the repeatable deviations). Two bounds stand beside it, because a difference between two flies' ORN recordings is in part a difference of the imaging and not of the fly's input: the deviations as measured, the upper bound, and the repeatable deviations with each fly's gain on each glomerulus divided out, so that a difference in brightness between flies cannot enter, the lower. The control has each fly's repeatable deviations shuffled over the glomeruli within each odor, which keeps their size and breaks their structure. Every wiring is at its own breadth-2 APL-effect fit ([above](#wiring-population)); for each model fly the somatic threshold and the APL scale were set again until the numbers of responses with APL off and with APL on were the wiring's, and the main reading was also made with nothing set again. A population is read as the wirings were, the pair distances averaged over its model flies in each condition before the APL effect is taken. The main reading is on all eight wirings (72 model flies), the bounds and the control on four of them (the real wiring, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle). What would count was fixed before any run, through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) and against all recordings. The input flies move the target if the pattern part of the 72 model flies is lower than that of the eight wirings at the averaged input by 0.003 or more and lower on at least six of the eight wirings, each wiring's nine model flies set against the same wiring at the averaged input, with every population inside the realism bands. They do not move it if the change is below 0.0015 either way. And a shuffled control that gains half as much or more means that the size of the differences between flies does it, whatever their structure.

No fly has the averaged input: across the flies a response differs from the average by a factor of one and a half to nearly two (a standard deviation of {{lit:0.56 # results/E85_orn_fly_population/part_a.json, spread.median_sd_log2_above30: the median, over the glomerulus-by-odor entries whose mean response is above 30 % of the largest, of the SD across the nine flies of log2(fly / mean)}} for the strong responses and of {{lit:0.89 # results/E85_orn_fly_population/part_a.json, spread.median_sd_log2_all: the median over all glomerulus-by-odor entries of the SD across the nine flies of log2(fly / mean)}} over all, on a scale of logarithms to base 2), and per glomerulus a median of {{lit:0.91 # results/E85_orn_fly_population/part_a.json, reliability.r_g_median: the median over glomeruli of the share of the fly-to-fly variance that repeats across trials}} of that variance repeats across a fly's trials. A model fly is one wiring with one ORN fly's input: the averaged input plus the fly's deviation from the average over the nine flies, for the 12 odors and the glomeruli measured in that fly, so that the average over the nine inputs is the averaged input exactly. In the main reading each deviation is multiplied by the share of its glomerulus's variance between flies that repeats across trials (the repeatable deviations). Two bounds stand beside it, because a difference between two flies' ORN recordings is in part a difference of the imaging and not of the fly's input: the deviations as measured, the upper bound, and the repeatable deviations with each fly's gain on each glomerulus divided out, so that a difference in brightness between flies cannot enter, the lower. The control has each fly's repeatable deviations shuffled over the glomeruli within each odor, which keeps their size and breaks their structure. Every wiring is at its own breadth-2 APL-effect fit ([above](#wiring-population)); for each model fly the somatic threshold and the APL scale were set again until the numbers of responses with APL off and with APL on were the wiring's, and the main reading was also made with nothing set again. A population is read as the wirings were, the pair correlations averaged over its model flies in each condition before the APL effect is taken. The main reading is on all eight wirings (72 model flies), the bounds and the control on four of them (the real wiring, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle). What would count was fixed before any run, through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) and against all recordings. The input flies move the target if the pattern part of the 72 model flies is lower than that of the eight wirings at the averaged input by 0.003 or more and lower on at least six of the eight wirings, each wiring's nine model flies set against the same wiring at the averaged input, with every population inside the realism bands. They do not move it if the change is below 0.0015 either way. And a shuffled control that gains half as much or more means that the size of the differences between flies does it, whatever their structure.
