src: **Only the shuffled deviations lift the near pairs' APL effect, and a real fly's deviations are not of that kind.** In the shuffled control the four nearest pairs have an APL effect of {{E85/populations.csv:group=B4;unit=S;readout=cal:nearest_effect ~ +.3f}} against {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=S;readout=cal:nearest_effect ~ +.3f}} at the averaged input, about a seventh of what is missing, and the six pairs {{E85/populations.csv:group=B4;unit=S;readout=cal:six_effect ~ +.3f}} against {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=S;readout=cal:six_effect ~ +.3f}}. The reason is in the inputs (the row on the distance between the two odors' ORN inputs). Deviations shuffled over the glomeruli are independent between odors, so they set the two odors of a near pair far apart, at {{lit:0.248 # mean of column distance over the nine flies and the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows variant=permuted of results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}} on average for the four nearest pairs against {{lit:0.129 # mean of column lab_distance over the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep) in results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}} in the averaged input. A real fly's deviations are shared between similar odors, a glomerulus that responds more than the average to eb doing so to ep as well, and in each of their three forms they leave these pairs at {{lit:0.165 # mean of column distance over the nine flies and the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows variant=gainfree of results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}} to {{lit:0.188 # mean of column distance over the nine flies and the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows variant=measured of results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}}. The model's APL effect on a near pair thus does grow with the distance between the two inputs, and the differences between flies do not supply that distance. What the KC data show on these pairs, a larger distance with APL than without it, then has to come from what APL does to near-identical input and not from the variability of that input.
out: **Only the shuffled deviations lift the correlated pairs' APL effect, and a real fly's deviations are not of that kind.** In the shuffled control the four most correlated pairs have an APL effect of {{E85/populations.csv:group=B4;unit=S;readout=cal:nearest_effect ~ +.3f}} against {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=S;readout=cal:nearest_effect ~ +.3f}} at the averaged input, about a seventh of what is missing, and the six pairs {{E85/populations.csv:group=B4;unit=S;readout=cal:six_effect ~ +.3f}} against {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=S;readout=cal:six_effect ~ +.3f}}. The reason is in the inputs (the row on the correlation between the two odors' ORN inputs). Deviations shuffled over the glomeruli are independent between odors, so they make the two odors of a correlated pair much less correlated, at {{inv:lit:0.248 # mean of column distance over the nine flies and the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows variant=permuted of results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}} on average for the four most correlated pairs against {{inv:lit:0.129 # mean of column lab_distance over the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep) in results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}} in the averaged input. A real fly's deviations are shared between similar odors, a glomerulus that responds more than the average to eb doing so to ep as well, and in each of their three forms they leave these pairs at {{inv:lit:0.188 # mean of column distance over the nine flies and the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows variant=measured of results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}} to {{inv:lit:0.165 # mean of column distance over the nine flies and the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows variant=gainfree of results/E85_orn_fly_population/orn_distances_by_fly.csv}}. The model's APL effect on a correlated pair thus does grow as the correlation between the two inputs falls, and the differences between flies do not supply that decorrelation. What the KC data show on these pairs, a lower correlation with APL than without it, then has to come from what APL does to near-identical input and not from the variability of that input.

src: **What follows.** The averaged input stays the input of the models on this page, and every population number above stands as given. Differences between flies in what reaches the KCs are closed, for this family, as a carrier of the common error and of the near pairs' shortfall, and since the two bounds agree, how much of the spread between the ORN recordings is the flies' own does not have to be settled for that. The near pairs' shortfall stays with what happens between the claw and the soma, where a per-claw knee did not supply it either ([above](#claw-knee)): what is wanted there is a way for APL to hold near-identical inputs apart. The recordings have since been asked what does this in the flies. An inhibition that all the KCs share, growing with the odor's response over all of them, gives the four nearest pairs nearly the flies' APL effect when it is applied to the flies' own responses with APL output blocked (TNT), and an inhibition among KCs of similar tuning overshoots it; the shared inhibition applied to the responses with APL off of the fits as they are gives these pairs less than the model's own APL does, so that the shortfall is, by that reading, in the model's responses without APL ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)). The result is that of one family, at the model's 0.5 s pulse and without trial noise; the family with the firing ceiling was to be read the same way only if the target moved, and was not read. Two things are carried forward. Where single model flies are set against single recordings, or the spread between model flies serves as a yardstick, the model flies are to be drawn with input flies as well as wirings, since wirings alone vary too little. And for the reduced searched input, whose own controls have been run and hold ([above](#reduced-input)), the shuffled control here is a test of size without structure: deviations of the flies' size, shuffled, gain {{E85/populations.csv:group=B4;unit=S;readout=cal:gain_z8_pattern ~ .4f}} on four wirings, inside the margin of no move, so a change of the input of that size does not lower the pattern part merely by being a change. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

src: **The pattern of the flies' APL effect can be read from their own responses without APL. An inhibition that grows with the odor's response over all the KCs, and a little with how broadly the KC itself responds, applied to each recording with APL output blocked (TNT) with one constant set by the control flies' response rate, predicts the control flies' distances better than a uniform inhibition does on recordings it was not chosen on, and on all recordings it leaves a pattern part near the data's floor. The odor's strength is what carries it, and an inhibition among KCs of similar tuning is not what the recordings show. Applied to the models' responses with APL off, the same inhibition does no better than the models' own APL, and the models' APL effect among the esters stays too small under each inhibition of the kind that was read on them, so that by this reading the error common to the wirings lies in what the models' KCs do without APL and not in the form of their APL. Two results bound that reading. It is a reading of spike counts: simulated in place of the model's APL, as a rise of each KC's threshold, the flies' form does worse than the model's own APL, and the simulations do not follow the reading pair by pair. And it is the reading of a model that recruits in its own way. With how many KCs each odor recruits without APL set to the flies' on four wirings, the one respect of the responses that a saved handle can set, the model comes a third to a half of the way to what the flies' form does within a fly, the pattern of its own APL effect is no nearer the flies', and the flies' form applied to those responses does better than the model's own APL: a part of what is left is then read on the side of the model's APL. Simulated in place of APL on those responses, the form has since done far worse than the model's own APL ([below](#responder-sets)). What the form does within one fly is a target that needs no control flies and is known about twice as finely as the main target; it missed the test set for using it by a narrow margin, and by itself it is not a screen for the main target.** Every search for the common error has changed the model and read the model: APL's weight by glomerulus ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile)), what reaches the KCs ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side), [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit), [the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input), [the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)), the transfer at the claw ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)), where APL's inhibition falls in the calyx ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)) and the time course ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)). The form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses put the question to the recordings. A recording with APL output blocked (TNT) holds a fly's KC responses without APL, KC by KC, which is what every model is asked to turn into its responses with APL. If a simple inhibition of those responses gives the control flies' distances, the pattern of the flies' effect is in their responses without APL, and the same inhibition applied to a model's responses with APL off says on which side the model's error lies: in the form of its APL, if the flies' inhibition brings the model nearer the flies' effect than the model's own APL does, or in its responses without APL, if it does not.

src: A recording's responses are its trial means, KC by odor. A response is a value above the recordings' criterion of 1 z, and values not above it are set to 0 on both sides, the convention closest to a model's spike counts ([the main target](#apl-effect)); the flies' mean effect is then {{data:apl_effect_thresholded_mean ~ +.3f}} and its standard deviation across the 120 pairs {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=none:pattern ~ .3f}}. A form of inhibition reduces each KC's response to each odor by a constant times a power of the odor's strength times a power of the KC's breadth. The odor's strength is its mean response over the recording's KCs, relative to the mean over the 16 odors. The KC's breadth is the number of odors it responds to, or its response summed over the odors, relative to the mean over the KCs that respond. Both are taken from the same recording, with APL output blocked (TNT). The exponent on the strength was 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5 or 2 and the exponent on the breadth 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2, with either measure of breadth; the inhibition was either subtracted from the response or added to the criterion, the responses that stay above it keeping their values. That makes 90 forms, of which the one with both exponents at 0 is a uniform inhibition, the same amount off every response. Two further inhibitions stand beside them. One is given a part of the answer: it sets each odor's response rate to the control flies' own, by keeping the odor's strongest responses, and shows what an inhibition that differs only by odor does once it has every odor's response rate right. The other, an inhibition from KCs of similar tuning, reduces each KC's response to an odor in proportion to the responses to it of the other KCs, weighted by how alike their tuning over the other 15 odors is to its own. The one constant of a form is set so that the response rate over the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) becomes the control flies' {{data:ctrl_frac ~ .3f}}, and nothing else is fitted. The predicted distances with APL are the mean over those recordings of the cosine distances of the reduced responses, and the predicted APL effect is that minus the same recordings' own distances. No wiring, no ORN input and no model enter, so [the substituted ORN concentrations](#fn-concentrations) do not bear on this part. The forms were read as trial means, as the target is made, and with the trial noise removed (the form applied to the single trials of each repeat, at the criterion that gives the control flies' response rate on single trials, and the distances taken across repeats: [the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)), in the recordings' z and in [baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units). What would count was fixed before any run. A form was chosen, by the lowest pattern part, on one half of the recordings and scored on the other half, whose recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) then predict its own control recordings: for two splits of the flies into halves, each in both directions (the first split is that of the earlier searches, [above](#cross-wiring-fit)). A form beyond a uniform inhibition holds if, in the recordings' z, the chosen form's pattern part on the unseen half is lower than the uniform inhibition's there by 0.005 or more in at least three of the four readings and in their mean, both as trial means and with the trial noise removed, and if the same form with the odors' strengths permuted over the odors gains less than half as much.

src: **What the normalization had hidden.** In the flies a KC's unit grows with the number of odors the KC responds to ([the footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units) has the ratios), so that the responders' mean amplitude, about {{data:ctrl_resp_amp_mean_z ~ .0f}} z whatever the KC's breadth, is in baseline-noise units nearly twice as large in the control flies' KCs that respond to eight odors as in those that respond to one (the last row but one of the table; few KCs respond to exactly eight odors with APL on, in the flies and in the models, so the values at eight are rough). The flat amplitude in z is strongly growing responses compressed by the normalization.

The four most correlated ester pairs get an APL effect of {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=chosen:near4 ~ +.3f}} and {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=cal;data_reading=noise_free;responses=model;inhibition=chosen:near4 ~ +.3f}} under the flies' chosen form on the model's responses and of {{E87/two_by_two.csv:family=b2;readout=raw;data_reading=noise_free;responses=flies;inhibition=chosen:near4 ~ +.3f}} on the flies', where the flies have {{lit:+0.181 # mean of column effect over the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows unit=z, reading=noise_free, form=data of results/E87_inhibition_form/forms_pairs.csv}}. In the model, then, the KCs that the esters share respond with APL off in a way that no inhibition by the odor's strength and the KC's breadth that was tried separates, and in the flies they do not.

src: **A target that needs no APL.** What a form does within the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), the distances of their reduced responses minus their own, is itself a per-pair effect, and a model's responses with APL off can be scored against it by putting them through the same form. It is a comparison within each recording and needs no control flies, where the main target is a difference between two groups of flies. For the flies' chosen form the floor of its pattern part is about half the main target's in the same convention, two halves of the flies agree on it far better, and its ceiling is {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form_label=chosen;subset=all:ceiling ~ .2f}} against {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form_label=chosen;subset=all:main_ceiling ~ .2f}} (table above). The test for using it as a target had been set as a floor of at most half the main target's and a ceiling of 0.90 or more, in both readings. As trial means the floor is {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form_label=chosen;subset=all:floor_pattern ~ .4f}} where the main target's is {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form_label=chosen;subset=all:main_floor_pattern ~ .4f}}, a little more than half, so the test is missed there by a narrow margin; it is passed with the trial noise removed and within the six recordings that are alike. The target is therefore reported and not adopted. Against it the families are alike and further from its floor than they are from the main target's: the breadth-2 family reads {{E87/apl_free_models.csv:source=b2;readout=raw;unit=population;form_label=chosen;reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}} on raw counts, two and a half times the floor, the family with the firing ceiling {{E87/apl_free_models.csv:source=fc;readout=raw;unit=population;form_label=chosen;reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}}, and the 72 model flies that each have an ORN fly's own input ([above](#input-population)) {{E87/apl_free_models.csv:source=E85_model_flies;readout=raw;unit=population;form_label=chosen;reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .3f}}. Every saved model whose responses with APL off exist for the 16 odors was read against it as well, {{lit:1679 # count of the rows readout=raw of results/E87_inhibition_form/archive_scan.csv that were read without an error}} models of {{lit:75 # count of distinct folders among the rows readout=raw of results/E87_inhibition_form/archive_scan.csv that were read without an error}} experiments, each under both readings of its counts against the breadth-2 fit on the same wiring under the same reading. A model was to stand out if it read lower than that fit by 0.008 or more, with a mean effect of at least two thirds of the flies' and inside the realism bands. On raw counts none does: the nearest is {{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E80_remaining_candidates;variant=C2_B3_throff_noise;readout=raw:gain ~ .3f}} lower. Through the readout {{lit:seven # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_C.json, n_standout: 7 rows of archive_scan.csv with standout true, all of them readout=cal}} do. {{lit:Six # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_C.json, standouts: the six variants C2_B3_... of E80_remaining_candidates, on the real wiring}} of them are the [oracle](#fn-oracle) runs of one handle, in which each odor's response rates were put on the flies' by a threshold for each odor on the real wiring ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)): they read {{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E80_remaining_candidates;variant=C2_B3_thr_noise;readout=cal:noise_free_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E80_remaining_candidates;variant=C2_B3_throff_noise;readout=cal:noise_free_pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E80_remaining_candidates;variant=C2_B3_thr_noise;readout=cal:b2_same_wiring_pattern ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit there. The seventh is a fit from the replication of the structure-loss joint fits on re-drawn wiring, on one claw permutation ({{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E30_wiring_replication;variant=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_k2;readout=cal:noise_free_pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E87/archive_scan.csv:folder=E30_wiring_replication;variant=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_k2;readout=cal:b2_same_wiring_pattern ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit on that wiring), a different fit and not a handle that can be put on the family. How many KCs each odor recruits without APL is thus a part of what this target asks. How a saved model reads on the target says little about its own APL-effect loss (a Spearman correlation of {{lit:0.31 # Spearman correlation between columns noise_free_pattern and own_apl_loss over the 1489 rows readout=raw of results/E87_inhibition_form/archive_scan.csv that have both}} between the two over the saved models).

src: **Realism.** The reading of the recordings fits nothing to a model and adds no parameter, so its realism is what a form predicts for the control flies beside what they have (last three rows of the first table). The flies' chosen form gives the control flies' response rate by construction, their per-odor response rates (response rate ρ {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q1_p0.25_summed:rate_rho ~ .2f}}) and their distribution of the number of odors per KC almost exactly: {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q1_p0.25_summed:opk_tv ~ .3f}} from the control flies' mean distribution, where the uniform inhibition is at {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q0_p0:opk_tv ~ .3f}}, the square of the KC's number of odors at {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q0_p2_count:opk_tv ~ .3f}} and the most atypical control recording at {{data:ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}} from the others. Its responders are a little weaker than the control flies' ({{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q1_p0.25_summed:amp_ratio ~ .2f}} of their mean response). The form that predicts the distances best is thus also the one that makes the control flies' spread of responses over the KCs from the responses with APL output blocked (TNT), with one constant. What is hard to defend is the operation. The forms are static and act on time-averaged calcium signals; the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) are other animals than the control flies and have lived with the block, so that their responses need not be the control flies' responses without APL; a subtraction in z is not a subtraction of drive, which the divisive kind and the two units bracket; and while an inhibition in proportion to an odor's response over all the KCs is what a single APL that sums the KCs would give, the dependence on a KC's breadth has no measurement of APL behind it. In the simulations both response rates are the fits' by construction. The ratio of the response rates ({{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_q0_p2_P4:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}) and the largest spike counts ({{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_chosen_M3:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_chosen_real:max_count_on ~ .0f}} per KC and odor with APL on) stay those of the family's fits, and the number of odors per KC stays inside its band, at the edge under the uniform rise ({{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_M3:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution with APL on, against a band of {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}). {{lit:Eight # count of the 40 rows of results/E87_inhibition_form/runs_D.csv with a realism_flag (all of them the response rate ρ with APL on below 0.37)}} of the 40 runs fall below the band on the response rate ρ with APL on, down to {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_q1_p1_M3:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}: both exponents at 1 on four wirings, the flies' chosen form on three and the square of the number of odors on one. Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, {{lit:33 # count of the 40 rows of results/E87_inhibition_form/runs_D.csv with a realism_flag_zcrit}} of the 40 are outside a band. Every one of these runs is worse than the family's APL on the main target, none is recommended for anything, and no mean over wirings was read on the bands. The rise of the thresholds is itself large: the uniform form raises every threshold by {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_M2:c ~ .0%}} to {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_uniform_P3:c ~ .0%}}, and where the breadth enters alone, as the square of the number of odors, the constant is up to {{E87/runs_D.csv:D1_q0_p2_P3:c ~ .1f}} on a factor that is 1 for a KC of mean breadth and 4 for one of twice that. The runs with each odor's recruitment set are another matter: {{lit:all 12 # results/E87_inhibition_form/runs_D2.csv: none of its 12 rows has a realism_flag or a realism_flag_zcrit; results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_D2.json, n_flagged 0 in each arm}} are inside the four realism bands, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units and by the recordings' own criterion alike. The response rates with APL off are the flies' for each odor by construction, the response rate with APL on, which nothing holds where the thresholds act in both conditions, is {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_P2:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_M1:rate_on ~ .3f}} there, the ratio of the response rates is {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_M1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}, the response rate ρ with APL on is {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_throff_noise_P1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} or more, and the number of odors per KC is at most {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_P2:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution with APL on and {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_real:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} with APL off. They are oracles all the same. The thresholds differ between the odors by factors of {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_M1:thr_min ~ .2f}} to {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_P1:thr_max ~ .2f}}, set from the flies' response rates and from nothing in the model; where an APL scale is set for each odor it ranges from {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thrapl_noise_real:apl_min ~ .2f}} to {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thrapl_noise_M1:apl_max ~ .1f}} times the fit's, which no measurement supports; and with the thresholds in both conditions the largest spike count with APL on rises to {{E87/runs_D2.csv:D2_b3_thr_noise_P1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} on one wiring. The parts on the models carry, as everywhere, paa, euc and -aPine at [ORN input of another concentration](#fn-concentrations). Nothing was gained on the main target in the model here, so nothing was bought with the bands; what the recruitment gains on the target without APL is an oracle's, inside the bands.

src: **What follows.** The common error is restated in part. On the spike counts of the fits as they are, the flies' APL effect is, to within what the recordings resolve, what an inhibition that grows with an odor's response over all the KCs makes of the flies' responses without APL, which is in kind what the models' APL does, and the same inhibition makes no more of the models' responses than their own APL does. By that reading the models miss the effect first because their KCs' responses without APL are not the flies', among the esters above all, and the earlier reading that most of the common error lies in what APL does to particular pairs ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)) is narrowed to which KCs respond without APL and how strongly, which the distances with APL off do not show. Three results bound the reading. It is an operation on spike counts, which the simulated forms do not follow pair by pair. It is the verdict of the mean over the eight wirings: on single wirings, and for the four wirings of the earlier searches as a mean, the flies' form does better than the model's own APL on raw counts. And it holds for a model that recruits in its own way: with each odor's recruitment without APL set to the flies', the pattern of the model's own APL effect is no nearer the flies', and the flies' form on those responses does better than the model's own APL, so that a part of what is left is then on the side of the model's APL. The error is therefore not closed onto one side, and neither side alone has reached the main target here: not the flies' form in place of the model's APL on the model's own responses, and not the flies' recruitment with the model's own APL. The two together, the flies' form simulated on a base with the flies' recruitment, have since been run, and do far worse than the model's own APL does on either base ([below](#responder-sets)). A mechanism that changes the responses without APL is read on both targets, the one without APL for the responses and the main one for what the model's APL makes of them. Changes on APL's side are not the lead on the fits as they are and are not excluded; where they are taken up, it is on a base with the flies' recruitment. The shortfall on the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input ([above](#input-population)) is of a piece with this: in the flies a shared inhibition holds those pairs apart, and an inhibition among KCs of similar tuning, the kind that would hold near-identical inputs apart in a model, is not what the recordings show. Breadth-weighted APL keeps its place in the family, with some support from the KC data and at a smaller exponent than the family's; in the family itself a smaller exponent has since cost the main target, on the fits as they are and on a base with the flies' recruitment ([below](#breadth-weighting)); with APL's inhibition summed over a KC's claws, an exponent of 1 on that base has since read lower than the base's own family, by half of what the test set for it asks ([below](#summed-drive)). The effect of the form within a fly is given beside the main target for later models; whether it is given a place in fits is not decided, and by itself it would reward the per-odor recruitment. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

src: **With responses below the criterion set to 0, the similarity of two odors is exactly the product of three factors: how many KCs each odor recruits, how many times more often than chance a KC that responds to one odor responds to the other, and how strong the shared responders' responses are. The first two say who responds, the third how strongly. Putting the flies' factors into the models' product one at a time points to who responds: with the flies' responder sets and its own amplitudes the breadth-2 family has less than half of its pattern error left, and with the flies' amplitudes on its own responder sets it keeps most of it. By the test fixed beforehand this is not a verdict. On a model whose values without noise are known, the second factor is not estimated well enough through the trial noise, and against the six recordings that are alike the two readings disagree, so the split stands as a description. Four results stand beside it. In the model the two factors of who responds offset each other, each taken alone from the flies making the pattern worse, which would explain why setting each odor's recruitment to the flies' had moved nothing. The alcohols' responders that survive APL are shared more often than before in the flies, and less so in the models. The KCs that the model's APL removes although a cut by amplitude would keep them are the broadly responding KCs that its breadth weighting loads. And the flies' form of inhibition, simulated in place of APL on a base with the flies' recruitment, does far worse than the model's own APL, so that static inhibitions of this kind are closed on both bases.** The form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses had read the common error, on the spike counts of the fits as they are, as lying first in the models' responses without APL, and had left two things open ([above](#inhibition-form)). One was which respect of the responses carries the error. The other was a simulation: the flies' chosen form in place of APL on responses that recruit as the flies' do, since the readings on spike counts had not predicted the simulations on the fits as they are. The first question has an exact form, and it needs no simulation.

src: A response is a value above the criterion, and values not above it are set to 0, as in the readings of the flies' own responses above. The similarity of two odors, one minus the cosine distance of their responses over the KCs, is then exactly the product of three factors. The pair's recruitment is the geometric mean of the two odors' response rates. The co-response is how many times more often a KC responds to both odors than it would if the two odors' responders were independent of each other. The amplitude factor is the similarity of the responses divided by the similarity of the same responses reduced to responding or not; it says how strong the shared responders' two responses are against those of each odor's own responders. Recruitment and co-response together are the responder sets, who responds, and the amplitude factor is how strongly. A pair's APL effect is its similarity with APL off minus its similarity with APL on, the fall of the product when APL acts. The flies' factors were put into a model's product in place of the model's own, in both conditions: the two factors of who responds, the amplitude factor, the recruitment alone and the co-response alone. Each such combination was scored against the flies' per-pair APL effect as a model is, with the 15 pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms (the ester pairs below) and the 6 pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al (the alcohol pairs below), the two groups of the common error, read beside the pattern part. A combination holds the flies' own factors, measured in the recordings that make the target, so it is an attribution and not a model, and it can read below the floor that a model is held to; its own floor comes from taking the flies' factors from resampled recordings.

src: The comparison is fair only if the model is read as the flies are, since trial noise changes which KCs count as responders. Three readings were used. As trial means, the flies' three-trial means at 1 z are set against the model under the per-KC reading, on ten simulated recordings of three trials for each wiring, with the measurement noise that the reading sets on the model's counts (the reading's own noise below). The same reading was repeated with the model's noise raised until an odor's responder sets agree between two repeats as the flies' do: the mean cosine between the responder sets of two repeats of one odor is {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=real:mult_on_rel_target ~ .2f}} in the control flies and {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=real:mult_off_rel_target ~ .2f}} with APL output blocked (TNT), against {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=M2:mult_on_rel_r1 ~ .2f}} to {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=P4:mult_on_rel_r1 ~ .2f}} with APL on and {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=M2:mult_off_rel_r1 ~ .2f}} to {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=P3:mult_off_rel_r1 ~ .2f}} with APL off on the breadth-2 family's eight wirings at the reading's own noise, and the noise had to be multiplied by {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=M2:mult_on_mult ~ .1f}} to {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=P4:mult_on_mult ~ .1f}} with APL on and by {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=M2:mult_off_mult ~ .1f}} to {{E88/members.csv:population=b2;wiring=P3:mult_off_mult ~ .1f}} with APL off. With the trial noise removed, the similarities are estimated across repeats in the same way on both sides ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). The model without noise, on raw spike counts and through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), is given beside them against the flies with the trial noise removed. The models were the breadth-2 family on its eight wirings ([above](#wiring-population)), the family with the firing ceiling on four, and the four wirings of the earlier searches, unchanged and on the base with the flies' recruitment ([above](#inhibition-form)).

src: What would count was fixed before any run. The model's values without noise are known, so each factor's estimate was first checked against them: a factor whose mean over a group of pairs is off by more than 0.03, in units of the similarity, is not read in that reading. The error is in who responds if the flies' responder sets lower the breadth-2 family's pattern part by 0.015 or more and the flies' amplitudes lower it by at most half as much, as trial means and with the trial noise removed alike; it is in how strongly in the reverse case, and in both otherwise. A group's error goes with recruitment if the flies' recruitment alone at least halves it and the flies' co-response alone does not, and with the co-response in the reverse case. Every verdict is repeated against the six recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) that are alike, and one that changes there is reported as depending on the two strongest recordings ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)).

src: **The split cannot be read, because the co-response is not estimated well enough.** Recruitment and the similarity itself are inside the tolerance in both readings that the verdict rests on. The co-response is not. As trial means it is read too low with APL on for the pairs that are nearest each other: its error is {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;factor=L;group=six:err ~ +.3f}} for the six pairs with near-identical ORN input and {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;factor=L;group=nearest4:err ~ +.3f}} for the four nearest ester pairs, while for the ester and the alcohol pairs themselves it is inside the tolerance ({{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;factor=L;group=ester:err ~ +.3f}} and {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;factor=L;group=alcohol:err ~ +.3f}}). With the trial noise removed it is read too high in every group but the other 99 pairs, {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;condition=on;factor=L;group=ester:err ~ +.3f}} and {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;condition=on;factor=L;group=alcohol:err ~ +.3f}} for the ester and the alcohol pairs with APL on, and the amplitude factor is read too low ({{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;condition=on;factor=G;group=ester:err ~ +.3f}} and {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r2;condition=on;factor=G;group=alcohol:err ~ +.3f}}). At the flies' repeatability the trial-mean estimate of the co-response is off by as much as {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1b;condition=off;factor=L;group=six:err ~ +.3f}}. The errors run opposite ways in the two readings, and they grow with the noise, so the flies' own co-response probably carries an error of this order, which cannot be checked on the flies. By the rule the split is therefore not read, and what follows in this subsection on the factors is description.

src: **The alcohols' responders that survive APL are shared more often than before in the flies, and less so in the models.** What APL does to each factor can be read without putting one side's factors into the other's product (table above). In the flies and in the models alike APL cuts a pair's recruitment to about half, and the amplitude factor hardly changes (last five rows). What differs is the co-response of the alcohol pairs. In the flies it is {{E88/changes.csv:source=flies;member=mean;subset=all;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} times as large with APL as without (90 % interval over resampled recordings {{lit:1.42 to 1.75 # the exponentials of columns lo and hi (log units) of results/E88_responder_sets/changes.csv, row source=flies, member=mean, subset=all, reading=r1, factor=L, group=alcohol}}): the alcohols' responders that remain under APL are shared more often than their responders without it. In the breadth-2 family the factor is {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} at the reading's own noise and {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1b;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} at the flies' repeatability, in the family with the firing ceiling {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=fc;member=population;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} and {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=fc;member=population;reading=r1b;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}, and on the base with the flies' recruitment {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=D2_thrapl;member=population;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} and {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=D2_thrapl;member=population;reading=r1b;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}. A model's change was to count as different from the flies' if it lay outside their interval and differed by a factor of 1.10 or more at both noise levels. It does so in all three, the breadth-2 family's value at the flies' repeatability lying just below the interval. Against the six recordings that are alike ({{E88/changes.csv:source=flies;member=mean;subset=six;reading=r1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}, interval {{lit:1.36 to 1.69 # the exponentials of columns lo and hi (log units) of results/E88_responder_sets/changes.csv, row source=flies, member=mean, subset=six, reading=r1, factor=L, group=alcohol}}) it does so only on the base with the flies' recruitment. The ester pairs' co-response hardly changes under APL in the flies or in the models, and differs nowhere. The recruitment of the four nearest ester pairs, a factor that the check reads without bias, falls further under APL in the flies (to {{E88/changes.csv:source=flies;member=mean;subset=all;reading=r1;factor=R;group=nearest4:ratio ~ .2f}}, interval {{lit:0.38 to 0.51 # the exponentials of columns lo and hi (log units) of results/E88_responder_sets/changes.csv, row source=flies, member=mean, subset=all, reading=r1, factor=R, group=nearest4}}) than in the breadth-2 family ({{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1;factor=R;group=nearest4:ratio ~ .2f}} and {{E88/changes.csv:source=model;population=b2;member=population;reading=r1b;factor=R;group=nearest4:ratio ~ .2f}}); that difference is not there against the six recordings that are alike, nor on the base with the flies' recruitment. The size of the alcohols' difference carries the caveat of the estimate. Without noise the breadth-2 family's alcohol pairs have a co-response of {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=on;factor=L;group=alcohol:truth ~ .2f}} with APL on and {{E88/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;reading=r1;condition=off;factor=L;group=alcohol:truth ~ .2f}} with APL off, a ratio of {{lit:1.33 # the quotient of column truth of results/E88_responder_sets/estimator_check.csv in rows population=b2, reading=r1, factor=L, group=alcohol, condition=on (4.687) and condition=off (3.528)}}, which the trial means read as less at the reading's own noise and as more at the flies' repeatability. If the flies' value is too high in the proportion in which the model's is at their repeatability, the difference between the flies and the model is smaller than the table shows, and it remains.

The KCs that respond to both odors of a pair with APL off were divided into those that respond to both with APL on as well, those that the cut by amplitude would keep for both odors and the family's APL removes, and the rest (table above). The second class is {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=alcohol;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:share_of_overlap ~ .2f}} of a pair's shared responders for the alcohol pairs and {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=ester;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:share_of_overlap ~ .2f}} for the ester pairs. Its KCs are among the strongest responders of both odors. They respond to {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=alcohol;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:n_odors_off ~ .1f}} and {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=ester;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:n_odors_off ~ .1f}} of the 16 odors without APL, where the KCs that still respond to both with APL on respond to {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=alcohol;kc_class=survive:n_odors_off ~ .1f}} and {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=ester;kc_class=survive:n_odors_off ~ .1f}}; they have more claws and are more often γ KCs; and they receive {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=alcohol;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:apl_weight ~ .1f}} and {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=ester;kc_class=cut_kept_apl_removed:apl_weight ~ .1f}} times the mean APL→KC weight, where those that still respond receive {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=alcohol;kc_class=survive:apl_weight ~ .1f}} and {{E88/shared_kcs.csv:population=b2;wiring=pooled;group=ester;kc_class=survive:apl_weight ~ .1f}} times the mean. The model's APL thus takes out of the alcohols' and the esters' overlap the strongly and broadly responding KCs that a cut by amplitude keeps. It does not settle the side.

src: **What follows.** The common error keeps its two groups and gains a description of them that is not yet a verdict. Who responds is its likely address: the ester pairs' part with how large a share of an odor's responders APL removes, the alcohol pairs' part with whether the responders that survive APL are shared more often than before. For that to be relied on, the co-response needs an estimate that passes the check on a model with known values, at the reading's own noise and at the flies' repeatability; the split is then read again, without new simulations. Until it is, the amplitudes, and with them the readouts, the bounds on firing and the indicator's kinetics, are not closed as carriers of the two groups' errors by this route, although none of them carried those errors when it was tried ([the compressive readout of the model's spike counts](#readout); [the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling); [the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol); [the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)). Two things are carried forward as they are. The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL is given beside the main target for later mechanisms, on the fits as they are and on the base with the flies' recruitment: it is the difference between models and flies that shows at both noise levels and, on that base, against the six recordings that are alike as well. And on APL's side static forms are closed, so that what is pursued is the feedback APL's own weighting, with its breadth weighting first, since that weighting is what removes the shared responders that a cut by amplitude keeps. The verdicts that change with the six recordings that are alike, which are the overall split, the ester pairs' assignment to recruitment and the alcohols' difference on the fits as they are, wait on the experimenter's answer about the two strongest recordings. Both steps have since been taken, and both close: no estimate of the co-response passes the check, and no other breadth weighting does better than the family's own ([below](#breadth-weighting)). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

src: Five estimates of the co-response were put to the check of the first reading. Two existed: from the trial means, which reads the co-response of the pairs nearest each other too low, and with the trial noise removed, which reads it too high. Three were new: the geometric mean of those two, an estimate that sorts each KC's mean response to an odor into classes after the trial noise has been taken out of the distribution of the responses, and a correction of the trial means by each odor's measured agreement between repeats. Each is computed from a recording's three repeats, in the flies and in the models alike, and was checked on simulated recordings of the breadth-2 family's eight wirings and of the base with the flies' recruitment, with two seeds of the noise. The check was also made harder, with noise built as the flies' is ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). At the flies' repeatability a part of each KC's noise was shared by the odors of a repeat: the share at which two odors of the same repeat are closer than two odors of different repeats by as much as in the flies, counted on single trials with sub-threshold values set to 0, and half and one and a half times that share. An estimate was to be used only if recruitment, the co-response and the similarity were each within 0.03 of their values without noise, in units of the similarity, as the mean over each of five groups of pairs, in both conditions and with both seeds, at the reading's own noise and at all three shares. The split itself was to be read only with an estimate whose amplitude factor passed as well.

src: **No estimate passes, so the split stays a description.** The trial means read the co-response too low and the estimate with the trial noise removed reads it too high, at every noise level (first two rows of the table), so that their geometric mean comes closest. On the breadth-2 family it is inside the tolerance at the reading's own noise and with half and with the whole of the flies' share, where the two errors nearly cancel, and outside it at one and a half times that share ({{E89/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;seed=43;level=L3x;candidate=gm;condition=off;factor=L;group=nearest4:err ~ +.3f}}, for the four nearest ester pairs with APL off, with both seeds; the six pairs with near-identical ORN input and the alcohol pairs miss by nearly as much). Its amplitude factor is outside at half the flies' share as well ({{E89/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;seed=44;level=L3h;candidate=gm;condition=off;factor=G;group=six:err ~ +.3f}}), so that the split could not have been read with it in any case. On the base with the flies' recruitment its co-response is outside the tolerance from the flies' share on, and there the similarity itself, which every estimate has in common, is off by {{E89/estimator_check.csv:population=base;seed=44;level=L3;candidate=gm;condition=on;factor=s;group=six:err ~ +.3f}} at the flies' repeatability, so that no estimate could have passed. The classes of response hold up to half the flies' share on the family and nowhere on the base, and the correction by the agreement between repeats is far outside everywhere. By the rule fixed beforehand nothing is read with a new estimate and no further one is sought. With three repeats a recording, the co-response of the pairs nearest each other is not resolved to 0.03 at the flies' repeatability, and the earlier reading stands as it was left: it points to who responds and is not a verdict ([above](#responder-sets)). One choice in the check was open and does not decide it. The flies' share was set on single trials with sub-threshold values set to 0; set on the graded values it would be smaller, between no shared part and half the share used. That level was not run, and with no shared part the geometric mean is outside the tolerance as well ({{E89/estimator_check.csv:population=b2;seed=44;level=L2;candidate=gm;condition=off;factor=L;group=nearest4:err ~ +.3f}}).

src: **What follows.** The common error keeps its two groups, and its split into who responds and how strongly stays a description. No further estimate of the co-response is sought, and the amplitudes are not closed as carriers of the two groups' errors by this route, although none of them carried those errors when it was tried ([above](#responder-sets)). The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL stays beside the main target for later mechanisms, read with the geometric mean of the two estimates and with that estimate's error on known values beside it. It is a firm difference between the models and the flies, and it is not a lead on APL's side: the weighting sets it, and the main target does not follow. APL's side is thereby closed for the breadth weighting, as it is for static forms of inhibition ([above](#responder-sets)), for APL's profile over the glomeruli ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile); [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)) and for its weights by KC type ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)). Of the inhibitions tried on the breadth-2 family's responses, its own feedback APL is the best. The place where that inhibition is summed, at each claw or over a KC's claws, has since been varied as well and does not carry the error either; summed over the claws, an exponent of 1 reads lower than the family's on the base with the flies' recruitment, short of the test set for it ([below](#summed-drive)). The exponent stays at 2. The weighting is not fitted again with the family's other parameters free, nor read in the family with the firing ceiling, at the flies' pulse or through the trial noise; those steps were kept for a weighting that lowered the pattern part. The lead goes to the responses that APL acts on: which KCs respond to both odors of a pair before APL does anything, with the description of the model's shared responders, broad, many-clawed and often γ KCs, as the brief for a mechanism between the claw and the soma. The stages before the somata have since been read against recordings of them: where the models leave the flies is not resolved, and whether the model's KCs without APL bring two odors closer than their claw input depends on which claws are read ([below](#model-stages)). The verdicts that change with the six recordings that are alike wait, as before, on the experimenter's answer about the two strongest recordings. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

src: **Read against recordings of the PN dendrites, the PN boutons and the KC claws of wild-type flies, the best family cannot be placed: by the rule fixed beforehand, where it leaves the flies is not resolved for the ester pairs, the alcohol pairs or the other pairs. Whether the model's claws are more alike than the flies' depends on how much of a claw's signal is taken to come from its KC's spikes and on which claws are read, since a third of the wiring's glomeruli have no ORN input in the model; and how the model's steps from claws to somata compare with the flies' depends, beyond that, on how its somata are read and on the length of the odor pulse. What does not depend on a reading is mostly on the flies' side. In wild-type flies the step from claws to somata carries the pattern of the main target: with APL it is larger among the esters than among the alcohols, without APL it is not, and it passes, narrowly, the test set for a second reading of that pattern that uses no fly with APL output blocked (TNT). On the model's side one difference holds throughout: its step with APL on is too small for the six pairs with near-identical ORN input. For the ester pairs that step is the flies' when it is read from all claws and too small, in every reading of the somata and at either pulse, when it is read from the claws that the model's input drives. From those claws, which in the unit of the recordings read less alike than the flies', it is too small in every other group as well, so that the ester pairs' step with APL on is the lead which these readings leave, and one that hangs on which claws are read. Before the KCs, the model's antennal lobe evens out the odors' total drive, which the flies' PN dendrites do not, and its distances between odors are within 0.05 of the dendrites' once the noise between flies is removed.** Every test so far has held the models to the KC somata, and the search on APL's side had ended with the lead on the responses that APL acts on, with a mechanism between the claw and the soma as what is wanted ([the co-response read with a checked estimate and the breadth weighting inside the models' APL](#breadth-weighting)). For twelve of the panel's odors (2h, IaA, pa, 2-but, eb, ep, 6al, t2h, 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and ms) the stages before the somata have been recorded in wild-type flies: the ORNs and the PN dendrites glomerulus by glomerulus, and the PN boutons and the KC claws in the calyx, as the responses of imaged regions. The 66 pairs of these odors hold all 15 ester pairs and all 6 alcohol pairs of the common error. No model had been read against these recordings stage by stage. The model's stages against the flies' stages changed no model and fitted nothing, so that no number of the main target moved: through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) the family's loss is all pattern, {{E72/population.csv:group=all:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} for the mean over its eight wirings against a floor of {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}, as before. It read the family's PNs, boutons and claws as the recordings were made and asked, for each group of pairs, whether the model differs from the flies at a stage before the somata, at the step from claws to somata with APL on, or at that step without APL. A model's error in a pair's APL effect is its error at the first step minus its error at the second, so that the two steps say on which side of APL a group's error is made.

src: The model is the breadth-2 family on its eight wirings, each at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), run again at fixed parameters with the PN rates, the bouton rates and APL's activity kept. Every run reproduces its saved fit spike for spike, with APL on and with APL off, and a model value below is the mean over the eight wirings. The distance between two odors is one minus the Pearson correlation of their responses across the units of a stage: glomeruli, imaged regions, or the model's boutons, claws or KCs. That is the measure in which the bouton and the claw recordings exist; it is not the cosine distance of the main target. It is given as the mean over the pairs of a group: the 15 pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms, the 6 pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al, the 24 pairs of an ester with an alcohol, the 21 other pairs, and the six pairs with near-identical ORN input ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)), which are counted in the other groups as well. Noise makes two odors look less alike than they are, so the flies' values are given with it removed where the recordings allow. For the boutons and the claws, which were recorded in a unit scaled region by region and exist fly by fly only, the trial noise is removed within each fly: the correlation between two odors across blocks of trials is divided by how well each odor's own response repeats across blocks, and the flies are then averaged. For the ORNs and the PN dendrites, whose units are the same glomeruli in every fly, the values are those of the flies' mean pattern, with the noise between flies removed in the same way across halves of the flies, because the model's input is that mean. A stage of the model was read in three ways: as changes of rate; in the unit of the recordings, with each bouton's or claw's signal divided by its own standard deviation over a simulated session of the 16 odors; and in that unit through measurement noise at the flies' repeatability, with the noise then removed as it is for the flies. A bouton's or a claw's response to an odor is its mean during the odor minus its level before the odor, and every reading of the model's boutons, claws and steps in this subsection takes that level once the model's KCs and APL have settled, as the mean over the last quarter of a second before the odor ([why, and what that moved](#fn-preodor-startup)). On the model's known values the removal of the noise is right to within {{lit:0.004 # the largest absolute value of column error in results/E90_model_stages/settled_preodor/noise_check.csv over every stage, subset, claw version, condition, group and single wiring (0.0041; 0.0010 for the mean over the eight wirings; 0.0031 and 0.0012 in results/E90_model_stages/noise_check.csv, with the level before the odor taken over the whole half second)}} for every group, where 0.03 was allowed. What a claw's calcium signal reports is not known, so each claw of the model was read in three versions: its drive after APL's inhibition alone, and with a quarter or a half of its signal taken from its KC's spikes. The boutons were read on the 28 glomeruli that the recordings of the PN dendrites share with the model's input, the bouton recordings having been made with the same PN driver line, and the claws on all claws. The rule was fixed before any run. A stage or a step counts as different from the flies' if the model's value is 0.05 or more from the flies', lies outside their 90 % interval and has at least six of the eight wirings on the same side, in every reading and, for the claws and the steps, in every version of a claw. A group is then upstream if its boutons or its claws differ, at one of the two steps if only that step differs, and not resolved if the readings disagree. For the steps the rule read the model's somata through the calibrated readout.

src: **Before the KCs the model evens out the odors' total drive, which the flies do not; in the distances between odors it is close to the flies once their noise is removed.** The coefficient of variation, over the 12 odors, of the response summed over the 28 shared glomeruli is {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=change:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the model's PNs, for {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=orn_input:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in its ORN input; in the flies it is {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=pn_dend:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the PN dendrites (90 % interval {{E90/al_transfer.csv:section=summary;map=linear;stat=cv_total_pn:lo ~ .3f}} to {{E90/al_transfer.csv:section=summary;map=linear;stat=cv_total_pn:hi ~ .3f}}) and {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=orn_dff:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the ORNs. The model's antennal lobe thus removes most of the differences between odors in total drive, as had been seen from the model's side ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)), and the recordings of the PN dendrites do not show it. The distances between odors are another matter, and they depend on how the flies are read. Taken fly by fly and averaged, the PN dendrites hold two odors further apart than the model's PNs do, by {{diff:E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=per_fly;group=ester:mean -- E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=per_fly;group=ester:model_change ~ .2f}} among the ester pairs and {{diff:E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=per_fly;group=alcohol:mean -- E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=per_fly;group=alcohol:model_change ~ .2f}} among the alcohol pairs (third row of the table), and by the rule the PN stage would differ for the alcohol pairs and for the six pairs with near-identical ORN input. But a fly's own distances carry its trial noise and its own deviations from the mean over flies, and the model's PN stage has neither, since its input is that mean. Read on the flies' mean pattern with the noise between flies removed (first two rows), the dendrites are {{diff:E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=across_flies_noise_removed;group=ester_alcohol:mean -- E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=orn_pebbled28;reading=across_flies_noise_removed;group=ester_alcohol:mean ~ .2f}} to {{diff:E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=across_flies_noise_removed;group=other:mean -- E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=orn_pebbled28;reading=across_flies_noise_removed;group=other:mean ~ .2f}} less alike than the ORNs, the model's PNs keep the distances of the ORNs, and they are within 0.05 of the dendrites in every group, so that by the rule the PN stage does not differ. At the boutons the answer depends on the unit. As changes of rate the model's boutons keep the PNs' distances and are more alike than the flies' in every group but the ester pairs. In the unit of the recordings they are the flies' in every group but one, though the alcohol pairs lie at the margin of the rule ({{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=bouton;subset=shared;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:alcohol ~ .3f}} against the flies' {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=bouton_noise_removed;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}, less alike; of the two readings in this unit the one through the noise counts as a difference by the rule and the other does not): the six pairs with near-identical ORN input are {{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=bouton;subset=shared;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:near ~ .2f}} apart in the model and {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=bouton_noise_removed;group=near:mean ~ .2f}} in the flies (90 % interval {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=bouton_noise_removed;group=near:lo ~ .2f}} to {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=bouton_noise_removed;group=near:hi ~ .2f}}), and they are too close in all three readings, so that for these pairs the rule says "upstream". That verdict is not firm. The flies' boutons can only be read fly by fly, each fly's boutons carrying that fly's own input, where the model's carry the input averaged over flies. At the PN dendrites, where both readings can be made, the six pairs are {{E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=per_fly_trial_noise_removed;group=near:mean ~ .3f}} apart fly by fly with the trial noise removed and {{E90/pn_stage_noise_removed.csv:key=pn_dend28;reading=across_flies_noise_removed;group=near:mean ~ .3f}} for the flies' mean pattern, a difference nearly as large as the one at the boutons. The same reservation holds for every row of boutons and claws in the table: if a fly's own part is as large there as in the dendrites, the flies' values overstate the distances of the mean pattern, which is what the model is given.

src: **At the claws the answer turns on what is read.** With all claws and the drive alone, the model's claws are more alike than the flies' in every group, and by a wide margin in the four groups that make up the 66 pairs (the rows of the claws in the table). Two things qualify that. The first is what a claw's signal reports. With half of it taken from the KC's spikes, the model's claws come within 0.05 of the flies' for the ester pairs and the alcohol pairs in the unit of the recordings ({{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=all;share=0.5;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:ester ~ .3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=all;share=0.5;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:alcohol ~ .3f}} against {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=ester:mean ~ .3f}} and {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}), and for the ester, the alcohol and the other pairs as changes of rate. By the rule the claws thus differ in some versions and not in others, and only the pairs of an ester with an alcohol are more alike than the flies' in all nine. The second is which claws are read. The model's ORN input covers 36 of the wiring's 54 glomeruli, and the other 18 have no input for any odor. Their PNs carry only the antennal lobe's lateral signal, about {{lit:5 Hz # E90_model_stages.md, Summary, the claw-reading caveat: the PNs of the 18 glomeruli without ORN input carry about 5 Hz during an odor}} during an odor, and their claws are {{lit:17 % # E90_model_stages.md, Summary, the claw-reading caveat: 1679 of the real wiring's 9867 claws belong to the 18 glomeruli without ORN input}} of all claws. In the unit of the recordings each of those claws is scaled by its own small variability, which turns the lateral signal into a pattern that every odor shares and pulls every pair together. On the claws of the 36 glomeruli with ORN input, in the unit of the recordings and with the drive alone, the model's claws are less alike than the flies' for the ester pairs and the alcohol pairs ({{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:ester ~ .3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:alcohol ~ .3f}} against {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=ester:mean ~ .3f}} and {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}), and by {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:other -- E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=other:mean ~ .3f}} for the other pairs and {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:near -- E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=near:mean ~ .3f}} for the six nearest pairs; only for the pairs of an ester with an alcohol are they the flies' ({{E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:ester_alcohol ~ .3f}} against {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=ester_alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}). As changes of rate those claws are more alike than the flies' for the alcohol pairs, the pairs of an ester with an alcohol and the other pairs: for the alcohol and the other pairs the two units thus differ in direction. Which claws to read was chosen from how the recordings were made, all claws because a claw region is imaged whichever PN it receives from, after one wiring's readings had been seen and before the verdict. The reading on the 36 glomeruli was added after the verdict, as a check of how much it depends on that choice, and it is not the verdict. By the rule, with all claws the ester pairs, the alcohol pairs and the other pairs are not resolved and the pairs of an ester with an alcohol are upstream; with the claws of the 36 glomeruli, or of the 28 shared ones, all four groups are not resolved. Where the two groups of the common error leave the flies is not decided by these recordings.

src: **In wild-type flies the step from claws to somata carries the pattern of the main target.** The flies' own steps need no model. With APL the somata hold two odors further apart than the claws do in every group, and more so among the ester pairs than among the alcohol pairs: the ester pairs' step exceeds the alcohol pairs' by {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol ~ +.3f}} with the somata of wild-type flies (90 % interval {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_lo ~ +.2f}} to {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_hi ~ +.2f}}) and by {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_ctrl;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol ~ +.3f}} with those of the control flies ({{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_ctrl;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_lo ~ +.2f}} to {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_ctrl;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_hi ~ +.2f}}), over the same four claw flies. Without APL, with the somata of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), the step is small, its interval reaching zero in three of the four groups, and the two groups do not differ ({{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=off_tnt;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol ~ +.3f}}, {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=off_tnt;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_lo ~ +.2f}} to {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=off_tnt;claw=claw_noise_removed:ester_minus_alcohol_hi ~ +.2f}}). In the flies, then, most of what the somata add to the claws' distances needs APL, and the difference between the esters and the alcohols that the models miss is made with APL on, in flies that share nothing with the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT). Over the 66 pairs the step in wild-type flies follows the per-pair APL effect of the main target, with a Pearson correlation of {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:r_effect ~ .2f}} with the trial noise removed from the claws and {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_measured:r_effect ~ .2f}} with the claws as measured, and it runs against the common error ({{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:r_common_error ~ +.2f}}): the pairs on which the models' APL effect is too small are those with the larger step. A rule fixed beforehand said when this step may be used as a second reading of the target's pattern. The two halves of the four claw flies had to agree on it at 0.6 or more, and its floor, the distance between a step from resampled flies and the measured one, had to be at most half of its standard deviation over the pairs. It passes in both readings of the claws, clearly on the first condition and by a hair on the second (second table below).

src: **The model's steps depend first on the claws they start from; the step with APL on is too small for the nearest pairs throughout, and for the ester pairs it is the flies' from all claws and too small from the claws that the input drives.** From all claws the model's step with APL on is the flies' for the ester pairs ({{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=all;group=ester:model ~ +.3f}} against the control flies' {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=all;group=ester:flies ~ +.3f}}) and about twice the flies' for the alcohol pairs, the pairs of an ester with an alcohol and the other pairs (first of the two tables above). For the ester pairs it is {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:model ~ +.3f}} through the calibrated readout and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=raw_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:model ~ +.3f}} on raw spike counts against the control flies' {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=ester:flies ~ +.3f}}, and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_cosine;claws=input;group=ester:diff ~ +.2f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=raw_cosine;claws=input;group=ester:diff ~ +.2f}} from the flies' with the somata's distances taken as cosine; for the alcohol pairs it is {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:model ~ +.3f}} and {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=raw_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:model ~ +.3f}} against {{E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:flies ~ +.3f}}. A part of that shortfall is in turn the other side of claws that read too far apart. For the alcohol pairs it is nearly all of it: their claws are {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/stages_model.csv:stage=claw;subset=input;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=session_z;wiring=population:alcohol -- E90/stages_flies.csv:key=claw_noise_removed;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}} less alike than the flies' and their step through the calibrated readout is {{diff:E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:flies -- E90/settled_preodor/steps_by_reading.csv:step=on;soma=cal_pearson;claws=input;group=alcohol:model ~ .3f}} smaller, the somata being the control flies' in that reading ({{E90/stages_model.csv:stage=soma;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=cal_pearson;wiring=population:alcohol ~ .3f}} against {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=soma_ctrl;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}). src: **Realism.** Nothing was fitted and no parameter was added. Every run is a saved fit run again with its internal rates kept, and each reproduces its saved spike counts exactly, so that the runs are inside the four realism bands as their fits are: response rates of {{E90/variants.csv:real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E90/variants.csv:P3:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E90/variants.csv:P4:rate_acute_off ~ .3f}} to {{E90/variants.csv:P2:rate_acute_off ~ .3f}} with APL off over the eight wirings (the flies' {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_tnt_frac ~ .3f}}), and likewise the fit at the flies' 2 s pulse and the four fits with the firing ceiling. The experiment is itself a reading of the base model's realism below the somata, and what it finds is above: an antennal lobe that evens out the odors' total drive; a third of the wiring's glomeruli without ORN input, whose claws, a sixth of all, carry only a lateral signal; boutons that match the flies' in the unit of the recordings in every group but the nearest pairs, the alcohol pairs lying at the margin of the rule; and somata that with APL on are more alike than the control flies' among the ester pairs ({{E90/stages_model.csv:stage=soma;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=cal_pearson;wiring=population:ester ~ .3f}} through the calibrated readout and {{E90/stages_model.csv:stage=soma;subset=all;share=0.0;cond=on;reading=raw_pearson;wiring=population:ester ~ .3f}} on raw counts against {{E90/stages_flies.csv:key=soma_ctrl;group=ester:mean ~ .3f}} in this measure). At the 2 s pulse the family without a firing ceiling fires up to {{lit:124 # results/E90_model_stages/b5_realism.json, pulse2.max_count_on}} spikes per KC and odor with APL on and {{lit:236 # results/E90_model_stages/b5_realism.json, pulse2.max_count_off}} with APL off, far more than a KC has been recorded to fire, and the fits with the ceiling stay at {{lit:9 to 15 # E90_model_stages.md, Realism table: the largest spike count per KC and odor with APL on over the four firing-ceiling fits}} and {{lit:21 to 29 # E90_model_stages.md, Realism table: the largest spike count per KC and odor with APL off over the four firing-ceiling fits}}. What is hard to defend lies in the comparison more than in the model. The signal of the PN dendrites is calcium in the dendrites, not the PNs' output, and it saturates for the strongest responses; passed through a saturating map that bounds this, the dendrites' totals spread further still (a coefficient of variation of {{E90/al_transfer.csv:section=summary;map=saturating;stat=cv_total_pn:value ~ .2f}}). The dendrites and the boutons were recorded with a driver line that labels about seven PNs in ten. An imaged region is not one bouton or one claw: a claw region holds about {{lit:14 # notes/remy-summary.md, cited in E90_model_stages.md, Realism: a claw region averages about 14 claws of 14 KCs}} claws of as many KCs, where the model's units are single. A claw's signal may carry its KC's spikes. A fly's boutons and claws carry that fly's own input, and the model's the mean over flies. There are four claw flies and five bouton flies. And the stage recordings are of wild-type flies at 3 s pulses, the KC recordings of the main target of flies after three days at 31 °C at 2 s pulses, and the model's readings of a 0.5 s pulse. The stage recordings hold twelve odors, so that no pair of paa, euc, -aPine or B-myr is in any number of this subsection but those of the main target, and their [ORN input of another concentration](#fn-concentrations) enters the stage readings only through the calibrated readout's constant, which is set on all 16 odors.
