src: **What follows.** Where along the pathway the common error is made is not decided by these recordings, and the model's side of this subsection is a set of readings, not a verdict. What would decide it is on the flies' side: the responses of the imaged bouton and claw regions odor by odor and trial by trial, where only distances between odors are on hand, and the outline of the claw regions. With them the claws can be read on the regions that the model's input reaches, the share of a claw's signal that comes from its KC's spikes can be estimated from the claws' own time course, and a fly's own part can be told from the mean pattern, as it was for the PN dendrites. They are asked of the experimenter who made the recordings. Meanwhile four things are carried forward. The step from claws to somata in wild-type flies is given beside the main target for every later mechanism, with its floor: it reads the target's pattern on flies that share nothing with the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), and whether it is also kept out of fits as a test is a choice still to be made. The step with APL on joins the brief of the mechanism between the claw and the soma that the lead asks for ([above](#breadth-weighting)): for the nearest pairs in every reading, and for the ester pairs as a lead, their step being too small from the claws that the input drives and the flies' from all claws. A change at that step that leaves the responses without APL as they are, APL's inhibition summed over a KC's claws in place of clipped at each claw, has since been run and is level on the main target ([below](#summed-drive)). The step without APL does not join it as a result: that the model's KCs without APL bring two odors closer than their claw input holds from the claws that the input drives, in every reading of the somata, and not from all claws, so that a family which would not do so is read from both sets of claws, on raw counts and through the readout alike. The somata of both sides have since been read alike, the flies' with their trial noise removed and the model's as the recordings are normalized ([below](#steps-like-for-like)). With APL on the model's ester pairs are then too alike and its alcohol pairs too far apart in every reading. Without APL the model's somata are the flies' if a KC's signal is taken to saturate with its firing and too far apart if it is not, and in no such reading are the alcohol pairs too alike: the reading in which their excess is made at the step without APL, by somata that are too alike there, holds only with the calibrated readout set against the flies' trial means. The antennal lobe's evening-out of the odors' totals stands as a difference between the base model and the flies; a fit of that stage to the PN dendrites had been kept for a verdict that names the PN stage alone, which has not come, and the settings tried say that the main target would not reward it at fixed scales. And before the stages are read again, the 18 glomeruli without ORN input are given input or left out of the claws that are read, and the PN dendrites and the ORNs are read on the flies' mean pattern. The first has since been done for the ten of the 18 for which responses to the panel's odors have been measured, and the reading of the claws moves to the margin of the rule: with all claws the pairs of an ester with an alcohol, upstream with the lab's input, are narrowly not resolved with the fuller input, and on the claws of the glomeruli with input the four groups that make up the 66 pairs are not resolved ([below](#missing-glomeruli)). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

src: **In every model so far APL's inhibition of a KC is taken from each claw separately, and a claw can lose no more than its own input. Charging the inhibition that a claw cannot absorb to the KC's other claws, so that APL acts on the KC's summed drive, does not lower the pattern part. On the fits as they are it is level at the family's breadth weighting, at an exponent of 1 it gives back about a quarter of what the weaker weighting loses and at weaker weightings nothing, and against no half of the recordings is a setting with the summed form the best. The family fitted again with the summed form is level as well. Only on the base with the flies' recruitment does the summed form gain: there a weighting with an exponent of 1 reads lower than the base's own family, on the four wirings of the earlier searches and, against recordings that it was not chosen on, on the four others. That gain is half of what the test asks, an inhibition that is the same for every odor gives more than half of it, and it makes up about what that base costs against the fits as they are. What the clipping holds back sits in the many-clawed, broadly responding KCs that the family's weighting already loads, so that the summed form acts as a second breadth weighting. For the feedback APL's subtraction from the KCs, the weighting and now the place where it is summed are closed on the fits as they are; what was left on APL's side in this family, a gain on each claw's drive in place of the subtraction and the form of APL's inhibition of the boutons, has been run since, in the subsection that follows this one.** The search on APL's side had left one property of the feedback APL's inhibition of the KCs that nothing had varied ([above](#breadth-weighting)): the place where it is subtracted. In the model a claw's drive is its PN input minus APL's inhibition of that claw, and a drive below zero is set to zero before the KC sums its claws. A KC that an odor drives through one or two strong claws therefore loses little to APL, however many claws it has, while a KC driven through many weak claws loses most of its drive. If the inhibition acts on the sum instead, every claw's inhibition is charged whether the odor drives that claw or not, and APL removes the KCs with many undriven claws. That is a selection of responders made between the claw and the soma, with the responses without APL left exactly as they are. The KCs it would remove are of the kind that the model's APL had been found to remove among the shared responders, broad and many-clawed ([the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)), so that the summed form might have done the work of the family's weighting without weights as unequal as the family's.

src: **About two fifths of the common error is within the reach of a change of the input.** A change of the input acts with APL on and with APL off alike: it moves a pair's distance in both conditions. If a model's distances with APL on follow from its distances with APL off by a relation of its own, such a change moves a pair along that relation, and the part of the error that it reaches in this way is the part that comes from where the model's distances with APL off differ from the flies'.

src: **Read the same way on both sides, the model's KC somata differ from the flies' with APL on in every reading, and in opposite directions for the two groups of the common error: the ester pairs are too alike and the alcohol pairs too far apart. Without APL the verdict turns on one assumption of the reading. If a KC's signal is taken to saturate with its firing, the model's somata without APL are the flies' in every group of pairs but the four ester pairs with near-identical ORN input; if it is taken to grow in proportion to its firing, they are too far apart. In no such reading are the alcohol pairs too alike without APL, which is how the earlier comparison of the stages had read them through the calibrated readout. The two steps from claws to somata say no more than the somata, because both start from claws that read more alike than the flies'. Over the breadth weightings of APL the ester pairs' and the alcohol pairs' distances with APL on move together, along one line, and the control flies lie far off it. Of the saved changes of APL's inhibition that treat every glomerulus alike, none leaves that line toward the flies by more than about a thousandth; what leaves it are changes made glomerulus by glomerulus or odor by odor, to the input or to APL's weight, fitted to the recordings or taken from single flies. The one form of APL's inhibition of the KCs that the family had not run, a gain on each claw's drive in place of the subtraction, is worse at the family's weighting and at an exponent of 1, and better by one to three thousandths only at the weakest weightings, which stay far above the family; against no half of the recordings is a setting with the gain the best, and none is an equal. A divisive inhibition at the boutons, run for the record, is the only form on APL's side that moves the model clearly off the line toward the flies and brings the alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL to the flies'; at fixed scales it pays for both in the pattern part and in the mean APL effect. The summed form reads as the family with the clipping in its somata, its claws and its steps, and it lies on the line. The feedback APL's inhibition of the KCs is thereby closed in its form, after its weighting and the place where it is summed. What a mechanism between the claw and the soma has to do can now be said on the somata themselves: with APL on, hold the ester pairs further apart and the alcohol pairs closer together, both at once.** [The model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages) had set the model's steps from claws to somata beside the flies' and had left a lead and a reading that, as the claws were then read, hung on the readout: the ester pairs' step with APL on was too small from the claws that the model's input drives, and through the calibrated readout the model's KCs without APL brought two odors closer together than the flies' do, which would place the alcohol pairs' excess at the step without APL. At the somata that comparison had not treated the two sides alike. The flies' somata were trial means in the recordings' own unit, which carry the trial noise and each KC's own normalization, and the model's were spike counts without noise, or the calibrated readout of them. On APL's side two things had been left as well ([APL's inhibition on the KC's summed drive](#summed-drive)): a gain on each claw's drive in place of the subtraction, and the form of APL's inhibition of the boutons. The claw-to-soma steps read like for like and APL's inhibition as a gain at the claw took these up in three parts: a reading of saved runs that simulated nothing, the gain at fixed scales, and the runs with the summed form read as the first part reads the family. The reference throughout is the breadth-2 family with the subtraction clipped at each claw, whose pattern part through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) is {{E92/readings_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} on the four wirings of the earlier searches, for a floor of {{data:apl_effect_pattern_floor ~ .4f}}.

src: The first part reads the somata of both sides in the same unit and with the same treatment of the noise. On the flies' side, for every recording of the control flies and of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), the distance between two odors was taken as the trial means give it and with the trial noise removed, by the estimate across repeats ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)); in the recordings' own unit, each KC's trace z-scored over its recording, and in [baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units); and as one minus the Pearson correlation across the KCs, the measure of the stage recordings, and as cosine distance, the measure of the main target. A value is the mean over the recordings, with a 90 % interval over resampled recordings. The estimate was checked where the truth is known. Applied to simulated recordings of the model, of three trials each and at four levels of noise, it returns the model's noise-free distances of every group to within {{lit:0.013 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/estimate_check.json, largest_population_error: the largest absolute error of the estimate with the trial noise removed against the model's noise-free group distance, for the mean over the eight wirings, over the groups, the two conditions, the four noise levels, the two measures and the two units (0.0129)}} for the mean over the eight wirings, where 0.03 was allowed and where the trial means are off by up to {{lit:0.18 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/estimate_check.csv, rows wiring=population: the largest absolute value of column error_trial_mean (0.177)}}. On the model's side the saved runs of the breadth-2 family on its eight wirings, each at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), were read as the recordings are normalized, under the per-KC reading ([the per-KC normalization of the recordings](#per-kc-normalization)) set on each run's counts with APL on. That reading passes a KC's spike counts through a saturating map before it places them in a simulated recording. It was made with that map and with a linear map in its place, because whether a KC's calcium signal saturates over the range of its firing is not known. Each of the two was read in the reading's z against the flies in the recordings' own unit and in baseline-noise units against the flies in those units; without noise against the flies' values with the trial noise removed and through the reading's measurement noise against the flies' trial means; and as Pearson and as cosine. That makes 16 readings in which the two sides are treated alike. Raw spike counts and the calibrated readout were read beside them, against the flies in baseline-noise units. The groups of pairs and the rule are those of the stages comparison: a group differs from the flies' if the model's mean over the eight wirings is 0.05 or more from the flies' value, lies outside their 90 % interval and has at least six of the eight wirings on the same side. Of the six pairs with near-identical ORN input ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)), the four ester pairs, eb with ep, IaA with pa, 2h with pa and 2h with IaA, are read together, and the other two singly and as leads. The two steps from claws to somata were then read with the claws of the stages comparison on both sides, the model's as all claws with the drive alone, from their settled level before the odor ([footnote](#fn-preodor-startup)).

src: The same part asks what a change on APL's side can do to the two groups at once. For a model, the mean cosine distance with APL on over the 15 ester pairs, minus the mean over all 120 pairs, says how far apart APL leaves the ester pairs relative to the mean pair, and the same difference for the 6 alcohol pairs says it for them. For the 13 breadth weightings of APL on the fits as they are ([the co-response read with a checked estimate and the breadth weighting inside the models' APL](#breadth-weighting)), each as the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches, the two numbers fall close to a straight line, the weightings' line. Every saved variant of the family was placed against it, on raw spike counts and through the calibrated readout: {{lit:286 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, n_variants}} variants from {{lit:757 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, n_runs}} runs of ten earlier experiments, {{lit:265 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, n_in_bands}} of them inside the realism bands. A variant counts as off the line toward the flies if its distance from the line, on the side on which the control flies lie, is larger than the largest distance among the 13 weightings themselves, with the flies' point taken from either half of the recordings. A single run, or a mean over the four held-out wirings, is measured from the unchanged family on the same wirings.

src: **With APL on the model's somata differ from the flies' in every reading, the ester pairs too alike and the alcohol pairs too far apart.** Over the 16 readings the model's ester pairs lie {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=linear_z_none_pearson;group=ester:diff ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_cosine;group=ester:diff ~ +.3f}} from the flies' (the model's value minus the flies', so that a negative difference means pairs that are more alike). By the rule the group differs in {{lit:15 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, somata.ester.on.n_differ, of n_readings 16}} of the 16, the one that does not falling just short of the rule's 0.05. The alcohol pairs lie {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_expected_cosine;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=linear_z_none_pearson;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} from the flies', further apart in all 16, and differ by the rule in {{lit:14 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, somata.alcohol.on.n_differ, of n_readings 16}}. The four ester pairs with near-identical ORN input are too alike in all 16, lying {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=linear_z_none_pearson;group=near_ester:diff ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_cosine;group=near_ester:diff ~ +.3f}} from the flies'; the pairs of an ester with an alcohol are too alike in {{lit:11 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, somata.ester_alcohol.on.n_differ, of n_readings 16}}; and the other pairs differ in none (the first six rows of the table, for one of the readings, and the upper panels of the figure). One single pair goes with the alcohol pairs: 1-5ol with 1-6ol is too far apart in the model in all 16 readings, with APL on and without, and a single pair is a lead and no more. It is the removal of the flies' trial noise that brings the alcohol pairs out. Trial noise makes two odors look less alike than they are, and it does so most for the alcohol pairs: the control flies' trial means put them {{diff:E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=trial_mean;measure=pearson;group=alcohol:mean -- E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=noise_removed;measure=pearson;group=alcohol:mean ~ .2f}} further apart than the estimate without the noise does, for {{diff:E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=trial_mean;measure=pearson;group=ester_alcohol:mean -- E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=noise_removed;measure=pearson;group=ester_alcohol:mean ~ .2f}} to {{diff:E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=trial_mean;measure=pearson;group=ester:mean -- E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=noise_removed;measure=pearson;group=ester:mean ~ .2f}} in the three other groups. Against the trial means the calibrated readout had read the model's alcohol pairs with APL on as the flies', {{E92/somata_model.csv:run=all8;cond=on;reading=cal_pearson:alcohol ~ .3f}} for {{E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=trial_mean;measure=pearson;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}. Read alike, they are {{E92/somata_model.csv:run=all8;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson:alcohol ~ .3f}} with the saturating map and {{E92/somata_model.csv:run=all8;cond=on;reading=linear_z_none_pearson:alcohol ~ .3f}} with the linear one, for the flies' {{E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=ctrl;units=z;reading=noise_removed;measure=pearson;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}. The two groups' differences at the somata have the signs of their errors in the main target, an APL effect too small for the ester pairs and too large for the alcohol pairs, so that the two-signed part of the common error is seen at the somata with APL on, in every reading.

The four ester pairs with near-identical ORN input are too alike in all 16, lying {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=linear_z_none_pearson;group=near_ester:diff ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_cosine;group=near_ester:diff ~ +.3f}} from the flies'; the pairs of an ester with an alcohol are too alike in {{lit:11 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, somata.ester_alcohol.on.n_differ, of n_readings 16}}; and the other pairs differ in none (the first six rows of the table, for one of the readings, and the upper panels of the figure). The two groups' differences at the somata have the signs of their errors in the main target, an APL effect too small for the ester pairs and too large for the alcohol pairs, so that the two-signed part of the common error is seen at the somata with APL on, in every reading.

src: **Without APL the verdict turns on whether a KC's signal saturates with its firing.** With the saturating map of the per-KC reading the model's somata without APL are the flies'. Over its eight readings the four groups lie between {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=saturating_z_expected_pearson;group=ester_alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=saturating_noise_none_cosine;group=other:diff ~ +.3f}} of the flies', none differs by the rule but the other pairs in {{lit:one # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, by_map.saturating.somata_off.other.n_differ: 1 of n_readings 8, and 0 of 8 for ester, alcohol and ester_alcohol}}, and only the four ester pairs with near-identical ORN input are too alike, in {{lit:six # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, by_map.saturating.somata_off.near_ester.n_differ: 6 of n_readings 8}} of the eight. With the linear map the ester pairs, the alcohol pairs and the other pairs are too far apart, by {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=linear_noise_expected_pearson;group=ester:diff ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=linear_z_none_cosine;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}}, in {{lit:6 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, by_map.linear.somata_off.ester.n_differ, of n_readings 8}}, {{lit:7 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, by_map.linear.somata_off.alcohol.n_differ, of n_readings 8}} and {{lit:8 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/verdict_A.json, by_map.linear.somata_off.other.n_differ, of n_readings 8}} of its eight readings (the last six rows of the table, and the lower panels of the figure). The two maps part here and not with APL on because the saturating map compresses a KC's large responses, and without APL the KCs respond to more odors and more strongly. Beside the 16, against the flies in baseline-noise units, raw spike counts are too far apart as well, by up to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=beside;cond=off;reading=raw_cosine;flies_reading=noise_removed;group=other:diff ~ +.3f}}, and the calibrated readout lies between {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=beside;cond=off;reading=cal_cosine;flies_reading=trial_mean;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=beside;cond=off;reading=cal_pearson;flies_reading=noise_removed;group=other:diff ~ +.3f}} of the flies' for the ester, the alcohol and the other pairs. For the alcohol pairs this corrects the earlier comparison of the stages. There the model's somata without APL had read as too alike, which placed the alcohol pairs' excess APL effect at the step without APL; that reading set the calibrated readout against the flies' trial means in the recordings' own unit (in the table, {{E92/somata_model.csv:run=all8;cond=off;reading=cal_pearson:alcohol ~ .3f}} for {{E92/somata_flies.csv:genotype=tnt;units=z;reading=trial_mean;measure=pearson;group=alcohol:mean ~ .3f}}). In none of the 16 readings are the alcohol pairs too alike without APL. With the saturating map they are within {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=saturating_noise_none_cosine;group=alcohol:diff ~ .2f}} of the flies', and with the linear map they lie {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=linear_noise_expected_pearson;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=linear_z_none_cosine;group=alcohol:diff ~ +.3f}} from them, too far apart, which is the opposite sign. Which map is right is a question about the recordings and the indicator, whether a KC's calcium signal saturates over the range of the KC's firing, and not one about the model; these readings cannot answer it.

src: **Over the breadth weightings of APL the two groups move together, and the flies lie off the line.** Through the calibrated readout the 13 weightings hold the ester pairs at {{E92/line_points.csv:readout=cal;line=S;weighting=N_k1:ester ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/line_points.csv:readout=cal;line=S;weighting=F_k2:ester ~ +.3f}} relative to the mean pair, a negative value meaning closer together than the mean pair, and the alcohol pairs at {{E92/line_points.csv:readout=cal;line=S;weighting=none:alcohol ~ +.3f}} to {{E92/line_points.csv:readout=cal;line=S;weighting=S_k2:alcohol ~ +.3f}}, and the two go together. Along the weightings' line the ester pairs' value rises by {{lit:0.2652096271904637 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.slope ~ .2f}} for each unit of the alcohol pairs' (by {{lit:0.5714606526999498 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.slope ~ .2f}} on raw counts; Pearson correlations of {{lit:0.7356313615496841 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.r ~ .2f}} and {{lit:0.7482071151708288 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.r ~ .2f}} over the 13), and no weighting lies further than {{lit:0.009911938135506365 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.max_abs_resid ~ .3f}} from it ({{lit:0.017628248730717194 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.max_abs_resid ~ .3f}} on raw counts). A weighting that holds the ester pairs further apart, relative to the mean pair, holds the alcohol pairs further apart as well. That is the trade which the weightings had shown in the two groups' errors ([above](#breadth-weighting)), read here on the distances themselves. The control flies are not on the line. With APL on their ester pairs are nearly as far apart as the mean pair, at {{lit:-0.05065745385046694 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.ester ~ +.3f}} relative to it, for alcohol pairs at {{lit:-0.23140154814614666 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.alcohol ~ +.3f}}. That puts the flies {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}} from the line through the readout and {{lit:0.10701777447779079 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}} on raw counts, about ten and six times the weightings' largest distance, and {{lit:0.11029610987169114 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.noise_removed_all.resid ~ +.3f}} and {{lit:0.1328880364474679 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.raw.S.flies.noise_removed_all.resid ~ +.3f}} with the trial noise removed from the flies' distances. The family itself lies at {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2:line_cal_resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E92/beside_B.csv:variant=B_F_k2:line_raw_resid ~ +.3f}}, at the edge of the weightings' own scatter.

src: Local APL units had been tried early, on a model without the later mechanisms, and had left the KCs' odor-odor distances where a single APL puts them (among what did not matter, further up), with nothing measured to say how local APL is. The APL calyx maps against the connectome took that measurement from Yang's calcium imaging of APL itself and asked two things of it without fitting a model, both fixed beforehand: whether maps of APL's activity predicted from the wiring match the measured ones, and whether the nearness of glomeruli in the calyx predicts the common error on odors it was not fitted to, by removing 15 % or more of its squared sum and more than permuted glomerulus labels remove. Only with both was a spatially local APL to be fitted in the best family.

src: **What follows.** The feedback APL's inhibition of the KCs is closed in its form. A subtraction clipped at each claw, a subtraction summed over the claws and a gain at the claw read the same or worse on the main target at every weighting, on the fits as they are and at the model's 0.5 s pulse, and the reference stays the family with the clipping at each claw. With the static forms and the flies' form simulated in place of APL ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form); [the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)), the breadth weighting ([above](#breadth-weighting)) and the place where the inhibition is summed ([above](#summed-drive)), nothing is left to vary in how APL inhibits the KCs in this family. Two descriptions stay on APL's side, and neither changes a base. A divisive inhibition at the boutons is the one form that moves the model clearly off the weightings' line toward the flies and gives the alcohol pairs the flies' co-response change without taking from the ester pairs, at a cost in the pattern part and in the mean APL effect at fixed scales; it was not fitted. And on the base with the flies' recruitment the summed form moves the model a tenth to a fifth of the way to the flies' side of the line, under an oracle. APL's other path, the inhibition of the PN boutons, was then still open in its strength and in its form. It has been run since ([below](#bouton-share)): the fitted strength is the best, less or more of the inhibition at the boutons costs, and a gain there costs at every strength, so that APL's side of this family is closed at both of its sites. For the mechanism between the claw and the soma that the lead asks for ([above](#responder-sets)), the brief is now stated on the somata. With APL on it has to hold the ester pairs further apart and the alcohol pairs closer together, by the amounts above, in every reading that treats the two sides alike; this is the two-signed part of the common error. The weightings' line says why no re-weighting, summation or gain of APL's inhibition has done it: whatever holds one group further apart, relative to the mean pair, holds the other further apart too. From here a mechanism is placed against the line, beside the main target and beside the step from claws to somata in wild-type flies, and a change that moves the model along the line is read as one more weighting. Leaving the line toward the flies is asked of a mechanism and does not suffice, controls having left it. The earlier comparison of the stages ([above](#model-stages)) is qualified in two respects. Its lead on the ester pairs is now a difference at the somata in every like-for-like reading, with APL on. Its reading of the alcohol pairs, an excess made at the step without APL by somata that are too alike there, holds only with the calibrated readout set against the flies' trial means: read alike, the alcohol pairs are too far apart with APL on in every reading, and without APL they are the flies' or too far apart, never too alike. Whether anything is asked of the side without APL then depends on whether a KC's calcium signal saturates with the KC's firing, a question about the recordings that is with the pending work at the end of the page. The steps from claws to somata are not read again from all claws: what would let them place the error is still the stage recordings asked of the experimenter. On the input, what leaves the line toward the flies is made glomerulus by glomerulus or odor by odor, fitted to the recordings or taken from single flies, and the rows that have been measured for the glomeruli without input do not leave it ([below](#missing-glomeruli)); what such changes stand for in the flies' input or antennal lobe is open. Every reading here is of the model's 0.5 s pulse without trial noise, in the family without a firing ceiling; the readings at the flies' pulse, through the trial noise and with the ceiling had been kept for a setting that passed, and were not made.

src: **In the fits as they are, about seven tenths of what APL takes from the claws is taken at the boutons.** Over the odor pulse APL removes {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=M2:drive_removed ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P3:drive_removed ~ .2f}} of the claws' summed drive on the eight wirings, and {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P2:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:bouton_share ~ .2f}} of that loss is already made at the boutons, before the feedback inhibition at the claws acts. This bouton share is largest for the KCs with few claws: {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:bouton_share_1-4 ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=M3:bouton_share_1-4 ~ .2f}} for KCs with one to four claws, {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P2:bouton_share_5-8 ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:bouton_share_5-8 ~ .2f}} for those with five to eight and {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P2:bouton_share_9+ ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:bouton_share_9+ ~ .2f}} for those with nine or more, the KCs that the breadth weighting loads at the claws. It hardly depends on the odor, lying between {{E94/a1_by_odor.csv:wiring=P2;odor=1-5ol:bouton_share ~ .2f}} and {{E94/a1_by_odor.csv:wiring=real;odor=euc:bouton_share ~ .2f}} over the 16 odors and the eight wirings, because the subtraction itself hardly does. APL takes {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=M2:bouton_sub_p50 ~ .1f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P3:bouton_sub_p50 ~ .1f}} Hz from the median bouton, {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=M2:bouton_share_removed ~ .2f}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P3:bouton_share_removed ~ .2f}} of the boutons' summed rate, and at the median bouton that amount varies over the 16 odors by {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=P2:sub_cv_over_odors_median_bouton ~ .1%}} to {{E94/a1_path.csv:wiring=real:sub_cv_over_odors_median_bouton ~ .1%}} of its mean (its standard deviation over the odors as a fraction of the mean). APL's inhibition of the boutons therefore works as an offset. Every claw's input is lowered by about the same amount whatever the odor, and a KC loses in proportion to its number of claws, in effect a threshold that APL raises with a KC's claw count. The connectome does not suggest a path of that size: a fraction of {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, all:share_pn ~ .3f}} to {{E94/a2_connectome.csv:set=calyx, assigned, KCs with a type:share_pn ~ .3f}} of APL's output synapses in the calyx is onto PN boutons and the rest onto KCs, according to which synapses are counted. A share of synapses is not a share of inhibition, since nothing says that a synapse onto a bouton and one onto a claw inhibit alike, so that the two numbers are set side by side as a description. At the bouton stage alone the subtraction acts in the direction that the two-signed part of the common error asks for. With APL's activity as saved, it adds {{E94/a3_summary.csv:form=sub;dose=1.0;measure=cosine;signal=evoked;group=ester:change ~ +.3f}} to the cosine distance between the evoked bouton patterns of two ester odors and {{E94/a3_summary.csv:form=sub;dose=1.0;measure=cosine;signal=evoked;group=alcohol:change ~ +.3f}} to that of two alcohol odors at the fitted dose (the mean over the eight wirings), and more for the esters than for the alcohols at every dose and with the gain as well. More inhibition at the boutons had therefore been thought likely to raise the ester pairs' APL effect relative to the alcohol pairs'.

src: APL's inhibition of the PN boutons at other doses and as a gain, against the unchanged fits: the mean over the four wirings of the earlier searches, on the fits as they are with the tied APL scale set again, against the main target as measured, all recordings, through the calibrated readout. The bouton share is given as its range over the four wirings. The squares of the amplitude part and the shape part add up to the squared pattern part, and a spread below one means that APL moves the model's pairs apart more evenly than the flies'; no setting is chosen by a correlation ([why](#fn-pattern-split)). The mean error of a group is the model's per-pair APL effect minus the flies', each side's mean removed, over the 15 ester pairs and over the 6 alcohol pairs. The distance from the weightings' line is positive on the flies' side, and the co-response change is read as trial means at the reading's own noise; in the row of the KC data these two cells are the flies' own, the second with its 90 % interval. The first model row is the reference, and the last row is the family fitted again, for which the last two readings were not made

src: **More inhibition at the boutons costs as well, and does not make up for a weaker weighting.** At twice and at four times the fitted dose the APL→bouton scale is {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_P2:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_real:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} and {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_P2:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_real:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} times the baseline's, above the bound of three, and the bouton share {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_P2:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_real:bouton_share ~ .2f}} and {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_M1:bouton_share ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_real:bouton_share ~ .2f}}. APL then acts almost wholly before the claws, and the tied APL scale falls to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_P1:apl_factor ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_M1:apl_factor ~ .2f}} of the fit's at four times. The pattern part is {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, higher than the fits' in the shape part ({{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} for {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}}), where a change within 0.004 either way had been expected. As far as runs at fixed scales can say, the bound is therefore not what holds the family back. The two groups part. The alcohol pairs' excess shrinks from {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} to {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}, and the ester pairs' shortfall deepens from {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} to {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}}. The reading of the bouton stage had predicted the opposite for the ester pairs: what the subtraction adds to their distance at the boutons is lost again on the way to the KCs' responses, and what a change of APL does to the per-pair effect is once more read from simulations only. Against the weightings' line the two settings stay close to the family's place, at {{E94/line.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E94/line.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} for the family's {{E94/line.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and the flies' {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}}. The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL rises to {{E94/coresponse.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} and {{E94/coresponse.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} from {{E94/coresponse.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}, and at four times the fitted dose it is inside the flies' interval ({{E94/coresponse.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E94/coresponse.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d1;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_hi ~ .2f}}), at a cost of {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d4:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} in the pattern part. At an exponent of 1 more inhibition at the boutons makes the weaker weighting worse: {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k1_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k1_d4;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} at twice and at four times the dose, for {{E94/readings.csv:variant=B_sub_k1_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} at the fitted dose. An offset at the boutons is no substitute for the weighting at the claws.

src: **Realism.** No parameter was added. A scale that the family already has was multiplied, or the subtraction at the boutons was replaced by a gain, and both response rates were held, the one with APL on by the tied APL scale and the one with APL off by the fit's own run. The {{lit:44 # the 24 rows of results/E94_bouton_share/runs_B1.csv, the 8 of runs_B2.csv and the 12 of runs_B3.csv}} runs have response rates of {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.5_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_P1:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.5_M1:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.5_P2:rate_off ~ .3f}} with APL off (ratios of {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.5_M1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}), and the four refits {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=P2:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_on ~ .3f}} and {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=P1:rate_off ~ .3f}} ({{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=real:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=P1:ratio ~ .2f}}), for the flies' {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_tnt_frac ~ .3f}} ({{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}). {{lit:Two # the rows with a realism_flag in results/E94_bouton_share/runs_B1.csv (B_sub_k2_d0_real and B_sub_k2_d0.1_real); none in runs_B2.csv, runs_B3.csv or d_scores.csv; the same two in results/E94_bouton_share/verdict.json, flagged_runs}} runs are outside a band, both on the real wiring and both on the response rate ρ with APL on. Without the bouton path it falls to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0_real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, from the unchanged fit's {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, and at a tenth of the fitted dose it is {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0.1_real:rate_rho_on ~ .3f}}, just under the 0.37 that the band asks; on the three other wirings it is {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0_M1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0_P1:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} without the path. On the real wiring the per-odor pattern of response rates thus needs the boutons' offset as well. Neither setting is a chosen one or the equal, and the choice comes out the same with and without them. Every other run and the four refits are inside the four bands, with a response rate ρ with APL on of {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} or more and a distribution of the number of odors per KC that is at most {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.15_M1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' with APL on (band {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}) and {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=P2:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} with APL off (band {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}). Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, {{lit:six # the rows of results/E94_bouton_share/runs_B2.csv (B_sub_k1_d4_real, B_sub_k1_d4_P2 and B_sub_k1_d4_M1) and runs_B3.csv (B_gain_k2_d0.15_real, B_gain_k2_d0.15_P2 and B_gain_k2_d0.15_M1) with a realism_flag_zcrit and no realism_flag}} more runs would be outside the band on odors per KC with APL on: the exponent of 1 at four times the dose and the gain at 0.15 of the fitted weight, on three wirings each. The largest spike count of a KC to one odor with APL on is {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.02_P2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d0_P1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} over the runs, in a family that nothing bounds there ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). Three things bear on what can be defended. The doses above the fitted one put the APL→bouton scale at {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d2_P2:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} to {{E94/runs_B1.csv:B_sub_k2_d4_real:aplpn_multiple ~ .1f}} times the baseline's, above the bound of three, and they read worse; they do not silence the boutons, the share of bouton-by-odor entries at zero staying at {{E94/runs_B2.csv:B_sub_k1_d4_P2:bouton_zero_share ~ .1%}} or less in every run, where the estimate at APL's saved activity had put it at {{E94/a3_summary.csv:form=sub;dose=2.0;measure=cosine;signal=evoked;group=ester:zero_share ~ .0%}} and {{E94/a3_summary.csv:form=sub;dose=4.0;measure=cosine;signal=evoked;group=ester:zero_share ~ .0%}} at twice and at four times, because the tied APL scale and APL's own activity fall as the dose rises. The gain's divisor at the boutons is small, {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.02_M1:divisor_bouton_p50 ~ .2f}} to {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.15_P1:divisor_bouton_p50 ~ .2f}} at the median bouton and {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.02_M1:divisor_bouton_max ~ .1f}} to {{E94/runs_B3.csv:B_gain_k2_d0.15_P1:divisor_bouton_max ~ .1f}} at the most, which a shunt could do; the form that is easy to defend reads worse. And the family as fitted makes about seven tenths of APL's action on the claws' drive at the boutons, as an offset that hardly depends on the odor, where about a tenth of APL's calyx synapses are. That a synapse onto a bouton and one onto a claw inhibit alike is an assumption and not a measurement, and the model's share is of drive and not of synapses, so that this is reported beside the bands and is not one of them. The verdict was not bought with the bands or bent by them: the two runs outside a band are of settings that read worse in any case. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

src: The late spikes with APL off come from few KCs, with patterns further apart between odors than the onset's (a mean distance of {{E80/pulse_windows.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;window=0.5-1:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}} in the second half second against {{E80/pulse_windows.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;window=0-0.5:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}} in the first). They raise the distances with APL off toward those with APL on, which hardly move (fifth row), so the effect shrinks; the readout's saturation removes most of what the late spikes add to a KC's count, which is why its numbers hold. In the family with the firing ceiling the adaptation cuts the late spikes with APL off as well, and the mean effect falls less; but there the readout has nothing left to compress, so the one number that both definitions give rises with the pulse, to about the breadth-2 fit's loss under the readout (last two columns).

src: **The rows change which KCs respond, and the per-pair APL effect does not follow.** With the fuller input, over the eight wirings and with APL on, the KCs with a claw on VA4 have response rates of {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_2h_on ~ .3f}}, {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_IaA_on ~ .3f}} and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_pa_on ~ .3f}} to 2h, IaA and pa, where with the lab's input they had {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_2h_on ~ .3f}}, {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_IaA_on ~ .3f}} and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=VA4_claw;cls=True:rate_pa_on ~ .3f}} and where the other KCs now have {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=False:rate_2h_on ~ .3f}}, {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=False:rate_IaA_on ~ .3f}} and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=VA4_claw;cls=False:rate_pa_on ~ .3f}}. The KCs with a claw on DA4l or DA3 have {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=DA4l_or_DA3_claw;cls=True:rate_1-5ol_on ~ .3f}} and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=DA4l_or_DA3_claw;cls=True:rate_1-6ol_on ~ .3f}} to 1-5ol and 1-6ol, for {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=DA4l_or_DA3_claw;cls=True:rate_1-5ol_on ~ .3f}} and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=DA4l_or_DA3_claw;cls=True:rate_1-6ol_on ~ .3f}}. These are the odors that the receptors of those glomeruli respond to most. Of the KCs with more than four tenths of their claws on the ten glomeruli, {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=ten_share;cls=above 0.4:silent_share_on ~ .0%}} responded to no odor with APL on and {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=ten_share;cls=above 0.4:silent_share_on ~ .0%}} do now. The KCs with more than four tenths of their claws on any of the 18 glomeruli stay nearly silent, at a response rate of {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=F;kind=zero_filled_share;cls=above 0.4:rate_on ~ .3f}} for {{E93/who_responds_runs.csv:unit=pooled;input=I0;kind=zero_filled_share;cls=above 0.4:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on, since eight glomeruli keep no input. How many KCs respond to each of these five odors hardly changes, by {{lit:0.01 # E93_missing_glomeruli_input.md, Realism: the response fractions of 2h, IaA, pa, 1-5ol and 1-6ol with APL on (columns frac_2h_on to frac_1-6ol_on of results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/runs_B.csv) stay within 0.01 of those of the unchanged fits on every wiring}} of the KCs at most on any wiring, both response rates being held: the rows change which KCs respond and not how many. The main target does not gain from it. At the input the rows make the odors a little more alike, most of all within the two groups of pairs that carry the common error: the distance between two odors' inputs over the claws, as a mean over the pairs, falls from {{E93/input_distances.csv:input=I0;weighting=claw-weighted:ester ~ .3f}} to {{E93/input_distances.csv:input=F;weighting=claw-weighted:ester ~ .3f}} among the ester pairs and from {{E93/input_distances.csv:input=I0;weighting=claw-weighted:alcohol ~ .3f}} to {{E93/input_distances.csv:input=F;weighting=claw-weighted:alcohol ~ .3f}} among the alcohol pairs. In the model the errors of both groups then grow, over the eight wirings from {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} to {{E93/readings.csv:input=F;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_err_ester ~ +.3f}} for the ester pairs, whose APL effect is too small, and from {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} to {{E93/readings.csv:input=F;unit=all8;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} for the alcohol pairs, whose effect is too large (last row but one of the table, for the two sets of wirings). The control with the rows' values shuffled over the odors does not do this (last column of the same row), and it is in these two groups that it differs from the measured rows: input that the odors of a group share is added to pairs whose APL effect the model already misplaces. With one draw of the control this is a description. One pair had been named beforehand, 1-5ol with 1-6ol, the two odors that DA4l and DA3 respond to most. Its APL effect moves away from the flies', from {{E93/readings.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=cal:effect_15ol_16ol ~ +.3f}} to {{E93/readings.csv:input=F;unit=all8;readout=cal:effect_15ol_16ol ~ +.3f}} over the eight wirings for the flies' {{lit:0.1134560353229199 # results/E93_missing_glomeruli_input/verdict.json, pair_15ol_16ol.data: the KC data's APL effect of 1-5ol with 1-6ol, all recordings ~ +.3f}}; a single pair is a lead and no more. Two statistics that are given beside the main target for a change of the responses without APL do not gain either. The target without APL ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)) changes by less than 0.0015 in every population, {{E93/apl_free.csv:input=F;unit=all8;readout=raw;reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E93/apl_free.csv:input=I0;unit=all8;readout=raw;reading=noise_free:pattern ~ .4f}} on raw counts over the eight wirings. src: **For a KC, the best family's APL is close to a fixed raise of the KC's threshold while APL is on. What its APL takes from a KC's drive is nearly the same for every odor, at the PN boutons almost wholly and at the claws for the most part; at the boutons it goes with the KC's number of claws, and at the claws with the breadth weighting. Replaced by a fixed inhibition of each KC that is present only with APL on, the bouton path reads as it did: with each KC's own loss for each odor it is an equal of the family, and with one amount per KC it misses the margin of an equal by a hair, against one half of the recordings. The whole APL replaced in the same way reads three to five thousandths of the pattern part higher through the calibrated readout and, with one amount per KC, no higher on raw counts. The feedback, an inhibition that follows what each odor drives, thus adds little to the family's match, and adds it only through the readout. The number of claws alone can stand in for the bouton path, at a cost of about four thousandths, and cannot stand in for the whole APL. Against no half of the recordings is a setting other than the unchanged fits the best, so that nothing was read on held-out wirings. The offset that the boutons make can be made at the KCs instead. With the bouton path held at a tenth of its fitted strength, a part of the APL→KC weights that is the same on every claw brings back the mean APL effect that the family loses without it, and the family fitted again in that way reads about three thousandths above the unchanged fits, where the refit without that part had read about nine above them. That is just outside the margin of an equal, and such weights are not the connectome's, whose own weights per claw, put in the same place, lose the mean effect. Nothing is gained on the main target, and no base, bound or reference is changed. What is added is a description of the family and a third price. The family's match to the per-pair APL effect rests on a threshold difference per KC between the two conditions, where in the flies' own responses the inhibition grows with an odor's response over all KCs; and about two thirds of what the connectome's bouton share cost after a refit belongs to how the family's APL weights the KCs, and not to the site.** [The PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition](#bouton-share) had left a lead and a price. The lead was that the boutons' offset does for a KC what a higher threshold would do, with APL on only and in proportion to the KC's number of claws. None of the static forms of inhibition tried before had been of that make ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form); [the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)), and the control written for it had not been run. The price was that of holding the bouton path near the connectome's share. Whether it belongs to the site, the boutons themselves being needed, or to the family's weighting of the KCs, which loads the broad KCs and leaves most KCs nearly untouched at the claws, was not known.

src: **In the fits, what APL takes from a KC is close to one amount per KC.** Of the variance, over KCs and odors, of the drive that APL removes at the boutons, {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=P3;site=boutons;kcs=all:share_kc ~ .3f}} to {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=M3;site=boutons;kcs=all:share_kc ~ .3f}} on the eight wirings is an amount per KC that is the same for every odor, and {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=P4;site=boutons;kcs=all:share_odor ~ .3f}} to {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=M2;site=boutons;kcs=all:share_odor ~ .3f}} an amount per odor that is the same for every KC; of what it removes at the claws, the amount per KC holds {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=P3;site=claws;kcs=all:share_kc ~ .3f}} to {{E95/a1_split.csv:wiring=P1;site=claws;kcs=all:share_kc ~ .3f}}. The bouton part is in proportion to the KC's number of claws, with a slope of {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=P2:loglog_slope ~ .2f}} to {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=real:loglog_slope ~ .2f}} on logarithmic axes, and what the number of claws leaves follows the APL→bouton weights of the boutons that the KC samples, at a correlation of {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=P3:pearson_resid_bouton_apl ~ .2f}} to {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=M3:pearson_resid_bouton_apl ~ .2f}}. The claw part follows the family's breadth weighting, at a rank correlation of {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=P1:spearman_c_factor ~ .2f}} to {{E95/a2_per_kc.csv:wiring=real:spearman_c_factor ~ .2f}} with the KC's breadth factor; it is near zero for most KCs and large for the broad ones. Set against the KC's own threshold as the simulator sets it, the fitted somatic threshold plus twice the KC's spontaneous input, the bouton part is {{E95/a3_sizes.csv:wiring=M2;quantity=b:over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}} to {{E95/a3_sizes.csv:wiring=P3;quantity=b:over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}} of the threshold at the median KC, and both parts together {{E95/a3_sizes.csv:wiring=M2;quantity=b+c:over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}} to {{E95/a3_sizes.csv:wiring=P3;quantity=b+c:over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}}. src: **The bouton path is a static inhibition per KC.** Against all recordings the unchanged fits read a pattern part of {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, for a floor of {{data:apl_effect_pattern_floor ~ .4f}} (the figure, and the table). With the bouton path replaced by each KC's own loss for each odor, the population reads {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B5_bko:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher against all recordings and {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B5_bko:d_pattern_halfA ~ .4f}} and {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B5_bko:d_pattern_halfB ~ .4f}} higher against the two halves, inside the 0.003 allowed; its loss on raw counts is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B5_bko:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} higher, where 0.005 was allowed, its mean APL effect is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B5_bko;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} for the fits' {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, and its four runs are inside the bands. It is the one equal. With one amount per KC, the KC's mean loss over the odors, the pattern part is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B1_bk:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher against all recordings and {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B1_bk:d_pattern_halfA ~ .4f}} higher against one of the halves, a hair outside the margin; what the odor adds to the bouton path is at the edge of what the recordings resolve. The number of claws alone does a little less well, at {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B2_nk:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits, and of the powers of that number the proportional one is the best, the others reading {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B3_nk0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} to {{E95/equal.csv:variant=B3_nk2:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits. The two controls say what a rule by the number of claws lacks. With the KCs' own amounts permuted among the KCs with the same number of claws, one draw on each wiring, the pattern part is as low as with each KC's own, {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B4_bk_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B1_bk;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, while the mean APL effect falls to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B4_bk_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and the loss on raw counts rises to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B4_bk_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} from {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B1_bk;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}; permuted over all KCs the pattern part is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B4_bk_permall1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}. For the pattern of the effect it therefore does not matter which boutons a KC samples, beyond how many claws it has; what a rule by the number of claws lacks is that KCs with the same number of claws are not all raised by the same amount. The static forms of the bouton path leave the alcohol pairs' excess a little larger, {{E95/readings.csv:variant=B5_bko;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} for the equal where the fits have {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}. Against each of the four halves of the recordings the lowest pattern part is the unchanged fits' own, among the {{E95/choice.csv:half=A:n_eligible ~ .0f}} settings that could be chosen in this part and the two that follow, the unchanged fits among them, so that nothing went to the four held-out wirings.

src: **The whole APL is close to a static inhibition per KC, and what the feedback adds shows only through the readout.** With every APL scale at zero and each KC given one amount, the sum of its mean losses at the boutons and at the claws, the pattern part through the calibrated readout is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C1_bck:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits. On raw counts nothing is lost: the loss is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=C1_bck;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} for the fits' {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}, and the pattern part {{E95/readings.csv:variant=C1_bck;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}. With each KC's loss for each odor the pattern part is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits through the readout, and {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_pattern_halfA ~ .4f}} and {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_pattern_halfB ~ .4f}} against the two halves; its loss on raw counts is {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} higher, the mean effect on raw counts being smaller, so that it is not an equal, by a hair on the pattern part and by more on raw counts. src: **Fitted again with the component and the bouton path at a tenth, the family misses an equal narrowly, and gets back two thirds of what the refit without the component had lost.** The condition for the refit held, the best setting of the component being {{E95/equal.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits where 0.008 was allowed, and each wiring started from its own best run, which was the largest size on all four. The population reads a pattern part of {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}}, for the unchanged fits' {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} and for the {{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}} of the refit with the bouton path held at the same strength and no component ([above](#bouton-share); the last two rows of the table). That is {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} above the fits against all recordings, and {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:halfA -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:halfA_unchanged ~ .4f}} and {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:halfB -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:halfB_unchanged ~ .4f}} against the two halves, where an equal had to stay within 0.003 against all three. The loss on raw counts is lower than the fits', {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss ~ .4f}} for {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss_unchanged ~ .4f}}, the mean APL effect is the fits' ({{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}), and all four fits are inside the bands. Where the refit without the component had put the spread of the effect at the flies' and lost in its shape ({{E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:shape ~ .4f}}), this one keeps the family's spread ({{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:sd_ratio ~ .2f}} for {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}}) and has a shape part of {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:shape ~ .4f}}, for the fits' {{E95/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}}. By wiring the refit is lower than the unchanged fit on one claw permutation, level on the other and higher on the real wiring and on the matched shuffle, the four moving by {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P2:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P2:pattern_all_unchanged ~ +.4f}} to {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=M1:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=M1:pattern_all_unchanged ~ +.4f}}; on raw counts it is lower on all four. src: **Realism.** No mechanism was added to the base. An inhibition that the fits already make was given back as a fixed amount per KC, or a part was added to the APL→KC weights, and both response rates were held, the one with APL on by one factor in every run and the one with APL off by the fit's own run. The {{lit:88 # the 36 rows of results/E95_static_apl/runs_B.csv, the 24 of runs_C.csv and the 28 of runs_D.csv}} runs have response rates of {{E95/runs_B.csv:B1_bk_real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E95/runs_C.csv:C4_nkck_P1:rate_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E95/runs_B.csv:B1_bk_M1:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E95/runs_B.csv:B1_bk_P2:rate_off ~ .3f}} with APL off (ratios of {{E95/runs_D.csv:D2_connectome_d2_M1:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E95/runs_B.csv:B1_bk_P2:ratio ~ .2f}}), and the four refits {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_on ~ .3f}} to {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P2:rate_on ~ .3f}} and {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=real:rate_off ~ .3f}} to {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P2:rate_off ~ .3f}} ({{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=real:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=P2:ratio ~ .2f}}), for the flies' {{data:noise_ctrl_frac ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_tnt_frac ~ .3f}} ({{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}). {{lit:Four # the rows with a realism_flag in results/E95_static_apl/runs_C.csv (C5_bck_permall1_real, C5_bck_permall1_P1, C5_bck_permall1_P2 and C5_bck_permall1_M1); none in runs_B.csv, runs_D.csv or f_scores.csv; the same four in results/E95_static_apl/verdict.json, flagged_runs}} runs are outside a band, and they are one control on the four wirings. With the whole APL's static amounts permuted over all KCs, the distribution of the number of odors per KC with APL on is {{E95/runs_C.csv:C5_bck_permall1_P1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} to {{E95/runs_C.csv:C5_bck_permall1_M1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' (band {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}), {{E95/runs_C.csv:C5_bck_permall1_M1:static_over_max_drive ~ .0%}} to {{E95/runs_C.csv:C5_bck_permall1_P1:static_over_max_drive ~ .0%}} of the KCs being given more inhibition than their largest drive. It is neither a chosen setting nor an equal. Every other run and the four refits are inside the four bands, with a response rate ρ with APL on of {{E95/runs_B.csv:B4_bk_permall1_real:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} or more and a distribution of the number of odors per KC that is at most {{E95/runs_C.csv:C3_nk_M1:opk_on_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' with APL on and {{E95/f_scores.csv:unit=real:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} with APL off (band {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}). Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as the bands counted until 2026-11-10, {{lit:six # the rows of results/E95_static_apl/runs_C.csv (C3_nk_real, C3_nk_P1, C3_nk_P2 and C3_nk_M1) and runs_D.csv (D2_connectome_d2_real and D2_connectome_d2_P2) with a realism_flag_zcrit and no realism_flag}} more runs would be outside the band on odors per KC with APL on: the whole APL by the number of claws alone on all four wirings, and the connectome's own weights per claw at the largest size on two. The largest spike count of a KC to one odor with APL on is {{E95/runs_B.csv:B3_nk0_P2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} to {{E95/runs_D.csv:D2_connectome_d2_P1:max_count_on ~ .0f}} over the runs, in a family that nothing bounds there ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). Three things bear on what can be defended. As a static inhibition the whole APL asks more than a KC's own threshold of the KCs that it inhibits most: with one amount per KC, {{E95/runs_C.csv:C1_bck_P2:static_over_thr_max ~ .1f}} to {{E95/runs_C.csv:C1_bck_P1:static_over_thr_max ~ .1f}} times the threshold at the most and {{E95/runs_C.csv:C1_bck_M1:static_over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}} to {{E95/runs_C.csv:C1_bck_P1:static_over_thr_p50 ~ .2f}} at the median KC, where the bouton path's static form stays at {{E95/runs_B.csv:B1_bk_P1:static_over_thr_max ~ .2f}} of the threshold or less. The unweighted component is not in the connectome. It puts APL→KC weight on every claw alike, on the claws without an APL synapse as on the others, and the connectome's own weights per claw, which could be defended, lose the mean effect. And the equal is further from the flies at the step from claws to somata. Read like for like with the saturating map ([above](#steps-like-for-like)), with the claws taken from their settled level before the odor ([footnote](#fn-preodor-startup)), its step with APL on over the 66 pairs of the stage recordings is {{preodor_startup_check_viki/E95_static_apl_steps_settled.csv:family=B5_bko;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson;group=all66:model_settled ~ .2f}}, where the family's is {{preodor_startup_check_viki/E95_static_apl_steps_settled.csv:family=C2;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson;group=all66:model_settled ~ .2f}} and the flies' {{E95/steps.csv:family=C2;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson;group=all66:flies ~ .2f}}: the static form inhibits the KC and not its boutons, and its claws read more alike ({{preodor_startup_check_viki/E95_static_apl_steps_settled.csv:family=B5_bko;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson;group=all66:claw_model_settled ~ .2f}} for {{preodor_startup_check_viki/E95_static_apl_steps_settled.csv:family=C2;cond=on;reading=saturating_z_none_pearson;group=all66:claw_model_settled ~ .2f}}). This is a description of the one equal, and no other setting was read there. The verdict was not bought with the bands or bent by them: the only runs outside a band are a control's. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

src: **What follows.** Nothing is gained on the main target. The reference stays the family as fitted, no base and no bound is changed, and the static forms and the component are readings and not candidates. Three things are carried from here. The first is a description of the family. For the main target its APL is close to a table of thresholds: a fixed raise per KC that is present only with APL on, set at the boutons by the KC's number of claws and at the claws by the breadth weighting. What the feedback adds to that is three to five thousandths of the pattern part through the calibrated readout, and on raw counts nothing for the pattern. The flies' inhibition is not of that kind. In their own responses it grows with an odor's response over all KCs, and with its strengths permuted over the odors the gain is gone ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)). A change on APL's side that is to move the main target would therefore have to change which KCs' thresholds rise with APL on, or make the inhibition depend on the odor as the family's does not; none is proposed here. That the feedback's part shows only through the readout also bears on the choice, still to be made, of the reading that carries the model's side of the main target (the pending work at the end of the page). The second is a third price for the connectome's bouton share, beside the two already given ([above](#bouton-share)). Holding the bouton path at a tenth of its fitted strength costs {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} of the pattern part at fixed scales and {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} after a refit with the family's weights, and {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} after a refit in which a part of the APL→KC weights reaches every claw alike. The connectome's weights do not do that, and its own weights per claw, at fixed scales, lose the mean effect. Whether a limit on the bouton share replaces the bound on the APL→bouton scale, and at which of these prices, is still a choice to be made, and nothing here makes it. The third narrows an earlier statement. That no static inhibition does better in the model than its feedback APL holds, and one made of the family's own loss per KC comes within a few thousandths of it, as the earlier ones, set by an odor's strength and a KC's breadth, did not ([above](#inhibition-form); [above](#responder-sets)). Two readings are left for planning, and neither has been run: the family fitted with a static inhibition per KC and no feedback, which would say whether the feedback is needed at all for the main target, and APL→KC weights that reach every claw from the anatomy and not uniformly, which would say whether the three thousandths that remain at the connectome's bouton share are got back with weights that the connectome has (the pending work at the end of the page). The second has since been run ([below](#offclaw-synapses)): with the synapses that APL makes on the KCs outside their claws as such weights, the refit reads {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} above the fits, so that the three thousandths are not got back, and a part of the mean APL effect is lost besides. The two groups of the common error are where they were. Against the weightings' line ([above](#steps-like-for-like)) every setting but the permuted control of the whole APL stays at the family's place or a little further from the flies, between {{E95/line.csv:variant=C4_nkck;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E95/line.csv:variant=B5_bko;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} for the family's {{E95/line.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and the flies' {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}}. The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL stays below the flies' interval ({{E95/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E95/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_hi ~ .2f}}) in every setting that holds the mean APL effect, the family's being {{E95/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}; it enters the interval only for the whole APL by the number of claws alone and for the connectome's own weights per claw at the two larger sizes, which lose the mean effect. The limits of these readings are those of runs at fixed scales. The second, third and fourth parts set one factor again on four wirings and left every other parameter at the fit's, and only the refit moved the others, by one search from one start on each wiring. The static amounts are the fits' own losses, so that they say what the fitted APL does and are not a mechanism with a source of its own, and a family fitted without feedback was not run. The margin of an equal is a line, and three settings lie within a few ten-thousandths of it on one side or the other: the bouton path with one amount per KC, the whole APL with each KC's loss for each odor, and the refit. Every reading here is of the model's 0.5 s pulse without trial noise, in the family without a firing ceiling; the readings with the ceiling, at the flies' pulse and through the trial noise had been kept for a setting that passed, and a reading at the flies' pulse of the whole APL's static form for an equal of it, and none was made.

src: APL's synapses on the KCs outside the claws was run on the breadth-2 family, each wiring at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)) and with the lab's input throughout, in three parts. The first simulated nothing. In the connectome table that the model's weights are read from, and with the same filters, it split APL's synapses onto each of the model's KCs into those on a claw that the wiring keeps, those on a claw that it drops, those in the calyx on no claw and those in the peduncle, and set the counts against the KC's number of claws and against what the bouton path takes from the KC in its fit; in tables derived from four connectomes in separate work it also read how many of APL's calyx synapses onto KCs lie away from the KC's claws, a reading that is withheld here, the use of those tables being on hold ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)). The second ran at fixed scales on the four wirings of the earlier searches. The bouton path was held at a tenth of its fitted strength, the setting nearest the connectome's share ([above](#bouton-share)), and the off-claw component was added to the APL→KC weights where the unweighted component had been ([above](#static-threshold)), with the calyx alone and with the peduncle's, each at sizes of 0.5, 1 and 2. Beside them the component with the peduncle's was run in the summed form ([APL's inhibition on the KC's summed drive](#summed-drive)) at the three sizes, with the summed form without a component as the reference of those runs; at a size of 1 with its counts permuted among the KCs with the same number of claws and over all KCs, as controls; and at a size of 1 with no bouton path at all. All of APL's counted synapses were also given without the breadth weighting, each kept claw with its own count and the KC's synapses outside the claws spread over its claws, in the proportion in which they are counted, at the three sizes. In every run the tied APL scale was set again until the number of responses with APL on was the fit's; the somatic threshold and the KC–KC scale stayed the fit's and the responses with APL off are the fit's own, so that both response rates are held. Before any run was scored the new code was checked. On the real wiring it reproduces three earlier runs without one differing spike count: with a component of size zero, the run at a tenth of the fitted dose; with the component made uniform, the run with the unweighted component; and with the summed form and no component, the earlier run of that form. On all eight wirings its counts on the kept claws are the model's weights, claw by claw. What would count had been fixed as it was for the unweighted component ([above](#static-threshold)). A setting was to be read on the four held-out wirings, against the other half of the recordings, if its pattern part through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) was the lowest against one half and lower than the unchanged fits' by 0.0015 or more, with the unweighted component at the same size as its control. A setting was an equal of the family if its pattern part stayed within 0.003 of the family's against all recordings and against both halves of the first split of the flies, with its loss on raw counts no more than 0.005 higher, its mean APL effect within 0.01 of the family's and its runs inside the realism bands. And if the best setting of the off-claw component came within 0.008 of the unchanged fits, the family was to be fitted again on the four wirings of the earlier searches, with the bouton path held at a tenth and the size of the component free beside the family's other parameters: with the calyx alone unless the component with the peduncle's had read lower by more than 0.0005, and from two starts on each wiring, the wiring's own best run with the component and its refit with the unweighted component, the one component exchanged for the other at the same size. Of a wiring's two fits the one that ended at the lower value of the fit's own loss was to be kept, and the refit was to count as reading as well as the one with the unweighted component if it came within 0.0015 of it. Refits on the four held-out wirings had been kept for an equal.
