src: **Two fifths of APL's calyx synapses onto the model's KCs are not in the model's weights, and nearly every KC has some of them.** Of the {{E96/a2_distances.csv:kind=all;to=any_claw:n ~ ,.0f}} synapses that APL makes on the model's KCs in the calyx, the weights hold {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=kept:synapses ~ ,.0f}}, or {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=kept:share_of_calyx ~ .1%}}; {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:synapses ~ ,.0f}} lie on no claw and {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=dropped_claw:synapses ~ ,.0f}} on claws that the wiring drops, and {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=peduncle:synapses ~ ,.0f}} more lie in the peduncle. The synapses on no claw are not strays at a claw's edge. They lie a median of {{E96/a2_distances.csv:kind=no_claw;to=any_claw:d_p50 ~ .1f}} µm from the KC's nearest PN→KC synapse on a claw, where those on the kept claws lie {{E96/a2_distances.csv:kind=kept;to=any_claw:d_p50 ~ .1f}} µm from it. They are spread over nearly all KCs: {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:kcs_none_share ~ .1%}} of the KCs have none in the calyx and {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw+peduncle:kcs_none_share ~ .1%}} none in the calyx or the peduncle, so that as a part of the weights they leave {{E96/a1_per_claw.csv:quantity=comp_offclaw:zero_share ~ .1%}} of the claws without any with the calyx alone and {{E96/a1_per_claw.csv:quantity=comp_offclaw_ped:zero_share ~ .1%}} with the peduncle's, where the connectome's own weights per claw leave {{E95/a4_weights.csv:wiring=real:zero_share ~ .0%}}. And they grow with a KC's number of claws, less than in proportion. KCs with 1 to 4, with 5 to 8 and with 9 or more claws have a mean of {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=1-4:no_claw_mean ~ .1f}}, {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=5-8:no_claw_mean ~ .1f}} and {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=9+:no_claw_mean ~ .1f}} of them in the calyx, and of {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=1-4:no_claw+peduncle_mean ~ .1f}}, {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=5-8:no_claw+peduncle_mean ~ .1f}} and {{E96/a1_by_type_class.csv:by=claw_class;group=9+:no_claw+peduncle_mean ~ .1f}} with the peduncle's. On logarithmic axes the slopes are {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:loglog_slope_n ~ .2f}} and {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw+peduncle:loglog_slope_n ~ .2f}}, where the synapses on the kept claws have {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=kept:loglog_slope_n ~ .2f}}, what the bouton path takes from a KC in its fit {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=b:loglog_slope_n ~ .2f}} and the unweighted component, by its make, 1. Among KCs with the same number of claws the counts in the calyx have a coefficient of variation of {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:within_cv_min ~ .2f}} to {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:within_cv_max ~ .2f}}, of the order of that of what the bouton path takes ({{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=b:within_cv_min ~ .2f}} to {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=b:within_cv_max ~ .2f}}), and they do not follow it, the median correlation being {{E96/a1_counts.csv:kind=no_claw:within_r_b_median ~ .2f}}. Counted in synapses, those on no claw in the calyx are {{E96/runs_B.csv:B1_offclaw_d0.5_real:synapse_share ~ .2f}} of what a KC then receives from APL, on its kept claws and outside them, and with the peduncle's {{E96/runs_B.csv:B2_offclawped_d0.5_real:synapse_share ~ .2f}}. The counts are those of one connectome, the hemibrain, in the tables that the model reads. In tables derived from four connectomes in separate work, with a synapse taken as outside the claws when it lies more than 2 µm from the KC's nearest claw, it was also read what share of APL's calyx synapses onto KCs lies outside the claws and how their number per KC goes with the KC's number of claws. The use of those tables is on hold, and both readings are withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)); no run, component, refit or verdict of this subsection used them.

src: **At fixed scales the off-claw component reads on the pattern part as the unweighted component did, and it does not hold the mean APL effect.** Against all recordings the unchanged fits read a pattern part of {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, for a floor of {{data:apl_effect_pattern_floor ~ .4f}}, and the bouton path at a tenth with nothing in its place {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} (the table). With the off-claw component the pattern part is {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} over the three sizes with the calyx alone and {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} with the peduncle's, where the unweighted component had read {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}. Size for size the two differ by {{E96/vs_uniform.csv:B2_offclawped_d1:d_pattern_z8 ~ +.4f}} to {{E96/vs_uniform.csv:B2_offclawped_d0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ +.4f}}. On the pattern of the effect the synapses outside the claws thus do what the uniform part did. At fixed scales that is little: neither part moves the pattern part far from the run with nothing in the boutons' place, and every setting that could be chosen stays {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d2:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} to {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits. On the mean they do not do it. The mean APL effect is {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} with the calyx alone and {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} with the peduncle's, falling as the component grows, where the unweighted component had held {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, the fits have {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} and the flies {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}. With nothing in the boutons' place it is {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D0;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, so that the component with the peduncle's brings back about half of the lost mean at the most, and the calyx alone, at the two larger sizes, none of it. With the off-claw component the loss on raw counts is {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}, for the fits' {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} and the unweighted component's {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d2;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=raw:z8_loss ~ .4f}}. What the off-claw component has for itself is the spread of the effect, {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} of the flies' for the fits' {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} and the unweighted component's {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_sd_ratio ~ .2f}}; its cost against the fits is in the shape part ({{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}} for {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_shape ~ .4f}}). No setting is an equal. Two are inside the 0.003 on the pattern part against all recordings and both halves, all of APL's counted synapses and the summed form with the component, each at the largest size, and every setting misses on the other two counts: the mean APL effect moves by {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d2:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} from the fits', where 0.01 either way was allowed, and the loss on raw counts is {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B3_offclawped_d0.5_pool1:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} to {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d2:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} higher, where 0.005 was. Against three of the four halves of the recordings the lowest pattern part among the {{E96/choice.csv:half=A:n_eligible ~ .0f}} settings that could be chosen, the unchanged fits among them, is the fits' own. Against the fourth, all of APL's counted synapses at the largest size are lower by {{E96/choice.csv:half=D:gain ~ .5f}}, where 0.0015 had been asked for a reading on the held-out wirings, so that nothing went to them.

src: **Which KCs the synapses outside the claws are on carries nothing that a shuffle loses, and what loses the mean is not isolated.** With the counts of the component with the peduncle's permuted among the KCs with the same number of claws, one draw on each wiring, the pattern part is {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B4_offclawped_d1_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for the {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} of the counts themselves, and the mean APL effect {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B4_offclawped_d1_permclaw1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} for {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}. Permuted over all KCs, which removes their relation to the number of claws as well, they read {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B4_offclawped_d1_permall1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B4_offclawped_d1_permall1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}. The result does not rest on the other choices either. Without any bouton path the component reads {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B5_offclawped_d1_dose0;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, as it does with a tenth of it. In the summed form it reads {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B3_offclawped_d2_pool1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B3_offclawped_d1_pool1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, nowhere the 0.0015 below the clipped form that had been asked for a fit of its own; the summed form without a component, the reference of those runs, has the lowest pattern part of all, {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B3_pool1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, and loses the mean effect ({{E96/readings.csv:variant=B3_pool1;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}) and, on the real wiring, the per-odor pattern of the response rates (the paragraph on realism). With all of APL's counted synapses the pattern part is {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and the mean APL effect {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, where the connectome's own weights per claw had given {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D2_connectome_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} ([above](#static-threshold)): a part of the mean that those weights had lost comes back with the synapses that were missing, and size for size the mean is still {{E96/vs_uniform.csv:B6_allsyn_d0.5:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E96/vs_uniform.csv:B6_allsyn_d2:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} from the unweighted component's. What the unweighted component did for the mean is therefore not done by reaching nearly every KC. The off-claw component differs from it in two respects. A KC's total grows with its number of claws less than in proportion, and the weight is not the same from claw to claw. No run separates the two. As a description, at each of the three sizes the mean effect falls in the order of the second and not of the first (the table below), and the counts permuted over all KCs, which have no relation to the number of claws left, keep the mean of the counts themselves. The runs that separate the two have since been made ([below](#weight-evenness)): the first carries none of the loss, and of the second what carries it is the inequality of the amounts among KCs with the same number of claws.

src: Those pairs stay a target of their own, at about half the flies' APL effect and short mostly with APL on. What holds them apart in the flies is then not a transfer of this kind at the claw, nor a fixed change of the input ([above](#input-side)), nor the differences between flies in what reaches the KCs, which move these pairs apart with APL on and with APL off alike ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)); for inhibition that follows the calyx space that glomeruli share, the reading made with a static proxy is withheld with the connectome tables that it rests on ([above](#apl-calyx-maps)).

src: **Fitted again with the off-claw component and the bouton path at a tenth, the family reads about four thousandths above the unchanged fits: as the refit with the unweighted component on the pattern part, and not on the mean.** The condition for the refit held, the best setting of the component, the calyx alone at the smallest size, being {{E96/equal.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d0.5:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} above the fits where 0.008 was allowed. At their best sizes the calyx alone and the component with the peduncle's were within 0.0005 of each other ({{E96/readings.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and {{E96/readings.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}), so that the calyx alone was fitted, the form that does not rest on where in a KC the peduncle's synapses act; the summed form and all of APL's counted synapses had not met the conditions for fits of their own. The population of the four kept fits reads a pattern part of {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}}, for the unchanged fits' {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} (the last three rows of the table). src: **What follows.** Nothing is gained on the main target. The reference stays the family as fitted, no base and no bound is changed, and the off-claw component is a reading and not a candidate. Three things are carried from here. The first is a fourth price for the connectome's bouton share, and the first with weights that the connectome has. Holding the bouton path at a tenth of its fitted strength costs {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} of the pattern part at fixed scales. After a refit it costs {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} with the family's weights, {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} with the unweighted component, which the connectome does not have, and {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} with the off-claw component, which it has. The last comes with a mean APL effect of {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} for the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, with a loss on raw counts {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:raw_loss_unchanged ~ .4f}} above the fits', and with somatic thresholds and KC–KC scales away from the fits'. Whether a limit on the bouton share replaces the bound on the APL→bouton scale, and at which of these prices, is still a choice to be made, and nothing here makes it. The second is what the boutons' offset stands in for. For the pattern of the effect, the synapses that the model's weights had left out do at the KCs what the uniform part did, so that the three to four thousandths that stay with the connectome's bouton share are not a matter of reaching every claw. For the mean APL effect they do not, and which property of the uniform part held the mean is open: a KC's total in proportion to its number of claws, or a weight that is the same from claw to claw. The third is three leads for planning, and none has been run. One is the pair of runs that would separate those two properties: the off-claw counts rescaled so that a KC's total grows in proportion to its number of claws, against the same amounts per KC made unequal from claw to claw. Another is the same reading with the counts of another connectome, which needs that connectome's wiring in the model's format. The last is where on the dendrite the synapses outside the claws lie, relative to the claws that an odor drives, which the model does not represent. The first of the three has since been run ([below](#weight-evenness)), and the question above is closed: the uniform part held the mean by giving KCs with the same number of claws equal amounts, and not by a total in proportion to the number of claws. The two groups of the common error are where they were. Against the weightings' line ([above](#steps-like-for-like)) every setting with a component stays at the family's place or a little further from the flies, between {{E96/line.csv:variant=B6_allsyn_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E96/line.csv:variant=B3_offclawped_d0.5_pool1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} for the family's {{E96/line.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and the flies' {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}}, and the alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL stays below the flies' interval ({{E96/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E96/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_hi ~ .2f}}) in every setting, at {{E96/coresponse.csv:variant=B2_offclawped_d0.5;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E96/coresponse.csv:variant=B1_offclaw_d2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} for the family's {{E96/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}}. The limits are those of runs at fixed scales and of local searches. The second part set one factor again on four wirings and left every other parameter at the fit's. The refits are one search from each of two starts on a wiring, of {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P1;start=e95:n_evals ~ .0f}} to {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=P2;start=own:n_evals ~ .0f}} evaluations, and the rule that kept one of the two was the fit's own loss and not the pattern part. The margins are lines: the refit lies {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}} from the refit with the unweighted component, where 0.0015 was allowed, and {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} from the fits, where 0.003 was. Nothing here was read on the four held-out wirings. The counts are one connectome's as the model's loader reads it, and what the counts of other connectomes are like is among the readings that are withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)); the run in which a KC's count no longer follows its number of claws is the shuffle over all KCs, which read as the counts themselves did. Every reading here is of the model's 0.5 s pulse without trial noise, in the family without a firing ceiling; the readings with the ceiling, at the flies' pulse and through the trial noise had been kept for a setting that passed, and none was made.

src: **With the bouton path near the connectome's share, what loses the mean APL effect when APL's counted synapses are put in the bouton path's place is that KCs with the same number of claws get unequal amounts. That a KC's amount grows with its number of claws less than in proportion loses none of it. With the inequality removed and the slope kept, the synapses outside the claws hold the mean as the part that is the same on every claw does; with the slope removed and the inequality kept, they lose what they had lost. For the connectome's own weights on the claws the amounts per KC carry most of the loss through the calibrated readout and how the synapses lie over a KC's claws little of it; on raw counts the two share it. Half the inequality of the counts outside the claws already loses about a hundredth of the mean, and every part made of each KC's counted synapses is more unequal than that, so that none holds the mean however it is spread, and the family was not fitted again. The bouton path of the best family is not equal among such KCs either: it holds the mean in the other way, by following what each KC loses. The pattern part stays where it was in every setting. Nothing is gained on the main target, and no base, bound or reference is changed. What is added is the reason for the lost mean that goes with the fourth price of the connectome's bouton share.** [APL's synapses on the KCs outside the claws](#offclaw-synapses) had left that reason open. With the bouton path held at a tenth of its fitted strength, the unweighted component holds the mean APL effect, and the parts made of APL's counted synapses lose some of it: the off-claw component, all of APL's counted synapses and, most of all, the connectome's own weights per claw ([above](#static-threshold)). The counted parts differ from the unweighted component in three ways that no run had separated. A KC's amount, the sum of the part's weights over the KC's claws, grows with the KC's number of claws less than in proportion (the slope). KCs with the same number of claws get unequal amounts (the inequality). And where the synapses are on the claws, they lie unevenly over a KC's claws (the placement).

src: The experiment on the evenness of APL's weights among KCs and over a KC's claws was run on the breadth-2 family as the two before it were ([above](#static-threshold); [above](#offclaw-synapses)): on the four wirings of the earlier searches, each at its own fit ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)) and with the lab's input, with the bouton path at a tenth of its fitted strength and a part added to the family's APL→KC weights, its size in the unit of the unweighted component. In every run the tied APL scale was set again until the number of responses with APL on was the fit's; the somatic threshold and the KC–KC scale stayed the fit's and the responses with APL off are the fit's own, so that both response rates are held. Each new part changes one of the three properties of a counted part and keeps the others. Four were made from the counts outside the claws in the calyx, the off-claw component's. With the slope removed, every group of KCs with the same number of claws has the same amount per claw and each KC keeps its count relative to its group's mean. With the inequality removed, every KC has its group's mean. With half the inequality, each KC lies halfway between its own count and its group's mean. As presence alone, every KC that has such a synapse has the same amount per claw and the others none. The first two were run also at a size of 2 and with the peduncle's synapses. Two were made from the connectome's own weights on the claws: each KC's amount kept and spread evenly over its claws, and every KC given the same amount per claw, placed over its claws as its synapses lie. And each KC's count of all of APL's synapses, on the claws that the wiring keeps and outside the claws, was spread evenly over the KC's claws, with the peduncle's and without, at sizes of 0.5, 1 and 2. These last, and the amounts on the claws spread evenly, are counts as counted; the others are rearrangements that no connectome holds, made to isolate one property. A group with fewer than 20 KCs was joined to the group with the next lower number of claws. Before any run was scored the new code was checked. On the real wiring it reproduces four earlier runs without one differing spike count, those with the unweighted component, with the connectome's own weights per claw, with the off-claw component and with all of APL's counted synapses, and on each of the four wirings the two parts made from a count multiply back to it, claw by claw. What would count had been fixed beforehand. The loss of a counted part is the gap between its mean APL effect and the unweighted component's at the same size, for the mean over the four wirings through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout). A property carries the loss if removing it alone brings back 0.6 of the gap or more while removing the other brings back less than 0.25, and the reading holds by wiring if three of the four wirings give it from their own values. The family was to be fitted again with all counted synapses spread evenly, the bouton path held at a tenth, only if that part held a mean APL effect of +0.168 or more, within 0.01 of the flies', with a pattern part within 0.0015 of the unweighted component's at the same size. Only the counts as counted could be chosen against a half of the recordings or be an equal, by the rules of the two experiments before. And two descriptions of the seven means that had been saved, the mean APL effect falling with the variance of a part's weight per claw as a whole, or with its parts among KCs and within KCs separately, were written down with their predictions for every new setting before the first run.

And each KC's count of all of APL's synapses, on the claws that the wiring keeps and outside the claws, was spread evenly over the KC's claws, with the peduncle's and without, at sizes of 0.5, 1 and 2. These last, and the amounts on the claws spread evenly, are counts as counted; the others are rearrangements that no connectome holds, made to isolate one property. A group with fewer than 20 KCs was joined to the group with the next lower number of claws. Before any run was scored the new code was checked. On the real wiring it reproduces four earlier runs without one differing spike count, those with the unweighted component, with the connectome's own weights per claw, with the off-claw component and with all of APL's counted synapses, and on each of the four wirings the two parts made from a count multiply back to it, claw by claw. What would count had been fixed beforehand. The loss of a counted part is the gap between its mean APL effect and the unweighted component's at the same size, for the mean over the four wirings through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout). A property carries the loss if removing it alone brings back 0.6 of the gap or more while removing the other brings back less than 0.25, and the reading holds by wiring if three of the four wirings give it from their own values. The family was to be fitted again with all counted synapses spread evenly, the bouton path held at a tenth, only if that part held a mean APL effect of +0.168 or more, within 0.01 of the flies', with a pattern part within 0.0015 of the unweighted component's at the same size. Only the counts as counted could be chosen against a half of the recordings or be an equal, by the rules of the two experiments before. And two descriptions of the seven means that had been saved, the mean APL effect falling with the variance of a part's weight per claw as a whole, or with its parts among KCs and within KCs separately, were written down with their predictions for every new setting before the first run.

src: **The pattern part does not separate the settings.** Against all recordings the new settings read a pattern part of {{E99/readings.csv:variant=T2_d2;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E99/readings.csv:variant=W2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, for the unchanged fits' {{E99/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}}, the unweighted component's {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d0.5;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} to {{E95/readings.csv:variant=D1_uniform_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} and a floor of {{data:apl_effect_pattern_floor ~ .4f}}; the amplitude part, the shape part and the spread of the effect are in the table. Against three of the four halves of the recordings the lowest pattern part among the {{E99/choice.csv:half=A:n_eligible ~ .0f}} settings that could be chosen, the unchanged fits among them, is the fits' own. Against the fourth, all of APL's counted synapses without the peduncle's at the largest size are lower by {{E99/choice.csv:half=D:gain ~ .4f}}, where 0.0015 had been asked for a reading on the held-out wirings, so that nothing went to them. No setting is an equal either: the mean APL effect moves by {{E99/equal.csv:variant=T1_d0.5:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E99/equal.csv:variant=W1_d1:d_mean_effect ~ +.3f}} from the fits', where 0.01 either way was allowed, and the loss on raw counts is {{E99/equal.csv:variant=T1_d0.5:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} to {{E99/equal.csv:variant=W1_d1:d_raw_loss ~ .4f}} higher, where 0.005 was. The two groups of the common error are where they were. Against the weightings' line ([above](#steps-like-for-like)) every new setting stays at the family's place or a little further from the flies, between {{E99/line.csv:variant=W2_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and {{E99/line.csv:variant=W1_d1;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} for the family's {{E99/line.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:resid ~ +.3f}} and the flies' {{lit:0.09866993033793536 # results/E92_steps_like_for_like/line.json, lines.cal.S.flies.trial_mean_all.resid ~ +.3f}}. The alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL is {{E99/coresponse.csv:variant=K2_offclawped_d1;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E99/coresponse.csv:variant=T2_d2;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} over the new settings, for the family's {{E99/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} and the flies' interval of {{E99/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E99/coresponse.csv:variant=ref;reading=r1;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:flies_hi ~ .2f}}. It stays below the interval in every new setting but one, all of APL's counted synapses without the peduncle's at the largest size, which reaches the interval's lower edge and holds the least of the mean among the parts of all counted synapses.

src: **In the only recordings in which APL and the KCs' dendrites in the calyx, their claws, were imaged together, the two channels hold what they were taken to hold, and what the recordings were read for is not decided. A little of APL's green signal appears in the red channel of the KCs, and the size of that leak, measured in the two flies in which only APL carried an indicator, does not carry from one of them to the other. By the rule fixed beforehand, every reading of the KC channel with the leak taken out is then not decided, and with it whether APL's response is one function of the claws' response and whether APL's calcium follows the claws place by place; what is reported is how strongly the APL channel responds. There the flies' APL responds several times as strongly to pa as to ms, where the best family's APL responds about a quarter more strongly to pa than to ms. By the rule fixed beforehand the family is still inside the flies' interval, which is wide, through the steepest readings of the indicator and one estimate of ms's input; read in proportion it is flatter than the flies under every estimate. On the model's side that flatness is not made by APL. The family's APL follows the summed input to its claws, with APL on and with APL off, and the claws follow the PNs' summed response, which is nearly the same for pa and ms with the lab's input; with Hallem's receptor data as the input the same fits separate the two odors two to three times. Within a fly, APL rises faster than the KC channel from ms to pa and along concentration, and in five of the seven flies APL's map follows the KC channel's place by place, as recorded and with the leak taken out; both are leads and not results, since both rest on the KC channel. The experimenter who made the recordings has not yet checked their quality. No model is changed, and nothing is scored on the main target.**

src: The best family assumes two things about APL that a recording of APL alone cannot test: that APL is driven by the summed input to the KCs' claws, and that one APL variable serves the whole calyx. In its fits APL's activity is nearly the same for every odor of the panel ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)). Of two comparisons of that activity with the flies' own APL, one has since found the model's APL flatter than the flies' along concentration ([the strength of APL's response in the flies against the model's APL](#apl-strength), the next subsection) and one is still running (with the pending work at the end of the page). For a model's APL that is flatter than the flies', two repairs stand open that those comparisons cannot tell apart: a drive of APL by the KCs' spikes ([what drives APL](#apl-drive)), or a weaker normalization in the antennal lobe ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)). Under the first the flies' APL departs from the summed response of their claws; under the second it follows the claws, and it is the claws' own response that the model makes too even. The dual-colour recordings are the only ones that hold both sides: calcium in APL through a green indicator and in the KCs' claws through a red one, in the same plane of the same fly, with pa, paa and ms as concentration series. The claws' own map also stands where a prediction from the wiring would: whether APL's calcium follows the activity around it had been asked only through maps predicted from where the PN boutons lie ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)), which rest on connectome tables whose use is on hold and are withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)), and here it could be asked of the flies without a connectome. The experiment changes no model and scores nothing on the main target, so that [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect), its mean part and its pattern part stay where they are.

In its fits APL's activity is nearly the same for every odor of the panel ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)). Of two comparisons of that activity with the flies' own APL, one has since found the model's APL flatter than the flies' along concentration ([the strength of APL's response in the flies against the model's APL](#apl-strength), the next subsection) and one is still running (with the pending work at the end of the page). For a model's APL that is flatter than the flies', two repairs stand open that those comparisons cannot tell apart: a drive of APL by the KCs' spikes ([what drives APL](#apl-drive)), or a weaker normalization in the antennal lobe ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)). Under the first the flies' APL departs from the summed response of their claws; under the second it follows the claws, and it is the claws' own response that the model makes too even. The dual-colour recordings are the only ones that hold both sides: calcium in APL through a green indicator and in the KCs' claws through a red one, in the same plane of the same fly, with pa, paa and ms as concentration series. The claws' own map also stands where a prediction from the wiring would: whether APL's calcium follows the activity around it had been asked only through maps predicted from where the PN boutons lie ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)), which rest on connectome tables whose use is on hold and are withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)), and here it could be asked of the flies without a connectome. The experiment changes no model and scores nothing on the main target, so that [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect), its mean part and its pattern part stay where they are.

src: **What was read, and by which rules.** The verdicts rest on {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=L:recordings ~ .0f}} recordings from {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=L:flies ~ .0f}} flies, those that the experimenter listed as the dual-colour data; {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=V0:recordings ~ .0f}} earlier recordings of the same kind, from {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=V0:flies ~ .0f}} flies, are read beside them as a repetition and decide nothing. A response is the change in fluorescence over its baseline around its peak, averaged inside the outline of the calyx, as the mean over a stimulus's presentations with the response to the solvent in the same recording subtracted. Flies are the units, a ratio of two responses is the geometric mean over the flies, and its interval is the one in which nine in ten resamplings of the flies fall. Three things were asked, each with a verdict fixed before any map was read. The first needs no model: whether, within a fly, APL's response is one function of the claws' summed response whatever the odor. It is read as the difference between two odors' APL responses at a matched response of the claws, and granted if the flies' interval stays within a factor of one and a half for all three pairs of odors. The second sets the best family against the flies in three ratios, pa over ms and paa over ms near the panel's concentration and paa one log unit below the concentration of its input over paa at that concentration, each for APL, for the claws and for APL's ratio over the claws' ratio in the same fly. The model's side is the fits of the eight wirings run as they are, with nothing set again ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)): its APL and the summed input to its claws, the stage that was read against recordings of claws before ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)), each taken as its mean during the odor minus its mean during a blank in the same run, and each read through a family of indicator nonlinearities, from one in proportion to one about as steep as the reported cooperativity of the indicator. A wiring is inside a ratio if any of its readings lies in the flies' interval, for the two ratios over ms under any of the estimates of ms's input from the lab's recording sessions, and a ratio is classed when at least six of the eight wirings agree. The third is whether APL's calcium follows the claws place by place. The calyx is divided into squares four micrometres wide; the part of APL's map that is particular to a stimulus is taken from two of its presentations and correlated over the squares with the same part of the claws' map from its other two, which gives the agreement of the two maps as a Pearson r; and that agreement is set against what the claws' maps of other odors give. The two colours are not perfectly separate, and that governs how all of it is read. A little of the green signal appears in the red channel, with APL's own pattern. Its size is given by {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=G:recordings ~ .0f}} recordings from {{E101/a1_groups.csv:group=G:flies ~ .0f}} flies in which only APL carried an indicator while both channels were recorded, as the slope of the red channel on the green one. Every reading of the claws is made as recorded and again with that much of APL's map taken out, and a class counts only if both give it. One check was fixed with it: the red channel of each of these flies, corrected with the slope of the other, has to keep no more agreement with APL's map than other odors' maps give. If one keeps more, the leak is not known well enough to be taken out: every reading of the claws with the leak taken out and the test place by place are then not decided, and only the strengths of the APL channel are reported. The model's side, which reads no recording, was made before the recordings were read.

src: The family's APL separates two stimuli as its claws do and no further: APL's ratio over the claws' ratio stays near one in every row of the model. It does so with APL off as well, each run read against its own blank, so that it is not APL's own inhibition that makes the claws even. The claws in turn follow the PNs' summed response, which the model's antennal lobe returns nearly equal for pa and ms with the lab's input, although the ORN inputs of the two odors differ widely in total; over the odors of the stage recordings the coefficient of variation of the PNs' summed response, its standard deviation as a share of its mean, is {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=change:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the model and {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=pn_dend:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the flies' PN dendrites ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)). With Hallem's receptor data for the two odors as the input, through the same antennal lobe and the same fits, the PNs' summed responses differ more than threefold, and the family's APL separates pa from ms {{E101/c4_hallem_ratios.csv:wiring=M1;series=pa over ms;log10_conc=-4.0;cond=on;quantity=APL:linear ~ .2f}} to {{E101/c4_hallem_ratios.csv:wiring=real;series=pa over ms;log10_conc=-2.0;cond=on;quantity=APL:linear ~ .2f}} times, inside the interval of the flies' APL channel when read in proportion. The family's flat APL is thus set by what the model is given at its claws, in the input and in the antennal lobe, and no change in what drives APL is needed to make it less flat. Hallem's data come from another laboratory's odor delivery at nominal dilutions and cover a part of the model's glomeruli, so that this shows where the flatness is set and is not an estimate of the flies' input ([Hallem's receptor data as the weak odors' input](#hallem-input)).

src: **What follows.** Nothing is gained or lost on the main target, and no base, bound or reference family is changed. Four things are carried from here. The first is a request and not an experiment. The experimenter who made the recordings is asked for images of the baseline of both channels in each recording, from which each recording's own leak between the colours is measured, for the confirmation of which channel holds which indicator and of the alignment of the two channels, and for the check of the recordings' quality. With a leak measured for each recording, every reading of the KC channel and the three verdicts are made again by the rules already fixed. The second is for the two comparisons of APL's strength, of which one has been completed since ([the next subsection](#apl-strength)) and one is still running: in other flies than theirs, and with pa within one log unit of the model's input, the flies' APL separates pa from ms several times and falls further over the log unit of paa than the family's read in proportion, and the family comes inside the flies' intervals through the indicator family or through another session's estimate of the input. Their verdicts are their own and are not anticipated here. The third concerns the two repairs of a flat APL. On the model's side the flatness is set before APL, so that a less even input, or a weaker normalization in the antennal lobe, would carry through to the family's APL with no change in what drives it. On the flies' side the leads say that their APL is also steeper than their own KC channel, which would ask for a change in what drives APL as well. Which of the two the flies' steeper APL asks for is what the leak leaves open, and neither is proposed here. The fourth is that whether a part of APL's activity is local stays open: the test against the claws' own map, the one test of it that needs no connectome, is not decided, and the readings against maps predicted from the connectomes stay withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)). What such a test is about has since been measured in recordings of APL alone: the part of APL's map that is a stimulus's own returns with another vial of the same odor in another block of presentations, and not with another odor, so that it is the odor's and not the block's ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out)).

src: In the best family's fits APL's own activity is nearly the same for every odor of the panel, and a large part of it is there without an odor. On the eight wirings on which the family has been fitted ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)) it varies over the 16 odors by {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=P2:a_cv ~ .1%}} to {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=real:a_cv ~ .1%}} of its mean; {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=P3:a0_share ~ .0%}} to {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=real:a0_share ~ .0%}} of its mean during an odor is the level that it holds during a blank; and what an odor adds to that level varies by {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=P2:evoked_cv ~ .1%}} to {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=real:evoked_cv ~ .1%}}, with ms adding the least on every wiring, {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=real:ms_over_mean ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a4_profile_carrying.csv:wiring=M1:ms_over_mean ~ .2f}} of the mean over the odors. For the main target such an APL is close to a fixed raise of each KC's threshold ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)), where the flies' own KC responses ask for an inhibition that grows with an odor's response over all KCs ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)), and the evenness is made before APL, by an antennal lobe that returns the odors' total drive nearly equal ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)). APL's activity is the one variable of the model's inhibition that has been imaged directly, as calcium in APL in one plane through the calyx: {{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V2;reading=order_matched;subset=all:n_recordings ~ .0f}} recordings from {{E98/a3_ratios.csv:ratio_id=V2;reading=order_matched;subset=all:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies, each with pa, paa and ms as concentration series. Those maps had been read for where APL responds ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)); here they are read for how strongly. The experiment changes no model and scores nothing on the main target, so that [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect), its mean part and its pattern part stay where they are.

src: **What was read, and by which rules.** On the flies' side a response is the change in fluorescence over its baseline around its peak, averaged inside the outline of the calyx, with each presentation taken against the presentation of the solvent at the same place in its block, as the mean of a stimulus's two presentations. Two stimuli are compared as a ratio within a recording. The flies' ratio is the geometric mean over the flies, a fly's recordings averaged first, with the interval in which nine in ten resamplings of the flies fall, and a concentration that was not imaged is read between its two imaged neighbours on the logarithm of the concentration, inside the recording's imaged range. On the model's side the fits of the eight wirings are run again as they are, with nothing set again, on a longer list of stimuli, and every run gives its saved spike counts on the panel's odors again without one differing. The model's response is APL's mean activity while the odor is on minus its mean during a blank in the same run, the counterpart of what a change in fluorescence leaves out. The indicator need not report APL's activity in proportion, so that the model's ratio is read through a family of indicator nonlinearities, from one in proportion to one about as steep as the reported cooperativity of the indicator, each in two forms: with the level without an odor inside the indicator's baseline, and with only what the odor adds seen. A wiring is inside a comparison if any of its readings lies in the flies' interval, flatter if all of them are nearer to one than the interval or on the other side of one, and steeper if all lie beyond the interval's far end. A comparison takes a class when at least six of the eight wirings agree, and the class is held only if every reading that the measurement leaves open gives it, among them another way of taking the baseline from the solvent presentations, the recordings without three that had been set apart, and the model read against its level just before the odor in place of the blank's. Two comparisons carry the verdict, both fixed beforehand and both with the lab's input. Along concentration it is paa at 10^-5 over paa at 10^-4, the concentration of paa's ORN input, with the input at 10^-5 taken from the ORN recordings of the flies in which the input at 10^-4 was recorded. Across odors it is paa over ms at 10^-3. There the flies' interval spans both readings of paa's concentration, the 10^-4 at which its ORN input was recorded and the maps' concentration nearest the 10^-3 of the KC recordings, for which that input stands in ([ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations)), and the model is read under each estimate of ms's input that the lab's ORN recordings hold. Those recordings were made in three sessions, each in its own flies: that of the megamat panel, from which the model's ms input comes, that of the validation2 panel, from which its paa input comes, and one of two mixture panels. Each session also recorded a set of diagnostic odors, among them ms at 10^-3 and paa at 10^-5, and the control panel of the mixture session holds ms at 10^-3 as well, which gives five estimates of ms's input and three of paa's input at 10^-5. Across odors the family counts as inside if inside is held under any of the five, and as outside only if flatter or steeper is held under all of them.

src: same-repeat gap: The single-trial cosine distance between two different odors presented in different repeats of the panel minus the distance between the same two odors presented in the same repeat, averaged over odor pairs and recordings. It is positive when the odors of one repeat share part of their trial-to-trial variability.
out: same-repeat gap: The single-trial cosine similarity between two different odors presented in the same repeat of the panel minus the correlation between the same two odors presented in different repeats, averaged over odor pairs and recordings. It is positive when the odors of one repeat share part of their trial-to-trial variability.
by: a Fable subagent (claude-fable-5-2), spawned from viki 2026-11-16

src: estimate across repeats: A pair's distance without the trial noise, taken from single trials. One minus the cosine between trials of the two odors from different repeats, divided by the geometric mean of the two odors' cosines between their own trials across the same repeats. It assumes only that the noise of different repeats is independent.
out: estimate across repeats: A pair's correlation without the trial noise, taken from single trials. The cosine between trials of the two odors from different repeats, divided by the geometric mean of the two odors' cosines between their own trials across the same repeats. It assumes only that the noise of different repeats is independent.
by: a Fable subagent (claude-fable-5-2), spawned from viki 2026-11-16

src: re-specified noise: The model's trial noise set to the flies' two shares. A jitter of each KC's threshold that all odors of a trial share, at the level at which the model's same-repeat gap is the flies', plus a factor drawn independently for every KC, odor and trial that brings the distance between two presentations of one odor to the flies'.
out: re-specified noise: The model's trial noise set to the flies' two shares. src: - The correction for trial-to-trial noise that this page had used takes the noise of two odors to be independent, and it put the distances without noise too low; an estimate that needs only independence between repeats replaces it.

src: Every comparison of a model with the KC data as the data are made passes the model through [trial-to-trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) calibrated on one number, how far apart two presentations of one odor are, and every level quoted without the trial noise came from a correction that takes the noise of different odors to be independent. Each recording holds three repeats of the panel, so both can be checked against the flies. The flies' variability across the three repeats did that from the per-trial responses of the {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} control recordings and the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} with APL output blocked (TNT), with 90 % intervals from resampling the recordings. It then scored the saved models against the effect without the noise and read the best families again through a noise with the flies' make-up. No model was fitted.

src: **The odors of one repeat share part of their variability, and more of it with APL output blocked.** The same-repeat gap is the distance between two different odors presented in different repeats minus the distance between the same two odors presented in the same repeat, both between single trials. If the variability of two odors' responses were independent it would be zero. It is positive in every recording, {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl ~ .1f}} times larger with APL output blocked (TNT) than in control flies (90 % interval {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl.lo ~ .1f}} to {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl.hi ~ .1f}}), and largest over the six pairs with near-identical ORN input (table below). The size of the responses does not make it: with every entry reduced to responding or not, the gap is about the same.

src: **What follows.** Nothing is gained or lost on the main target, and no base, bound or reference family is changed. Four things are carried from here. The first is an experiment that is running, the antennal lobe's normalization at the strength the flies' APL asks for (with the pending work at the end of the page). It takes the one change that moved the family's fall towards the flies' to the eight wirings and to a refit, and measures what it costs on the pattern part of the APL-effect loss, with the comparison across odors, which that change moves the wrong way, and the KCs' recruitment at low concentration read beside it. The other places at which the scaling could be lost stay open: an input that scales more than the one session's estimate at the lower concentration, and a drive of APL by the KCs' spikes, which did not scale in the saved bases either and whose test in the flies waits on the leak between the two colours of the dual-colour recordings ([above](#apl-vs-claws)). The second is the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations, a comparison in other recordings of APL that is still running (with the pending work at the end of the page). The third is a table for the experimenter who imaged APL. The three odors imaged cannot tell a nearly even APL from one that follows the KCs' response, since the KC data's response rates to them lie close together. For every pair of the panel's odors the table gives the ratio of the family's APL, the ratio of an APL in proportion to the KCs' response rates with APL output blocked (TNT) and, from the spread between flies in the maps, the number of flies that would tell the two apart. Among the pairs whose ORN input is at the concentration of the KC recordings, those that set eb, 1-6ol, 2h, ep or 2-but against 1-8ol separate the two most: the family's APL gives {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2-but;denominator=1-8ol:family_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2h;denominator=1-8ol:family_max ~ .2f}} there and the proportional one {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2-but;denominator=1-8ol:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=1-6ol;denominator=1-8ol:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}}, which about {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=1-6ol;denominator=1-8ol:flies_needed_sd_median ~ .0f}} flies would tell apart for each pair. Against -aPine the two lie further apart ({{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2-but;denominator=-aPine:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=1-6ol;denominator=-aPine:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}} for the proportional one), but -aPine's ORN input was recorded at another concentration than that of the KC recordings. {{lit:67 # results/E98_apl_response_strength/a6_power_carrying.csv: the pairs whose flies_needed_sd_median is 3 or less, counted from the table's 120 rows}} of the 120 pairs need three flies or fewer at the median spread between flies, and the request goes with the data asked for at the end of the page. The fourth are two leads. KC recordings of a panel odor at a second concentration, paa at 10^-5 first, would say whether the flies' APL follows their KCs along concentration, as the response rates suggest that it may across odors. And the dependence of paa over ms on the depth of the plane seemed to belong with the question of a spatially local APL ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)). Both the comparison across odors and that dependence on depth have since been read again in a further series of the same experimenter's recordings, held out from every rule fixed here ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out), the next subsection). The dependence on depth does not return there, so that this lead is closed. Across odors the held-out flies lie between these recordings and flies recorded in 2022 and hold the family inside their interval under every estimate of ms's input; and two vials of one odor differ there by enough that a ratio between two odors read from one pair of vials is known to no better than a factor of about one and a half, with which the comparison across odors made here and the numbers of flies in the table for the experimenter are to be read.

The other places at which the scaling could be lost stay open: an input that scales more than the one session's estimate at the lower concentration, and a drive of APL by the KCs' spikes, which did not scale in the saved bases either and whose test in the flies waits on the leak between the two colours of the dual-colour recordings ([above](#apl-vs-claws)). The second is the flies' APL at the weak odors and at the panel's concentrations, a comparison in other recordings of APL that is still running (with the pending work at the end of the page). The third is a table for the experimenter who imaged APL. The three odors imaged cannot tell a nearly even APL from one that follows the KCs' response, since the KC data's response rates to them lie close together. For every pair of the panel's odors the table gives the ratio of the family's APL, the ratio of an APL in proportion to the KCs' response rates with APL output blocked (TNT) and, from the spread between flies in the maps, the number of flies that would tell the two apart. Among the pairs whose ORN input is at the concentration of the KC recordings, those that set eb, 1-6ol, 2h, ep or 2-but against 1-8ol separate the two most: the family's APL gives {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2-but;denominator=1-8ol:family_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2h;denominator=1-8ol:family_max ~ .2f}} there and the proportional one {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2-but;denominator=1-8ol:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=1-6ol;denominator=1-8ol:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}}, which about {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=1-6ol;denominator=1-8ol:flies_needed_sd_median ~ .0f}} flies would tell apart for each pair. Against -aPine the two lie further apart ({{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=2-but;denominator=-aPine:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}} to {{E98/a6_power_carrying.csv:numerator=1-6ol;denominator=-aPine:proportional_tnt ~ .2f}} for the proportional one), but -aPine's ORN input was recorded at another concentration than that of the KC recordings. {{lit:67 # results/E98_apl_response_strength/a6_power_carrying.csv: the pairs whose flies_needed_sd_median is 3 or less, counted from the table's 120 rows}} of the 120 pairs need three flies or fewer at the median spread between flies, and the request goes with the data asked for at the end of the page. The fourth are two leads. KC recordings of a panel odor at a second concentration, paa at 10^-5 first, would say whether the flies' APL follows their KCs along concentration, as the response rates suggest that it may across odors. And the dependence of paa over ms on the depth of the plane seemed to belong with the question of a spatially local APL ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)). Both the comparison across odors and that dependence on depth have since been read again in a further series of the same experimenter's recordings, held out from every rule fixed here ([the flies' APL across odors in the held-out vial series](#apl-held-out), the next subsection). The dependence on depth does not return there, so that this lead is closed. Across odors the held-out flies lie between these recordings and flies recorded in 2022 and hold the family inside their interval under every estimate of ms's input; and two vials of one odor differ there by enough that a ratio between two odors read from one pair of vials is known to no better than a factor of about one and a half, with which the comparison across odors made here and the numbers of flies in the table for the experimenter are to be read.

src: **The readings of the flies' APL disagreed about ms. In the recordings of the strength comparison APL responds to ms about as strongly as to paa, and in flies recorded a year later paa evokes two to three times as much as ms. A further series by the same experimenter, with the genotype of the first and made as a control with three vials of one odor in every recording, was read by rules fixed before any of it was opened. Its flies lie between the two. Their APL responds a third to three quarters more strongly to paa than to ms, more than in the first series by about what five flies against eight can just show, and on pa against ms and on ms's own fall with concentration they are as the first series, far from the flies of the later year. Which side they are on changes with the reading, so that by the rule nothing is decided and no interval is pooled over the two series. The best family, whose ratio lies above that of the first series at the concentration of paa's input, is inside the held-out flies' interval under every estimate of ms's input. Two vials of one odor at one concentration differ persistently by more than had been expected, so that a ratio between two odors read from one pair of vials is known to no better than a factor of about one and a half; the difference between the two years is larger than that, and the difference between the two series of one year is not. The part of APL's map that is a stimulus's own returns with another vial of the same odor and not with another odor, so that it is the odor's. The dependence of paa over ms on the depth of the plane does not return. The experimenter who made the recordings has not checked their quality. No model is changed, and nothing is scored on the main target.**

src: **The earlier noise correction is biased, and the target is not.** The correction divided each pair's cosine by the two odors' signal norms, on the assumption that the noise adds nothing to the product of two different odors' responses. What the odors of a repeat share does add to that product, and the correction counted it as similarity between the odors. It therefore put the distances too low, most with APL output blocked (TNT), where the shared part is larger, and so the mean APL effect too high. The estimate across repeats uses only products of trials from different repeats, which that shared part does not enter: one minus the cosine between single trials of the two odors from different repeats, divided by the geometric mean of the two odors' cosines between their own trials across the same repeats.

src: **The part of APL's map that is a stimulus's own is the odor's.** In the earlier maps most of a recording was one pattern common to all of its stimuli, and what was left of a stimulus's map, the remainder, repeated between its presentations ([the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)). Those presentations lay in one block, so that the remainder could have belonged to the block, to a drift of the plane or to the state of the fly, as well as to the odor. Three vials of one odor in separate blocks tell these apart. The pattern common to a recording is taken from the nine stimuli of ms and of the first vials of paa and pa and removed from every map, and the remainders, smoothed over 5 pixels, are correlated over the pixels inside the outline, in the recordings of every depth. Between the two halves of a stimulus's presentations in its block the Pearson r is {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-10-29_fly3_L;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_rep ~ .2f}} to {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-11-09_fly5_R;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_rep ~ .2f}} over the {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:n_calyces ~ .0f}} calyces; between the second and the third vial of one odor at one concentration, which lie in different blocks, it is {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-11-07_fly1_L;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_vial ~ .2f}} to {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-11-07_fly1_R;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_vial ~ .2f}}; and between such a vial and another odor at the same rank of concentration it is {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-10-22_fly1_L;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_odor ~ .2f}} to {{E103/d_m_calyces.csv:calyx=2021-10-29_fly3_L;blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:r_odor ~ .2f}}. As a share of what repeats within a block, from none of it to all of it, what returns with another vial of the same odor is {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:share ~ .2f}} ({{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:hi90 ~ .2f}}, the interval over resampled flies), and the same odor agrees better than another odor in {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:n_vial_over_odor ~ .0f}} of the {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=5.0;variant=carrying:n_calyces ~ .0f}} calyces, where the rule asked for an interval above one half and for seven calyces. At the three other smoothings the share is {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=20.0;variant=carrying:share ~ .2f}} to {{E103/d_m.csv:blur_px=2.0;variant=carrying:share ~ .2f}}, and the class is the same before the common pattern is removed. The share exceeds one because the agreement within a block is between halves of a block's presentations, which noise lowers more than it lowers the agreement between whole blocks; the class does not rest on that. The correlation with another odor is mostly below zero because removing one common pattern from the maps of three odors leaves their remainders opposed. An odor-specific map of the flies' APL thus exists against the control that it had lacked, and with a size.

src: **What follows.** Nothing is gained or lost on the main target, and no base, bound or reference family is changed. Five things are carried from here. The first is how the family's APL is read across odors. Near the panel's concentration the flies' APL does not at present constrain it: every reading of paa over ms or of pa over ms against the family is given with the series that it comes from, and the family is called neither too even nor too uneven across odors while the series disagree. The verdict of the strength comparison stands as written ([above](#apl-strength)), and its class across odors, inside, is found again in flies on which no rule had been fixed, at the series' own concentrations and under every estimate of ms's input. The second is for the antennal lobe's normalization at the strength the flies' APL asks for (with the pending work at the end of the page). No interval pooled over the two series of 2021 goes to it, the interval fixed for its ratio between odors stands, and the held-out flies' intervals are a record beside that interval, inside which the family's ratio stays at both steps of the weaker normalization read so far. The third is the vials. A ratio between two odors that has to be known to better than a factor of about one and a half needs vials made anew on several days, with the days averaged; that bears on the table of pairs left for the experimenter, whose numbers of flies take the spread between flies as the only uncertainty ([above](#apl-strength)), and on the comparison of ms with pa at the panel's concentrations that is still being read in the flies of 2022 (with the pending work at the end of the page). The fourth is a set of questions to the experimenter, which hold nothing meanwhile: whether the vials of the held-out series were made anew each day and diluted separately; whether ms's stock, its vials or its delivery differed between 2021 and 2022, which decides which flies' ms to trust and so whether the family's paa over ms is judged against the flies of 2021 or against those of 2022; and whether a note against one block in two of the recordings excludes the block or the recording. Until the second is answered, a change of ms's input as a handle on the main target is not proposed. The fifth concerns a spatially local APL. Its premise from the maps now has a measured object, the part of APL's map that is the odor's, with a size and with its control. The readings against maps predicted from the connectomes stay withheld ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)) and the test place by place against the claws stays undecided ([the flies' APL against their KC claws in the dual-colour recordings](#apl-vs-claws)), so that no local APL is fitted; and the dependence on depth that had pointed the same way is closed, so that verdicts on responses averaged over the calyx need no restriction to one depth. One lead is left for the planning of further readings: recordings of the KCs' claws alone in the calyx, in other flies, would give the claws' side of the same ratios across odors without the leak between the two colours.

src: The plot below tracks, for nine of the statistics used throughout this page, how far the best model found so far had closed the gap between the first measured model and the KC data, against the time each experiment finished. Two of the lines are the main target: the APL-effect loss, for which lower is better and 100 % is the data's floor ({{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}}, the loss a model with the flies' true effect would still show, not zero), and ρ on the per-pair APL effect (ceiling {{data:apl_effect_rho_ceiling ~ .2f}}). Each line follows the best value of its own statistic, so the two are not the record of one model: the variants with the highest ρ are mostly not those with the lowest loss, and no model is chosen by its ρ ([why](#fn-pattern-split)). These two lines count only variants inside the realism bands (a response rate with APL on of 0.045 to 0.085, an APL-off / APL-on response rate ratio of 1.6 to 2.9, a response rate ρ with APL on of at least 0.37, and a distribution of the number of odors each KC responds to within {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .2f}} of the control flies' with APL on and within {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .2f}} of that of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) with APL off, the flies' responses counted in [baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units); a variant whose responses were not saved is held to the first two), so that a loss lowered through the response rates, or by gathering the responses in few KCs, does not show as progress. The fourth band decides one step of the loss line. Before the APL-effect fits the line stood at {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, the joint fit to both matrices run at breadth exponent 3, which is at the limit of that band with APL off ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution, the band's own value to three decimals); the one variant on the plot's terms with a lower loss, breadth-weighted APL alone on the bouton baseline ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E12_breadth_apl;tag=spikes_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}), is outside that band with APL off. The APL-effect fits took the line to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplraw_k3_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, the lowest loss on raw counts among [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits) without a glomerulus gain: the first joint fit's family at breadth exponent 3, fitted on raw counts at the flies' response rate and scored on all four bands and inside the one on odors per KC with APL off ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplraw_k3_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution, against a band of {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}). It is one of the fits that give up KC–KC inhibition and the block for a larger mean effect, with APL→bouton at {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplraw_k3_cap3:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} times the baseline's against a bound of three. The line is on deterministic runs: there the breadth-2 fit of the best-models table, which keeps both, stands at {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, and through the matched trial noise the breadth-3 fit holds its loss while the breadth-2 fit falls narrowly below it ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)). The firing ceiling then took the line to {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, the breadth-2 fit made again with a firing ceiling at its stronger setting, inside all four bands ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). The line now ends at {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E76_data_side_target;tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, the same fit made once more with the response-rate terms of its loss against the flies' response rates counted in baseline-noise units, inside all four bands as well ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)); that last step, of {{diff:E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse -- apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E76_data_side_target;tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, is smaller than what one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}). The best-models table carries the fit at the literature setting ({{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}), the one whose spike counts agree with whole-cell recordings of KCs; through the matched trial noise the two settings score alike, both below every fit without a ceiling. The line of ρ on the per-pair APL effect then takes a small step, from {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E76_data_side_target;tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_spearman ~ .3f}} to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E82_flies_protocol;tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_spearman ~ .3f}}, taken by a fit of the same family made at the flies' 2 s odor pulse with the ceiling's adaptation at 3 s, inside all four bands ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)); on the loss line that fit stands at {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E82_flies_protocol;tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, level with the line's end. That experiment's points are of fits made at the flies' pulse; every point before them is of the model's 0.5 s pulse. The ρ line ends with two larger steps, to {{summary_progress/progress_best.csv:metric=apl_rho;exp=E83:value ~ .3f}} and to {{summary_progress/progress_best.csv:metric=apl_rho;exp=E86:value ~ .3f}}, which are of another kind: each is an input searched against half of the recordings, read on one re-drawn wiring, on raw counts and against all recordings ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit); [the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input)).
