src: - **The responses without APL: which KCs respond to both odors of a pair.** The two steps that the split of the common error had left have been taken, and both close ([the co-response read with a checked estimate and the breadth weighting inside the models' APL](#breadth-weighting)). No estimate of the co-response passes the check, so that the split into who responds and how strongly stays a description and no further estimate is sought, three repeats a recording setting the limit. And no other breadth weighting of the model's APL, by any of three measures of a KC's breadth or at any exponent from 0 to 2, has a lower pattern part than the family's own, on the fits as they are or on the base with the flies' recruitment: a weaker weighting gives the alcohol pairs the flies' co-response change and takes from the ester pairs and from the mean APL effect. After static forms of inhibition, APL's profile over the glomeruli and its weights by KC type, the breadth weighting is the fourth change on APL's side that does not carry the common error, and the feedback APL of the breadth-2 family is the best inhibition tried on the model's responses. The lead is therefore the responses that APL acts on, as the flies' own responses had read it on the spike counts of the fits ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)). Two experiments were set up for it, and both have been run. The first changed no model: it read the best family's stages before the somata, the PNs, the PN boutons and the KC claws, against recordings of those stages in wild-type flies ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)). By its rule it does not say whether the models leave the flies before the claws, at the step from claws to somata with APL on, or at that step without APL: that turns on what a claw's signal reports and on which claws are read, and at the step without APL, where a difference in the responses without APL would show, on how the model's somata are read as well. What it leaves is with the next item of this list. The second took up the one property of the feedback APL's inhibition of the KCs that none of the four changes above touched, the place where it is summed: at each claw, as in every model so far, or on the sum of a KC's claws ([APL's inhibition on the KC's summed drive](#summed-drive)). Summed over a KC's claws, the inhibition leaves the pattern part where it was, on the fits as they are and in the family fitted again with it: what the clipping at each claw holds back sits in the broad, many-clawed KCs that the weighting already loads. On the base with the flies' recruitment it lets a weighting with an exponent of 1 read lower than the base's own family, by half of what the test asks and mostly through how strongly each KC is inhibited. That setting, whose weights are far less unequal than the family's, is the first to be read if a mechanism gives the model the flies' recruitment without the [oracle](#fn-oracle). The change lay between the claw and the soma and left the responses without APL as they are, so it was a test of what the model's APL makes of the same responses, and not the mechanism that the lead asks for. A third experiment has since run the last form of the feedback APL's inhibition of the KCs that the family had not been given, a gain on each claw's drive in place of the subtraction, and has read the KC somata of the flies and of the model in the same way ([the claw-to-soma steps read like for like and APL's inhibition as a gain at the claw](#steps-like-for-like)). The gain is worse at the family's weighting and is the best setting against no half of the recordings, so that the inhibition of the KCs is closed in its form as it is in its weighting and in the place where it is summed. One form on APL's side stays as a description: a divisive inhibition at the boutons moves the model off the weightings' line toward the flies and gives the alcohol pairs the flies' co-response change, at a cost in the pattern part and in the mean APL effect at fixed scales. Whether that cost belongs to the fixed scales or to the form was not read, the family not having been fitted with it. APL's inhibition of the PN boutons, the part of APL's side that this left open, has since been run in its strength and in its form ([the PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition](#bouton-share)). The fitted strength is the best: less of the inhibition at the boutons costs, more of it costs, a gain there costs at every strength, and the family fitted again with the path held near the connectome's share is worse, so that APL's side of the family is closed at both of its sites. Two things stay from it. One is a choice still to be made. In the fits as they are about seven tenths of the drive that APL takes from the claws is taken at the boutons, where the connectome puts about a tenth of APL's calyx synapses, and a bouton share near the connectome's costs {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} of the pattern part at fixed scales and {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} after a refit, half the fitted strength being an equal. Whether a limit on the bouton share replaces the bound on the APL→bouton scale, and at which price, is not decided, and until it is the family stays as fitted. The other was a lead, and it has been read ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)). What the boutons' offset does for a KC is to raise its threshold, with APL on only, in proportion to the KC's number of claws and nearly alike for every odor: given as such a fixed inhibition of each KC, the bouton path reads as the family does, and the whole APL given so reads {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} to {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C1_bck:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher in the pattern part through the calibrated readout and, with one amount per KC, no higher on raw counts. For the main target the family's APL is thus close to a threshold difference per KC between the two conditions, which the flies' inhibition is not, and no setting other than the unchanged fits was the best against any half of the recordings. The same experiment added a third price to the choice above: with a part of the APL→KC weights that is the same on every claw, the refit near the connectome's share costs {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}}, just outside the margin of an equal and with weights that the connectome does not have. Two readings were left from it for planning. One is not run: the family fitted with a static inhibition per KC and no feedback, set by the KC's number of claws, by a spread among KCs with the same number and by the breadth weighting. If it matches the family on wirings and recordings that it was not fitted on, the feedback is not needed for the main target, and a change on APL's side has to change which KCs' thresholds rise with APL on; if it does not, the few thousandths that the feedback adds at fixed scales understate it. The other has been run: APL→KC weights that reach every claw from the anatomy and not uniformly, made of the synapses that APL makes on a KC outside its claws ([APL's synapses on the KCs outside the claws](#offclaw-synapses)). The refit near the connectome's share then reads {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} above the unchanged fits, {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}} more than the uniform part had left, with a mean APL effect of {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} where the fits have {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, so that the share keeps a price with weights that the connectome has, and the choice above has a fourth price to weigh. Of what that experiment left for planning, the runs that would say which property of the uniform part held the mean APL effect have been made ([the evenness of APL's weights among KCs and over a KC's claws](#weight-evenness)). It is amounts that are equal among KCs with the same number of claws, and not a KC's total in proportion to its number of claws; where on a KC's claws the synapses lie carries little of the loss through the calibrated readout, and no part made of each KC's counted synapses holds the mean, so that the fourth price stands as it was read. What the two experiments leave for planning is not run: whether a quantity that the anatomy defines for each KC gives an inhibition that is nearly equal among such KCs or that follows the KC's own input, and the same readings with the counts of another connectome, which wait on the hold on the derived tables or on further connectome outputs ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)). The mechanism that this item's lead asks for, one between the claw and the soma that changes which KCs respond to an odor without APL, is still to be proposed, and the static reading does not supply it: it was made with APL on only and left the responses without APL as they are. The readings of the stages do not settle the step without APL for it. That the model's somata without APL are too alike, with the alcohol pairs' excess made at that step, holds only with the calibrated readout set against the flies' trial means; with the two sides read alike the alcohol pairs are never too alike without APL, and the model's somata are the flies' if a KC's signal saturates with its firing and too far apart if it does not (the next item of this list). What the like-for-like reading adds to the brief is on the side with APL. In every such reading the model's ester pairs are too alike and its alcohol pairs too far apart with APL on, and under every weighting, summation and gain of APL's inhibition the two groups move together along one line, off which the flies lie. A mechanism has to leave that line toward the flies, and it is placed against it beside the two targets. Its brief is the description of the model's shared responders ([the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)): the KCs that respond to both odors of an alcohol or an ester pair without APL, and that the model's APL removes although a cut by amplitude would keep them, are broad, many-clawed and often γ KCs. The stages before it have not carried the error so far: neither a selection of responders at the claw nor the input changed for each odor, whose one candidate carries a few thousandths of the pattern part and no more (the second item of this list) ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee); [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit); [the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input)). Such a mechanism is read on two targets, the one that needs no APL for the responses themselves and the main target for what the model's APL makes of them. It is read on the four wirings of the earlier searches and then on the four others, against the half of the recordings that it was not chosen on, by the test that the fitted changes were put to. Beside the targets goes the alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL, read with the geometric mean of the two estimates and with that estimate's error on known values: {{E89/changes.csv:source=flies;candidate=gm;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} in the flies, and {{E89/changes.csv:source=model;candidate=gm;population=b2;level=L1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E89/changes.csv:source=model;candidate=gm;population=b2;level=L3h;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} in the breadth-2 family. If the pattern part falls on the wirings and the recordings that the mechanism was not chosen on, and the two groups' errors fall with it, the common error is in which KCs the model recruits before APL acts. The mechanism is then fitted with the family's other parameters, the breadth exponent among them, since what a weighting does has depended on the rest of the model, and it is read in the family with the firing ceiling, at the flies' pulse and through the trial noise. If the responses come nearer the flies' on the target without APL and the main target does not follow, the two sides do not add in the model, as recruitment and the co-response did not, and APL's side, closed on the present responses, would have to be read again on the new ones. If neither target moves, the description of the shared responders was not a handle, and the stage between the claw and the soma joins those that have not carried the common error. As before, what is at stake on the main target is the share of the pattern error that the two groups of pairs carry, not the whole of it. Three things go with this. A verdict that holds with all the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) and not with the six that are alike, as the ester pairs' assignment to recruitment does, is not a target for a model until the experimenter has answered about the two strongest recordings (the first item of this list); the alcohols' difference, read like for like, now holds against the six as well on the breadth-2 family, by a narrow margin, and on the base with the flies' recruitment. Beyond the families in which only the weighting differs, the saved models are not screened by the factors again until the rule for standing out is tightened: a co-response change that comes toward the flies' joined to a pattern part that does not rise, a comparison that does not rest on the weakest wiring's fit, and handles chosen and not counted. And the two choices left by the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses stand. Whether the target without APL is given a place in fits is not decided: it missed the test fixed for using it by a narrow margin as trial means and passed it with the trial noise removed, by itself it rewards the per-odor recruitment, and until the choice is made it is given beside the main target. And the exponent on a KC's breadth that the recordings ask for is larger in the two strongest recordings than in the six that are alike, so that it waits, as the target itself does, on the experimenter's answer about those two recordings and on the recordings of the panel that the target does not use (the first item of this list); in the model the exponent stays at the family's 2 meanwhile, a smaller one having cost the main target.

The change lay between the claw and the soma and left the responses without APL as they are, so it was a test of what the model's APL makes of the same responses, and not the mechanism that the lead asks for. A third experiment has since run the last form of the feedback APL's inhibition of the KCs that the family had not been given, a gain on each claw's drive in place of the subtraction, and has read the KC somata of the flies and of the model in the same way ([the claw-to-soma steps read like for like and APL's inhibition as a gain at the claw](#steps-like-for-like)). The gain is worse at the family's weighting and is the best setting against no half of the recordings, so that the inhibition of the KCs is closed in its form as it is in its weighting and in the place where it is summed. One form on APL's side stays as a description: a divisive inhibition at the boutons moves the model off the weightings' line toward the flies and gives the alcohol pairs the flies' co-response change, at a cost in the pattern part and in the mean APL effect at fixed scales. Whether that cost belongs to the fixed scales or to the form was not read, the family not having been fitted with it. APL's inhibition of the PN boutons, the part of APL's side that this left open, has since been run in its strength and in its form ([the PN boutons' share of APL's inhibition](#bouton-share)). The fitted strength is the best: less of the inhibition at the boutons costs, more of it costs, a gain there costs at every strength, and the family fitted again with the path held near the connectome's share is worse, so that APL's side of the family is closed at both of its sites. Two things stay from it. One is a choice still to be made. In the fits as they are about seven tenths of the drive that APL takes from the claws is taken at the boutons, where the connectome puts about a tenth of APL's calyx synapses, and a bouton share near the connectome's costs {{E94/equal.csv:variant=B_sub_k2_d0.1:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} of the pattern part at fixed scales and {{diff:E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E94/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} after a refit, half the fitted strength being an equal. Whether a limit on the bouton share replaces the bound on the APL→bouton scale, and at which price, is not decided, and until it is the family stays as fitted. The other was a lead, and it has been read ([APL's inhibition as a static threshold raise per KC](#static-threshold)). What the boutons' offset does for a KC is to raise its threshold, with APL on only, in proportion to the KC's number of claws and nearly alike for every odor: given as such a fixed inhibition of each KC, the bouton path reads as the family does, and the whole APL given so reads {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C2_bcko:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} to {{E95/equal.csv:variant=C1_bck:d_pattern_z8 ~ .4f}} higher in the pattern part through the calibrated readout and, with one amount per KC, no higher on raw counts. For the main target the family's APL is thus close to a threshold difference per KC between the two conditions, which the flies' inhibition is not, and no setting other than the unchanged fits was the best against any half of the recordings. The same experiment added a third price to the choice above: with a part of the APL→KC weights that is the same on every claw, the refit near the connectome's share costs {{diff:E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}}, just outside the margin of an equal and with weights that the connectome does not have. Two readings were left from it for planning. One is not run: the family fitted with a static inhibition per KC and no feedback, set by the KC's number of claws, by a spread among KCs with the same number and by the breadth weighting. If it matches the family on wirings and recordings that it was not fitted on, the feedback is not needed for the main target, and a change on APL's side has to change which KCs' thresholds rise with APL on; if it does not, the few thousandths that the feedback adds at fixed scales understate it. The other has been run: APL→KC weights that reach every claw from the anatomy and not uniformly, made of the synapses that APL makes on a KC outside its claws ([APL's synapses on the KCs outside the claws](#offclaw-synapses)). The refit near the connectome's share then reads {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all_unchanged ~ .4f}} above the unchanged fits, {{diff:E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all -- E95/f_scores.csv:unit=S:pattern_all ~ .4f}} more than the uniform part had left, with a mean APL effect of {{E96/d_scores.csv:unit=S:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} where the fits have {{E96/readings.csv:variant=ref;unit=S;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}}, so that the share keeps a price with weights that the connectome has, and the choice above has a fourth price to weigh. It is amounts that are equal among KCs with the same number of claws, and not a KC's total in proportion to its number of claws; where on a KC's claws the synapses lie carries little of the loss through the calibrated readout, and no part made of each KC's counted synapses holds the mean, so that the fourth price stands as it was read. The readings of the stages do not settle the step without APL for it. That the model's somata without APL are too alike, with the alcohol pairs' excess made at that step, holds only with the calibrated readout set against the flies' trial means; with the two sides read alike the alcohol pairs are never too alike without APL, and the model's somata are the flies' if a KC's signal saturates with its firing and too weakly correlated if it does not (the next item of this list). What the like-for-like reading adds to the brief is on the side with APL. In every such reading the model's ester pairs are too alike and its alcohol pairs too weakly correlated with APL on, and under every weighting, summation and gain of APL's inhibition the two groups move together along one line, off which the flies lie. A mechanism has to leave that line toward the flies, and it is placed against it beside the two targets. Its brief is the description of the model's shared responders ([the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)): the KCs that respond to both odors of an alcohol or an ester pair without APL, and that the model's APL removes although a cut by amplitude would keep them, are broad, many-clawed and often γ KCs. The stages before it have not carried the error so far: neither a selection of responders at the claw nor the input changed for each odor, whose one candidate carries a few thousandths of the pattern part and no more (the second item of this list) ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee); [the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit); [the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input)). Such a mechanism is read on two targets, the one that needs no APL for the responses themselves and the main target for what the model's APL makes of them. It is read on the four wirings of the earlier searches and then on the four others, against the half of the recordings that it was not chosen on, by the test that the fitted changes were put to. Beside the targets goes the alcohol pairs' co-response change under APL, read with the geometric mean of the two estimates and with that estimate's error on known values: {{E89/changes.csv:source=flies;candidate=gm;subset=all;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} in the flies, and {{E89/changes.csv:source=model;candidate=gm;population=b2;level=L1;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} to {{E89/changes.csv:source=model;candidate=gm;population=b2;level=L3h;factor=L;group=alcohol:ratio ~ .2f}} in the breadth-2 family. If the pattern part falls on the wirings and the recordings that the mechanism was not chosen on, and the two groups' errors fall with it, the common error is in which KCs the model recruits before APL acts. The mechanism is then fitted with the family's other parameters, the breadth exponent among them, since what a weighting does has depended on the rest of the model, and it is read in the family with the firing ceiling, at the flies' pulse and through the trial noise. If the responses come nearer the flies' on the target without APL and the main target does not follow, the two sides do not add in the model, as recruitment and the co-response did not, and APL's side, closed on the present responses, would have to be read again on the new ones. If neither target moves, the description of the shared responders was not a handle, and the stage between the claw and the soma joins those that have not carried the common error. As before, what is at stake on the main target is the share of the pattern error that the two groups of pairs carry, not the whole of it. Three things go with this. A verdict that holds with all the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) and not with the six that are alike, as the ester pairs' assignment to recruitment does, is not a target for a model until the experimenter has answered about the two strongest recordings (the first item of this list); the alcohols' difference, read like for like, now holds against the six as well on the breadth-2 family, by a narrow margin, and on the base with the flies' recruitment. Beyond the families in which only the weighting differs, the saved models are not screened by the factors again until the rule for standing out is tightened: a co-response change that comes toward the flies' joined to a pattern part that does not rise, a comparison that does not rest on the weakest wiring's fit, and handles chosen and not counted. And the two choices left by the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses stand. Whether the target without APL is given a place in fits is not decided: it missed the test fixed for using it by a narrow margin as trial means and passed it with the trial noise removed, by itself it rewards the per-odor recruitment, and until the choice is made it is given beside the main target. And the exponent on a KC's breadth that the recordings ask for is larger in the two strongest recordings than in the six that are alike, so that it waits, as the target itself does, on the experimenter's answer about those two recordings and on the recordings of the panel that the target does not use (the first item of this list); in the model the exponent stays at the family's 2 meanwhile, a smaller one having cost the main target.

src: - **The stages before the somata: what would place the common error, and the step from claws to somata beside the main target.** Read against recordings of the PN dendrites, the PN boutons and the KC claws of wild-type flies, the best family could not be placed: whether its claws differ from the flies' depends on what a claw's signal reports and on which claws are read, a third of the wiring's glomeruli having no ORN input in the model, and how its steps from claws to somata compare with the flies' depends first on which claws they start from, and then on how its somata are read ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)). Four things follow. The first is a request and not an experiment. The experimenter who recorded the boutons and the claws is asked for the responses of the imaged regions odor by odor and trial by trial, where only the distances between odors are on hand, and for the outline of the claw regions. With them the model's claws are read on the regions that its input can reach, the share of a claw's signal that comes from its KC's spikes is estimated from the claws' own time course, a fly's own part is separated from the mean pattern that the model is given, and the verdict is read again by the rule already fixed. If the model's claws are then the flies' and one step differs, that group's part of the common error is made between claw and soma, on that side of APL, and mechanisms there are judged on that step as well as on the main target. If the claws differ, what reaches the KCs is not the flies' at a recorded stage, and changes of the input are held to the stage recordings, so that a change fitted to them can be tested on the main target with every recording, which the fitted inputs so far could not be ([the input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once](#cross-wiring-fit)). If the readings still disagree, the stages stay a description. The second is a practice. The step from claws to somata in wild-type flies is reported beside the main target for every later mechanism, as the model's steps by group against the flies' and their correlation over the 66 pairs, with the step's floor ({{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:floor ~ .3f}} for a standard deviation over the pairs of {{E90/steps_flies_summary.csv:step=on_remy;claw=claw_noise_removed:sd_over_pairs ~ .3f}}). It shares no fly with the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), whose number bounds what a fitted pattern can be shown to carry (the second item of this list), and it passed the test for such use narrowly, with four claw flies. A mechanism that lowers the pattern part and brings the model's step with APL on toward that of wild-type flies has two readings on its side; one that lowers the pattern part and moves the step away has fitted the recordings that it was scored on. Whether the step is also kept out of fits as a test is a choice still to be made. The third concerns the mechanism between the claw and the soma that the lead asks for (the item before this one). What these readings add to its brief is the step with APL on: it is too small for the six pairs with near-identical ORN input in every reading, and for the ester pairs when it is read from the claws that the model's input drives, at either pulse. For the ester pairs it stays a lead: from all claws their step is the flies', and from the claws that the input drives, which read less alike than the flies', every group's step is too small. The experiment on where APL's inhibition is summed changed exactly that step and has been run: the summed form is level on the main target ([APL's inhibition on the KC's summed drive](#summed-drive)), so that the step is still open for a mechanism. The stages of its runs have been read since, and its somata, its claws and its steps are those of the family with the clipping ([the claw-to-soma steps read like for like and APL's inhibition as a gain at the claw](#steps-like-for-like)). The same later experiment read the KC somata of both sides alike, the flies' with their trial noise removed and the model's as the recordings are normalized, and it changes what is carried here. With APL on the model's somata differ from the flies' in every such reading, the ester pairs too alike and the alcohol pairs too far apart, and that joins the brief. The step without APL is no longer carried in the form it had. That the model's KCs without APL bring two odors closer than their claw input, where the flies' do not, holds from the claws that the model's input drives and not from all claws, and in no reading that treats the two sides alike are the model's somata without APL too alike. They are the flies' if a KC's signal is taken to saturate with its firing, and too far apart, by up to {{E92/verdict_rows_A.csv:element=soma;set=like_for_like;cond=off;reading=linear_z_none_cosine;group=alcohol:diff ~ .2f}}, if it is taken to grow in proportion to it. Which of the two holds is a question about the recordings and not about the model, whether a KC's calcium signal, as it was recorded, saturates over the range of the KC's firing, and it is a question for the experimenter, with those of the first item of this list. If the signal saturates, nothing is asked of the model's somata without APL as far as the distances between odors go, and the two groups' errors are made with APL on. If it does not, the model's KCs without APL hold the odors too far apart, and that side stays open for a mechanism, which is then judged on raw counts and through the readout alike and taken up only if it lowers the pattern part as well. The steps themselves add nothing to this while they start from all claws, which read more alike than the flies'. The fourth was on the model's input, and it has been taken up ([the measured input for the glomeruli without ORN input](#missing-glomeruli)). The 18 glomeruli of the wiring without ORN input carry only a lateral signal, and their claws are a sixth of all claws. Ten of them were given the responses that have been measured for them, from the lab's other ORN recordings and from Hallem's receptor data, and the stages were read again. With all claws read, the pairs of an ester with an alcohol, upstream with the lab's input, are narrowly not resolved with the fuller input; on the claws of the glomeruli with input the four groups that make up the 66 pairs are not resolved, as before; and eight glomeruli stay without input, no recording of the panel's odors existing for them. On the main target the fuller input is an equal of the lab's input and a little worse, so that the fits and the stage readings stay on the lab's input until it is decided whether the fuller input becomes the base model's. The list of single changes that the reduced searched input left was read in the recordings of the PN dendrites in the same experiment, and the dendrites do not bear it out (the open measurement question, below). A fit of the antennal lobe to the PN dendrites is not taken up: with the noise between flies removed the model's PN stage does not differ from the dendrites in the distances between odors, and evening out the totals less cost the pattern part at fixed scales. The stage recordings hold twelve odors, so that no pair of paa, euc, -aPine or B-myr enters these readings.

src: - **The glomeruli's shares of the claws in other connectomes.** This experiment is on hold. The proportions of the other mushroom bodies that it puts onto the model's wirings come from tables of claws derived from the connectomes' synapses in separate work, and the use of those tables is on hold ([footnote](#fn-derived-tables)). Its counts and most of its runs on the eight wirings had been made when the hold began; the scoring of the runs, the steps after them and every verdict wait, and no count or reading of it is given here. If other connectome outputs take the tables' place, the counts are made again from them before anything else. What it asks and how it is to be judged are as they were set. Every wiring that the best family has been read on, the real wiring, the four within-type claw permutations and the three matched shuffles ([the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), gives each glomerulus the number of claws that it has in the hemibrain, so that the error common to all wirings has been common to wirings with one fly's proportions. The same was asked of the input and answered: with each ORN fly's own input on each wiring, the mean over the model flies has a pattern part of {{E85/populations.csv:group=B1;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} against {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for the eight wirings at the averaged input ([the ORN input as a population of flies](#input-population)). The averaged input is already a mean over flies, though, and the hemibrain is one fly. The question is whether a glomerulus's share of the claws in FlyWire's two mushroom bodies and in the male CNS's two, read from tables of claws derived from their synapses, differs from its share in the hemibrain read the same way, and how such differences compare with the single-glomerulus changes on which the searches of the input agree, a response lowered to about two thirds or raised to about one and a half times ([the controls and the replication of the reduced searched input](#reduced-input)). What those changes stand for is open, the PN dendrites not bearing them out ([the measured input for the glomeruli without ORN input](#missing-glomeruli)), and a glomerulus with more claws in the recorded flies than in the hemibrain is one candidate. The experiment first counts, with no simulation: per glomerulus the claws, the boutons and the PNs of each mushroom body, as shares and as ratios to the hemibrain's; the hemibrain's derived table against the model's wiring; and the searched inputs' factors against the ratios, by a rule fixed beforehand. It then moves claws between glomeruli on the eight wirings, each at its own fit, within each type of KC and with every KC keeping its number of claws, to the proportions of each of the four other mushroom bodies and to the mean proportions of the three brains, holds both response rates, and reads the results as populations, as the wirings and the input flies were read. The controls are the ratios permuted among the glomeruli, the ratios inverted, the ratios at half and at twice their size and a second draw of the claws that are moved. Nothing is fitted to the KC data, so every reading is against all recordings, with the six recordings that are alike beside them. It is judged on the pattern part of [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect) through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:z8_pattern ~ .4f}} for the eight wirings as they are against a floor of {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}, with its amplitude part and its shape part beside it ([how the pattern part is split](#fn-pattern-split)); the mean APL effect, {{E85/populations.csv:group=lab;unit=all;readout=cal:mean_effect ~ +.3f}} against the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, is held with the response rates and is expected to stay. If, by a rule fixed before any run, the pattern part at the mean proportions falls by three thousandths or more, and by half of that on each half of the wirings, while the permuted ratios gain less than half as much, the inverted ones do not gain, at least half of the gain is kept against the six recordings that are alike and every run is inside the realism bands, a part of the common error is one fly's proportions. The family is then fitted again at the mean proportions and, if the gain holds there, read in the family with the firing ceiling, at the flies' pulse and through the trial noise; which proportions the population of wirings is read on becomes a choice to be made, the common error is computed again on that population before another mechanism is aimed at it, and wirings of FlyWire and of the male CNS in the model's format become a proposal with a measured stake. A smaller fall, of half of that or more and with the same controls, is the same case with a smaller stake. If the pattern part moves by less than half of that either way, the likelier outcome by far, the hemibrain's proportions are a fair stand-in for the main target, as the averaged input was: the common error is common to three brains' proportions as well, the other connectomes' wirings are not built for the main target, and the lead that APL's synapses outside the claws left, the same reading with another connectome's counts, stays a question about APL's counts alone ([APL's synapses on the KCs outside the claws](#offclaw-synapses)). That expectation rests on two earlier readings: a glomerulus's weight divided by its number of claws did not lower the pattern part on the real wiring ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)), and the common error is in almost every saved model, most random wirings of an early model among them ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile)); any gain is expected in the shape part. If the pattern part rises by half of that or more, the hemibrain's proportions are nearer to what the recordings ask than the three brains' mean, the ratios at half and at twice their size say whether that is graded, and the hemibrain stays. If the model flies of all five mushroom bodies' proportions gain as a population and their permuted control gains at least half as much, what gains is a mean over more model flies and not these proportions, and it is recorded beside the populations of wirings and of input flies. src: - **The antennal lobe's normalization at the strength the flies' APL asks for.** Unlike the comparisons of the model's APL with the flies' APL, which change no model, this experiment changes the model's antennal lobe and is scored on the main target. By the pattern part of [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect), which decides, it is expected to cost, and it is run to measure that cost where it has not been measured and to read beside it what the change buys. It follows from a first verdict among those comparisons and is the proposal that they had kept for that verdict. [The strength of APL's response in the flies against the model's APL](#apl-strength) has since been read along concentration: in the recordings of APL in the calyx the response to paa at 10^-5 is {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:flies_lo90 ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:flies_hi90 ~ .2f}} of the response at 10^-4 (the interval over resampled flies), and in the best family's fits it is {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:model_linear_min ~ .2f}} to {{E98/comparison_table.csv:comparison=V2, paa at 10^-5 from validation2/diag:model_linear_max ~ .2f}} on the eight wirings with the indicator read in proportion, flatter than the flies on all eight by the rule fixed beforehand, and against the recordings with the concentrations in shuffled order as well. The verdict rests on one recording session's estimate of paa's ORN input at the lower concentration; with the two other sessions' estimates the family is inside the flies' interval through the steeper readings of the indicator and still flatter read in proportion. Against the further recordings of the same flies taken together, whose quality the experimenter who made them has not checked, it is not decided. On the model's side the flatness is made before APL ([the flies' APL against their KC claws in the dual-colour recordings](#apl-vs-claws)): the family's APL follows the summed input to its claws, the claws follow the PNs' summed response, and the model's antennal lobe returns that response nearly equal for every odor. Over the odors of the stage recordings the coefficient of variation of the odors' totals is {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=change:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the model's PNs for {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=orn_input:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the model's ORN input, against {{E90/pn_stage.csv:reading=pn_dend:cv_totals ~ .3f}} in the flies' PN dendrites ([the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages)): the model's antennal lobe cuts the spread of the odors' totals to under a third, and the dendrites show no such evening-out. Of the changes read beside the verdict on the real wiring, only a weaker normalization moved the family's APL towards the flies'. At the third and at the last of the four steps of the earlier screen, each a weaker normalization than the one before ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side)), the ratio read in proportion falls from {{E98/comparison_table_b_points.csv:point=real;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} to {{E98/c_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd1000;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}} and {{E98/c_b_points.csv:point=E77_inhadd3141;comparison=V2;window=win:ratio_linear ~ .2f}}, still above the flies' interval, which it enters through the steeper readings of the indicator. A drive of APL by the KCs' spikes, in the saved fits of earlier bases ([what drives APL](#apl-drive)), a pulse twice as long, the fuller input and the refit near the connectome's bouton share all leave it where it was. What such a normalization does to the per-pair APL effect is known only at fixed scales on the real wiring, where the screen held both response rates and every step is inside the realism bands; in this family none has been read on the eight wirings, fitted, or read at low concentrations. Through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) the pattern part rises from the fit's {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=base:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=S1_inhadd100:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} at the first step and {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=S1_inhadd3141:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} at the last (worse; the floor is {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}). When the comparison with the flies' APL was set, the family fitted with such a change had been expected to be level on the main target and to gain in the KCs' recruitment at low concentration; with the screen read again neither is expected, and the experiment reads both. In the model's antennal lobe a PN's gain is divided by a term that grows with the ORNs' mean activity and stands for lateral inhibition. If it is better and holds on the held-out wirings, nothing is concluded before a control designed for it has run. The family's flat APL then stands as a stated departure from the flies, with its price; the fit of the antennal lobe that had twice been set aside is closed with a number; and the third strength says how much scaling the family takes for nothing. If no step brings the ratio read in proportion inside the flies' interval, judged at about two in three, the normalization alone does not give the flies' fall with concentration, and the chain of totals says whether the rest is the PNs' saturation or the input itself: by first readings the lab's ORN recordings at 10^-5 to 10^-8 hold a small response in most glomeruli, half or more of those stimuli's totals, which [Hallem's receptor data](#hallem-input) do not hold at low concentration, and whether it is response or a floor of the measurement is a question about the ORN recordings. Against the further recordings of the same flies taken together, whose quality the experimenter who made them has not checked, it is not decided. What such a normalization does to the per-pair APL effect is known only at fixed scales on the real wiring, where the screen held both response rates and every step is inside the realism bands; in this family none has been read on the eight wirings, fitted, or read at low concentrations. At the entries on which the runs agree, the dendrites' responses, set against the ORNs' responses in the same glomeruli, do not depart in the list's direction: by a rule fixed beforehand the reading is neither with the list nor against it, and it leans against. The changes are therefore not shown to belong to the antennal lobe, the list stays what a search for these pairs reaches for in this model, and no measurement is asked for it. Of the searches' entries this item keeps only those where a search and Hallem's data point opposite ways, DL1's response to ms and DM6's to paa. src: - **Model and readout changes still worth making:** a saturating APL unit nonlinearity, a calcium readout with the indicator's kinetics (the static saturating readout is done, [above](#readout), so is the recordings' per-KC normalization without the kinetics, [above](#per-kc-normalization), and so is a reading over the flies' response window, first with kinetics that were assumed, [above](#flies-protocol), and then with the kinetics measured in these recordings, which make it nearly a plain count of the spikes at the flies' pulse, [above](#trace-time-course); what is missing is the per-KC reading with those kinetics), measured ORN time courses, real weights for the KCs of unknown type, and, from the weak-odor analyses, better-constrained ORN input for ms, B-myr, euc, paa and 1-8ol (concentrations and glomerular profiles; Hallem's receptor data, [tried above](#hallem-input), cover ms and paa but not B-myr or euc, and at ten times Yang's concentration). From the compressive readout: a mechanism that makes the block through which KCs respond, joined to the best models' mean effect and scored under the compressive and the binarized readout; and, as a constraint that no readout touches and that is now one of [the realism bands](#apl-effect), the number of odors each KC responds to with APL off (the reference model leaves {{E65/model_amplitude.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:odors_0_off ~ .0%}} of its KCs silent and has {{E65/model_amplitude.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:odors_8plus_off ~ .0%}} responding to eight or more of the 16 odors, against {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_0 ~ .0%}} and {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_8plus ~ .0%}} in the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), at nearly the same overall response rate). From the per-odor profile of the APL effect ([above](#apl-effect-parts)): the number-of-odors breadth in a fit of the main target (the exponent of the spike-total breadth has been fitted in the first joint fit's family, where the loss is lowest near 2, [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)); for the pair-specific part, gain sets without DM5 fitted and scored on it, and a form of the breadth weighting that keeps APL off the high-firing KCs without leaving the distance between two odors to the few KCs they share through one glomerulus; and no per-odor APL rule fitted to the response rates, which the per-odor APL oracle shows would not move the main target. From the low end of the readout ([above](#readout)): the amplitudes of the responses with APL off as a second constraint for later fits of the main target, beside the number of odors per KC and like it independent of how the target is defined (with APL output blocked (TNT) {{data:tnt_share_z_above_4 ~ .1%}} of the flies' KC × odor entries are above 4 z and their responders' mean amplitude is {{data:tnt_resp_amp_mean_z ~ .2f}} z, about as in the control flies; the reference model with APL off, read as in the table of amplitudes there, has {{E68/partB_amplitude.csv:model=ref40;config=floor_noise:share_above_4_off ~ .1%}} and {{E68/partB_amplitude.csv:model=ref40;config=floor_noise:resp_amp_mean_off ~ .2f}} z); and, for the recordings, what makes the negative values, now that how the trial means are made is known (each KC's trace z-scored over the whole recording, the 5 s before the odor as the baseline, 0.7 of the neuropil subtracted; [the footnote on baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units)), which leaves the order of the odors within a repeat to look at (the order is on hand now and has not been read for them; what it and the repeats show of the flies' variability is [above](#repeat-structure)), since the negative values, which repeat across trials, make up a fifth of the control flies' entries ({{data:ctrl_share_z_below_m025 ~ .0%}} below −0.25 z). From [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits): the three fits that went through the trial noise run again on further seeds of the noise, since on raw counts the breadth-2 fit's margin over the breadth-3 fit is about the difference between the two noise levels (if the margin holds over seeds, the breadth-2 family is the lowest under both definitions; if it does not, raw counts do not separate a model that has the block from one that gave it up, and the block has to be held as a target of its own); the breadth-2 fit repeated on shuffled draws of the wiring, the replication the earlier joint fits were given, has been run as the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings ([above](#wiring-population)): its loss returns on the draws, so the family is the model to build on (what follows from it is listed further down); a mechanism that spreads the recruitment with APL off over more KCs, which neither a term on odors per KC in the loss nor the fitted parameters do, was the next step and has been run as the input-scaled KC threshold ([above](#input-scaled-threshold); what follows from it is listed further down); and, for the block under the readout, the mechanism acting on which KCs respond that is listed above, now with the breadth-2 fit as its base, since a block term in the loss does not raise that fit's block under the readout. From the high-firing KCs that survive APL ([above](#high-firing-kcs)): a carrier of the block that is not a few over-driven KCs, which the mechanisms acting on the set of responding KCs are, joined to a model without such cells; the single pseudo-recordings of a model through the matched trial noise, scored as single pairs of recordings were, have been run since, and the breadth-2 fit is already as close to the data's mean as a single pair of recordings is ([above](#input-scaled-threshold)). The route through the weak-input odors' input is not taken up, because the archived models that already take it change the survivors and the mean effect little: in the reference model as fitted at 5 %, leaving DP1m's gain out leaves {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__loo_DP1m:n_survivors ~ .0f}} survivors against {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__full:n_survivors ~ .0f}} with all eight glomeruli gained and a mean APL effect on raw counts of {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__loo_DP1m:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} against {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__full:raw__mean ~ +.3f}}; with every odor's input scaled until its response rate with APL on is the flies', the reference model has {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E62_rate_oracle;tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_on:n_survivors ~ .0f}} against {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:n_survivors ~ .0f}} and {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E62_rate_oracle;tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_on:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} against {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} (the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}). No further re-draws of single cells' claws are planned. From the firing ceiling for the KCs ([above](#firing-ceiling)): whether the ceiling joins the base model, and at which strength, which needs one number, the largest spike count of a fly KC to a 0.5 s odor (the bound used is a reading of the recordings' means and standard deviations; through the trial noise the literature setting is as good as the stronger one, so it is the setting to adopt if the ceiling joins); the literature setting fitted on re-drawn wirings has been run ([above](#wiring-population)): the gain on raw counts returns on each of the three wirings tried, and the mean over wirings with the ceiling scores on raw counts what it scores under the readout; the same mean has since been read through the trial noise ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), where it is level with the mean of the family without a ceiling, so that the gain on raw counts belongs to the model without noise and to single wirings; the block and the natural-source alignment on a base with the ceiling, which takes them away with the strong responders as the readout does, so that the carrier of the block listed above has to work on that base; the recruitment with APL off, which the ceiling leaves as it was and the input-scaled KC threshold moves off the many-claw KCs at a cost on the main target ([above](#input-scaled-threshold)); and, if the ceiling is adopted, a less schematic adaptation (two time constants, or synaptic depression at the claws); the check that its effect does not need a time constant longer than the odor has been made, and at the flies' 2 s pulse it does need one to keep its level in full, the 1 s adaptation raising the loss by {{diff:E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r1.29_d20.7:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} to {{diff:E84/protocol_readings_measured_kernel.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.05_d21.9:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} there with the indicator's kinetics as measured ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol); [the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)). From the input-scaled KC threshold ([above](#input-scaled-threshold)): which KCs carry the APL effect, which has been run as the APL effect split by odors per KC ([above](#apl-effect-by-class); what follows from it is listed further down); the family with the firing ceiling and the scaling at a small power under the reading of the per-KC normalization of the recordings, which the same experiment fitted and where the scaling cost nothing only because the fit left the two-spike operating point, so that the fit is to be made again with its response-rate terms on the two-spike criterion, as fits now are, if that reading is taken up for fits (if the scaling then costs less than a draw of the wiring moves the loss, the ceiling with the scaling is the candidate base and is compared on re-drawn wirings, where it has not been run; if it costs more, it stays out under every reading); a fit with the scaling and a term on the number of odors per KC in the loss, to see what the main target costs when the broad responders are held at the flies' share; other forms of the scaling (a threshold set from each KC's drive over a reference set of odors, a normalization of the drive per glomerulus), which were not tried and matter only if a fit with the scaling is taken up; and, for the realism bands, whether the band on the number of odors per KC should also hold the spread of that number, which in the breadth-2 family is above every recording's on all eight wirings it has been fitted on and which the band as defined does not see. From the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings ([above](#wiring-population)): whether the main target is defined on a mean over wirings read through the trial noise, as the data's mean is one over flies and trials, which is a choice about the target like the readout (until it is made, that mean is given beside the single-wiring number, and two fits closer than about the draw term are compared on the real wiring and at least two re-drawn ones); the error common to all wirings as the target of the next mechanisms, the too-small APL effect among the esters and on the pairs of eb, 1-8ol, IaA and ep above all, read beside the APL effect split by odors per KC, which is reported for each fit and not fitted ([above](#apl-effect-by-class)) (a mechanism that lowers that error on the real wiring and on re-drawn ones moves the family toward the floor, while one that lowers the loss on the real wiring alone has fitted that wiring's own remainder); the first such mechanism, a profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli, has been run and does not carry that error ([above](#glomerulus-profile); what follows from it is listed further down); recruitment at the weakest input in the family without a per-claw threshold, ma at 10^-7 first, through a per-claw transfer that adds drive at low input in place of a softened threshold (if it brings ma to the flies' fraction at no cost on the 16-odor panel, the low-concentration recordings become constraints the family meets; if it costs there, they stay a regime of their own); and, of the two checks on wirings that were left, the mean over wirings with the firing ceiling read through the trial noise has been run ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), and the input-scaled KC threshold on re-drawn wirings beside the ceiling fits made there has not. From the per-KC normalization of the recordings ([above](#per-kc-normalization)): which definition the model's side of the main target is held to, raw counts, the calibrated readout or the per-KC reading, the one of the three that is taken from how the recordings were made (the reading and the readout order the models alike, so the choice moves the numbers more than the ranking; until it is made every fit is reported under all three, with its response-rate terms on the two-spike count); a mechanism, or a term of the readout, by which a KC that responds to many odors responds more strongly to each of them, as the flies' KCs do and the models' do not (if a model gets that growth inside the realism bands, its amplitudes with APL off, listed above as a second constraint, and its units under the reading come nearer the flies' together; if the growth can only be had with the strong firing that the firing ceiling removes, it belongs to what the calcium signal adds to the spike count, and the readout is the place for it); the reading with the indicator's kinetics, since a response in the recordings outlasts its window and the loss of the family without the ceiling moves with that share while the family with the ceiling does not (the kinetics are on hand now, a rise of about {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=onset:rise ~ .1f}} s and a decay of about {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=onset:decay ~ .0f}} s: [the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)); the data side of the main target, which is still computed from the z-scored values, has been measured ([above](#data-side)): the flies' per-pair APL effect, its floor and its split by odors per KC were computed with each KC's responses in baseline-noise units, beside the effect as measured, and only the mean effect depends on the unit, so the pattern part and the order of the models stand and the unit is a choice about the mean, like the readout (what follows from it is listed further down); and, before the amplitudes, response rates or numbers of odors per KC of Remy's wild-type megamat KC recordings are compared with these, a check of how those recordings were normalized. From the APL effect split by odors per KC ([above](#apl-effect-by-class)): the split of the APL effect over the classes of KCs is reported for every later fit beside the realism bands, as a statistic of its own and not as a term of a loss, since the family that is asked for it pays on the total and its pattern part does not move; the pattern part is looked for in the per-pair errors that remain whatever the classes do, which the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition took up ([above](#glomerulus-profile); what follows from it is listed further down); and, if the main target stays in the recordings' z-scored units, what would bring the class at four to seven odors to the flies' is a mechanism that makes the KCs of that class carry less of the overlap between odors with APL on, which is where the models differ from the flies in it (in the archive a per-claw threshold and the input-scaled threshold do that, each with a higher pattern part; if a mechanism does it on re-drawn wirings without that cost, the model comes nearer the flies in which KCs carry the effect at no price on the target, and if none does, the class stays a known difference that the total does not need); with each KC's responses in baseline-noise units the flies' class at four to seven carries none of the effect, and there is nothing to bring the models' class to ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)). From the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition ([above](#glomerulus-profile)): the common error, a too-small APL effect among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms and a too-large one among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al on every wiring, stays the target of the next mechanisms. They were looked for first in what reaches the KCs, which has been run as the input side of the error common to all wirings ([above](#input-side); what follows from it is listed further down). A fixed profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli did not carry it, and the few saved models with less than half of it, the oracle co-responder suppression apart, change the input and not APL: a weaker antennal-lobe normalization and random wirings on the early model with one unit per KC, Hallem's receptor data as the input for the weak odors, a 130 Hz per-claw threshold followed by a cap. Each is on an earlier model and carries a different error, not a smaller one, than the breadth-2 fit's, and scaling APL's inhibition of the PN boutons is not among them. The test for each was the one the profile was put to, in the best family: whether it lowers the common error on the real wiring and on re-drawn ones without adding as much error elsewhere. What it has to change is known in outline: on raw counts the model has the distances among those six esters about right with APL off and too small with APL on, and, counted above 1 z, the KCs that respond to four to seven odors carry too much of the overlap between odors with APL on ([above](#apl-effect-by-class)). No change of the input screened in the best family does this, on the real wiring or carried over to re-drawn ones, and only about two fifths of the common error is in the geometry that the two conditions share; scores fitted directly in simulation on several wirings at once have since been tried and carry a small part of the common error to wirings and recordings they were not fitted to, short of the test set for them and at a cost on raw counts ([above](#cross-wiring-fit)), so that what is left on APL's side is inhibition that depends on the odor otherwise than by growing with a bouton's or a claw's own input, the form that was emulated and did not help. The two changes at the cell site that raised the block under the readout to the flies' on the real wiring have since been run on the seven re-drawn wirings, where they lower the pattern part of the mean over them by {{E83/existing_changes.csv:change=A1_ridge_x0.5;unit=draws7:z8_gain ~ .4f}} and {{E83/existing_changes.csv:change=A1_C2_four_x2;unit=draws7:z8_gain ~ .4f}}; the block was not read in those runs, so whether a block made through which KCs respond, the carrier listed above, holds in the best family or belongs to the hemibrain wiring is still to be read from them. Each of these states its target against all the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) and against the six that are alike, because the test on split halves of the recordings failed through the other two; the two have since been found stronger and not different in the pattern of their distances, so the mean over all eight is the target and the six are given beside it ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)); their responses have since been found to decay about three times faster than every other recording's, and one of them is recorded as having APL unlabelled, so that whether the two stay in the target is with the experimenter ([the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)). And the firing ceiling's case for the base model has its like-for-like number: as a mean over four wirings read through the trial noise, the family with the ceiling is level on raw counts with the family without it, so that the case rests on single wirings, on the model without noise and on realism. From the data side of the main target ([above](#data-side)), which the response criterion of the realism bands ([footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units)) had left to measure: which unit the flies' side of the target is held to, the recordings' z-scored values, as elsewhere on this page, or baseline-noise units, the unit of the realism bands, with the mean over all the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) in either case (the choice moves the mean part of [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect) and nothing else, so until it is made the families are ranked on the pattern part and the mean part is given against both effects; if the target stays on the z-scored values, the mean part is nearly closed for the family with the firing ceiling and the pattern part is what remains; if it moves to baseline-noise units, the mean part is open again for every model, by {{diff:data:noise_apl_effect_mean -- E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ .3f}} for the best family fitted to that effect and by more through the trial noise); for that case, a KC response that grows with the KC's breadth, the mechanism or term of the readout listed above from the per-KC normalization of the recordings, as the way to a larger mean effect that is not more responses with APL off, the route that the fit to the effect in baseline-noise units took at a cost on the pattern and toward the edge of the band on the ratio of the response rates (if a model gets the growth inside the realism bands, the mean part closes without that cost; if it does not, the mean part stays open in those units for this family; read since without simulation, the growth alone does not close it, weighting the best fit's spike counts by the KC's breadth moving its mean effect by {{diff:E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p_is_flies=True;target=noise:mean -- E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p=0.0;target=noise:mean ~ +.3f}} at most: [the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)); the split of the effect by odors per KC reported in both units for every later fit; and the state of the two strongest recordings, in which blocking APL output brings the pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms far closer than in the other six, as a target of its own for the mechanisms that change what reaches the KCs, if the experimenter's answer keeps the two in the target ([the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course); the fixed changes of the input screened in the input side of the error common to all wirings, [above](#input-side), were scored against all eight recordings and against the six, not against the two, and none lowered the common error; the high per-claw knee without a dead zone, [above](#claw-knee), was scored in the same way, and where it lowers the ester group's error, with little or nothing passed below the knee, the pattern part is higher), since neither a weaker APL nor a shifted threshold makes that state in the model. The readout itself stays as it is, with no measurement noise, one-spike floor or membrane-potential term. From the input side of the error common to all wirings ([above](#input-side)): the common error stays the target, and the handles on the input that were screened are closed for this family. None lowers it; an input searched within a factor of two on the real wiring does not hold on other wirings at the size the search gave it, and at 0.6 of that size holds on wirings and recordings that it had not seen ([above](#cross-wiring-fit)), with its controls holding and by less than the test asks once a second split of the flies is read ([above](#reduced-input)); and the weak odors' input stays the lab's, since neither Hallem's receptor data nor the input searched for the weak odors helps the best family. Of the changes to what reaches the KCs, the high per-claw knee without a dead zone was not among the handles and has been run since ([above](#claw-knee)): it holds the pairs with near-identical ORN input apart only with a dead zone that silences ms and B-myr, and the per-claw transfer is closed for this family on the main target. Nor does the comparison's definition make the common error: against the six recordings that are alike and against the effect in baseline-noise units it is as large ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)). What else is left to propose lies outside what was screened: how APL's inhibition unfolds in time and adapts, differences between types of KCs, and inhibition that depends on the odor otherwise than by growing with a bouton's or a claw's own input (of these, the length of the odor pulse, thresholds that differ between the two conditions as an adaptation to the block would leave them, the types of KCs and each odor's recruitment have since been run on the real wiring, and none lowers the common error: [the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates); APL's time constant has been run as well and does not lower it: [the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)). Each is put to the test that the profile and the input were put to, on the real wiring and on re-drawn ones, against all the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) with the six that are alike beside them (a mechanism that lowers the common error on wirings it was not chosen on moves the family toward the floor of the pattern part; one that lowers the loss on the real wiring alone has fitted that wiring's remainder, as the searched input did at the size the search gave it). What such a mechanism has to change is mostly not the distances that the two conditions share: about two fifths of the common error is inherited from the distances with APL off, and the larger part is in what APL does to particular pairs. Read from the flies' own responses, on the spike counts of the fits, that larger part is, while the model recruits in its own way, not in the form of APL's inhibition but in the responses that APL acts on; with each odor's recruitment without APL set to the flies' on four wirings the pattern part does not fall, and a part of what is left is then read on APL's side ([the form of APL's inhibition in the flies' own responses](#inhibition-form)). The flies' form simulated in place of APL on those four wirings has since done far worse than the model's own APL, and the split of the error into who responds and how strongly points to who responds without being a verdict ([the common error split into who responds and how strongly](#responder-sets)). The two steps that followed from both, an estimate of the co-response that passes its check and the breadth weighting inside the models' APL, have been taken, and both close ([the co-response read with a checked estimate and the breadth weighting inside the models' APL](#breadth-weighting)), and the place where the feedback APL's inhibition is summed has been varied since and is level ([APL's inhibition on the KC's summed drive](#summed-drive)); what follows from them is the item on the responses without APL above. Two descriptions go with it as leads: an odor's term in the common error follows how much more its response fraction grows in the model than in the flies when APL is removed, less so against the six recordings that are alike; and the model's antennal lobe evens out the odors' total drive, which a weaker normalization undoes at a cost on the pattern part. The input has since been taken up again as a change fitted on several wirings at once, tested by whether two halves of the recordings give the same factors: they do not, and the fitted input does not hold on the half of the recordings that it did not see ([above](#cross-wiring-fit); what follows from it is the item on the reduced searched input above). From the APL calyx maps against the connectome ([above](#apl-calyx-maps)): the common error stays the target, and a spatially local APL at the boutons has not been fitted in the best family. The view, the dorsal direction, the size of a pixel and the plane of each recording are now known; which edge of the image is medial and where the zero of the depth was set are asked (listed with the data below). With them the prediction of APL's map from the wiring is tested at one orientation and one depth: if it matches the measured maps and the co-localization at that depth passes the test that was set for it, the local fit is taken up; if it matches and the co-localization does not pass, APL's activity is local and its locality does not carry the pair error, and the class closes with a measured length; if it does not match, PN input alone does not make APL's map. The model with local APL units is not a base for such a fit as it stands, since its maps are flatter and less alike between odors than the measured ones at every coupling; if units are taken up again, those two statistics are what their coupling is set by. On the model's side the per-claw knee and the candidates outside the calyx have both been run, and neither carries the common error ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee); [the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)); what the pulse leaves to decide is above. From the high per-claw knee without a dead zone ([above](#claw-knee)): the per-claw transfer is closed for this family on the main target. The six pairs with near-identical ORN input stay a target of their own and are reported for every later mechanism beside the common error; where a mechanism is read through the trial noise, their correlations are taken without the noise by the estimate across repeats. The best fit has about half the flies' APL effect on them and is too high mostly in their correlation with APL on. And a selection of responders at the claw that needs no dead zone is a lead for the release with APL off: if one moves the release off the many-claw KCs and brings the spread of the number of odors per KC to the flies' while ms and B-myr keep their responses, it is put to the main target on the real wiring and on re-drawn ones, as the input-scaled KC threshold was ([above](#input-scaled-threshold)); if such a selection can only be had with the dead zone, the release through the many-claw KCs stays a known difference of this family. From the flies' variability across the three repeats ([above](#repeat-structure)): the levels of the KC data without the trial noise are the estimates across repeats, and the pipeline stays the way a model is read as the data are made, its numbers having held under a noise with the flies' shares. A trial noise that is right where the present one is not needs a source of shared variability that is larger without APL, most of it a slow drift over the session, so a slow change in a subset of the KCs or in the input, and is held to the same-repeat gap of the responders with APL off, which every noise tried leaves a third short of the flies'. It is taken up when a result comes to rest on the make-up of the noise, as the block through the noise does: a mechanism proposed for the block has its block read through both noises (if the block holds through both, it does not depend on what the trials share; if it holds only through the re-specified noise, it is read as the three fits of the reference family are now; if only through the pipeline's, it rests on shared jitter that the flies do not have).

src: **The alternatives, and why not.** A linear fit of control on APL output blocked (TNT) assumes the change is proportional; with the saturation near 1 it explains less of the control variance (R² 0.85 against 0.94) and leaves curved residuals, so its block estimate (+0.098) mixes the pair-specific effect with the curvature the line cannot follow. A parametric saturating curve (a power or logistic function) has fewer degrees of freedom but imposes a shape the data would have to meet, and the block estimate then depends on that choice. Rank correlation alone (Spearman 0.87) tests monotonicity but gives no per-pair residual, so it cannot locate the block. Comparing the two matrices with the expectation from response density (the confound controls) asks a different, complementary question (whether two odors share more KCs than their response fractions predict) and is reported separately as the excess shared responders. The isotonic fit's own limitation is that a step function through 120 points can follow local noise, so its R² is an upper bound for any smooth monotone curve; that is why the residual is read for a block of nine pairs rather than for single pairs, and why the measurement ceiling is computed with the same fit.

src: **The earlier recipe, and why it was dropped.** From 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-13 the matrix mixed two recipes. The 72 pairs within a panel (66 among the megamat odors, 6 among the validation2 odors) were correlated within each fly and the correlations averaged over flies. The 48 pairs across the panels, for which no fly has both odors, used the fly-mean responses, as now. A correlation within one fly carries that fly's measurement noise, which lowers it, so the pairs within a panel sat further apart than their fly-mean responses are and the pairs across the panels did not: the two kinds of pairs were on different scales, by an amount that depends only on the panel an odor was imaged in. The table gives the matrix, and the KC matrices' agreement with it, by both recipes.

src: What changes is the distances with APL output blocked: there the odors start more alike than they end, their mean distance rising through the window and past it, while the control flies' rises little after the third second (first row). Its pattern across the pairs is the target's from the second second on and least so in the first (sixth row).
