src: The first fits better, with a root mean square misfit of {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=onset:rms ~ .3f}} against {{E84/kernel_fits.csv:level=subset;subset=control flies;selection=resp;fit=free;drive=steady:rms ~ .3f}} of a KC's baseline noise, and on synthetic traces with the recordings' volume rate and noise the fit tells firing that lasts 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 s apart in every draw. But the fitted rise shortens as the firing is taken to last longer, so that what the traces leave open is the form of the kernel between the two limits, and both are carried below. Either way the decay is several times the 3 s that the reading of the models as the flies were recorded had assumed, and four times the slowest that it read beside it.

src: Two of the page's statistics (the structure vs wild-type somata, and the 66-pair residual that the natural-source alignment is computed from) rest on Remy's wild-type megamat KC data: trial-mean responses of KC somata imaged in 18 flies (4 from 2022 and 14 from 2018–19 with partial odor panels), 17 megamat odors at 10^-3, distances as one minus the Pearson correlation across KCs. Yang's APL16 data share 12 of those odors ({{data:n_ref_pairs ~ .0f}} pairs), at the same concentrations, with distances as one minus the cosine similarity across KCs, per recording and averaged. On those pairs the two labs' wild-type matrices agree at ρ={{data:rho_ctrl_remy_soma ~ .2f}} on odor-odor distances (90 % interval over Yang's recordings {{data:rho_ctrl_remy_soma.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:rho_ctrl_remy_soma.hi ~ .2f}}; Pearson r {{data:pearson_ctrl_remy_soma ~ .2f}} between the two sets of distances; {{data:rho_ctrl_remy_soma_2022 ~ .2f}} against Remy's 2022 flies alone), against a measurement ceiling of {{data:ctrl_ceiling_66 ~ .2f}} for Yang's control matrix on these pairs; a single control recording agrees with Remy's mean at ρ={{data:ctrl_rec_rho_remy_soma ~ .2f}} and with the mean of the other ten control recordings at {{data:ctrl_rec_rho_loo ~ .2f}}. Remy's KC claws agree less ({{data:rho_ctrl_remy_claw ~ .2f}}). The ranking is what agrees; the levels are on different scales (correlation and cosine distance), with Remy's somata at a mean of {{data:remy_soma_mean_66 ~ .2f}} and Yang's control flies at {{data:ctrl_mean_66 ~ .2f}} on the same pairs.

src: Remy's wild-type somata sit closer to the ORN input than Yang's control KCs do (ρ on odor-odor distances with the ORNs {{data:rho_remy_soma_orn ~ .2f}} against {{data:rho_ctrl_orn_66 ~ .2f}}; Yang's flies with APL output blocked {{data:rho_tnt_orn_66 ~ .2f}}), and Yang's APL-blocked matrix agrees with Remy's somata as well as the control matrix does ({{data:rho_tnt_remy_soma ~ .2f}} against {{data:rho_ctrl_remy_soma ~ .2f}}): on this panel, Remy's somata are intermediate between Yang's two genotypes in their ORN-likeness. What they share with the control matrix in particular is the part beyond the ORN input: the 66-pair residuals agree at ρ={{data:ctrl_struct_wt ~ .2f}} for the control flies and {{data:tnt_struct_wt ~ .2f}} with APL output blocked, which is why the "structure vs wild-type somata" of a model is read against the control flies' value. src: The noise is per-KC excitability jitter. On each simulated trial every KC's spiking threshold is multiplied by its own random factor, 1 + σ ξ, with ξ a standard normal draw made once per KC and trial and shared by that trial's APL-on and APL-off runs (a factor below 0.01 is clipped to 0.01). σ is calibrated per model so that the model's single-trial same-odor floor, one minus the cosine similarity between two trials of the same odor, matches the control flies' {{data:ctrl_single_trial_floor ~ .2f}}, and the mean threshold is re-tuned so that the per-trial APL-on response rate stays at the deterministic run's. Thirty such trials, drawn from a seeded generator so that every model gets the same draws, are grouped into ten pseudo-recordings of three and processed as the KC data are: the three trials of a recording are averaged, the cosine distances between odors are taken on those means and averaged over the recordings, and the fruity × small-ester block is the mean isotonic excess of the nine pairs; the grand mean over all thirty trials is reported beside it. "The pipeline" on this page is this procedure, and "the block through the noise" its block. Noise on the PN firing rates was tried first and set aside because it averages out over the response window and cannot reach the data's floors; jitter of each glomerulus's input gain reaches them as the threshold jitter does and is the alternative the trial-to-trial variability experiment kept beside it.

src: **How this noise compares with the flies'.** Because ξ is drawn once per KC and trial, a KC's threshold is off by the same factor for all odors of a trial: all of the model's trial-to-trial variability is shared between the odors of a trial. In the recordings only part of it is. The same-repeat gap, the single-trial distance between two odors of different repeats minus that between two odors of the same repeat, is {{data:repeat_gap_ctrl ~ .3f}} in control flies and {{data:repeat_gap_tnt ~ .3f}} with APL output blocked (TNT), and at its matched level the pipeline gives the breadth-2 APL-effect fit {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;condition=both:gap_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;condition=both:gap_off ~ .3f}} with APL off. With the noise re-specified to the flies' shares, a smaller shared jitter plus noise independent between odors, the scores of the populations of wirings read through the pipeline hardly move, and the block of the reference family's fits is cut by less ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)).

src: The margin proxy predicts what the pipeline would measure (the floors, the per-trial response rates, the odor-odor distances, the block through the noise) from one deterministic run, without simulating the noise. It does so by replaying trials: for each of the pipeline's thirty trials it takes the exact jittered thresholds the pipeline draws for that trial (the same seeded draws, the same re-tuned mean threshold, the same clipping) and integrates every KC's recovered drive at those thresholds; the spike counts per KC and odor that come out are one replayed trial, and the thirty are processed exactly as the pipeline processes its simulated trials. The one difference from the pipeline is that nothing else in the network reacts to the jitter: each KC's drive carries the KC–KC inhibition from the deterministic run's spikes, not from the other KCs' spikes on that noisy trial. APL is driven by the claws and the PN layer is not jittered in these models, so the KC–KC inhibition is the only feedback the replay leaves out, which is why the proxy reproduces the pipeline exactly for a model without KC–KC inhibition and departs from it in proportion to that inhibition's weight relative to the threshold.

src: **What is done.** A model's distance between two odors is a cosine distance across KCs on spike counts (one count per KC and odor, the spikes in the response); the flies' is a cosine distance on z-scored trial means of a nuclear calcium signal, which compresses large responses. The readout replaces each spike count n by n / (n + k) before the model's distances are taken; k, the half-saturation count, is the number of spikes at which the readout reaches half of its maximum of 1. Zero stays zero and a larger count always reads larger, so which KCs respond (two or more spikes), every response rate and the realism bands are exactly as on raw counts; what changes is how much each responding KC weighs in the cosine. With the current reference model's k of {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=saturating_cal_pr:param ~ .1f}} spikes, a KC that fires 2 spikes reads {{lit:0.16 # n / (n + k) at n = 2 with the reference model's calibrated k, 10.46 spikes (results/E65_spike_count_readout/key_models.csv, readout saturating_cal_pr, column param)}}, one that fires 20 reads {{lit:0.66 # n / (n + k) at n = 20 with the reference model's calibrated k, 10.46 spikes (results/E65_spike_count_readout/key_models.csv, readout saturating_cal_pr, column param)}}, and the model's most active KC with APL on, at {{E65/model_amplitude.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes, reads {{lit:0.88 # n / (n + k) at n = 78, the reference model's largest APL-on count, with its calibrated k, 10.46 spikes (results/E65_spike_count_readout/key_models.csv, readout saturating_cal_pr, column param)}}: it weighs {{lit:5.5 # the readout of 78 spikes over the readout of 2 spikes, n / (n + k) with the reference model's calibrated k, 10.46 spikes: 0.882 / 0.160}} times as much as the 2-spike KC, where on raw counts it weighs {{lit:39 # 78 spikes, the reference model's largest APL-on count (results/E65_spike_count_readout/model_amplitude.csv, column max_count_on), over 2 spikes}} times as much.

src: **How k is set.** k is set for each model separately, on that model's spike counts with APL on, and never on the APL effect. The quantity matched to the flies is the participation ratio of an odor's response vector, (Σx²)² / (N Σx⁴) over the N KCs' values x: the effective fraction of the KCs that carry the odor's squared response, the quantity a cosine weighs (1 when all KCs carry it equally, 1/N when one KC carries all of it). It is computed on responders only (in a recording, trial means at or below 1 set to 0; in a model, entries under two spikes set to 0, for this statistic alone) and averaged over the 16 odors and, in the flies, over the {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} control recordings. The control flies' value is {{data:ctrl_participation_ratio_resp ~ .1%}} ({{data:tnt_participation_ratio_resp ~ .1%}} with APL output blocked (TNT)); the current reference model's raw counts with APL on give {{E65/model_amplitude.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:participation_ratio_resp_on ~ .1%}}, a response more concentrated than the flies'. A small k evens out the responders and raises the ratio, a large k leaves the counts almost as they are, and k is the value at which the readout of the model's APL-on counts has the control flies' ratio, found by bisection on log k between 0.001 and 1000 spikes (when no k in that range reaches it, the nearer end is used, as for {{lit:47 # results/E65_spike_count_readout/by_variant_readout.csv: rows with readout saturating_cal_pr whose at_bound is true}} of the {{E65/readout_summary.csv:readout=saturating_cal_pr:n_variants ~ .0f}} saved models). The same k is then applied to the model's APL-off counts, every count read, single spikes included. Nothing from the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) and nothing about the effect enters the calibration, so the APL-off distances and the per-pair APL effect remain predictions. The calibration gives {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=saturating_cal_pr:param ~ .1f}} spikes for the current reference model, {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k2;readout=saturating_cal_pr:param ~ .1f}} for the first joint fit and between {{lit:4.5 and 15 # results/E65_spike_count_readout/key_models.csv, readout saturating_cal_pr, column param: 4.52 to 14.94 over the nine key models (E65_spike_count_readout.md)}} spikes across the models examined most closely, far from both a k below one spike, which would count every firing KC alike, and a k above the largest counts, which would leave the counts as they are. Fits of the main target that carry the readout in their loss set k again at every evaluation, on that evaluation's APL-on counts.

src: **The alternatives, and what the readout is not.** Other ways of fixing the compression without reference to the APL effect were run beside this one: a power-law readout, n raised to a power below 1, calibrated in the same way; the saturating readout calibrated instead to the share of an odor's squared response held by the top 1 % of KCs among the control flies' responders ({{data:ctrl_top1_share_resp ~ .0%}}), to the coefficient of variation (standard deviation over mean) of their responders' amplitudes ({{data:ctrl_resp_amp_cv ~ .2f}}) or to their participation ratio on all values, sub-threshold ones included ({{data:ctrl_participation_ratio_all ~ .1%}}); and a map that sends the model's APL-on counts, rank for rank, onto the control flies' pooled responder amplitudes. They agree: for the current reference model the APL-effect loss is between {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=power_cal_pr:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} and {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=saturating_cal_pr_all:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} under these alternatives, against {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=saturating_cal_pr:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} under the readout used and {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} on raw counts (lower is better; the data's floor is {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}}), and an uncalibrated square root gives {{E65/key_models.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3;readout=sqrt:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}. With so little between them, the participation ratio was kept because it measures directly what the cosine weighs and is computed in the same way on the model and on the recordings. The readout is a static, elementwise map, not a model of the imaging: it has no indicator kinetics and no nuclear localization, and it does not emulate the recordings' per-KC normalization (a z-score of each KC's trace over the whole recording; [the footnote on baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units)), which a separate reading of the models does ([the per-KC normalization of the recordings](#per-kc-normalization)). Below the response criterion the readout holds nothing, where the recordings hold weak and negative values; giving it measurement noise and a calibrated weight for single spikes was tried and leaves the scores where they were ([the next footnote](#fn-readout-low-end)), so it carries neither. Whether the main target is scored on raw counts or through this readout is still to be decided, and until then both are reported; in a model whose KCs have a firing ceiling the two scores nearly coincide ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)).

src: **The recordings below the response criterion.** Everything here is computed per recording, from the z-scored value of each KC, odor and trial, and averaged over the recordings of a genotype; a KC × odor entry is a responder when its mean over the three trials is above 1 z and sub-threshold otherwise. For the reproducibility of a band of values, entries are selected by their mean over two of the three trials and read on the third, each trial held out in turn. For the three terms, a pair's cosine similarity is written as a sum over KCs (the product of the KC's two trial means, divided by the norms of the two odors' response vectors), and each KC's product goes to the term for two responders, for a responder and a sub-threshold entry, or for two sub-threshold entries. The terms add up to the cosine, and a distance is one minus a cosine, so the terms' changes between the control flies and the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) add up to the pair's APL effect. The intervals come from drawing the recordings of each genotype again with replacement. A term's share of the pattern is its covariance with the whole effect across the 120 pairs divided by the variance of the whole effect, so the three shares add up to 1. The responder × sub-threshold term divides further by its sub-threshold entry: of its {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}}, {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one_weak__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} comes from weakly positive entries, {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one_negative__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} from negative ones and {{E68/data_effect_terms.csv:one_unreliable__effect_mean:observed ~ +.3f}} from entries with a trial above 1.5 z, responses that did not repeat. Part of the sub-threshold structure is a baseline of the KC that also shows in its response to the solvent, part is weak broad tuning, and part of the noise is shared by the trials of one repeat; the negative values in particular depend on how the trial means are made: each KC's trace is z-scored over the whole recording and a trial's response is taken relative to the 5 s before the odor ([the footnote on baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units)).

src: **What was added to the model's readout.** The readout's values are put in the recordings' units by a factor c, set so that the share of the model's APL-on entries above 1 z is the control flies' response rate. The measurement noise is independent Gaussian noise of the control flies' per-trial size on every KC × odor entry, in ten recordings of three trials per model, processed as the recordings are (for the reading as measured, its expected effect on the distances is computed in closed form). The one-spike floor is the offset b in (n + b) / (n + b + k) for a KC with at least one spike; 0 stays 0. k, b and c are found together, by iteration to a fixed point, so that through the noise the model's APL-on entries have the control flies' response rate above 1 z, share between 0.5 and 1.5 z and participation ratio among responders. Nothing from the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), no distance and nothing about the APL effect enters, and the same values are applied to the APL-off counts. The offset was first to be set on the share between 0.5 and 1 z; that share hardly moves with b once c holds the response rate, the calibration ran to its bounds in most models, and the band was widened. With the wider band it still reaches a bound in part of the saved models (k in {{E68/medians.csv:config=floor_noise;reading=graded:n_K_at_bound ~ .0f}} and b in {{E68/medians.csv:config=floor_noise;reading=graded:n_floor_at_bound ~ .0f}} of the {{E68/medians.csv:config=floor_noise;reading=graded:n ~ .0f}} behind the medians), the reference model and the first joint fit not among them. Models in which fewer entries hold any spike than the control flies have responders cannot reach the recordings' response rate under any c; these {{E68/medians.csv:config=floor_noise;reading=graded:n_rate_unreachable ~ .0f}}, mostly early models tuned to 5 %, are left out of the medians. A first probe had found the first joint fit's pattern part sensitive to the weight of a single spike; that was with k held fixed, and it disappears once k is calibrated together with the offset. The model's noise is independent for every KC, odor and trial, while part of the recordings' is shared within a repeat and across a KC's odors.

src: **The membrane-potential terms.** Six models (the reference model, the 70 Hz fit of its family, the first joint fit and the fit of its family with breadth exponent 3, and the best fit so far under each definition from [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits), which were still running) were simulated again at their fitted parameters, with APL on and with APL removed, with every KC's membrane potential saved; their spike counts equal the saved ones entry for entry. Each KC × odor trace is reduced to its mean over the odor window, relative to the last 100 ms before the odor and as a fraction of the distance to the KC's threshold (its peak in place of the mean gives nearly the same results). For an entry without a spike the readout adds a weight times the depolarization, at most the reading of one spike; for every non-responding entry (fewer than two spikes) it subtracts a weight times the hyperpolarization. The two weights are set together with k, b and c, on the APL-on run through the noise, so that the model has the control flies' share of entries between 0.25 and 1 z ({{data:ctrl_share_z_025_1 ~ .1%}}) and below −0.25 z ({{data:ctrl_share_z_below_m025 ~ .1%}}). Three controls separate what the potential holds from what any added term does: each term alone, the potential permuted across the non-spiking KCs within each odor and condition, and the APL-on potential used for both conditions. The terms are a test of where the recordings' low end could come from in the model, not a proposed readout.

src: Every wiring is at its own breadth-2 APL-effect fit ([above](#wiring-population)), the halves are those of the earlier search, split by fly with the two strongest recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) apart, and at every reading both response rates were set again. The test was fixed before any run. It is read on the mean over the four other wirings (two claw permutations and two matched shuffles), with each change at 0.6 of its size (its scores, or the logarithms of its factors, multiplied by 0.6), the share of one half's pattern that the other half reproduces.

src: **The two settings that were fitted.** The literature gives no largest spike count for a KC, only means and standard deviations per response: {{lit:4.9 ± 3.0 # spikes per response of α′/β′ KCs to a 500 ms odor (mean ± standard deviation, whole-cell recordings, APL intact), Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent (2008), as quoted in E69_kc_firing_ceiling.md, Design (part B), Realism and Caveats}} spikes for α′/β′ KCs and {{lit:2.2 ± 1.2 # spikes per response of α/β KCs to a 500 ms odor (mean ± standard deviation, whole-cell recordings, APL intact), Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent (2008), as quoted in E69_kc_firing_ceiling.md, Realism and Caveats}} for α/β KCs in whole-cell recordings with a 0.5 s odor (Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent, 2008; other odors and concentrations than the KC data's, APL intact). The bound used is the mean plus three standard deviations of the α′/β′ KCs, about {{lit:14 # the bound on a KC's spike count to one odor with APL on that the firing ceiling for the KCs takes from whole-cell recordings: the mean plus three standard deviations (4.9 + 3 x 3.0 = 13.9) of the spikes per response of α′/β′ KCs to a 500 ms odor in Turner, Bazhenov and Laurent (2008); E69_kc_firing_ceiling.md, Design (part B) and Caveats}} spikes, a reading that a measured largest count would replace. The literature setting is the weakest of the three strengths, at which the largest count of the breadth-2 APL-effect fit with APL on ({{E69/stats_variants.csv:e67cal_r3_a1_t1000:max_count_on ~ .0f}} at fixed scales, {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} once fitted) is nearest that bound. The stronger setting is the middle strength, the weakest at which the half-saturation of [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) runs to the upper end of its range for that fit: the model's counts with APL on are then no more concentrated than the control flies' responses, the readout has nothing to compress, and the two definitions of the model's side give the same scores. There the largest count of the breadth-2 fit with APL on is {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes and the 99th percentile of its responders' counts {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:p99_resp_count_on ~ .0f}}, about the mean of the α′/β′ KCs in the recordings, so the setting allows those KCs less than they show; in the reference model, whose counts are higher, the same strength gives a largest count of {{E69/stats_variants.csv:thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:max_count_on ~ .0f}}. Each fit is the joint fit under the APL-effect loss with the term on raw counts and the term under the calibrated readout at equal weight, the response rates held as constraints at the flies' response rate, the ceiling fixed and the usual four parameters free (the somatic threshold, the APL→KC scale with the KC→APL scale tied to it, the APL→bouton scale up to three times the baseline's, and the KC–KC scale), started from the run of its setting at fixed scales. For the breadth-2 family the fit without a ceiling is that family's fit with both definitions in the loss, which had ended at practically the same model as its fit under the readout, the one in the best-models table. Every fit simulated again at its fitted parameters reproduces its saved spike counts exactly.

src: **What the ceiling is not.** One adaptation variable per KC with one time constant is the simplest form that bounds a count. Real KC adaptation has several time scales (calcium-activated potassium currents, synaptic depression at the claws), and a time constant longer than the odor makes the model's version close to a cap on the number of spikes per odor. The result needs that: at the flies' 2 s pulse the 1 s adaptation wears off within the odor and about a fifth of the level on raw counts is lost, with the indicator's kinetics as measured in the recordings ([the time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces](#trace-time-course)), and it returns with an adaptation of 3 s ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)). Whether it holds with a less schematic adaptation has not been tested. The strength stays a choice until the largest spike count of a fly KC to a 0.5 s odor is measured.

src: **Caveats.** The baseline noise has been computed only for the recordings of this odor panel, those behind the two KC matrices; the other KC recordings this page refers to (the low-concentration panels, the wild-type recordings) are still in their own units, and no band uses them. A baseline-noise unit is not a unit of activity: the signal is not divided by a resting fluorescence, so a response in these units still depends on how bright a KC is, and the KCs that respond to many odors are the brighter ones on average; the baseline noise itself is no larger in those KCs than in the ones that respond to nothing, and does not differ between the genotypes by more than the recordings differ among themselves. Spikes and noise-normalized fluorescence are both fixed units but not the same unit: what ties them is the calibration at the control flies' response rate, at that one point, and the flies' responses are counted through measurement noise where the models' are not. The main target is not touched by any of this: the flies' odor-odor distances, and with them the per-pair APL effect and its floor, are computed from the recordings' z-scored values as before. Whether they too should be taken in baseline-noise units is a separate question, measured in [the data side of the main target](#data-side) and not yet decided: in these units the flies' mean APL effect is larger and its pattern across pairs is the same.

src: **What is done.** Distances are taken as similarities, one minus the distance. On each side, the flies' and the model's, one curve is fitted across the 120 pairs that gives a pair's similarity with APL on from its similarity with APL off: a power curve, the similarity with APL off raised to a power and multiplied by a factor, both found by least squares. A curve gives every pair an APL effect from its similarity with APL off alone. A pair's error, the model's APL effect minus the flies', is then exactly the sum of three terms. The inherited term is the effect that the flies' curve gives at the model's similarity with APL off minus the effect it gives at the flies' own: the error the model would have if it followed the flies' curve without departures. The curve term is the effect that the model's curve gives at the model's similarity with APL off minus the effect that the flies' curve gives there. The departures are the model's departure from its own curve on that pair minus the flies' departure from theirs. With each term's mean over the pairs removed, a term's share is its sum of products with the pattern error divided by the pattern error's squared sum; the three shares add to one, and a share is negative when its term offsets the others.

src: **The measured maps.** A recording holds one map per presentation, the mean of five frames around the peak of the response as a change over the baseline fluorescence, in blocks of three presentations: the solvent, then one odor at one concentration twice; one block is the solvent three times. A stimulus's map is the mean of its two presentations, each minus a solvent map. The solvent map was taken in three ways: the presentation at the same position within the solvent-only block, which is the baseline of the statistics of the measured maps in the text; the mean of all solvent presentations, which is the baseline of the comparison with the predicted maps (the first gives the same there); and the mean of the solvent presentations that open the blocks. The reliability of the maps, the likeness of different odors' maps and the direction of pa's shift against ms hold under each. Correlations between maps are over the pixels inside the calyx outline after a Gaussian smoothing of 2 pixels. The pattern common to a recording's stimuli is the first singular vector of its stimulus × pixel matrix, and the remainder of a map is the map without its part along that pattern. The remainder's statistics are over each odor's two highest concentrations, and its length is the distance at which the cross-correlation between the remainders of the two presentations falls to 1/e, which leaves out the noise that the presentations do not share. For the positions of two odors' responses, a recording's two concentrations are those at which the mean responses over the calyx are closest, among maps with a positive mean and a correlation between presentations of 0.5 or more; a fly's two hemispheres are averaged, and the intervals are from 10,000 resamplings of the flies.

src: **The co-localization proxy.** The inhibition of a glomerulus for an odor is either the same for all glomeruli, a strength times the odor's mean PN rate, or its local field, the PN rates of all glomeruli weighted by their co-localization with it, scaled so that the mean inhibition over odors and glomeruli is the same under both rules; negative evoked rates are set to zero. Subtractive inhibition takes the inhibition from the rate, with a floor at zero (strengths 0.5 and 1), and divisive inhibition divides the rate by one plus the inhibition over the mean rate (strengths 1 and 4). The proxy of a pair is its cosine distance under the local rule minus that under the global one. For a setting, the proxy, with its mean over the pairs removed, is multiplied by one factor fitted by least squares to the common error on the 105 pairs among 15 odors, and what is left of the common error on the 15 pairs of the left-out odor is summed, as squares, over the 16 odors; the share removed is one minus that sum over the common error's squared sum. The null permutes the glomeruli of the co-localization matrix, rows and columns together, 1,000 times, for each setting and for the best of all settings in each permutation. The test asked for 15 % or more removed on left-out odors, at or above the 95th percentile of the null.

src: **What it moved.** Taken over the whole half second, the level gives each claw an offset that is the same for every odor, and in the unit of the recordings, where a claw's signal is divided by its own variability, the pairs of odors read more alike with that offset than without it. From the settled level the model's claws are less alike and every step from claws to somata is smaller by as much; the boutons with APL on move by about a hundredth, the readings as changes of rate by less than that, and {{E90/settled_preodor/silent_claws.csv:wiring=M2;subset=all;cond=on:became_silent ~ .0f}} to {{E90/settled_preodor/silent_claws.csv:wiring=P3;subset=all;cond=on:became_silent ~ .0f}} of a wiring's {{E90/settled_preodor/silent_claws.csv:wiring=real;subset=all;cond=on:n_units_e90 ~ ,.0f}} claws, which APL holds at zero before and during every odor, have no response and leave the readings in that unit. In [the model's stages against the flies' stages](#model-stages) no verdict of the rule changed, and these readings did (the table has most of them). The claws of the glomeruli with ORN input, which over the half second had read as alike as the flies' for the ester pairs and the alcohol pairs, read less alike than the flies'. The steps with APL on from those claws, of which only the ester pairs' and the nearest pairs' had been too small in every reading of the somata, are too small in every group. From those claws the model's somata without APL are more alike than its claws in every reading of the somata, where on raw spike counts they had not been. At the flies' 2 s pulse the ester pairs' step with APL on from those claws is too small on raw counts as well. And from all claws the ester pairs' step with APL on, which on raw spike counts had been larger than the flies', is the flies' in every reading of the somata. The difference between a group's two steps, its error in the APL effect, is the same at either level, since both steps start from the same claws.

src: **Inhibition among KCs of similar tuning is not what the recordings show.** It moves the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input apart far more than the flies do: the four nearest ester pairs get an APL effect of {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=similar_pow1:near4 ~ +.3f}} where the flies have {{lit:+0.182 # mean of column effect over the four nearest ester pairs (2h with IaA, 2h with pa, IaA with pa, eb with ep), rows unit=z, reading=trial_means, form=data of results/E87_inhibition_form/forms_pairs.csv}} and the chosen form gives {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=sub_q1_p0.25_summed:near4 ~ +.3f}}. Its pattern part on all recordings, {{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=similar_pow1:pattern ~ .3f}}, is no better than that of no inhibition at all ({{E87/forms.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form=none:pattern ~ .3f}}), and on unseen halves it is {{lit:0.031 # results/E87_inhibition_form/verdict_A.json, similar_counts.mean_gain (sign reversed): the mean over the eight held-out readings in z (trial means and trial noise removed) of the similar-tuning form's pattern part minus the chosen form's}} worse than the chosen form on average, where 0.003 better had been set for it to count (last column of each half of the second table). What holds near-identical odors apart in the flies with APL is reproduced, in their own responses, by an inhibition that all KCs share, without one aimed at the KCs that respond alike.

src: **A target that needs no APL.** What a form does within the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), the distances of their reduced responses minus their own, is itself a per-pair effect, and a model's responses with APL off can be scored against it by putting them through the same form. It is a comparison within each recording and needs no control flies, where the main target is a difference between two groups of flies. For the flies' chosen form the floor of its pattern part is about half the main target's in the same convention, two halves of the flies agree on it far better, and its ceiling is {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form_label=chosen;subset=all:ceiling ~ .2f}} against {{E87/apl_free_target.csv:unit=z;reading=trial_means;form_label=chosen;subset=all:main_ceiling ~ .2f}} (table above).

src: A mechanism that changes the responses without APL is read on both targets, the one without APL for the responses and the main one for what the model's APL makes of them. Changes on APL's side are not the lead on the fits as they are and are not excluded; where they are taken up, it is on a base with the flies' recruitment. The shortfall on the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input ([above](#input-population)) is of a piece with this: in the flies a shared inhibition holds those pairs apart, and an inhibition among KCs of similar tuning, the kind that would hold near-identical inputs apart in a model, is not what the recordings show.

src: A rule fixed beforehand said when this step may be used as a second reading of the target's pattern. The two halves of the four claw flies had to agree on it at 0.6 or more, and its floor, the distance between a step from resampled flies and the measured one, had to be at most half of its standard deviation over the pairs. It passes in both readings of the claws, clearly on the first condition and by a hair on the second (second table below).

src: The step from claws to somata by group of pairs: the distance across the somata minus the distance across the claws, as the mean over a group's pairs. The flies' steps use the claws of wild-type flies with the trial noise removed and are given with the 90 % interval over resampled flies of both stages. The model's are the mean over the eight wirings, from its claws with APL on, the drive alone, in the unit of the recordings and from their settled level before the odor; the rule read its somata through the calibrated readout, and raw spike counts are given beside for the claws of the 36 glomeruli

src: **What follows.** Where along the pathway the common error is made is not decided by these recordings, and the model's side of this subsection is a set of readings, not a verdict. src: The earlier comparison of the stages ([above](#model-stages)) is qualified in two respects. src: **What is fitted.** The 120 pair distances of the control matrix are regressed on the 120 pair distances of the APL output blocked (TNT) matrix with isotonic regression: the fitted curve is the non-decreasing step function that is closest to the control values in the least-squares sense (the pool-adjacent-violators algorithm; scikit-learn's IsotonicRegression with increasing=True). "Isotonic" means order-preserving: the curve may bend any way as long as it never goes down, so a pair that is farther apart with APL output blocked is predicted to be at least as far apart in control flies. The isotonic R² is the fraction of the control variance the curve explains (0.94); a pair's residual is its control distance minus the curve's value at its APL output blocked (TNT) distance; and the block is the mean residual of the nine fruity × small-ester pairs ({{data:block ~ +.3f}}), with its confidence interval from resampling recordings.
out: **What is fitted.** The 120 pair correlations of the control matrix are regressed on the 120 pair correlations of the APL output blocked (TNT) matrix with isotonic regression: the fitted curve is the non-decreasing step function that is closest to the control values in the least-squares sense (the pool-adjacent-violators algorithm; scikit-learn's IsotonicRegression with increasing=True). "Isotonic" means order-preserving: the curve may bend any way as long as it never goes down, so a pair that is more correlated with APL output blocked is predicted to be at least as correlated in control flies. The isotonic R² is the fraction of the control variance the curve explains (0.94); a pair's residual is its control correlation minus the curve's value at its APL output blocked (TNT) correlation; and the block is how far the nine fruity × small-ester pairs sit below that curve on average, the fit's value minus the measured correlation ({{data:block ~ +.3f}}), with its confidence interval from resampling recordings.

src: **Why this fit.** The hypothesis being tested is that APL's output is a uniform sparsening: every pair moves in the same direction by an amount that depends only on how far apart the pair already is. Any such effect is a monotone map from the APL output blocked (TNT) matrix to the control matrix, and isotonic regression is the most general monotone map, so its residuals contain only what no uniform effect can produce, the pair-specific part. It assumes nothing about the shape of the map (the data's map is strongly compressive at the top, where KC distances saturate near 1), it has no tuning parameter, and its R² can be compared directly with the measurement ceiling computed the same way between halves of the recordings.

src: **The alternatives, and why not.** A linear fit of control on APL output blocked (TNT) assumes the change is proportional; with the saturation near 1 it explains less of the control variance (R² 0.85 against 0.94) and leaves curved residuals, so its block estimate (+0.098) mixes the pair-specific effect with the curvature the line cannot follow. A parametric saturating curve (a power or logistic function) has fewer degrees of freedom but imposes a shape the data would have to meet, and the block estimate then depends on that choice. Rank correlation alone (Spearman 0.87) tests monotonicity but gives no per-pair residual, so it cannot locate the block.

src: Thirty such trials, drawn from a seeded generator so that every model gets the same draws, are grouped into ten pseudo-recordings of three and processed as the KC data are: the three trials of a recording are averaged, the cosine distances between odors are taken on those means and averaged over the recordings, and the fruity × small-ester block is the mean isotonic excess of the nine pairs; the grand mean over all thirty trials is reported beside it. "The pipeline" on this page is this procedure, and "the block through the noise" its block. Noise on the PN firing rates was tried first and set aside because it averages out over the response window and cannot reach the data's floors; jitter of each glomerulus's input gain reaches them as the threshold jitter does and is the alternative the trial-to-trial variability experiment kept beside it.

src: The margin proxy predicts what the pipeline would measure (the floors, the per-trial response rates, the odor-odor distances, the block through the noise) from one deterministic run, without simulating the noise. src: **Why this split.** The two parts point at different kinds of mechanism. An APL that acts too strongly or too weakly on one odor moves all of that odor's pairs together and shows in the per-odor part; an error in which KCs two particular odors have in common shows in the pair-specific part. The assignment is to parts of the error, not to causes: a per-odor part can come from which KCs an odor recruits as well as from how many APL removes, which is what the oracle was built to separate.

src: **What is done.** Distances are taken as similarities, one minus the distance. On each side, the flies' and the model's, one curve is fitted across the 120 pairs that gives a pair's similarity with APL on from its similarity with APL off: a power curve, the similarity with APL off raised to a power and multiplied by a factor, both found by least squares. A curve gives every pair an APL effect from its similarity with APL off alone. A pair's error, the model's APL effect minus the flies', is then exactly the sum of three terms.

src: The inherited term is the effect that the flies' curve gives at the model's similarity with APL off minus the effect it gives at the flies' own: the error the model would have if it followed the flies' curve without departures. The curve term is the effect that the model's curve gives at the model's similarity with APL off minus the effect that the flies' curve gives there. The departures are the model's departure from its own curve on that pair minus the flies' departure from theirs. With each term's mean over the pairs removed, a term's share is its sum of products with the pattern error divided by the pattern error's squared sum; the three shares add to one, and a share is negative when its term offsets the others.

src: **Why this split.** A change of the input changes a pair's distance in both conditions. Where a model's distances with APL on follow its curve, such a change moves a pair along the curve, and the error it reaches in this way is the inherited term. The curve term belongs to how strongly APL separates pairs at a given similarity, and the departures to what APL does to particular pairs, the block among them. The split says where an error lies, not what causes it, and it is not a bound: an input set freely for every glomerulus of every odor also moves a wiring's departures, as the search on the real wiring did.

src: The pattern common to a recording's stimuli is the first singular vector of its stimulus × pixel matrix, and the remainder of a map is the map without its part along that pattern. The remainder's statistics are over each odor's two highest concentrations, and its length is the distance at which the cross-correlation between the remainders of the two presentations falls to 1/e, which leaves out the noise that the presentations do not share. For the positions of two odors' responses, a recording's two concentrations are those at which the mean responses over the calyx are closest, among maps with a positive mean and a correlation between presentations of 0.5 or more; a fly's two hemispheres are averaged, and the intervals are from 10,000 resamplings of the flies.
